articles.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
articles.text:
Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file.
Patches for the flaw were released last month by Apple in versions iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, acknowledging that it may have been exploited in sophisticated attacks against specific individuals using devices running iOS before iOS 27.
The fixes have now been expanded to include iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11, which support iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR, iPad 7th generation, iPad Air 4th generation and later, iPad 9th generation and later, and iPad mini 6th generation and later.
"Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27," the company said.
iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11 also address a logic issue in Audio (CVE-2026-65339) that could be exploited by an app to leak sensitive user information and an access vulnerability in CoreMedia (CVE-2026-86990) that could be abused by a malicious app to access the camera without user permission.
The release comes as Apple shipped iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, tvOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, and Safari 27.2, fixing hundreds of vulnerabilities, including many in AppleAVD, CoreAudio, ImageIO, kernel, Model I/O, Screen Sharing Server, Spotlight, StorageKit, and WebKit.
Notable among the defects is an authorization issue in Apple Intelligence (CVE-2026-86987) that could be exploited by a remote attacker to access sensitive user data. The iPhone maker said the issue was addressed in iOS and iPadOS with improved entitlement checks.
Although Apple makes no mention of any of these flaws being exploited in the wild, it's always a good practice to update the devices to the latest version for optimal protection.

articles.title: Fadi Ghandour and Hamad Al Hajri to lead discussions at Doha's Downtown Tech Summit
articles.text: Msheireb Properties and Inc. Arabia have announced the speaker lineup for the second Downtown Tech Summit, scheduled for November 17, 2026, at Barahat Msheireb in Doha, Qatar. The event will feature Hamad Al Hajri, founder and CEO of Snoonu, and Fadi Ghandour, Executive Chairman of Wamda Capital, alongside Khaled Talhouni of Nuwa Capital, Soumaya Ben Beya Dridje of Rasmal Ventures and Dr. Ammar Alali of Strataphy. The summit will bring together startup founders, venture capital investors and technology leaders to discuss scaling regional companies internationally, responding to market disruption and applying emerging technologies to business challenges. It will also host the live pitch finale of the Azal Innovation Programme. The event precedes the inaugural Best in Business Awards Qatar ceremony on November 18, which has received more than 180 nominations. Organisers have now extended the nomination deadline to November 4. Press release: Msheireb Properties, Qatar’s leading sustainable real estate developer, and Inc. Arabia, the Middle East edition of the global media brand Inc., have revealed the expanded speaker line-up and agenda for the second edition of the Downtown Tech Summit, featuring headline speakers including Snoonu founder and CEO Hamad Al Hajri and Wamda Group Executive Chairman Fadi Ghandour. The announcement comes as the inaugural Doha edition of the Best in Business Awards passes a milestone 180 nominations, prompting organisers to extend the submission deadline to 4 November 2026. Taking place on 17 November, 2026, at Barahat Msheireb in Msheireb Downtown Doha, the Summit is organised with the strategic participation and support of various entities, including Qatar Science & Technology Park (QSTP) and Siemens. The gathering will bring together leading venture capitalists, technology innovators, and regional business leaders, including: Hamad Al Hajri, founder and CEO, Snoonu (Qatar) Fadi Ghandour, Executive Chairman, Wamda Capital (UAE) Khaled Talhouni, Managing Partner, Nuwa Capital (UAE) Soumaya Ben Beya Dridje, Partner, Rasmal Ventures (Qatar) Dr. Ammar Alali, founder and CEO, Strataphy (KSA) Running from 4:00 PM to 8:30 PM, the Summit features a dynamic format combining keynote presentations, panel discussions, and fireside chats. Topics being explored include how regional tech ecosystems can scale companies to compete globally, strategies for turning market disruption into growth opportunities, and practical applications of emerging technology to drive real-world business impact. Additionally, the Summit will host the live pitch finale for the Azal Innovation Programme, an initiative launched by Doha Design District, part of Msheireb Properties, where shortlisted innovators and entrepreneurs will pitch their ideas directly to investors and industry experts. The ecosystem showcase will conclude on 18 November, 2026, at Barahat Msheireb with the gala ceremony for the inaugural Qatar edition of the Best in Business Awards, honouring standout enterprises and leaders. Submissions are open until 4 November at [ Link ]. Noora Al Qubaisi, Acting Director of Corporate Communication at Msheireb Properties, said, "Bringing founders and investors of this calibre to Msheireb Downtown Doha provides Qatar’s business and tech community with direct access to leaders who have built and scaled landmark companies in the region. Alongside the remarkable response to the Best in Business Awards, this reflects a private sector that is confident, resilient, and expanding. Msheireb was intentionally designed to serve as a living platform for innovation and meaningful dialogue, and we look forward to welcoming the community to Barahat Msheireb this November.” Anas Abbar, co-founder and Group CEO of 7awi Media Group, the media house behind Inc. Arabia, added, "Surpassing 180 nominations for the inaugural edition of the Best in Business Awards Doha speaks volumes about the ambition and maturity of Qatar’s business ecosystem. Extending the deadline gives more companies, founders, and leaders the opportunity to put their achievements forward. We look forward to celebrating their impact while also indulging in the insights shared by the visionary speakers taking the stage at the Downtown Tech Summit.” Registration to attend the Downtown Tech Summit is now open at [ Link ].

articles.title: Halloween : Intego ONE Advanced passe à 65,99€ pour 2 ans sur Mac (-40 %)
articles.text:
Pour Halloween, Intego retire 40 % à la formule de sa suite Mac qui ajoute le nettoyage du disque à l’antivirus et au pare-feu. Intego ONE Advanced revient à 65,99 € pour deux ans, sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours, mais notre test a relevé un moteur anti-malware gourmand en mémoire.
Intego ONE a remplacé au printemps 2026 l’ancienne gamme X9 de l’éditeur, avec une application unique pour protéger et entretenir un Mac. La suite se décline en trois formules : Essential réunit l’antivirus et le pare-feu, Advanced y ajoute SmartClean, Complete y ajoute encore un VPN.
L’offre Intego ONE Advanced à 65,99 € pour deux ans couvre un Mac, avec 40 % de réduction. Elle vise ceux qui veulent une protection pensée pour macOS et un disque désencombré, sans payer pour un VPN dont ils n’ont pas l’usage.
Intego ONE Advanced pour 1 Mac pendant 2 ans passe à 65,99 € au lieu de 109,99 € sur le site d’Intego, soit 2,75 € par mois.
Pourquoi choisir Intego ONE Advanced ?
- Une détection confirmée par un laboratoire : En mars 2026, AV-Test a attribué à Intego ONE la note maximale de 6/6 en protection, performance et utilisation, avec 100 % de détection sur 405 malwares macOS récents. Les fichiers suspects sont placés en quarantaine.
- Un pare-feu qui montre qui se connecte : Le pare-feu affiche les connexions de vos applications, souvent en arrière-plan, et vous laisse les autoriser ou les bloquer une par une.
- SmartClean pour récupérer de l’espace : C’est l’apport de la formule Advanced : SmartClean repère les fichiers inutiles, les caches et les journaux, montre comment le stockage est occupé et désinstalle une application sans laisser de fichiers résiduels.
Protéger un Mac et faire de la place, dans la même application
Au quotidien, l’antivirus surveille les téléchargements, les pièces jointes et les fichiers partagés, avec des analyses rapides, complètes ou personnalisées que l’on peut planifier. Il détecte aussi les malwares Windows, utile quand des fichiers passent d’une machine à l’autre. SmartClean suit l’usage du processeur, de la mémoire et du disque, et vous laisse choisir ce qui part à la corbeille. Sur un Mac dont le SSD sature, c’est lui qui justifie Advanced plutôt qu’Essential.
Dans notre test d’Intego ONE, nous avions apprécié une interface claire et visuelle, mais relevé deux réserves qui comptent à l’usage. Au premier lancement, le pare-feu multiplie les alertes et demande de valider chaque application installée. Surtout, l’ensemble des processus occupait environ 1,3 Go de mémoire au repos, dont 1,03 Go pour le seul moteur anti-malware. Sur un Mac doté de 8 Go, le minimum exigé par l’éditeur, cette empreinte pèsera davantage que sur une machine de 16 Go.
Advanced, la formule du milieu face aux suites concurrentes
Advanced ne contient ni VPN, réservé à la formule Complete, ni contrôle parental, ni filtre anti-phishing dédié. Bitdefender Total Security, deuxième de notre comparatif des meilleurs antivirus pour Mac, intègre justement une protection web et anti-phishing et propose un essai de 30 jours, quand Intego mise sur une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours. Norton 360 vise plutôt les familles. Intego ONE garde la première place de ce classement, pour sa suite pensée pour macOS.
✅ Les points forts
- Note maximale chez AV-Test en mars 2026, avec 100 % de détection
- Pare-feu avec règles par application
- SmartClean pour nettoyer le disque et désinstaller proprement
- Prix sous le plus bas des 30 derniers jours
- Garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours
❌ Les limites
- Environ 1,3 Go de mémoire occupée au repos selon notre test
- Alertes du pare-feu nombreuses au premier lancement
- Ni VPN, ni contrôle parental, ni anti-phishing dédié
- Renouvellement automatique à 109,99 € tous les 2 ans
L’offre Halloween ramène Intego ONE Advanced à 2,75 € par mois pendant deux ans, sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours.
Passer sous le plus bas des 30 derniers jours donne à cette remise Halloween un intérêt réel. La formule réunit une protection validée par AV-Test, un pare-feu complet et un outil de nettoyage utile sur un Mac à l’étroit. Elle convient aux propriétaires de Mac qui veulent une suite unique, pensée pour macOS, et qui ont déjà un VPN ou n’en voient pas l’utilité.
Elle convaincra moins sur un Mac limité à 8 Go de mémoire. Si le phishing vous inquiète davantage que les malwares, une suite comme Bitdefender, dotée d’un filtre web, colle mieux à votre besoin. Pensez aussi au renouvellement automatique à 109,99 € dans deux ans : noter l’échéance dès l’achat vous laisse le temps de comparer avant de rempiler.

articles.title: Meet the TechRadar Product of the Year 2026 winners — our editors choose their favorite gadgets of the last 12 months
articles.text:
Though 2026 has been a tumultuous time for technology when it comes to price hikes and shortages, the tech that's reached us has been excellent — in fact, it's been a banner year in most areas, just with some downsides for your wallet.
We've already crowned the best tech of the year as chosen by you in our TechRadar Readers' Choice Awards 2026 — but this is where we let our experts have their say.
Our writers and editors chose their favorite products in nearly 100 categories, ranging across all the kinds of products we review. In some cases, we agree with the readers; in lots of cases, we don't. So read on to see which gadgets we rate as being the most impressive of the last 12 months.
Phones & tablets
Phone of the Year
Apple iPhone 18 Pro
Wherever you look, the iPhone 18 Pro excels. It might not have the biggest camera sensor or the longest-lasting battery of any phone on the market, but it does offer a near-unrivaled combination of premium flagship features. From its variable aperture feature and pro-level video capabilities to its phenomenal performance and gorgeous display, the 18 Pro is the Swiss Army knife of 2026 smartphones.
Read our full iPhone 18 Pro review
Phone Brand of the Year
Honor
The Chinese company has brought something competitive to the table at every turn in 2026. The Honor Magic 8 Pro is an extremely capable flagship. The Magic V6 is easily one of the best foldables you can buy. The Honor 600 series offers some serious value for money in the mid-range sector. The MagicPad 4 is an iPad-beating tablet in several ways. And the Robot Phone is, well, the Robot Phone. Honor’s products aren’t globally available in the same way as, say, Apple's or Samsung’s, but those who have tried the brand’s phones and tablets will know about their level of hardware quality.
Phones Innovation of the Year
Honor Robot Phone
Sticking with Honor, it’s hard to see past the Robot Phone as the most exciting Phones Innovation of the Year in 2026. There's been some competition from foldables in this area this year, but Honor deserves credit for bringing something wildly different to the market (in China, at least). Will we ever see the Robot Phone and its fully motorized mechanical gimbal arm in Western markets? I doubt it — but that doesn’t make it any less exciting.
Read our Honor Robot Phone hands-on
Best Value Phone
Motorola Edge 70 Fusion
The Motorola Edge 70 Fusion is in another world for pure value compared to most phones — for example, compared to the iPhone 17e, it costs almost exactly half the price and offers an extra camera, a much larger battery, faster charging, and a higher display refresh rate. The Edge 70 Fusion is not a flashy phone, but it certainly punches above its budget price tag.
Best Mid-Range Phone
Apple iPhone 17
The Apple iPhone 17 is over 12 months old now (it just slips into this year’s eligibility window), and it wasn’t replaced with a successor in September — but it didn’t need to be. With its 120Hz refresh rate, two great rear cameras, powerful A19 chipset, and still-industry-leading Center Stage selfie camera, the iPhone 17 is still the iPhone we recommend to most people.
Best Folding Phone
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the only globally available passport-shaped foldable we’ve tested fully (and that's eligible for this year's awards), and it's earned our pick as the Best Folding Phone of the year. We were skeptical about the practicality of the Z Fold 8’s stumpy form factor, but after living with the phone for a month, we came around to its charming oddness.
Read our full Samsung Galaxy Z fold 8 review
Best Flip Phone
Motorola Razr Ultra 2026
The Motorola Razr Ultra 2026 (or Motorola Razr 70 Ultra, as it’s called in certain regions) is, for us, the best phone you can buy in this category. The Galaxy Z Flip 8 has better software, a newer chipset, and is slightly more affordable — but the latest Razr Ultra has a larger battery, faster charging, and better cameras. It’s a close-run thing, but this is the flip phone we'd choose.
Best Camera Phone
Oppo Find X9 Ultra
The Oppo Find X9 Ultra is an absolute beast of a camera phone. It boasts a 200MP main lens, a 50MP ultra-wide lens, a 200MP 3x telephoto lens, and a 50MP 10x telephoto (f/3.5) lens, which is a combination that helped it beat the Galaxy S26 Ultra and hold its own against even the Lumix TZ300 and Nikon Z8 in our head-to-head comparisons. It’s heavy, thick, and eye-wateringly expensive, but the Find X9 Ultra is the closest we’ve come to a truly camera-rivaling smartphone.
Read our full Oppo Find X9 Ultra review
Best Gaming Phone
RedMagic 11 Pro
If you’re looking for an unashamedly gamer-y smartphone, it doesn’t get much better than the RedMagic 11 Pro. With its exposed water-cooling system, capacitive shoulder buttons, powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset, and gorgeous 6.85-inch OLED display, it’s more handheld console than phone.
Read our full RedMagic 11 Pro review
Best AI Phone
Google Pixel 11 Pro
Even though Google’s latest Pixel series doesn’t bring much newness to the table, it’s hard to argue against the Pixel 11 Pro’s status as the Best AI Phone money can buy. There’s Camera Coach, Magic Cue, Magic Editor, Magic Capture, Rambler, and, of course, system-wide Gemini integration to take advantage of with Google’s latest flagship. If AI is your jam, the Pixel 11 Pro should be your phone.
Read our full Google Pixel 11 Pro review
Best Phone Accessory
DJI Osmo Mobile 8P
Phone gimbals aren’t the flashiest products around, but the DJI Osmo Mobile 8P deserves credit for being one of the best phone accessories money can buy. As we noted in our review, the 8P adds a remote control and even better tracking capabilities to the already impressive Osmo Mobile 8 formula, and as such, it’s an easy recommendation for content creators.
Read our full DJI Osmo Mobile 8P review
Best Tablet
Honor MagicPad 4
The Android tablet market is a real mix of good, bad, and terrible right now, but the Honor MagicPad 4 surprised us by being a genuinely iPad-rivaling slate in testing this year. For a lower price than the latest iPad Air, the MagicPad 4 offers a thin and lightweight design, a stunning OLED screen, an excellent eight-speaker stereo setup, and near-unbeatable update support. Here’s hoping Honor continues its hot streak into 2027.
Read our full Honor MagicPad 4 review
Best eReader
Amazon Kindle Scribe (2025)
The last 12 months have seen plenty of great ereaders and digital note-takers come to market, but the Amazon Kindle Scribe (2025) has become our go-to recommendation for those after an ereader/notebook hybrid. It's pricey, yes, but the Scribe’s 11-inch E Ink Carta 1300 display is a joy to behold.
Read our full Amazon Kindle Scribe (2025) review
Cameras & drones
Camera of the Year
Sony A7R VI
Perfect ratings are rare, but the A7R VI earned five stars with its 66.8MP stacked full-frame sensor, image stabilization, new processor and improved subject-detection autofocus, which combine for class-leading quality and performance. Whether you shoot landscape photography or action, the A7R VI can handle it all, and its excellent handling and new and improved battery was the cherry on the cake. Our verdict? "Sony can stop making cameras now."
Read our full Sony A7R VI review
Brand of the Year
Sony
Following a relatively quiet year, Sony has stood out in 2026 with three top cameras and a raft of new lenses. We gave a perfect five-star rating to the Sony A7R VI, which received high praise from our veteran Cameras Editor who said it had "no weaknesses". The A7 V took top spot in our best mirrorless cameras guide, while the RX10 V revived bridge cameras and extended Sony’s lead at the top in this category. Add Sony’s stellar macro lens to the mix and this award was inevitable.
Camera Innovation of the Year
Antigravity A1
The Antigravity A1 was a first-of-its-kind drone, one that can shoot true 360 degree video thanks to its dual camera array. The Insta360-backed company effectively gave us an airborne Insta360 X5, with immersive 8K video recording that sees in every direction. At the launch event, we donned the company’s goggles and followed racing cars around a track, and the whole experience was intuitive — but most of all immersive. You don’t need to worry about framing the shot, because that happens later using Insta360’s clever software, which can frame and compile videos after the fact.
Read our full Antigravity A1 review
Best Beginner Camera
OM System PEN
It was a tight call between the OM System PEN and the Lumix L10, but ultimately we felt that the PEN is the better starting point for beginner photographers, at a much lower price point. Not only is the PEN easy on the eye, but it features image stabilization, a rangefinder-style EVF, a weatherproof body, and a host of clever computational photography modes that smartphone upgrades will feel at home with, and that encourage creativity. A huge choice of lenses and a new weatherproof kit lens complete the package.
Read our OM System PEN review
Best Mid-range camera
Sony A7 V
The mid-range full-frame category is fiercely contested by Canon, Nikon, Sony and Panasonic, but Sony stole back its crown with the new A7 V, in a year that Canon also released the stellar EOS R6 Mark III. Between those two 5-star cameras, we felt the A7 V had the (slight) edge overall; there's nothing to choose in terms of resolution, but the A7 V has a partially stacked sensor for what should be quicker readout speeds, plus snappier subject detection autofocus, wider dynamic range, versatile flip-and-tilt screen, and class-leading battery life.
Read our Sony A7 V review
Best Professional Camera
Sony A7R VI
It’s actually been a quiet year in the professional camera category, but that's probably good for the other companies, because the A7R VI would’ve been hard for anyone to compete with. It ups the bar with a class-leading 66.8MP full-frame stacked sensor that's backed up with the power, speed and pro-grade body that make the camera a formidable tool in any pro photography scenario. We shot landscape, portrait and wildlife photography, and the pro camera thrived in all situations.
Read our full Sony A7R VI review
Best Compact and Instant Camera
Ricoh GR IV
Being intimately familiar with the GR III, we were super excited about the GR IV launch and the upgrades it would bring. A new 26MP APS-C sensor with five-axis stabilization and improved battery life topped the improvements, but we’ll have to keep fingers crossed for next time for the improved build quality, a tilt screen and built-in-flash we wished for. Even still, the GR IV can shoot the best quality photos from a truly pocketable camera, with a dedicated Monochrome edition that came alter to boot. The price hike stung, but no other brand is making a compact like Ricoh is.
Read our Ricoh GR IV review
Best Action and Vlogging Camera
DJI Osmo Pocket 4P
It’s been a busy year in this category, with Insta360 and DJI in particular trading blows. First came DJI's Pocket 4, which was a modest upgrade of the Pocket 3, but DJI had something extra special up its sleeve; a twin-lens gimbal camera Pocket 4P, which would change the game for vlogging. Insta360 then tried to steal DJI’s thunder with its innovative Luna Ultra's twin lenses and removable remote module — but DJI's Pocket 4P feels like the more polished of the two, and the one we have found ourselves turning to more often for shooting stabilized 4K content.
Read our DJI Osmo Pocket 4P review
Best Camera Lens
Sigma 135mm f/1.4 DG | Art
Lenses is a competitive category year after year, and 2025-2026 was no different, with a top Sony macro optic, Nikon's slimmed down 70-200mm f/2.8 and a number of superb-value Viltrox optics. However, we must recognize innovation and give credit where it's due, which is why Sigma’s first 135mm telephoto lens with a f/1.4 aperture blew us away. Bulky, yes, but we gave it five stars in our review, calling the 135mm F1.4 DG / Art the 'bokeh master' — if you want the dreamiest portraits, look no further.
Read our Sigma 135mm f/1.4 DG | Art review
Best Camera Accessory
Insta360 Mic Pro
DJI and Insta360 have been trading blows all year, but it was Insta360’s Mic Pro that was the final piece of the jigsaw for the 360 camera maker’s ecosystem. Insta360 fans using the likes of the class leading X6 360-degree camera, Ace Pro 2 action cam and Luna Ultra vlogging cameras can enjoy all the benefits of direct compatibility with one of the best wireless mics we’ve ever tested — mixing and matching their camera with a third party mic is no longer necessary. And what a mic it was — the Mic Pro has DJI-beating noise cancellation and an eye-catching, customizable e ink display.
Read our Insta360 Mic Pro review
Best Drone
DJI Avata 360
First came the Antigravity A1 drone, and then came the DJI Avata 360, which felt like the more polished and versatile 360-degree drone of the two. Where the A1 has two fixed lenses to capture 360-degree footage, the Avata 360’s twin lenses are mounted to a gimbal which can rotate 90 degrees to switch between regular (front-facing) single-lens and top/bottom facing 360-degree use. The product also joins DJI's existing Avata ecosystem, which already includes superb FPV goggles and motion controller accessories. Bottom line — the A1 came first, but the Avata 360 upped the bar, and it costs much less.
Read our DJI Avata 360 review
Computing
Laptop of the Year
Apple MacBook Neo
If there's one laptop that has made the biggest impact in 2026, then it's the MacBook Neo. When Apple announced its brand-new MacBook earlier this year, along with the impressively-affordable starting price of $599 / £599 / AU$1,049, it sent shockwaves through the industry. That might sound like hyperbole, but by releasing a budget laptop that still features a premium-feeling (and looking) design and without too many compromises when it comes to features and performance, the MacBook Neo shook rival PC makers out of their complacency and got them to up their budget laptop game. We had numerous laptop makers freely admit that they were releasing $600 laptops to challenge the MacBook Neo. For the sheer impact alone, the MacBook Neo has to be our pick as laptop of the year.
Read our full MacBook Neo review
Computing Brand of the Year
Nvidia
Once again, Nvidia has dominated the computing industry this year — all without releasing a new consumer graphics card. While the AI bubble, and Nvidia's role in it, continues to have a huge impact on the computing industry, the company has continued to innovate. DLSS 4.5 brought improved image quality to Nvidia's upscaling tech, while also introducing 6x Multi Frame Generation that can help improve gaming performance, especially on lower-end cards. Nvidia also released RTX Spark, its Arm-based System-on-Chip (SoC) aimed at taking on Apple's M-series chips, especially in regards to creative and local AI tasks. Even its controversial DLSS 5 feature has won over some critics since its announcement.
Best Computing Innovation
Intel Arc G3 Extreme
This year's release of the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chip — yes, another SoC, this time one that's been specifically designed for mobile gaming devices by concentrating on graphics performance and power efficiency. So, it's not surprising that it is the beating heart of many of the most powerful and exciting PC gaming handhelds that have come out this year, including the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, Acer Predator Atlas 8, and OneXPlayer 3. They're all expensive, sadly, but they offer truly brilliant gaming performance in even the most graphically-intensive titles, and the Intel chip is why.
Best Value Laptop
Dell XPS 13 (2026)
While we were very tempted to give the MacBook Neo our award for the best value laptop of 2026, we've actually gone for one of the laptops it influenced: this year's XPS 13. In the past, Dell's XPS 13 laptop was a premium thin and light laptop, but Dell relaunched it as an affordable alternative to Apple's laptop, initially targeting the same $600 starting price. This isn't a conspiracy — Dell explicitly compared the XPS 13 to the MacBook Neo when showing off the laptop to us. The reason we're giving the XPS 13 the edge is that it feels like Dell made fewer compromises with its affordable laptop, especially when it comes to backlit keyboard and faster USB-C ports.
Read our full Dell XPS 13 (2026) review
Best AI Laptop
Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra
Pretty much any laptop these days ships with some form of AI feature included, even baked into the operating system — but of all the laptops that have come out this year, the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra is, in our view, the best AI laptop because it doesn't just settle for adding AI features from other companies. Instead, Samsung has included its own Galaxy AI features, which offer additional tools, and work across its laptops, smartphones, and tablets. While not every Galaxy AI feature is a killer app, it shows a level of ambition and investment that many of its competitors lack.
Read our full Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra review
Best Gaming Laptop
Razer Blade 18
Razer has been putting out excellent gaming laptops for years, marrying cutting-edge technology with thin and light designs that banish any memory of big and bulky gaming laptops of yore. This year's Razer Blade 18 is no exception, offering almost desktop-levels of performance thanks to some of the most powerful components on the market today, with up to an RTX 5090 GPU and 128GB of DDR5 RAM. You can throw any game at this thing and it'll handle it like a champ, and its large 18-inch display offers UHD+ resolution at 240Hz, and FHD+ at an incredibly fast 440Hz, for unbelievably slick performance in games.
Read our full Razer Blade 18 (2026) review
Best PC Gaming Handheld
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
While all the Intel Arc G3 Extreme-powered PC gaming handhelds that we saw at Computex were impressive, one stood out: the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+. Not only was it one of the first handheld to come with Intel's latest hardware, but MSI completely redesigned the device itself to make it feel more comfortable and responsive when playing. This bore out in our full review, which highlighted the incredible performance (for a handheld) and the bright and vibrant screen that really made the games look spectacular.
Read our full MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review
Best Gaming Keyboard
Corsair Makr Pro 75
Reliability, performance, and build quality are all incredibly important considerations in a keyboard, and the Corsair Makr Pro 75 ticks every box. Its Corsair MGX Hyperdrive magnetic hot-swappable hall effect switches are an absolute joy to type on, and the overall build quality is exceptional (if a little heavy). It's expensive, and the software isn't great, but when crowning 2026's top gaming keyboard, there was only one choice here.
Read our full Corsair Makr Pro 75 review
Best Gaming Mouse
Razer Naga V3 Pro
The Razer Naga V3 Pro is an incredibly versatile gaming mouse that, thanks to its swappable side plates that offer gamers two, six, or 12 additional buttons, will appeal to almost any one, no matter what time of games you play. We use this mouse with the six-button side plate (which is easily attached via magnets) for quick access to macros and shortcuts while playing current obsession Planet Coaster 2. The mouse feels very comfortable to use, the 50K optical sensor offers fantastic control and with an 8,000Hz polling rate, even when used wirelessly, this is a mouse that can give you a serious competitive advantage.
Read our full Razer Naga V3 Pro review
Best Gaming Monitor
Alienware AW3426DW QD-OLED
The Alienware AW3426DW is an ultra-wide gaming monitor with a stunning five-layer tandem OLED panel that offers incredible, vision-spanning image quality. It supports Dolby Vision HDR, and a very fast 280Hz refresh rate that makes it a great choice for fast and frantic competitive games. The 3440x1440 (offering a 21:9 ultrawide aspect ratio) offers plenty of detail without putting too much strain on your GPU, and that wider field of vision, along with the fast refresh rate, could make a huge difference when playing.
Read our full Alienware AW3426DW QD-OLED review
Gaming
Gaming Device of the Year
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite
The Arctis Nova Elite is the best gaming headset we've ever tested. It's simply that good. It's not just a headset that has you covered by collecting features you'll find elsewhere altogether either; this is a genuinely individual beast. The design and build are of premium materials: SteelSeries has made a custom Carbon Fiber driver with a brass surround ring for spectacular hi-res audio. Connectivity is all you could ever want in terms of need and convenience, and the whole experience is absolutely fantastic. A world-beater of a gaming headset and device that is peerless.
Read our full SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite review
Gaming Brand of the Year
Asus
With an enormous number and diversity of products being launched by the gaming brand, from first attempts at desktop soundbars to quality PC gaming handheld follow-ups, and more excellent gaming monitors with the latest panels in that you can shake a stick at, Asus has been the hardware brand to beat this past year.
Gaming Innovation of the Year
Nvidia DLSS 4.5
With PC gaming becoming increasingly demanding, DLSS has never been more important, and DLSS 4.5 is one of the biggest leaps forward for upscaling tech yet. It delivers such high image quality and clarity that you can barely tell the difference between Quality and Performance modes, helping supported games like Doom: The Dark Ages and Arc Raiders look better and run better than ever before.
Best Console Accessory
Corsair Novablade Pro
A pleasant surprise in the past year or so's gaming hardware releases, the Novablade Pro leverless fightstick is a fantastic game controller that oozes quality and prioritizes customization to make life easier and better for fighting game players.
Best Gaming Service
Amazon Luna
With hardware prices spiraling out of control, cloud gaming has never been a more attractive proposition — and Amazon continues to offer one of the best services in the space. This year saw Amazon Luna games integrated directly into the Prime Video app on Fire TV devices, making it easier than ever to access great games wherever you are.
Best Gaming Controller
8BitDo Pro 3
The 8BitDo Pro 3 looks like a small upgrade compared to the Pro 2, but in real-world use, the improvements are simply astronomical. 8BitDo has crammed drift-eliminating TMR thumbsticks, magnetic hot-swappable face buttons, trigger locks, and an extra pair of optional remappable buttons into a versatile, budget-friendly package that is miles ahead of the competition.
Best Gaming Headset
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite
The best gaming headset we've ever tested. The Nova Elite raises the bar for premium, do-it-all, high-end gaming headsets, and this ticks every box from feature set to battery life, and from connectivity to audio quality, design, and build.
Best Gaming Chair
Secretlab Atlas
Secretlab's latest chair is a hit. This practical task chair offers the brand's supreme materials and build quality in a less gaming-oriented format, making it perfect for your work-from-home setup. It's attractive, comfortable, and feature-packed — what more could you ask from your seat?
TV & home theater
TV of the Year
LG C6
In terms of all-around performance, features and versatility balanced with price, the C6 is the best TV around. When we tested it next to its predecessor, the LG C5, it was a noticeable upgrade: one that's rare to come across, and that was helped by LG adding its highest-end image processing. If you want a TV that can do it all, the C6 is that TV. Few TVs have impressed me as much this year as the C6, and that's why it takes the top spot.
Read our full LG C6 review
Home Entertainment Brand of the Year
Sony
Sony released two RGB LED TVs this year after years of teasing, and both of them were best-in-class, and are the TVs that most have me believing that OLED really should watch its back based on where this technology could do. Outside of this, the brand has also produced some excellent soundbars and speakers across the board, including the ground-breaking Bravia Theater Trio wireless LCR system, which is something we've been hoping to see a company make for years.
Home Entertainment Innovation of the Year
Sony True RGB
RGB TVs have been the big buzz of the TV world in 2026, and while it's been a mostly mixed bag, Sony's version called 'True RGB' stands above the rest. While it delivers spellbinding colors and superb brightness, it's the OLED-level black tones that impressed me most. I've tested Sony's two True RGB TVs and it's the best that dark and high-contrast scenes have ever looked on a backlit TV. In terms of innovation, it doesn't get more impressive than this in 2026.
Best Gaming TV
LG C6
For gaming, there's no better option in 2026 than the LG C6. Not only does it have a full list of features — 4K at up to 165Hz, full variable refresh rate support, and Dolby Vision Gaming — and fantastic performance, but it's also available in 42-83-inch sizes to suit all gaming spaces. When I played games on the C6, I had a fantastic time thanks to its buttery-smooth response times and excellent picture quality. There are other great gaming TVs around, but none delivers such a good all-round experience for the same price.
Read our full LG C6 review
Best TV for Sound
Sony Bravia 9 II
While TV sound is often a mixed bag, no other TV delivers better built-in audio in 2026 than the Sony Bravia 9 II. It delivers impeccable detail and clarity with a wide soundstage and pinpoint accuracy. Watching our reference scenes just impressed us across the board — very few other TVs have ever delivered such a level of audio authenticity.
Read our full Sony Bravia 9 II review
Best OLED TV
LG C6
Our TV of the Year is also the best OLED TV of 2026. More premium models may deliver better picture or more features, but none deliver a more complete package that's a significant step above their predecessor for a seriously competitive price. The C6 is a jack-of-all-trades TV that ticks every box a user could need across a wide range of sizes, and no other OLED has impressed me as much as the LG C6 when compared to last year's models.
Read our full LG C6 review
Best Mini-LED TV
Sony Bravia 9 II
RGB mini-LED is the next step in the evolution of mini-LED and no other TV this year does it better than the Sony Bravia 9 II. It delivers fantastic backlight control, OLED-rivaling black tones, vibrant, rich colors and realistic detail. No backlit TV has ever wowed our reviewers more than the Bravia 9 II, and it's an exciting sign for the future of mini-LED.
Read our full Sony Bravia 9 II review
Best Value TV
TCL QM7L/C7L
It really doesn't get better in terms of bang-for-your-buck value than the TCL QM7L (US model) and TCL C7L (UK and Australian version). The new SQD panel delivers great brightness and color, as well as excellent backlight control. Its great for gaming for a near-full suite of features, and it has credible built-in sound. The real highlight however is its price-to-size ratio, where you can get a big screen at a ridiculously affordable price, given how good the picture looks. If you want the best value, the QM7L/C7L is our top pick.
Read our full TCL QM7L review
Best Projector
Hisense XR10
This projector simply creates the most impressive pictures you can expect from a living-room-friendly projector — anything beyond this requires going pro. It's bright enough to work for lit rooms as well as dark-room viewing, and looks fantastic in both cases — and it even has a slick decor-friendly design. Sure, it lacks 120Hz at 4K, but cinephiles won't care — and this is made for cinephiles, make no mistake. Our full review will land shortly.
Best Soundbar
Sonos Beam Ultra
This wasn't the only soundbar this year to earn a rare five-star rating, but it's the one with the most 'wow' factor, because it's hard to believe such an expansive sound is coming from such a small design. The Dolby Atmos effect reaches a scale you'd never expect for a compact bar, and does it with clarity and precision of spatial audio. This feels like a premium bar, but with a mid-range price, and that's why it earns this award.
Read our full Sonos Beam Ultra review
Best Wireless Home Theater Speakers
Sony Bravia Theater Trio
This is product option we've wanted for so long: a wireless LCR system (meaning left, center, right channels) that's as easy to set up as a soundbar, but with the better width and impact that you get from a separates system. And that's what you get here: tons of power, a super-immersive Dolby Atmos experience, and a sense of scale to match a projector screen or giant-screen TV in a way a soundbar can't match. It's the wireless living home theater dream come true, especially with its easy expansion to add rears and subs. Our full review is coming soon.
Streaming
Streaming Service of the Year
HBO Max
Three years on after winning our coveted Best Streaming Service of the Year crown, HBO Max has done it again — and with good reason. Its long-overdue launch in multiple European nations, including the UK and Ireland, and the introduction of new user-friendly features are two such reasons why it was an early contender for this year’s prize. Throw in its unrivaled catalog of unmissable new shows and returning TV favorites, ongoing movie-exclusive partnership with acclaimed indie studio A24, and ever-expanding live sports coverage, though, and no other platform came close to besting it.
Best for Movies
Prime Video
Movie lovers should flock to Prime Video, as it boasts a library of over 20,000 movies in the US. The streaming service regularly adds new movies from Hollywood blockbusters, independent films, and classic cinema across the years, as well as its own Prime Video Original movies. Recent additions include the romantic comedy Love of Your Life and survival horror The Devil's Mouth.
Best for Documentaries
Netflix
Considering Netflix has everything from true crime to celebrity-fronted food documentaries, it's the place to be if you love all things real life. There's plenty of shocking stories of scandals, murders, mysteries and more, as well as lighter options for those in need of some escapism. Whatever you're after, Netflix probably has it. Recent must-see documentaries include a nail-biting series called Worst Neighbor Ever and the shocking Titan: The OceanGate Disaster.
Best for TV Shows
Apple TV was the most awarded streaming service at the 2026 Emmys, with many of its original series being hailed as the best. We’re inclined to agree, considering the quality of Apple TV shows has been consistently excellent across the board. Whether you want a mind boggling thriller like Severance or a horror comedy like Widow’s Bay, there’s plenty on offer for all tastes.
Best Free Streaming Service
Tubi or not Tubi? That’s the question we ask ourselves who should win our annual Best Free Streaming Service of the Year award. Well, this year, it is Tubi. Supported on over 30 devices — the most of any ad-supporting video on demand (AVOD) service — it’s available to every kind of person working to every kind of budget. Add in its movie and TV show catalogs, which number hundreds of thousands of offerings covering numerous genres, as well as its ongoing featuring of myriad live television channels and networks, and it’s the 2026 people’s AVOD champion.
Audio
Headphones of the Year
Apple AirPods Max 2
As we said in our full review, these cans are "doubtless the best noise-cancelling iPhone headphones on the planet" — and we weren't expecting to love them as much as we did. Aside from the USB-C lossless audio and incredible comfort, they also boast some of the best voice capture on any headphones we've ever experienced. This was a really hot year for headphones, the AirPods Max 2 still lag behind the competition for battery life (and the weird bra case continues to mystify) — but that they won out should tell you just how good they are in every other way.
Read our full AirPods Max 2 review
Audio Brand of the Year
iFi
Hi-res specialist iFi isn't afraid of conquering the whole hi-fi market, serving up launches such as the excellent five-star elite iFi iDSD GR2 and the cheap and cheerful Go Cable this year. We love seeing this hard-working visionary outfit in full flow. Whatever level you're at, it's got something for you — and it's hard to look past a brand that hires out London's Tower Bridge, gets its entire team into black tuxedoes, plasters the walls with the word 'Phantom' so it feels as if 007 himself could drop in at any minute and then unveils the most stunning-sounding flagship DAC we've ever heard. Bravo, iFi. For you, the world is not enough…
Audio Innovation of the Year
Cambridge L/R S speakers
Before I heard these speakers, I thought Cambridge had taken a big risk here. Then, I gave them a thorough listen and I knew they were winners. The L/R S is a genuinely active stereo speaker system, so it does not involve a powered primary speaker and a dumb counterpart to make a pair. OK, only the primary speaker receives power, but there are two channels of amplification for each speaker. Then, there's a full DSP crossover which acts as a PWM signal to each amp — and that's before the bespoke four-conductor cable to connect the primary speaker to the secondary! Might we call them over-engineered? Maybe — or you could simply call Cambridge's work ethic ‘admirable’, as I do.
Read our full Cambridge L/R S review
Best Wireless Headphones
Nothing Headphone (a)
There's something so untethered about Nothing's approach to audio architecture and design that it makes these cans downright joyous in their appeal — we actually have the pair with yellow accents (you can call them over-easy eggs if you like, that actually makes me dig them even more). The company upgraded and finessed the audio compared to the original Headphone (1), while keeping the excellent on-ear controls (the roller for volume is a true highlight) stellar battery life, very good ANC and truly useful app — then somehow shaved a load off the price. A deserved winner.
Read our full Nothing Headphone (a) review
Best Wireless Earbuds
Soundpeats H3
These delightfully different, affordable and sonically superb buds from Soundpeats sound better than some buds at twice their price (and at around $129 / £129, they're really quite humbly priced), thanks to their triple-driver array per bud, a secure fit, plus aptX, aptX Adaptive, aptX Lossless and LDAC support. Audiophile on a budget? Add this name to your list.
Read our full Soundpeats H3 review
Best Open Earbuds
Shokz OpenFit Pro
Our Audio Editor uses these superb, if pricey, open earbuds multiple times per week, and it's hard to look past the personal recommendation. The fit is sports-worthy (aided by extra optional bands in the box, useful for sports that require a different fit, such as tennis) but they're also office-friendly and professional in terms of design — and the excellent active noise reduction is as unusual as it is class-leading. As far as I'm concerned, Shokz served an ace here.
Read our full Shokz Openfit Pro review
Best Value Headphones
CMF Headphone Pro
We knew we loved these minty fresh cans as soon as we slipped them over our ears. Would you expect hearing tests for a personalized sound profile, LDAC support, an excellent volume 'roller' control on the right ear cup, glorious build quality, zealous wireless sound, exemplary battery life and 3.5mm hi-res wired listening for under $100 / £100? The design flair, energetic audio quality and additional perks won this race.
Read our full CMF Headphone Pro review
Best Value Earbuds
JLab JBuds Mini ANC
Look at them! The JLab JBuds Mini ANC's one perceived failing stems from their biggest selling point: because they're tiny enough to fit on a keyring (they are the smallest ANC earbuds on the planet), you might think they're little more than junk. I'm here to tell you emphatically that they are not — in fact, they're so far from junk that you can't lose them. They're the first earbuds to have support for Apple's Find My network. I don't think any rival came particularly close to the value you get here for $39 / £39 — our full review is coming soon.
Best Value Open Earbuds
Baseus Bowie MC2
We think a Labyrinth-era Bowie (that's 1986, to save you the bother of checking) in full Goblin King Jareth regalia would've put these dark, cuff-style open earbuds on without a second thought — and he'd have looked fantastic in them. These cheap clip-style buds often had us wondering whether you even need to spend more on a flagship set from class-leaders such as Shokz or Bose. If all you need is good sound with surprisingly regimented, impactful bass (and you're prepared to forego expensive extras) these Baseus buds are a winner.
Read our full Baseus Bowie MC2 review
Best Wired Headphones
Meze Audio Strada
We're going for a set of stunning racing green closed-back headphones that sound as airy and spacious as open-back headphones, except nobody hears your playlist. As a closed-back option, they're also relatively easy to drive and they're capable of supremely detailed, organized and thoroughly addictive audio.
Read our full Meze Audio Strada review
Best Wired Earbuds
Sennheiser CX 80U
I said it before (because these were your choice too, dearest reader) and I'll say it again: when people ask me, "What's the cheapest way to get better sound from my phone?" my first response is to suggest these delightfully inexpensive 2026-release USB-C wired earbuds. For around $35 / £30 you really cannot do better. You don't get volume controls on the in-line remote and the mic doesn't deliver crystal-clear calls, as our Sennheiser CX 80U review explains. What you do get is acutely nimble but impactful bass, clear mids and sparkling, appealing highs. Pair that with their surprisingly effective passive noise isolation and you’re looking at an incredibly good pair of wired buds for the money.
Best Bluetooth Speaker
JBL Xtreme 5
Do you want a Bluetooth speaker you'll be able to slip into a purse and take to the park for a podcast, or do you want a party-ready beast with a shoulder strap all of its own? Because JBL's Xtreme 5 is in the latter camp, but if that's what you want, you'll be delighted with it. This is one of the best bigger Bluetooth belters we've ever tested — as our five-star JBL Xtreme 5 review will impress upon you at great length. OK, enough talk: let's dance!
Best Wireless Speaker
Denon Home 400
I got a chance to hear this speaker among its siblings (the Home 200 and 600) at launch, and it is my favorite of Denon's 2026 wireless home trio. It is also the best-looking new wireless speaker on the market, for me (it's about the size of a chopping-board rack or bread bin, fitting neatly on shelves and bookcases while serving up delicious sound). Another great feature is that during setup, you are encouraged to list where the speaker is placed — far from a wall, close to one wall or in a corner — within the HEOS companion app. You can then opt for a 'pure' stereo hi-fi mix, or add 'width' to boost the horizontal spaciousness of the sound field. The spatial and directional stuff is a lot of fun to play with and, as our full Denon Home 400 review explains, provided you don't rely on a voice assistant to do your bidding at home (I do not) it's a hugely talented wireless speaker.
Best Portable Audio Player
Astell & Kern PD5
I absolutely get why the TR readership chose Astell & Kern's newest 'entry level' hi-res audio player, called the A&K PD5 (I put 'entry level' in quotation marks because A&K's definition and ours may well differ). And while I've been lucky enough to listen to the May 2026-release flagship Astell & Kern SP4000T, very briefly — and I have to tell you, it's excellent — it is a huge chunk of cash. This option is far more palatable from a purely financial perspective and is still a fantastically gifted DAP. We gave the PD5's wonky, quirky SR35 older sibling a glowing five-star review, and now this glorious successor is here in a more conventional form factor. Our full review is almost here, but here's a spoiler alert: it's good news. I predicted this category would be won by Activo's parent company, and so it has come to pass — the hi-res DAP specialist is truly bossing the quality portable music machine market.
Best Turntable
Fluance RT87
This is a player for the purist, and so it is pretty light on convenience-focused features — there's no built-in phono preamp, for example — but we don’t think that is a bad thing. The Fluance RT87 is designed for someone who is ready to enter a more serious vinyl listening state and is prepared for manual tone arm adjustment and tweaking to make the turntable as flat as possible using the provided bubble level. This means you won't damage your particularly irreplaceable presses when you spin them — that's the kind of person this turntable is aimed at, and it nails that brief.
See our full Fluance RT87 review
Best DAC
iFi iDSD GR2
When we chose iFi as our Audio Brand of the Year, one of the key deciding factors was this phenomenal digital-analog-converter. It's all stunning design, punchy power, exceptional performance, and a brilliant OLED touchscreen for extra features. I love iFi's dedication to K2HD restorative mastering tech, and its fan-fave XBass and XSpace filters. This DAC even has a lower asking price than its xDSD Gryphon predecessor at launch. It would be churlish to ask for much more than that in 2026.
Read our full iFi iDSD GR2 review
Best Stereo Speakers
Dali Sonik 1
While these may be small and budget-friendly, sonically they’re huge and luxurious. Think clear-headed, stunning vocals with more room to breathe than should be possible at this level, plus tangible transients through to a deep, thrumming low-end. They are far from the first of this type of speaker, and they certainly won’t be the last — but they’re emphatically among the best currently on the market, especially at such a wallet-friendly price.
Read our full Dali Sonik 1 review
Health & Fitness tech
Health & Fitness Device of the year
Garmin Fenix 9 Pro
Expensive the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro may be, but the ultimate adventure smartwatch is one of the best devices Garmin has ever produced, building on years of technical advancements. It's a money-no-object powerhouse with amazing build quality: the all-titanium case houses a powerful battery, behind the super-tough sapphire crystal lies a vibrant AMOLED screen, and during my test runs against a heart rate monitor it's consistently accurate. I've been wearing the 43mm version non-stop since getting my testing unit — a clear indicator that it's first in line for valuable wrist real estate this year.
Read our full Garmin Fenix 9 Pro review
Health & Fitness Brand of the Year
Garmin
Garmin has had a strong 2026. It's revamped its cycling range, brought out a few new features such as AI-powered nutrition tracking to justify the cost of its Garmin Connect+ service, and has developed a few extremely well-reviewed gadgets — notably, the screenless Garmin Cirqa fitness tracker and the top-flight Garmin Fenix 9 series, both of which feature in this list to no-one's surprise. It remains the brand to beat in the endurance world, but the Cirqa shows that it's making inroads with the gym crowd too.
Health & Fitness Innovation of the Year
Huawei Watch D3
This watch advances the smartwatch-as-medical-device category further into refinement, boasting more than its signature medical-grade blood pressure cuff technology. With emergency fall detection, blood pressure trends, sleep tracking and six days of battery life compared to the Apple Watch's 24 hours, it's the watch I recommend to people looking for a health-orientated smartwatch for seniors. It's all packed into a sleek Apple-inspired design.
Read our full Huawei Watch D3 review
Best Smartwatch
Apple Watch Ultra 4
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 retains its crown for another year as this year's top smartwatch. Like every other Apple Watch Ultra model before it, this is an iterative update to an already-excellent watch, rather than a top-down redesign, but did we expect anything else from Apple? If it ain't broke, don't fix it. What has changed is the back of the watch: a redesigned LED Health Sensing System ensures better-than-ever accuracy and more frequent heart rate readings, enabling improved sleep tracking (along with a boost in battery life, as you're less likely to take it off to charge it) and the new Readiness Score.
Read our full Apple Watch Ultra 4 review
Best Running Watch
Garmin Fenix 9 Pro
The Garmin Fenix 9 Pro is back. The redesigned Maps feature places you right into the middle of things, mimicking your perspective to reduce the glance-to-interpretation delay when you're trying to find your way on long runs, which even the Apple Watch doesn't do. It's a triathlon athlete or ultra marathon's dream watch thanks to its trail features, while its battery life is more impressive than the Ultra 4. Recommended workouts based on your Training Readiness score and Garmin Coach training plans are the icing on the cake.
Read our full Garmin Fenix 9 Pro review
Best Fitness Tracker
Garmin Cirqa
The Garmin Cirqa narrowly beats up the Fitbit Air: even though it's more expensive up-front, the lack of reliance on a subscription service and its tactile button (just click it to start tracking, no messing around with the app) means it's the screenless fitness tracker of choice this year, and the best new fitness tracker overall.
Read our full Garmin Cirqa review
Best Smart Ring
Oura Ring 5
The competition was super-hot this year, but Oura came back swinging with the Oura Ring 5. It's thinner than ever, which is so important in a smart ring, earning top marks for design in our review. Its slickly-orientated app and smorgasbord of metrics justify the ongoing, mandatory subscription, making this a great premium smart ring option.
Read our full Oura Ring 5 review
Best Electric Toothbrush
Suri Core 1.0
The Suri Core 1.0 takes the original Suri brush's elegant, simplified aesthetics and environmental credentials, and manages to cut a few corners to shave some money off the price. A bio-plastic handle rather than aluminium, and a slightly less powerful motor and battery, helps keep the Core affordable. You can still recycle the brush heads for free, and the unit still looks nice and stylish, especially with its slick magnetic mount. Its battery life will last over a month between charges.
Read our full Suri Core 1.0 review
Best Connected Fitness Tech
Withings BodyScan 2
Withings is a brand that's quietly been making excellent health products for years, from discreet hybrid smartwatches to under-mattress sleep analyzers and, well, smart scales. The Withings BodyScan 2, with its handle creating a circular current and offering a comprehensive list of 40 different metrics, is not just its best yet, but our best smart scale at the premium tier. It tracks blood oxygen levels, hypertension risk and estimates your vascular age. And you thought scales were just for BMI!
Read our full Withings BodyScan 2 review
Home tech
Home Device of the Year
DJI Romo P
The Romo P is DJI's first robot vacuum, but you wouldn't know from its performance. It offers the best obstacle avoidance of any robovac we've tested, as well as superb wet cleaning on hard floors, and very good vacuuming on carpet. It gets our seal of approval as this year's best robot vacuum, if your wallet can take the hit.
Read our full DJI Romo P review
Home Tech Brand of the Year
Philips Hue
Philips Hue is the biggest name in smart lighting for a reason, and this year it's become more accessible than ever with the launch of Hue Essential — a range of budget-friendly bulbs and LED strips that are an affordable entry to the smart lighting ecosystem. Meanwhile, power users can enjoy AI-powered lighting tools thanks to the new Hue Bridge Pro, which supports over 150 lights in a single network.
Home Tech Innovation of the Year
Dyson Find+Follow Purifier Cool
The smartest fan we’ve tested this year, the Dyson Find+Follow uses AI to track you as you move around the room, ensuring you’re kept cool and comfortable at all times. It blew us away with its 350 degrees of oscillation, super quiet operation, and smooth air flow — and its voice and app controls make operating it a breeze.
Read our full Dyson Find+Follow Purifier Cool review
Best Home Light Tech
Philips Hue Omniglow Strip Light
The Omniglow uses tiny micro LEDs to produce a seamless gradient unlike any LED lightstrip we’ve seen before — and it looks amazing. Not only are the individual LEDs invisible, it’s also incredibly bright, and looks particularly stunning when flowing from one color to the next in a Dynamic Scene. One of the most exciting smart lights I’ve seen in recent years.
Read our Philips Hue Omniglow review
Best Home Security Device
Aqara Camera Hub G350
It might look like a children’s toy, but the Aqara Camera Hub G350 is a serious home security camera, and one you can trust to guard a whole room thanks to its 360-degree panning. Despite its cute looks, the G350 is packing a 4K wide-angle camera, plus a 2.5k telephoto lens for getting up close. It’s compatible with all the main smart home ecosystems, and you can store footage on an SD card so there’s no subscription necessary. And, for some reason, it has detachable bunny ears. What more could you want?
Read our full Aqara Camera Hub G350 review
Best Robot Vacuum
DJI Romo P
DJI's first robot vacuum is a triumph — the company has put its expertise in obstacle-detection to good use, and the DJI Romo P is the best robovac we've ever tested when it comes to avoiding common hazards. Its cleaning is top-notch as well, with its mopping function proving particularly effective at removing tough spills from hard flooring.
Read our full DJI Romo P review
Best Vacuum
Roborock F25 Ultra
The F25 Ultra packs a lot more cleaning power than your typical wet/dry vacuum, with steam-cleaning, hot-water degreasing, and powerful suction to tackle huge amounts of dirt and water. Its power-assisted wheels make it feel surprisingly nimble too. Perfect for households with pets, children, or both — your floors won't know what hit them.
Read our full Roborock F25 Ultra review
Best Air Fryer
Ninja French Door Premier Air Fryer Convection Oven Toaster
This is much more than just an air fryer — it’s a full countertop oven, with an extra-large cooking area that can accommodate an entire pizza or chicken. It cooks astonishingly fast, with 10 dedicated modes, and produced perfect fries, vegetables, quesadillas, and even bagels during our tests. It looks great as well, and you can open the French doors one-handed for easy access.
Read our full Ninja French Door Premier Air Fryer Convection Oven Toaster review
Best Coffee Machine
Meraki Espresso Machine Gen 2
The classiest coffee maker we've tested in the last 12 months, and the one I'd be proudest to have in my own kitchen, the Meraki Gen 2 is a pleasure to use, automating certain parts of the brewing process without taking over, and helping you hone your own barista skills. The results? Sensational coffee, provided your wallet can stand the hit.
Read our full Meraki Espresso Machine Gen 2 review
Best Value Coffee Machine
Philips Baristina
If you're looking for an affordable coffee maker, you can't go wrong with the Philips Baristina — an innovative little appliance that combines the best features of manual and automatic espresso machines. It handles the whole brewing process for you, but without the awkward maintenance of your typical bean-to-cup machine. Look for the version bundled with a milk frother and you'll never bother buying takeout coffee again.
Read our full Philips Baristina review
Best Fan
Dyson Find+Follow Purifier Cool
Dyson's smartest fan to date, the Find+Follow tracks your movement as you walk around the room, and makes sure its airflow is always angled in your direction. The airflow is smooth and quiet, which makes the Find+Follow an ideal choice for night time as well, and the filtration system effectively removes dirt and allergens while it's keeping you comfortable.
Read our full Dyson Find+Follow Purifier Cool review
