articles.title: Lazarus Abuses South Korean Security Software to Deploy Malware Using Post-Quantum Encryption
articles.text:
The North Korea-linked Lazarus Group has been attributed to a cyber espionage campaign dubbed Operation FlashHole targeting at least three organizations in South Korea spanning the construction, software, and wire-communication equipment manufacturing sectors.
According to Russian cybersecurity company Kaspersky, the campaign has been active since at least July 2025. It's assessed to pick up from where Operation SyncHole left off.
"The group targeted victims more selectively, sending spear‑phishing emails with links to fabricated but relevant sites, such as portfolio and résumé pages tailored to each target," Sojun Ryu, senior security researcher at Kaspersky GReAT, said in an exhaustive analysis.
Operation SyncHole was first documented by Kaspersky in April 2025, detailing the state-sponsored adversary's targeting of South Korea's software, IT, financial, semiconductor manufacturing, and telecommunications industries since November 2024 to deliver malware such as ThreatNeedle, AGAMEMNON, wAgent, SIGNBT, and COPPERHEDGE.
The attacks were characterized by the exploitation of a security flaw in iniLINE Cross EX for malware delivery. Cross EX is a mandatory financial security software program installed by South Korean internet users on their computers to support security software across various browser environments when accessing online banking and government services.
The exploit was designed to launch the legitimate "SyncHost.exe" process and inject shellcode into it to load the ThreatNeedle backdoor. The attack chain also incorporated a one-day vulnerability in the Innorix Agent file transfer solution version 9.2.18.496 for lateral movement.
Operation FlashHole continues the prior wave's targeting of South Korea-focused software to breach targets. Where SyncHole exploited Cross EX, FlashHole has been found to abuse Initech's INISAFE CrossWeb EX, another mandatory financial security solution necessary to access online banking and government portals in the country.
According to iniLINE's website, the company entered into a strategic alliance with Initech as far back as 2010 to develop CrossWeb. It's currently marketed by Initech as a certificate-based authentication and electronic-signature solution.
That said, the Lazarus Group has a long history of abusing this software to meet its goals. In Q3 2021, it was used to deploy a downloader named Racket in connection with a long-running campaign called DeathNote.
| Operation FlashHole attack flow during initial compromise | 
Between 2022 and 2023, AhnLab also disclosed attacks in which the threat actor exploited a security flaw in the software to distribute DLL malware ("SCSKAppLink.dll") via watering hole attacks, with the DLL payload retrieved from IIS web servers compromised by the threat actor.
"The group first hacks Korean websites and modifies the content provided from the site," AhnLab noted in a July 2023 report. "When a system using a vulnerable version of INISAFE CrossWeb EX V6 visits this website via a web browser, the Lazarus malware (SCSKAppLink.dll) is installed from the distribution site through the INISAFECrossWebEXSvc.exe vulnerability."
| Initial infection chain | 
The findings also come against the backdrop of a joint July 2026 advisory published by the Korea Internet and Security Agency (KISA) and domestic cybersecurity vendors, highlighting the Lazarus Group's exploitation of vulnerabilities in such financial security programs like AnySign4PC to distribute backdoors like Struggle (aka SIGNBT 3.0) and Brandoor (aka COPPERHEDGE) after tricking victims into visiting malicious URLs through spear-phishing and watering hole techniques.
"The attackers induced targets to access malicious URLs through various methods, including watering hole and spear-phishing attacks, and then exploited the vulnerabilities to ultimately install backdoor malware," AhnLab said, calling the campaign Operation Double Barrel.
The precise initial access vector for FlashHole is unclear, but signs point to malicious websites hosted on GitHub pages, one version of which hosted the résumé of a senior network appliance developer along with a profile photo likely generated using artificial intelligence (AI).
| Expanded infection chain after gaining persistence | 
It's suspected that targets are sent spear-phishing emails containing links to the malicious site, visiting which triggers an infection sequence involving CrossWeb EX to launch the legitimate Windows binary "fsquirt.exe," which is then used to launch a malicious DLL called TechHub via DLL sideloading.
"The infection chain is rather complex and reveals the Lazarus Group's advanced operational techniques on targeted hosts," Kaspersky said. "These techniques conceal their malicious payloads, intent, and their sophisticated malware delivery framework."
"Significantly, the execution chain below exists only in memory during the initial infiltration, highlighting the attackers' considerable efforts to hide the initial compromise."
TechHub, for its part, downloads from GitHub a malware called TouchHub, which leverages a DLL sideloading a second to launch a rogue DLL payload dubbed TOUCHSHIFT ("mscoree.dll") for setting up persistence by kicking off the in‑memory execution of another TechHub instance.
| Overlaps between Lazarus Group Attacks | 
This second TechHub instance retrieves another malware family known as ClientHub to download and load LPEClient into memory. LPEClient serves as a conduit for Cubridge, the orchestration component of the malware framework designed to fetch various plugins, modules, and tools.
Additional details about the malware toolset is as follows -
- TechHub, an advanced version of the CLOUDBURST and NickelLoader downloader that communicates with GitHub to fetch additional payloads like TouchHub and ClientHub, as well as collect information about the device and its running processes.
- Cubridge, an improved version of SIDESHOW and LightlessCan capable of communicating with a command-and-control (C2) server and downloading reusable plugins, DLL utilities for one-off tasks, and additional modules to expand its functionality, thereby allowing it to gather comprehensive system information, run commands, and steal files and web browser data. It's also assessed to be an advanced version of CookiePlus.
- TouchHub, a parent installer for TouchShift.
- TouchShift, a malware dropper capable of delivering keyloggers, screenshot utilities, and backdoors.
- ClientHub, a previously undocumented backdoor that comes in two versions: one that communicates with an attacker controlled server, using HTTPS and another that interacts with the Dropbox API. The end goal of the malware is to deploy additional plugins and DLLs. The plugins allow the malware to create ZIP archives, collect files matching a search pattern, delete specific files, and monitor local drive changes and return the collected status information.
- LPEClient, a longstanding victim profiling and payload delivery tool used since 2019.
In August 2026, Check Point revealed that LPEClient was deployed following the zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-68820, a privilege escalation flaw affecting Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock, to deploy the FudModule rootkit.
What's notable about the latest version of the malware is that it uses ML-KEM-1024, a post-quantum cryptographic algorithm, to establish an encrypted connection with the attackers' server before downloading and running additional malware directly in memory.
"Operation FlashHole is the latest wave in the broader Cascade Hole campaign, which involves the use of South Korean software as a potential entry point to deliver malware targeting the country," Kaspersky said.
The cybersecurity company said the emergence of Operation FlashHole coincided with a fresh wave of attacks targeting various South Korean organizations using the COPPERHEDGE backdoor. In at least one case, the backdoor infection is said to have resulted in the exfiltration of data to a dark web leak site named ULOSE, in a manner similar to Gunra ransomware attacks directed against South Korean entities around the same time.
"Lazarus continues to expand its operations, launches new campaigns while introducing new tools and reworking familiar ones to meet its needs," Ryu said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.
"What deserves closer attention is Lazarus’s adoption of cryptography designed to withstand future quantum threats. Our findings trace its use back to at least September 2024, showing that these capabilities were already protecting the group’s malware communications more than a year before this disclosure."

articles.title: Apple étend Siri AI à 5 nouvelles langues, mais les utilisateurs européens restent exclus
articles.text:
Siri AI débarque en français, mais toujours pas en France sur iPhone, iPad et Apple Watch. Cependant, les restrictions d'usage se feront nombreuses avec le plan d'utilisation gratuit.
Apple a annoncé l'ajout du français, du japonais, du coréen, du portugais et de l'espagnol à Siri AI avec la mise à jour vers la version 27.2. Cette nouvelle version, si intéressante soit-elle, n'est toutefois pas encore disponible en France ni dans certains pays d'Europe.
Siri boosté à l'intelligence artificielle
Cette version repensée de l'assistant vocal mise sur l'intégration d'Apple Intelligence pour apporter plus de contexte à l'utilisateur. L'objectif est de permettre à Siri de retrouver des informations dans les messages, les mails, les photos et d'autres contenus, lorsque l'utilisateur en a besoin.
Parmi les fonctionnalités proposées figurent la rédaction de mails depuis une simple instruction, ainsi que des outils d'édition et de partage de photos. Siri AI intègre également une fonction de reconnaissance de l'écran, lui permettant de répondre à des questions ou d'exécuter des actions en lien avec le contenu affiché. L'assistant dispose en plus d'une base de connaissances générales et peut fournir des informations actualisées sur de nombreux sujets.
Toujours pas disponible dans l'UE
Apple précise, dans les mentions légales accompagnant l'annonce, que Siri AI demeure en version bêta pour l'ensemble des systèmes d'exploitation intégrant la mise à jour 27.2. Son utilisation nécessite par ailleurs un matériel compatible avec Apple Intelligence.
La fonctionnalité reste indisponible dans l'Union européenne sur iOS, iPadOS et watchOS. La marque à la pomme indique travailler à trouver une solution permettant son déploiement chez nous. Siri AI n'est pas non plus accessible aux utilisateurs de moins de 13 ans.
- Intégration transparente dans l'écosystème Apple
- Respect de la confidentialité des données
- Outils d'écriture puissants
Pour profiter de Siri AI, il faudra impérativement un appareil sous iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2 ou watchOS 27.2 compatible avec Apple Intelligence.
Un déploiement progressif et quelques limites
Cette mise à jour s'ajoute à la prise en charge existante de l'anglais. Apple prévoit de poursuivre cette extension linguistique d'ici la fin de l'année avec l'intégration du chinois traditionnel, du norvégien, du turc et du vietnamien.
L'entreprise californienne rappelle également que certaines fonctionnalités d'Apple Intelligence reposent sur des modèles hébergés sur ses serveurs et sont, à ce titre, soumises à des limites d'utilisation quotidiennes. Cela concerne notamment Siri AI, les outils d'édition de photos basés sur l'intelligence artificielle, Image Playground, ainsi que les modèles AFM 3 Cloud utilisés dans l'application Raccourcis. Apple devrait par ailleurs proposer des abonnements payants à l'avenir, pour élargir l'accès à ces fonctionnalités actuellement plafonnées.
Source : NeoWin

articles.title: Microsoft and others scramble to patch 'HTTP2Shell' flaw which could be the next PHP-level issue — Node.js problem may also affect millions of sites
articles.text:
Microsoft and others scramble to patch 'HTTP2Shell' flaw which could be the next PHP-level issue — Node.js problem may also affect millions of sites
An RCE flaw was found in Brotli
- A critical Brotli compression flaw, dubbed HTTP2Shell, could enable memory corruption and remote code execution
- The vulnerability affects widely used software including Node.js, Python packages, and .NET applications
- Vendors released patches, and administrators are urged to update immediately despite no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation
Multiple tech companies and projects have recently pushed patches for a vulnerability called “HTTP2Shell” which could enable remote code execution (RCE) attacks, similar to the recent “PHP2Shell” vulnerabilities.
HTTP2Shell was found in Brotli, a Google-built open source data compression algorithm that reduces file sizes without losing information, thus achieving faster transmission times while using less bandwidth.
It is a popular algorithm used on the web to compress HTTP responses such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and is supported by most web browsers, servers, and software libraries.
Fixes and patches
The bug itself is described as an out-of-bounds write flaw, and is also dubbed Node2Shell, and Broccoli2Shell. It is tracked as CVE-2026-111497, and was given a severity score of 9.2/10 (critical). According to the National Vulnerability Database, the bug causes a buffer overflow which could lead to memory disclosure, denial of service and, in some cases, even remote code execution.
Brotli can be found in all sorts of software, all of which is now at risk. That includes Node.js, brotlicffi, HTTP clients such as Requests, urllib3, httpx and aiohttp, but also other apps that use Brotli decoders such as Bun and Envoy deployments.
Google fixed the bug on October 21 2026, by releasing Brotli versions 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1. However, there are other software that either bundle or use vulnerable Brotli versions, so updating Google’s library alone may not protect every application.
Over the last weekend, Microsoft released an emergency update to sort the bug in .NET, saying successful exploitation could lead to privilege escalation.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Since it also bundles the Brodli decoder, Node.js released its patch on October 21, too. “An invalid block switch was reported as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer,” the organization explained. “An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory, or remote code execution.”
The vulnerability was said to be affecting Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
BleepingComputer reports that PyPI packages containing the fixes became available two days later, on October 23.
Here is a detailed list of patched versions:
Google Brotli 1.0.10, 1.1.1, 1.2.1
Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1
Python Brotli 1.2.1
Python brotlicffi 1.2.1.0
Dedicated website
At the same time, someone set up a dedicated website, Broccoli2Shell.com, which describes the issue, tracks vulnerable versions, and reports on attempted exploits in the wild. On the site, it is said that proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for the bug already exist, but reports of malicious exploitation in the wild are yet to be seen.
“A public proof of concept appeared on GitHub on 2026-10-22,” the site reads. “It reportedly reaches code execution only on a deliberately weakened build. On standard builds it causes a crash and a limited memory read.”
System administrators are advised to apply the provided patches as soon as possible; restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Those that cannot do that immediately can somewhat mitigate the risks. Python users should uninstall the vulnerable Brotli and brotlicffi packages and remove optional dependencies such as httpx[brotli].
Admins can also configure proxies, load balancers or web application firewalls (WAF) to reject incoming requests containing Brotli-compressed bodies. It’s worth mentioning that this doesn’t protect apps that download and decompress malicious HTTP responses.
Node.js has no complete workaround, it was said.

articles.title: Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers
articles.text:
A criminal using the Amadey malware can no longer access or steal data from 180,000 infected computers around the world, including some in Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) says. The agency's operators gained access to the criminal's operation's backend and cut it off from those computers.
"The next steps that we took were to disconnect that Amadey controller from all those victims," Tauri Gregory, ASD's acting deputy director-general of intelligence, told ABC News in an interview published on October 27.
ASD is Australia's foreign signals intelligence and cyber security agency. Its offensive cyber operations need explicit approval from the Australian government and can disrupt cybercriminals overseas by disabling their infrastructure.
Amadey was sold to criminals as a service in 2018, according to ESET's analysis of Amadey. Each buyer runs its own control panel on its own servers.
Computers infected with Amadey check in with their buyer's command-and-control (C2) server and carry out its orders. Amadey's main job is to install more malware, such as the StealC infostealer. It can also steal credentials and give the buyer remote access to the machine.
The most common ways Amadey reached computers were fake software updates, cracked software installers, and other malware loaders.
The criminal's Amadey operation was one of many. In its tracking, ESET identified 53 separate Amadey botnets that did not share infrastructure.
Disconnecting a controller from its victims also does not undo earlier theft. Credentials stolen by infostealers can sit unused for months before attackers use them, according to Microsoft's analysis. A stolen session cookie can allow an attacker to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA).
ASD's annual cyber threat report, published on October 27, does not describe the operation.
Amadey's infrastructure was also disrupted in June by Operation Endgame, an international law enforcement operation that works with private partners. Between June 15 and 19, the operation targeted servers associated with Amadey, StealC, and the SocGholish malware.
Australia is one of nine countries whose law enforcement and judicial authorities run Operation Endgame together, according to Europol's June announcement. It was not on Europol's list of countries that took part in the June action week, and the announcement does not mention ASD.
In a separate case, ASD said it received a tip that 5 terabytes of data stolen from a business were for sale. The business did not know it had been hacked. The data included business documents, personal data, and login credentials and passwords.
The agency broke in and destroyed the data before it could be sold. The destroyed files included an estimated 4.8 million stolen from Australians and hundreds of thousands taken from victims in other countries.

articles.title: Faire tourner ses jeux Steam sur PS5 : ce launcher gratuit réalise le fantasme des joueurs
articles.text:
Et si votre PlayStation 5 pouvait aussi faire tourner les jeux de votre bibliothèque Steam ? C’est la promesse de Playden, un launcher gratuit et open source qui fait fonctionner certains titres Windows directement sur la console. Une prouesse technique qui nécessite toutefois un jailbreak et quelques précautions.
Voir tourner des jeux PC sur une PlayStation 5 n’est plus seulement un fantasme de bidouilleur. Un développeur vient de mettre à disposition Playden sur GitHub, un client Steam non officiel et open source capable de télécharger les jeux vidéo de votre bibliothèque Steam et de les exécuter directement sur la console de Sony. Chaque titre dispose même de sa propre icône sur l’écran d’accueil comme s’il s’agissait d’un jeu PS5 classique.
Le projet, disponible gratuitement sur GitHub, est encore expérimental. Mais ses premiers résultats ont de quoi intriguer, notamment avec des titres aussi exigeants que Cyberpunk 2077.
Comment des jeux Windows peuvent-ils tourner sur PS5 ?
Playden ne nécessite pas Windows ni SteamOS. Il s’appuie sur prospero-win, une adaptation de Wine qui permet d’exécuter des logiciels Windows sur le système de la PlayStation 5.
Le processeur AMD de la console utilisant la même architecture x86-64 que la plupart des PC, les jeux 64 bits n’ont pas besoin d’une émulation complète du processeur. La principale difficulté se situe plutôt du côté des bibliothèques système et de l'affichage.
Pour les graphismes, DXVK traduit les instructions Direct3D 8 à 11 vers Vulkan, tandis que vkd3d-proton assure la compatibilité avec Direct3D 12. Le launcher prépare ensuite un environnement distinct pour chaque jeu, qui peut être lancé directement depuis l’interface de la PS5. Sur le papier, le résultat est séduisant. Dans les faits, tout dépend encore du jeu choisi.
Cyberpunk 2077 fonctionne, mais ne criez pas victoire trop vite
Le développeur publie une liste de compatibilité qui comprend déjà plusieurs titres jouables dont Cyberpunk 2077, DOOM Eternal ou, encore, Dead Cells.
Le cas de Cyberpunk mérite néanmoins quelques précisions. Le jeu aurait bien démarré avec ses menus, la création du personnage et les premières minutes de l’aventure. Mais le test documenté est limité à treize minutes d'utilisation sans mesure du nombre d’images par seconde. Difficile, dans ces conditions, de garantir une expérience réellement satisfaisante sur la durée.
D'autres limites persistent. Les jeux protégés par Denuvo Anti-Tamper, ceux utilisant certains anti-triches au niveau du noyau ou nécessitant des launchers supplémentaires ne sont pas pris en charge. Le jeu en ligne reste également problématique.
Surtout, Playden exige une PS5 jailbreakée. Son développeur utilise principalement le firmware 13.60 et ne garantit pas le fonctionnement sur les autres versions. L’installation demande aussi plusieurs outils non officiels et un ordinateur relié au même réseau.
Attention à votre compte Steam et à vos sauvegardes
Playden est encore en version alpha, et son créateur ne cache pas les risques. L’application peut conserver un jeton de connexion Steam non chiffré sur la console potentiellement accessible à toute personne disposant d’un accès aux fichiers. Il est heureusement possible de désactiver la connexion persistante.
Le développeur alerte également sur la synchronisation avec Steam Cloud. Un bogue pourrait remplacer une sauvegarde valide par un fichier plus ancien ou corrompu. Il conseille donc d’en conserver une copie de secours hors de Steam Cloud avant de tester Playden.
Le jailbreak expose également à des dysfonctionnements et à d’éventuelles sanctions de Sony, notamment concernant l’accès aux services en ligne.
Pour profiter de Steam sur son téléviseur sans ces complications, un PC relié en HDMI ou un Steam Deck avec son dock restent des solutions plus simples. Steam Link permet également de diffuser les jeux sur un appareil compatible à condition de disposer d’un ordinateur qui les fait tourner.
- Une PS5 plus compacte, plus légère
- Le repositionnement du bouton Eject
- Un SSD de 1 To (822 Go d’espace disponible au déballage)
- Améliorations graphiques significatives
- Technologie PSSR efficace quand bien implémentée
- Efficacité énergétique
- Mini-PC compact et cro-meugnon
- Association Steam/Steam Controller
- Performances honnêtes, en 2026

articles.title: Anthropic says it will be burning lots of natural gas to feed the AI boom
articles.text:
Anthropic says it will be burning lots of natural gas to feed the AI boom
Anthropic reveals spending threats associated with fossil fuels as it prepares to go public
- Anthropic is becoming increasingly reliant on fossil fuels as the queue to join the power grid grows
- Competing with other hyperscalers and conflict in the Middle East is increasing fuel costs
- Trump is trying to increase fossil fuel energy production while simultaneously killing renewable energy projects
In order to meet the massive power demands of AI data centers, Anthropic is becoming increasingly reliant on natural gas to fuel its buildout.
The United States power grid is lagging behind on the demands of an enormous number of requests for grid connections from data centers, prompting many developers to equip their sites with natural gas burning turbine generators.
While this does counter having to build the necessary grid infrastructure and anger from consumers over rising electricity prices, it has left Anthropic vulnerable to fluctuations in fossil fuel prices made worse by conflict in the Middle East.
Data centers turn to fossil fuels
“Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense,” Anthropic said in documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission as the company prepares to go public.
Anthropic also acknowledged in the same filing that increasing global temperatures - caused by climate change - would contribute towards increased operating costs, leaving the company in something of an impasse. To remain competitive, the company needs to continue expanding data center capacity, and the only way to do that is to rely on fossil fuels.
But the same tactic that Anthropic is using to cut down wait times for grid connections is also being used by other hyperscalers and AI companies. Anthropic has predicted that “This competition could drive up the price of natural gas.”
The Trump administration has attempted to make it easier than ever for new fossil fuel projects to be approved, scrubbing the climate-improving red tape in favor of quick input to the energy grid. Old fossil fuel sites, shuttered and set for demolition by the Biden administration, have also been brought back online in an attempt to quell the growing backlog of new grid connections.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
But in order to appease some of the dissatisfaction of Americans dissatisfied with the enormous buildout of data centers and the associated downstream costs, Trump has urged developers to shoulder the costs of new grid infrastructure and contributory price increases - which Anthropic said “could adversely affect our cost structure and limit our ability to scale our compute infrastructure, develop and deploy our models, and service our customers.”
Anger against data centers is snowballing
From the harms to local environments and the wider climate, to noise pollution and lowered property values - data centers have become a great unifier across the political spectrum as Democrats and Republicans oppose the unprecedented buildout of AI data centers across the US.
Two-thirds of Americans said they oppose the construction of new facilities, and it has become a key issue in the lead up to the most important election of 2026: the November midterms. Candidates aligned with Trump’s AI first rhetoric have been buoyed by political action committees, but face a difficult time at the polls.
One of the biggest issues facing everyday Americans is the cost of living. Rising energy prices caused in tandem by the US war on Iran and the increased demand from AI data centers is at the front of voters' minds, and prices are unlikely to come down any time soon.

articles.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
articles.text:
OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown.
OpenAI's reasoning models work through a problem before answering, and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read. The method got past the protections OpenAI added in August against this kind of reasoning theft. OpenAI confirmed the problem and fixed it on October 23, according to Xint.
Xint ran the technique against gpt-5.6-sol, one of OpenAI's reasoning models, using math and algorithm puzzles its researchers wrote themselves. The reasoning it pulled out came from those same requests, and Xint did not claim the method could reach another user's reasoning.
Xint says it cannot prove the copied text is word-for-word the model's real reasoning, because it never had the original to compare against. Two cheaper models each repeated the item and produced the same text, which rules out mistakes in the copying step but leaves open the possibility that compaction reworded the text.
Compaction is an OpenAI feature that uses a model to squeeze a long conversation into a smaller, encrypted item that carries the context forward.
Xint sent a task to gpt-5.6-sol and kept the encrypted reasoning it returned. It then called the compaction step on the same model and told it to copy that reasoning into the compacted item word-for-word, with every space changed to a tab to get past OpenAI's usage-policy filters.
Because compaction items can move between models, Xint passed the item to the cheaper gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o models and asked each to repeat its input exactly, which they did.
The method worked around a fix OpenAI had already shipped. In August, researchers behind a paper called Stolen Thoughts showed that encrypted reasoning from a strong model could be replayed into a weaker model from the same company, which would then repeat it as plain text. OpenAI and others blocked that cross-model replay soon after.
Compaction got past that block, Xint said, because the compaction step runs on the same model that made the reasoning, so it never triggers the cross-model check.
The idea built on Xint's earlier work, called GhostCompact, which showed the compaction step can be pushed to run tasks of the attacker's choosing. Xint has published the code in its GitHub repository.
The fix was on OpenAI's side, so developers who build on the API do not need to change anything. Xint called it an undisclosed fix and said OpenAI paid the researchers a $6,000 reward.
Xint tested only gpt-5.6-sol and did not check whether GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's newer model, is affected. It is not known whether anyone used the method before OpenAI closed it. Xint also argued that fixing this one path may not be enough because, in its view, any server-side step that reads a model's decrypted reasoning and follows the user's instructions could leak it.
OpenAI keeps raw reasoning hidden partly to stop distillation, where one company trains a cheaper model on another's outputs. Raw reasoning makes better training data than the final answer alone, because it shows how the model worked through the problem, which is what makes it worth stealing for a rival.
OpenAI said in September that it had disrupted a July campaign that tried to expose its models' hidden reasoning, and linked a core part of it to people associated with China's Moonshot AI.
Anthropic and a joint U.S. government advisory have each reported China-based labs targeting the hidden reasoning of American models. None of that is tied to Xint's compaction method, which is a demonstration rather than an attack seen in the wild.

The Google Pixel 11 has hit a new record low at Mint Mobile — get up to $900 off plus a cheap plan
Easily the best Pixel 11 deal yet from the well-known carrier

articles.title: Qué aprendió Jeff Bezos trabajando como cocinero de comida rápida antes de fundar Amazon
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos tenía 16 años cuando consiguió su primer empleo de verano en McDonald’s, en 1980. Antes de convertirse en fundador de Amazon y uno de los hombres más ricos del mundo, el joven pasó varios meses friendo hamburguesas y aprendió lecciones que, según sus propias declaraciones, marcaron su forma de entender los negocios.
Bezos trabajó como cocinero, no como cajero. “No me dejaban acercarme a los clientes. Era mi época de adolescente con acné. Me decían: ‘¿Por qué no trabajas en la cocina?’”, relató el empresario a Fast Company, con un tono de broma sobre su rol en la parrilla.
El desafío de mantener el ritmo en horas pico
Como parrillero, la mayor dificultad para Bezos consistía en sostener la producción al ritmo adecuado durante los momentos de mayor demanda. “Cuando eres cocinero, lo más complicado es que todo salga a tiempo y bien, sobre todo en hora punta”, explicó el empresario, según consta en declaraciones recogidas por el periodista Cody Teets para su libro ‘Golden Opportunity: Remarkable Careers That Began at McDonald’s (2012)’.
Esa experiencia fue, de acuerdo con Wired, el primer contacto directo de Bezos con el sector minorista. Durante el verano, observó de cerca el sistema de automatización que empleaba la cadena de comida rápida: pitidos y señales que indicaban el momento exacto de revolver los huevos, dar la vuelta a las hamburguesas o retirar las papas fritas de la freidora.
Alcanzar esa precisión en las rutinas le permitió comprender, desde joven, que las operaciones a gran escala premian el orden y la disciplina.
El servicio al cliente, una lección aprendida desde la cocina
Aunque no tenía trato directo con el público, Bezos pudo observar de cerca el trabajo de atención al cliente que realizaban sus compañeros en la caja. De esa experiencia extrajo tres lecciones que consideró valiosas: identificar con claridad lo que pide el cliente, asistirlo cuando es necesario y saber disculparse si algo sale mal, según confesó en una entrevista con Wired.
“Aprendí que es realmente difícil”, declaró Bezos a Fast Company sobre el servicio al cliente. Esa noción temprana derivó, años después, en uno de los pilares de su empresa: la obsesión por el cliente, definida como el primero de los principios de liderazgo de Amazon.
Trabajar bajo presión y la importancia del equipo
Bezos también destacó la dificultad de actuar bajo presión ante la cantidad de imprevistos que pueden surgir en un restaurante, un desafío mayor para alguien que recién comenzaba y era muy joven. Con el tiempo, comprobó que un buen desempeño laboral genera confianza de manera progresiva.
A esto sumó otro aprendizaje: la relación con los compañeros de trabajo incide directamente en el ambiente laboral y, en consecuencia, en el resultado final del negocio con los clientes. Ese concepto de colaboración también quedó documentado en el libro de Teets.
Del verano en McDonald’s a su primer proyecto propio
La experiencia en la cadena de comida rápida duró apenas un verano. Al año siguiente, Bezos emprendió uno de sus primeros proyectos empresariales junto a su entonces novia, Ursula “Uschi” Werner: el DREAM Institute, un campamento de verano orientado a enseñar métodos de razonamiento en ciencias y literatura a jóvenes.
La iniciativa logró reunir a seis estudiantes, entre ellos dos hermanos del propio Bezos, que pagaron 600 dólares por participar. Werner afirmó que ese fue solo el comienzo de las aspiraciones del empresario, quien “siempre soñó con amasar una fortuna” a partir de sus ideas.
El consejo de Bezos para los jóvenes
Para Bezos, cualquier trabajo, sin importar cuán sencillo parezca, ofrece una oportunidad de aprendizaje si se lo encara con seriedad. “Se puede aprender lo que es la responsabilidad en cualquier tipo de trabajo, si te lo tomas en serio, incluso si es dando vueltas a unas hamburguesas”, afirmó en el libro de Teets.
El empresario remarcó además que ese tipo de experiencia temprana aporta un aprendizaje distinto al que se adquiere en la educación formal: “Se aprende mucho trabajando de joven en McDonald’s. Es diferente a lo que se puede aprender en el colegio”, sostuvo, y agregó que no debe subestimarse el valor de ese tipo de vivencias.

articles.title: Noté 9,7/10, Proton VPN Plus passe à 2,49 €/mois pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Proton VPN a décidé de ne pas attendre plus longtemps pour lancer son offre Black Friday. Du 26 octobre au 30 novembre 2026, sa formule VPN Plus bénéficie de 75 % de réduction dans le cadre d’un abonnement de 24 mois.
Le Black Friday commence tôt chez Proton VPN. Dès ce lundi 26 octobre, le service suisse réduit de 75 % le tarif de l’abonnement VPN Plus souscrit pour deux ans. Que vous soyez déjà utilisateur de l’offre gratuite de Proton VPN ou que vous désiriez souscrire à une solution fiable pour sécuriser votre connexion, c’est une opportunité intéressante qui s’accompagne d’une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours.
Pourquoi passer de Proton Free à VPN Plus pendant le Black Friday ?
La version gratuite de Proton VPN permet de tester le service sur un seul appareil, sans bridage de vitesse, et donne accès à des serveurs sélectionnés automatiquement dans dix pays. Cela peut satisfaire les besoins modestes, mais si vous désirez aller plus loin sur ces points, opter pour VPN Plus est sans nul doute le choix le plus pertinent.
Tout d’abord, cette formule permet de connecter jusqu’à dix appareils en même temps, ce qui est utile pour équiper votre foyer. Elle donne également accès à plus de 20 000 serveurs répartis dans plus de 140 pays, et vous laisse le choix de l’emplacement de votre connexion.
Cela vous permet d’opter, par exemple, pour un serveur proche afin de privilégier la rapidité, ou pour un serveur étranger plus lointain en fonction de vos besoins. Enfin, on peut également évoquer VPN Accelerator, disponible aussi dans l’offre gratuite : selon Proton, cette technologie peut augmenter les performances de la connexion VPN jusqu’à 400 % dans certaines conditions, notamment avec un serveur éloigné.
Opter pour Proton VPN Plus vous donne donc accès à plus de fonctionnalités, plus de choix de serveurs, le tout sur davantage d’appareils.
Des outils avancés pour renforcer la confidentialité
Proton VPN Plus ne s’arrête pas là, notamment en matière de sécurité. Une fois connecté à un serveur distant, le service masque votre adresse IP réelle et chiffre les données qui transitent par le tunnel sécurisé. Pour cela, il utilise des protocoles reconnus, dont WireGuard et OpenVPN. Ses applications sont open source et font l’objet d’audits indépendants.
VPN Plus donne également accès à NetShield, un outil de filtrage DNS qui bloque les connexions vers des domaines associés aux logiciels malveillants. Il peut aussi filtrer les publicités et limiter le chargement des traqueurs présents sur les sites que vous visitez.
On peut également citer Secure Core, qui fait transiter le trafic de la connexion par plusieurs serveurs afin d’en renforcer la protection, ainsi que le kill switch, qui peut interrompre l’accès à Internet si la connexion au VPN se coupe. Autant de solutions qui évitent les mauvaises surprises durant votre navigation.
Un VPN fort bien noté par Clubic
Dans le test de Clubic, Proton VPN s’est vu attribuer la note de 9,7 sur 10. La rédaction salue notamment son niveau de confidentialité, ses applications accessibles et les performances de ses serveurs européens.
Point intéressant : si le test souligne que les tarifs affichés par Proton VPN sont généralement plus élevés que ceux de ses concurrents, la remise actuelle de 75 % rend le service particulièrement compétitif. En effet, elle fait passer le tarif mensuel de l’offre VPN Plus de 9,99 € sans engagement à l’équivalent de 2,49 €. Cependant, il faut tenir compte du fait que l’abonnement de 24 mois vous sera débité en une fois, soit 59,76 €, au moment de votre souscription. L’offre Black Friday de Proton VPN est valable jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026.

articles.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
articles.text:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has issued an alert warning of unauthorized remote access to video surveillance systems manufactured by Dahua.
"Cases of compromising IP cameras and DVRs with access to the video stream, changing the device configuration and creating third-party accounts have been recorded," the State Special Communications Service of Ukraine (SSSCIP) said in an alert issued last week.
The primary initial access vector used in the attacks is via Easy4IP, a peer-to-peer (P2P) platform that allows users to remotely monitor homes or small businesses by connecting their Dahua IP cameras, NVRs, and DVRs via a smartphone app or web browser by scanning a QR code or entering the hardware Serial Number (SN).
The agency has warned that the serial numbers have a predictable structure containing a 10-character model prefix that's identical for all units of the same device family and a five-character hexadecimal counter that's incremented almost sequentially (e.g., 7K01F36PCA003E8).
This, in turn, allows attackers to guess them at scale through a brute-force attack and identify if they are connected to the cloud without hitting rate limits or lockouts. As a result, all devices with active P2P functionality are at risk even if they cannot be accessed directly via the internet.
"The assumption that the serial number is unknown to anyone is not a reason to consider the device secure," CERT-UA said.
Authentication barriers are overcome by leveraging weak or known passwords, or by exploiting authentication bypass vulnerabilities in outdated firmware versions, such as CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045. CERT-UA has shared the following indicators of compromise associated with the activity -
- Presence of unknown accounts
- Unauthorized configuration changes
- Audit logs containing authentication events using the manufacturer's native protocol (DVRIP) and from a local address (127.0.0.1), a sign of P2P access.
To counter the threat, it's advised to disable the P2P feature if not required, avoid exposing them directly to the internet, and keep the software up-to-date.
The agency has not disclosed who was targeted, when these infections occurred, how many devices had been infected, or who was responsible for the activity. However, the findings share similarities with two clusters of activity that Hunt.io disclosed as targeting IP cameras in Ukraine and Russia.
One of the campaigns, attributed to a Russian-speaking operator, singled out internet-exposed cameras in Ukraine using known Dahua and Hikvision vulnerabilities, ultimately compromising 58 devices. The activity involved the exploitation of the following flaws by integrating Ingram, a publicly available webcam vulnerability scanner -
- CVE-2017-7921 - An authentication bypass vulnerability in Hikvision
- CVE-2020-25078 - A credential disclosure vulnerability in D-Link
- CVE-2020-25169 - An unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in Reolink
- CVE-2021-33044 / CVE-2021-33045 - Authentication bypass vulnerabilities in Dahua that allow passwordless login
- CVE-2021-36260 - An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Hikvision.
In parallel, the threat actor is also said to have undertaken scanning and exploitation of TP-Link and MikroTik routers and cameras using vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-53375 and CVE-2024-57049 across 15 European countries, including Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Moldova, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, the U.K., and Austria.
The second campaign, codenamed Operation CameraSwarm and attributed to a lone threat actor, is believed to have compromised over 14,530 Dahua IP cameras between June 17 and July 22, 2026, using a combination of credential brute-force attacks and the exploitation of the CVE-2021-33044-CVE-2021-33045 chain.
The attack scans for TCP port 37777, which is the default proprietary management and video streaming port used by Dahua, followed by collecting serial numbers, breaking into those devices by employing the aforementioned two exploitation methods, and then deploying a persistent backdoor account ("p2pwn / p2password") on nearly 2,000 cameras in a manner that can survive password change and a factory reset.
"1,923 cameras carry a persistent backdoor account (p2pwn / p2password), installed over RPC after either bypass," Hunt.io noted at the time. "It is stored independently of the admin password and survives a password change and, on most firmware, a factory reset. 283 cameras were reached by serial number alone through Dahua's cloud relay, with no device address and, in most cases, no credentials."
In some instances, the attackers have been found to abuse Dahua's cloud relay to reach cameras behind NATs using only their serial numbers.
Earlier this year, Dutch intelligence agencies warned that Russian actors are compromising IP cameras across the E.U., NATO states, and Ukraine to conduct systematic digital espionage operations and acquire military intelligence.
"This actor performs automated analysis of imagery through image recognition software to conduct targeted searches for military vehicles and the military cargo they are transporting," the July 2026 bulletin said.
"This provides the actor with, among other things, relevant military data, such as E.U. and NATO military transport routes, weapon deliveries to Ukraine, and the locations of Ukrainian military personnel. The information from IP cameras in Ukraine is used in attempts to neutralize Ukrainian military personnel and to destroy their military material."

articles.title: GMKtec's M6 Ultra mini PC is our top-tested pick for home offices
articles.text:
The GMKtec M6 Ultra is our favorite mini PC overall — now Amazon has it on a limited-time deal for $500
Our number one mini PC pick for most people gets a limited-time price cut
The GMKtec M6 Ultra is the mini PC we recommend for most people who want a compact desktop for everyday work and general office tasks. For me, it's the daily driver of the mini PC world.
What we particularly like about this mini computer, which scored 4.5 stars in our review, is the value you get here. The M6 Ultra is currently on sale for $500 (was $700) at Amazon, coming equipped with 16GB DDR5 and 1TB SSD. Both can be upgraded, too.
• Best for: home and office users who want an affordable, upgradeable mini PC for productivity, media, and casual gaming.
• Why we like it: We rated the GMKtec M6 Ultra as the best mini overall - it does everything most users want, with plenty of scope for expansion if you're running more demanding workloads. Alongside the Ryzen 5 7640HS chip, it also has two USB4 ports for fast accessories or hooking up an external GPU. Rounding out the connectivity are dual 2.5G Ethernet ports, and Wi-Fi 6E.
A compact mini PC with a six-core, 12-thread AMD Ryzen 5 7640HS, Radeon 760M integrated graphics, dual-channel DDR5 memory (up to 128GB), and two M.2 NVMe slots. It has two USB4 ports, HDMI 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4, dual 2.5G Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E, and Bluetooth 5.2, and it can be VESA mounted behind a monitor.
Why we recommend it
In our GMKtec NucBox M6 Ultra review, Alastair Jennings tested the 32GB and 1TB configuration and gave it four stars, with full marks for value. He found it handled everything he threw at it, praised how easy it is to upgrade the RAM and storage, and said it stays quiet during everyday use. He noted that fans get louder under load and that gaming is limited to lower settings without a dedicated graphics card, though its USB4 ports leave the door open to adding an external GPU.
For more picks, including the M6 Ultra, see our guide to the best mini PCs.
Price Context & Historical Value
Since the start of the component cost crisis, this is the general sale price we see on the GMKtec M6 Ultra. But I will note that the Amazon offer is better than anything else I'm seeing on the same machine. On the GMKtec website, $500 buys you the M6 Ultra with 16GB memory and 512GB SSD. So, I'd pick it up from Amazon while the deal lasts.
You could hold out for Black Friday, where it may get a slightly deeper discount (but no guarantees given the state of tech prices right now, and I'd expect it to go no lower than about $20 more if it does). All told, a good price and time to buy for a great machine.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the GMKtec M6 Ultra if... you want a compact, quiet PC for office work, media streaming, and casual gaming. The memory and storage expansion with eGPU support gives it extra versatility for different workloads.
❌ Skip the GMKtec M6 Ultra if... you want to play modern games at high settings without buying an external GPU.

articles.title: Auroch Announces and Unannounces Mass Layoffs Following Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 Launch but
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Auroch Announces and Unannounces Mass Layoffs Following Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 Launch but
Auroch Digital, the studio behind Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War! recently posted an announcement to its LinkedIn page, breaking the news that it would be laying off as much as 25% of its workforce due to "market conditions." However, shortly after the studio announced the layoffs, as covered by GameIndustry, the announcement post disappeared. The original post read:
Auroch Digital via GameIndustryOver the past year our colleagues have delivered amazing games like Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War! to wonderful reception from our players. Despite that creative success, the same market conditions that have challenged so many of our fellow developers have now also affected us. Consequently, we have made the decision to restructure the studio to work through a turbulent and uncertain time in our industry.
The announcement added that the studio will be conducting "a redundancy consultation process affecting around a quarter of roles at the studio."
While the post publicly announcing the layoffs has since disappeared, PC Gamer reports that two employees at Auroch have since confirmed the layoffs. The layoffs come just shy of two weeks after one week after Auroch Digital released Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 and while Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life and Warhammer Survivors are still in development, with a release date for the former pending announcement. It's likely that the announcement will reappear online once the requisite workers unions and government institutions have been informed, as is usually the case with redundancy negotiations.

articles.title: El iPhone y el Mac ya ejecutan juegos de Nintendo Switch como aplicaciones nativas y sin emulación
articles.text:
Un proyecto de código abierto permite que el iPhone y el Mac ejecuten juegos de Nintendo Switch como aplicaciones nativas y sin emulación. Se trata de nxnative, una herramienta desarrollada por la comunidad que convierte el código original de los videojuegos en programas que corren de forma directa sobre los procesadores de Apple, sin necesidad de simular todo el hardware de la consola.
La propuesta llega en un momento en el que la Nintendo Switch original ha perdido buena parte de su protagonismo. Lanzada en 2017 con un chip Tegra de NVIDIA de potencia limitada incluso para su época, la consola quedó relegada tras la llegada de la Switch 2, capaz de ejecutar todo su catálogo con mejor calidad y rendimiento.
Cabe señalar que nxnative ofrece una vía alternativa para seguir disfrutando de esos juegos, esta vez desde dispositivos Apple.
Qué es nxnative y cómo logra ejecutar juegos sin emulación
Nxnative es un proyecto de código abierto disponible en GitHub pensado para dispositivos con procesadores ARM de Apple, lo que incluye iPhone, iPad y ordenadores Mac con Apple Silicon. Su diferencia frente a los emuladores tradicionales radica en el método que utiliza para hacer funcionar los juegos.
En lugar de recrear por completo el sistema operativo y el hardware de la Nintendo Switch, la herramienta ejecuta directamente el código original de los videojuegos sobre el procesador de Apple. Esto reduce parte de la carga de procesamiento que normalmente exige la emulación tradicional.
La clave técnica está en la arquitectura compartida entre ambos sistemas. La Nintendo Switch utiliza un procesador NVIDIA Tegra X1 con arquitectura ARM, la misma familia de instrucciones que emplean los chips Apple Silicon.
Aunque existen diferencias entre ambas plataformas, esa coincidencia permite reutilizar gran parte de las instrucciones originales de los juegos sin necesidad de traducirlas a otra arquitectura.
Esta aproximación, basada en técnicas de recompilación y adaptación de código ARM64, es lo que explica por qué nxnative puede ofrecer un rendimiento superior al de la consola original, incluso en dispositivos con especificaciones modestas dentro del ecosistema Apple.
Requisitos para instalar nxnative en iPhone, iPad y Mac
El funcionamiento de nxnative no está disponible para cualquier dispositivo Apple. En móviles, la compatibilidad se limita al iPhone 15 Pro y modelos superiores, mientras que en tablets se requiere como mínimo un iPad con chip M1.
Esta restricción responde a una cuestión técnica concreta: la compatibilidad con las texturas comprimidas BC que utilizan los videojuegos de Nintendo Switch. Sin el soporte adecuado para este tipo de compresión, los juegos no pueden ejecutarse de forma correcta en el dispositivo.
A nivel de sistema operativo, es necesario contar con iOS 26 o iPadOS 26 para que la herramienta funcione. En el caso de los ordenadores Mac, el requisito mínimo es un procesador M1, sin necesidad de versiones posteriores del chip.
Rendimiento de los juegos de Nintendo Switch en dispositivos Apple
Las pruebas realizadas hasta el momento incluyen alrededor de 70 juegos de Nintendo Switch, que en su mayoría funcionan sin complicaciones relevantes. En numerosos casos, el rendimiento obtenido alcanza los 30 cuadros por segundo e incluso llega a duplicar esa cifra.
Decenas de títulos ya se ejecutan a 60 FPS, el doble de la tasa de cuadros habitual en la Nintendo Switch original, que solía moverse en torno a los 30 FPS y con frecuencia de manera inestable.
En el apartado de ordenadores, un video publicado por Andrew Tsai muestra el comportamiento de varios juegos funcionando bajo nxnative. Uno de los ejemplos más llamativos es Monster Hunter Rise, que alcanza los 60 FPS en un MacBook Air de 2020 equipado con apenas 8 GB de RAM.
En equipos con mayor capacidad de procesamiento, como los modelos MacBook Pro, el margen de rendimiento es todavía mayor. En estos dispositivos resulta posible ejecutar varios juegos de Nintendo Switch de forma simultánea, cada uno a 60 FPS, sin que se produzcan caídas significativas en la fluidez.

articles.title: Voyage au Japon : l'eSIM Saily à -10% pour éviter le hors forfait
articles.text:
Hors de l’Union européenne, la data de votre forfait français peut vite faire grimper la facture, et le Wi-Fi des hôtels reste un pari. Avec le code CLUBIC, Saily, l’eSIM de voyage de l’éditeur de NordVPN, retire 10 % sur tous ses forfaits, mais ne fournit que de la data, sans appels ni SMS.
Saily vend des forfaits de données mobiles pour plus de 200 destinations, pour un pays, une région ou le monde entier. Le service est édité par Nord Security, la société derrière NordVPN, et s’achète sur saily.com ou dans l’application iOS et Android. Sur les deux, le code CLUBIC retire 10 % sur tous les forfaits Saily, y compris ceux déjà affichés en promotion et les abonnements Ultra.
Il se saisit à la page de paiement, dans le champ « Vous avez un code promo ? ». L’offre s’adresse d’abord à ceux qui partent hors de l’Union européenne sans vouloir changer de carte SIM.
Sur saily.com comme dans l’application, le code CLUBIC déduit 10 % du prix de chaque forfait eSIM Saily avant le paiement, quelle que soit la destination.
Pourquoi choisir l’eSIM Saily ?
- Une installation avant le départ : Vous achetez le forfait dans l’application et l’installez chez vous : la connexion démarre à l’arrivée, sans toucher à votre carte SIM physique. Le forfait Monde s’active seul dans le premier pays visité, ou 30 jours après l’achat.
- Des forfaits taillés pour le séjour : Vous choisissez un pays, une région ou le forfait Monde valable dans 121 pays, puis le volume et la durée. Les formules illimitées offrent 5 Go par jour en haut débit, puis un débit réduit à 1 Mb/s.
- Une protection héritée de NordVPN : Un bloqueur de publicités, une protection contre les sites malveillants et plus de 115 emplacements virtuels sont inclus sans surcoût. Selon Saily, le bloqueur économise jusqu’à 28,6 % de data.
Du séjour aux États-Unis au tour du monde, ce que change une eSIM
Fin septembre, nous relevions 10 Go valables 30 jours aux États-Unis à 19,84 €, soit 17,86 € avec le code, et le forfait Monde de 10 Go sur 180 jours passait de 49,18 € à 44,26 €. Le partage de connexion est possible, pratique pour dépanner un ordinateur portable. Dans notre avis sur Saily, nous saluions aussi une application simple à prendre en main et une assistance joignable par chat 24 h/24.
Le service vise d’abord le voyageur qui sort de l’Union européenne, où la data du forfait français devient vite coûteuse, et celui qui enchaîne les pays avec une seule eSIM. Les crédits de fidélité, 3 % de chaque achat réutilisables sur un prochain forfait, récompensent ceux qui repartent souvent. Saily convient moins si vous avez besoin d’un numéro pour appeler ou recevoir un SMS de vérification sur place, puisque le service ne fournit que de la data. Il faut enfin un smartphone compatible eSIM, et une connexion Internet au moment de l’activation.
Saily face à Airalo, Holafly et Ubigi
Toutes ces eSIM promettent de la data dès l’arrivée, sans carte physique. Dans notre comparatif des meilleures eSIM internationales, Saily arrive en tête pour son rapport qualité-prix, avec des tarifs presque toujours inférieurs à ceux d’Airalo. Holafly reste plus indiqué pour la data illimitée, Ubigi pour la 5G incluse, et Airalo propose avec Discover+ une formule dotée d’un numéro, ce que Saily n’offre pas. Saily est aussi le seul des quatre à ne pas préciser l’opérateur local utilisé, quand ses concurrents l’indiquent.
✅ Les points forts
- Code CLUBIC valable sur tous les forfaits, y compris en promotion et Ultra
- Plus de 200 destinations, du pays unique au forfait Monde
- Bloqueur de publicités et emplacements virtuels inclus sans surcoût
- Installation avant le départ, connexion dès l’arrivée
- 3 % de chaque achat rendus en crédit pour le forfait suivant
❌ Les limites
- Data uniquement, sans appels ni SMS
- Opérateur local non précisé avant l’achat
- Volume de data limité sur certaines offres
- Activation impossible sans connexion Internet
Avant votre prochain départ, les forfaits Saily se commandent en quelques clics, et le code CLUBIC s’ajoute aux remises déjà affichées.
Avec 10 % de remise, Saily devient une option sérieuse pour ne plus subir le hors forfait en dehors de l’Union européenne. La remise reste modeste en valeur, deux euros environ sur un forfait de 10 Go aux États-Unis, mais elle s’applique partout et se cumule avec les promotions du moment. Les outils de protection hérités de NordVPN font la différence face à des concurrents qui vendent seulement de la data.
Ceux qui ont besoin d’un numéro local ou d’appels sur place regarderont plutôt du côté d’Airalo et de sa formule Discover+. Même chose si vous tenez à savoir quel réseau vous utiliserez avant de payer. Et si vous restez dans l’Union européenne, vérifiez d’abord ce que prévoit votre forfait français. Pour tous les autres, mieux vaut installer l’eSIM la veille du départ, tant que le Wi-Fi de la maison est là.

articles.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments -
- CVE-2026-109618 - An out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-109619 - A stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
The addition of the two flaws to the KEV catalog comes after Adel Karimi, detection and response lead at Perplexity, confirmed successful instances of remote code execution against honeypot systems on October 24, 2026.
"This is now confirmed RCE with usable memory disclosure, not just a crash followed by a suspicious process," Karimi said. "The response delivered an 800 KiB decoded cookie dump, and a function address derived from that dump using the public exploit's offsets appears in the subsequent execution payload."
"The evidence demonstrates this chain on the intentionally favorable single-worker mod_php profile; it is not a measurement of exploit reliability on other worker counts, PHP builds, or applications."
The issues have been addressed in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 released on October 21, 2026. Federal agencies have time until October 29, 2026, to apply the necessary fixes.
PHP, short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, is a server-side scripting language used in roughly 70% of all websites on the internet. According to estimates shared by Censys, more than 32.51 million PHP services are still running an affected version.
The severity of the vulnerabilities has prompted numerous advisories from software and security vendors and government agencies across the world, including -
- ABB
- Arista Networks
- Belden
- Broadcom
- Canon
- Citrix
- Craft CMS
- Dell
- Dormakaba
- Drupal
- ExpressionEngine
- F5
- Hikvision
- HP
- HPE
- Hitachi Energy
- HMS Networks
- Huawei
- IBM
- Ivanti
- Johnson Controls
- Mitel
- Moxa
- NETGEAR
- October CMS
- Okta
- QNAP
- Rockwell Automation
- Ruckus Wireless
- Salesforce
- Schneider Electric
- Siemens (1), (2)
- SonicWall
- Splunk
- Synology
- Veeam
- Wibu-Systems
- WordPress
As of October 26, 2026, the PHP Foundation also released Windows builds 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 to address CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Brotli decoder library that could also result in privilege escalation and unauthenticated remote code execution.
The vulnerability, also known as Broccoli2Shell, HTTP2Shell, and Node2Shell, affects Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.0.9, 1.1.0, and 1.2.0. It has been patched in versions 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, along with other projects that include the C library, including Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, .NET, and Python.
"In PHP Windows builds, the vulnerable decoder can be reached through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled," the PHP Foundation said. "This is disabled by default in cURL, but applications and HTTP client libraries can enable it."

articles.title: Sony veut-il vraiment tuer le Blu-ray ? Le paradoxe d'un géant qui joue sur les deux tableaux
articles.text:
Sony prépare la fin des jeux sur disque pour les nouvelles sorties PlayStation, retire des films achetés en numérique et abandonne son dernier lecteur Blu-ray 4K au Japon. Pourtant, le géant japonais a encore de bonnes raisons de soutenir le format physique. Derrière ces décisions apparemment contradictoires se cache une logique économique que nous décryptons en vidéo.
Sony tourne-t-il vraiment le dos au Blu-ray ? Notre vidéo décrypte les contradictions apparentes de sa stratégie, les atouts du disque 4K face au streaming et les raisons économiques qui pourraient assurer la survie du format.
Difficile de suivre la stratégie de Sony. D'un côté, PlayStation a annoncé la fin des jeux sur disque à partir de janvier 2028, pour les nouvelles sorties. De l'autre, au Royaume-Uni, la plateforme avait annoncé le retrait de 551 contenus StudioCanal pourtant achetés par ses utilisateurs, à compter du 1er septembre 2026, en raison d'accords de licence arrivés à expiration.
Et comme si cela ne suffisait pas, Sony vient de cesser les expéditions de son dernier lecteur Blu-ray 4K au Japon. Faut-il en conclure que le constructeur souhaite définitivement tourner la page du disque ?
Le Blu-ray 4K résiste, malgré le déclin du physique
Pas si vite. Car si les dépenses consacrées aux DVD et Blu-ray continuent de reculer, le Blu-ray 4K fait figure d'exception. Aux États-Unis, les dépenses consacrées à ce format ont progressé de 12 % en 2025, selon le Digital Entertainment Group, alors que l'ensemble du marché physique reculait de 9,3 %.
Un marché de niche, porté par des cinéphiles attachés à la qualité audiovisuelle, aux éditions collector et à la possession de leurs films. Une dernière notion qui prend tout son sens lorsque des achats numériques peuvent disparaître d'une bibliothèque.
Pourquoi Sony n'a pas intérêt à abandonner le Blu-ray
Sony n'est pas seulement PlayStation. Si sa division jeu vidéo privilégie le numérique, le groupe possède aussi Sony Pictures, fait partie des créateurs du Blu-ray et détient des brevets liés au format. Depuis 2024, il assure également la distribution de films Disney sur supports physiques en Amérique du Nord.
Autrement dit, abandonner la fabrication de lecteurs ne signifie pas nécessairement renoncer aux revenus générés par les disques. Et l'ironie est assez savoureuse : au Japon, la PS5 équipée d'un lecteur optique reste désormais le seul appareil Sony encore commercialisé capable de lire des Blu-ray 4K.
Le Blu-ray 4K pourrait-il devenir le nouveau vinyle du cinéma ? Chiffres du marché, comparaison avec le streaming, intérêts croisés des différentes activités de Sony : on fait le point dans cette nouvelle vidéo.

articles.title: Channel 4 is coming to Disney+, and I think that weakens the UK government's pitch to extend the TV licencing fee to include streaming
articles.text:
Channel 4 is coming to Disney+, as the UK government considers a 'YouTube tax' on streaming services
Another "landmark agreement" between Disney and a UK broadcaster
- Disney+ will be bringing Channel 4 content to its streaming platform in early 2027
- The collaboration aims to expand Channel 4's content on Disney+, while enhancing the British broadcaster's audience reach
- ITV joined forces with Disney+ in 2025 for a similar partnership
The Walt Disney Company has announced a new Disney+ content agreement that will bring Channel 4 into its roster of broadcasting partners in early 2027.
The partnership, which a press release claimed is a "first-of-its-kind collaboration", will see a number of Channel 4 titles become available on-demand each year on Disney+ in the UK and Ireland at the same time as airing on Channel 4. That means Disney+ subscribers can expect upcoming shows, including drama series Maya, comedy show Stepping Up, and popular reality series Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins, to be available to stream, alongside Channel 4's main live TV channel.
But given you can already stream Channel 4 content for free on its own All 4 service, what's the purpose of the partnership? For both parties, it’s all about expanding their audiences — and it could have ramifications for the proposed 'YouTube tax' changes to the BBC licensing fee.
For Disney+, it gets to expand its library of on-demand content for existing subscribers, combining quality public service programming with a premium streaming experience. At the same time, the partnership is designed to enhance Channel 4’s audience reach, giving Disney+ subscribers who don’t use public service broadcasting platforms a taste of what Channel 4 has to offer.
"Local broadcaster partnerships are very important as we build our content libraries and serve fans around the world," said Adam Smith, chairman of direct-to-consumer at Disney Entertainment. "Channel 4 has created shows with strong appeal to audiences in the UK and Ireland, and we’re excited to bring some of those favourites to Disney+", he added.
Priya Dogra, Channel 4’s chief executive, is also naturally excited by the partnership, saying. "We’re thrilled to be working with Disney+ to give audiences even more ways to discover and enjoy Channel 4’s brilliant shows," she said.
When the collaboration launches early next year, programming will be listed in a Channel 4-branded section of the Disney+ app, distinguishing it from other content on the platform. In addition to new and upcoming shows, subscribers will also have access to some of Channel 4’s existing popular titles, including Big Mood, Tip Toe, and 24 Hours in A&E — all at no extra cost.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Disney+ has secured similar collaborations with broadcasters across the EMEA region, including ARD and ZDF in Germany and RAI in Italy, but this isn’t the first time a UK broadcaster has linked up with the streaming platform to increase audience reach.
In July 2025, the streaming giant partnered with ITV to bring select Disney+ titles to the free ad-supported ITVX streaming platform. The ‘Taste of Disney+’ section allowed viewers to access a small handful of Disney+ shows for free without having to sign up for a subscription. At the same time, Disney+ launched the ‘Taste of ITVX’ collection on its own service, bringing a number of popular ITVX titles to the platform and expanding the free platform’s audience reach. However, as it stands, the deal between Disney and Channel 4 won't see Disney+ content shown on Channel 4, like it did with ITV.
What does this mean for the rumored 'YouTube tax'?
As British broadcasters increasingly partner with US streaming giants like Disney+, the UK government's proposal to expand the TV licence fee to include platforms like Netflix and YouTube could gain support.
After all, it could allow more people to access a live public broadcast channel while being able to avoid paying the licence fee, as it would be harder to police who is watching what inside a third-party app. It also becomes tougher to argue that British public television and streaming services are two different beasts.
But critics already argue this so-called 'YouTube tax' is merely a bailout for the BBC's funding shortfalls. Because many UK households intentionally ditched traditional broadcasters for streaming, this proposal would force consumers to effectively pay twice. With networks like Channel 4 and ITV proving they can independently negotiate major commercial deals, the justification for a broader streaming tax will, for many, become even weaker.
As for when exactly Disney+ subscribers can expect Channel 4 content to be integrated into the platform, it doesn’t have an exact launch date yet. But the broadcaster says "further details on launch timings and content available will be confirmed in due course".

articles.title: Call of Duty Crosses $40 Billion in Lifetime Revenue, Xbox CEO Confirms
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Call of Duty Crosses $40 Billion in Lifetime Revenue, Xbox CEO Confirms
Call of Duty has crossed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue, according to Microsoft Gaming CEO Asha Sharma. She shared the milestone on X on October 26, a few days after Modern Warfare 4's full launch on October 23, calling it one of the most celebrated games in the series' history and thanking both the Activision team and the players. The series debuted in 2003 and has seen a new entry almost every year since, along with Warzone and mobile spin-offs, so that figure covers a lot of ground. PC Gamer's math puts it at a staggering $4,762,472 a day, which is hard to wrap your head around. It's also worth remembering that this is revenue, not profit, and Activision doesn't disclose development or marketing budgets for its games.
Sharma, however, didn't say how Modern Warfare 4 is selling, or whether it was the game that pushed the franchise over the line. Early signs have been good, at least on PC. The game picked up a 90% positive Steam rating during campaign early access, a far cry from the reception Black Ops 7 got, and even climbed the Steam Top's Sellers list rapidly. Activision has also called it the conclusion of the current Modern Warfare series, with a new sub-franchise set to follow. For some context, Microsoft paid $68.7 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard back in 2023, though only some of that $40 billion would have come in under Microsoft's ownership.
Sources:
				Asha Sharma on X, 				via PC Gamer
