articles.title: The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is an affordable, no-nonsense wet and dry vacuum that vacuums up crumbs and mops floors in a single pass
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus might not have the longest battery life, but its performance is so good, that's not an issue. It's superb for both wet and dry cleaning, and getting under furniture is easy with its 180-degree hinge. I do wish it could handle larger debris, though.
Reasons to buy
- + Great job vacuuming and mopping
- + Gets to edges (along the right side)
- + Lies almost flat to get under furniture
Reasons to avoid
- - Can’t pick up larger pieces of debris
- - Solid and wet debris in same tank
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum: two-minute review
The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus looks like an almost mid-range vacuum. And it largely is. It has an all plastic build, doesn’t come with a bunch of attachments, and really does one thing. But, it does that one thing really well and that is be a wet-dry vac. In fact, when using it to simultaneously vacuum and mop, it picks up anything and everything smaller than a Cheerio. Crumbs of all sorts. Dog hair. Spilled parmesan. Coffee grounds. You get the idea.
Plus, if you compare it to the best wet-dry vacuums, you’ll see that it’s quite affordable, even if it is among the more expensive Bissell models. I do have a few quibbles, such as the fact that there’s an upper limit on the size of the debris it can suck up or the fact that all the debris goes into the same dirty water tank making emptying it a bit of a mess.
Still, for the price, it might be the best vacuum with wet-dry capabilities out there. Just be aware that the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is the same as the Bissell CrossWave Reach, but comes with a charging base.
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum: price & availability
- List price: $329.99 (about £250 / AU$470)
- Launched: September 2026
- Available in the US
The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus comes in at decidedly Bissell level prices. You don’t have to plop down the cash you would for something like the Dyson V15s Detect Submarine and its list price of $949.99 / £599.99 / AU$949. It’s even cheaper than some Chinese models like the Tineco Floor One S7 Pro with its list price of $799.99 / £599.99 / AU$999). Of course, that model does come with a larger capacity and a more impressive display.
Basically, the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus goes for $329.99 (about £250 / AU$470). This price includes the vacuum, the charging tray, two different sample sized bottles of cleaning solution, and a measuring cup for the solution.
It’s a price that I would consider mid-range for a vacuum, though it’s relatively cheap for a wet-dry vacuum. It’s also an expected price point for a higher-end Bissell product (Shark hits similar price points in my opinion). You can get the non-Plus version for $279.99. The only difference is that it comes without the charging tray.
- Value for money score: 4.5 out of 5
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum specs
| Weight (total): | 8.8 lb / 3.99 kg | 
| Weight (body only) | 8.8 lb / 3.99 kg | 
| Bin size | 450ml (clean tank) / 600ml (dirty tank) | 
| Runtime in Min mode | 23 mins | 
| Runtime in Max mode | 39 mins | 
| Charge time | 4 hrs 35 min | 
| Size (H x W x L) | 10.7 x 8.6 x 43.6 inches / 27.2 x 21.8 x 110.7 cm (L x W x H) | 
| Max suction | 7AW | 
| Modes | Eco, Hi, Turbo | 
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum: design
- Dirty water tank contains solid debris too, for better or worse
- Has a self-cleaning feature
- Can lie flat to get under furniture
The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus may be an all-plastic build, but it looks durable and cuts a somewhat dashing figure. Not quite a stick vacuum, it’s ever so slightly modular insofar as the handles comes separated from the body. It's also slim at around 4.5 inches across the body.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The power and mode buttons (eco, high, turbo) are on the handles, and are within thumb’s reach during use. The battery indicator, which shows battery life using three LEDs, as well as the indicators showing which mode the vacuum, are all on the body facing you while you clean. There’s also a button here to run the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus’s Clean-Out Cycle — a nice feature for self-cleaning the brushroll after use.
The 600ml dirty water tank clipped into the back of the body is easy to remove for emptying. When removed, the filter on top pulls right out exposing whatever debris is inside. The one downside here is that, unlike the best robot vacuums that vacuum and mop, everything goes into the same tank. Vacuumed up a bunch of rice and sucked up a spill? You’ll have to empty everything out into the same place.
The clean water tank is clipped onto the top of the floorhead. Its 450ml capacity is decent, though will require somewhat regular refilling (of water and a cup of one of the included solutions). I do like the exposed look of it, though.
As far as the rest of the floorhead, it can swivel and has a hinge for the vacuum to lay up to 180 degrees back — essentially flat — to get under furniture. And it has one large tangle-free brushroll that’s removable for cleaning or replacing and can handle just about any hard surface one would mop. Also worth noting is that it’s rated as having a 10.6 inch cleaning path, though when I measured it, I would say it’s actually 9.6 inches. You lose an inch to the plastic bezels on either side.
Lastly, the charging tray that comes with this vacuum is essentially a molded piece of plastic with charging contacts so that if you put it back in the tray after use, it will start charging automatically.
- Design score: 4.5 out of 5
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum: performance
- Great vacuuming except for larger debris
- Flawless mopping
- Can get pretty close to edges
When I first started using the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus, I found myself struggling to find something to dislike about it. After spending some time with it, that’s still mostly the case.
This is a wet-dry vacuum and mop, and it does both duties concurrently; there's no vacuum only mode, and no opportunity to only get the floor wet. Despite that, I’m going to try and separate these two functions just to give you a better idea of what to expect.
I performed a few tests when vacuuming. I threw a bunch of tea leaves on the floor as well as a bunch of rice. For both sizes of debris, the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus sucked them right up in the first go.
Because of the way the floorhead is arranged — there’s just the mop brushroll at the front end with a forward-angled silicon liner behind — it isn’t quite as successful on picking rice and similar sized debris when pulling the vacuum back as it can get caught by that liner. However, when pushing the vacuum forward, everything gets sucked up immediately.
The one caveat to that and a valid reason to still keep a regular vacuum around is the fact since the only moving part helping pick up debris is that brushroll, larger pieces of debris like cereal or popcorn will just get pushed around the front of it like a curling puck.
I found basically nothing to complain about its mopping capabilities, however. It lays down an even layer of water and detergent solution that is enough to fully mop whatever area’s been covered. And I found the floor to be dry within minutes after mopping.
I also tested the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus’s mopping by throwing a bunch of ketchup, mustard, and coffee (separately) on the floor. In each instance, whatever was on the floor was removed in one swipe. However, it takes a few passes to remove odors (and they can still persist for a short while).
Getting to the edges and corners with a vacuum is a concern, especially one without additional accessories for tight spaces. But that’s not too much of a concern here. I found that going up to edges with this vacuum allowed me to get as close as a quarter inch when moving with the right side towards the wall. With the left side of the vacuum facing the wall or edge, the three quarters of an inch closest to the wall is left untouched, while the front of the vacuum won’t touch that last inch closest to the wall. So, I was able to get pretty close to the wall but the vacuum orientation matters.
Generally, maneuvering the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is easy. It does want to pull forward so pushing the vacuum in the direction I want to go feels effortless. When pulling back in a typical vacuuming fashion, I do feel some resistance since it wants to go in that direction. Turning is just as effortless thanks to the swivelling floorhead, and the fact that it can lie almost flat means it’s a cinch to get under furniture.
Lastly, the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is not a quiet vacuum, but is in line with other cordless vacuums such as the Bissell PowerClean FurFinder. On eco mode, it reaches around 64dB. In turbo mode, it gets up to 67dB. And it hits about 65dB during its Clean-Out Cycle.
- Performance score: 4.5 out of 5
Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum: battery life
- Four and a half hour recharge time
- Up to 40 minutes of use on a single charge
Let’s get the bad out of the way. When fully drained, the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is going to take over four and a half hours to recharge. If you are an infrequent charger, then, first, shame on you, and, second, you’ll have to suffer through what amounts to almost half a day of waiting if you have to charge from empty. That said, that’s actually a normal amount of time for a cordless vacuum to recharge, though I wish the battery was removable.
The good news is that the twenty minutes it lasts on turbo, specifically 23 minutes and 21 seconds, or almost forty on eco mode, 39 minutes and 49 seconds, is more than enough battery life for a regular home. These numbers are about in line with some of Bissell’s other offerings, though not quite up to what we see with the best cordless vacuums.
Because of how well it picks up debris (with the earlier size-related caveats), I was able to clean a 800 square foot area in about ten minutes. I ended up wandering in circles with the vacuum in tow waiting for the battery to die. That’s on turbo. The almost forty minutes on eco mode is more than enough for anyone not cleaning an office building.
- Battery life score: 4 out of 5
Should you buy the Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus Cordless Wet-Dry Vacuum?

Buy it if...
You care about value
At just over three hundred bucks, this wet-dry vacuum punches above its weight. It might not have the capacity or battery life of the competition, but it does a good job at a lower price.
You need to get under furniture
Getting under furniture is always tough with a vacuum. Well, almost always. Thanks to that 180-degree hinge, it’s easy for the Reach Plus since it can lie straight back to get under that couch that’s too heavy to move.
You’re OK with simultaneous vacuuming and mopping
This Bissell is a wonder on all sorts of hard flooring, but its simultaneous vacuuming and mopping is a package deal. You can’t do one without the other.
Don't buy it if...
You need something capable of deep cleaning
The Bissell CrossWave Reach Plus is quite good at what it does, but it’s still a smaller vacuum that can’t vacuum up anything.
You have a whole building to mop
For a typical home — big or small — its 20-40 minute battery life is more than plenty to cover every square foot.

articles.title: Apple Creator Studio ahora tiene agentes de IA: así cambia la forma de editar en Mac, iPad y iPhone
articles.text:
Apple anunció una actualización de Apple Creator Studio con nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y herramientas para editar vídeo, imágenes, música y documentos. La colección incorporará contenido de MotionVFX en Final Cut Pro, Relleno generativo en Pixelmator Pro y asistentes inteligentes en Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages y Numbers. Las novedades llegarán a la App Store en noviembre de 2026 y estarán incluidas para quienes ya estén suscritos.
Aunque el titular de la actualización apunta a los agentes de IA, las funciones varían según la aplicación. Algunas ayudan a realizar tareas mediante instrucciones en lenguaje natural; otras conectan herramientas de terceros con las aplicaciones para leer y modificar contenido. Apple las presenta como una forma de facilitar flujos de trabajo y ayudar a los usuarios a aprender a utilizar sus programas.
Final Cut Pro integra contenido de MotionVFX
Final Cut Pro para Mac ofrecerá acceso integrado a miles de elementos de MotionVFX, entre ellos plantillas, gráficos, títulos y transiciones, además de recursos para rotoscopia, seguimiento y gradación de color. Los suscriptores también podrán abrir desde la aplicación un centro de contenido seleccionado por Apple con vídeos, fotografías y fondos de archivo.
La actualización conectará Final Cut Pro con Pixelmator Pro. Los editores podrán abrir una imagen de la línea de tiempo en esa aplicación, modificarla y guardar los cambios directamente en el proyecto. Apple también señala que será posible generar imágenes a partir de descripciones de texto y aplicar ediciones rápidas.
Entre las mejoras del flujo de trabajo figuran nuevas opciones para suavizar fotogramas clave, la posibilidad de separar clips de la historia principal y colocarlos en otras partes de la línea de tiempo, y la incorporación de 23 idiomas de transcripción. Según la compañía, esto facilitará la creación de subtítulos y la búsqueda de momentos dentro del material grabado.
Motion también sumará complementos de MotionVFX y herramientas para generar y editar imágenes mediante texto. Compressor, por su parte, podrá codificar vídeos grabados en modo Cine con el iPhone 18 Pro y el iPhone Duo.
Pixelmator Pro permitirá editar imágenes con instrucciones
La principal novedad de Pixelmator Pro es Relleno generativo. La herramienta permite seleccionar una zona de la imagen y describir qué cambio se quiere realizar. También se puede delimitar el área con las opciones de selección libre, rápida o magnética de la aplicación.
Apple afirma que la función adapta la iluminación, la perspectiva y la textura para integrar el elemento añadido en la imagen. Los resultados podrán ampliarse con superresolución y combinarse con las capas del proyecto, ya sea como parte de una capa existente o como una nueva con máscara inteligente.
Asistentes de IA en Logic Pro y las aplicaciones de productividad
Logic Pro para Mac incorporará un asistente inteligente en versión beta, basado en modelos de Apple y OpenAI. Podrá orientar a los usuarios en tareas de producción, ayudar a comenzar una canción o configurar una pista vocal mediante una instrucción. La beta estará disponible en inglés de Estados Unidos y requerirá macOS 27 Golden Gate o posterior en un Mac compatible con Apple Intelligence.
Keynote, Pages y Numbers también tendrán asistentes beta para suscriptores. En Keynote, ayudarán a diseñar y perfeccionar diapositivas; en Pages, a redactar y reorganizar textos; y en Numbers, a organizar y visualizar datos, recomendar gráficos y crear tablas a partir de instrucciones. Estas funciones también exigirán un dispositivo compatible con Apple Intelligence y un sistema operativo de la versión 27 o posterior.
Las tres aplicaciones añadirán compatibilidad con Model Context Protocol (MCP), que permitirá a herramientas y agentes externos leer contenido, realizar ediciones y ejecutar acciones automatizadas. Keynote admitirá además el formato abierto .keyx, diseñado para que sistemas externos puedan acceder a sus archivos.
Disponibilidad y precios
Las actualizaciones llegarán en noviembre y serán gratuitas para los suscriptores actuales. En Estados Unidos, la suscripción costará 12,99 dólares al mes o 129 dólares al año, con un mes de prueba. Estudiantes universitarios y docentes podrán acceder por 2,99 dólares mensuales o 29,99 anuales. Hasta seis personas podrán compartir la suscripción mediante En familia.
Apple mantendrá también las versiones de compra única de varias aplicaciones en la Mac App Store. Las funciones beta de IA, en cambio, tendrán requisitos de sistema y compatibilidad específicos, por lo que no estarán disponibles en todos los dispositivos.

articles.title: 22 nouveaux émetteurs DAB+ viennent d’être allumés en France, on les a listés pour vous
articles.text:
TDF a mis en service, ce mardi, 22 nouveaux émetteurs DAB+ répartis sur 18 sites un peu partout en France. Cette nouvelle vague renforce la radio numérique terrestre sur huit autoroutes et dans treize communes.
Le déploiement du DAB+ en France se poursuit, puisque ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, TDF a annoncé avoir mis en service vingt-deux nouveaux émetteurs de radio numérique sur dix-huit sites, dans le cadre justement du plan de déploiement national. Moins de quatre mois après la salve de juillet, l'opérateur renforce le signal sur huit autoroutes, de l'A75 à l'A85, et améliore l'écoute dans des villes comme Bayeux, Nevers ou Brive-la-Gaillarde. Et si ces trois lettres suivies d'un petit « plus » vous laissent encore perplexe, c'est l'occasion de faire les présentations.
22 nouveaux émetteurs DAB+ viennent d’être allumés en France
Pour ce nouveau lot d'émetteurs DAB+, TDF a d'abord pensé aux automobilistes et à la continuité d'écoute de la radio numérique sur la route. Les grands axes concentrent donc l'essentiel des nouveautés. L'A75, qui descend vers la Méditerranée à travers le Massif central, gagne deux émetteurs, à Sévérac-le-Château (Aveyron) et à Massiac (Cantal). En Normandie, l'A88 s'appuie sur celui de Falaise-Villers, dans le Calvados, et l'A28 sur le site d'Alençon-Saint-Germain, dans l'Orne. L'A85, elle, hérite d'une mise en service à Huismes, en Indre-et-Loire.
Dans le Loiret et la Nièvre, l'A77 et l'A19 profitent des sites de Montargis-Amilly, Gien-Arrabloy et Pouilly-sur-Loire. Au pied des Pyrénées, l'A64 compte désormais sur Lannemezan-Peyrehitt (Hautes-Pyrénées), tandis que dans le Limousin, l'A20 accueille l'émetteur de Razès-Les Prades (Haute-Vienne). Pour l'automobiliste, il s'agit d'une meilleure continuité d'écoute, kilomètre après kilomètre, pour que la station du moment ne s'évapore pas entre deux sorties.
Plus loin cette fois des bretelles d'autoroute, treize communes captent aussi mieux les radios nationales. La Normandie en compte trois, avec Bayeux, Falaise et Alençon, tout comme le Centre-Val de Loire, avec Montargis, Gien et Huismes. Nevers et Cosne-sur-Loire en profitent en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, Brive-la-Gaillarde en Nouvelle-Aquitaine et Massiac en Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes. L'Occitanie complète le tableau avec Lodève, Saint-Chély-d'Apcher et Lannemezan. Toutes reçoivent mieux les multiplex M1 et M2, ces deux « bouquets » qui réunissent les radios nationales.
Le DAB+, c'est quoi au juste (et faut-il changer de poste) ?
Si vous vous sentez un peu largué(e) lorsqu'on vous parle du DAB+ (Digital Audio Broadcasting), sachez qu'il s'agit du standard de diffusion numérique de la radio par voie hertzienne. Autrement dit, il est à la radio ce que la TNT est à la télévision. L'écoute reste gratuite, comme en FM, avec un son numérique et des informations, voire des visuels, liés au programme qui s'affichent à l'écran. Il est complémentaire de la FM et enrichit l'offre radiophonique, à la maison comme en voiture.
Évidemment, pour en profiter, il faut un récepteur compatible. Les postes DAB+ sont en vente en France depuis plusieurs années, et depuis 2021, tous les autoradios des véhicules neufs vendus en Europe intègrent la technologie. Pour vérifier un appareil, cherchez la mention DAB+ sur le boîtier, l'emballage, la notice ou dans les menus de réglage. Sur un autoradio, un mode de recherche DAB proposé en plus de la FM est bon signe. Au moindre doute, la notice du fabricant ou la fiche produit feront foi.
Ces mises en service ont été longuement réfléchies. On sait que chaque site a d'abord été étudié et préparé par les ingénieurs de TDF, puis équipé en fonction de sa configuration. Selon les lieux, les équipes ont pu recourir à une grue pour hisser le matériel, voire à un hélicoptère pour l'acheminer. Aux manettes, on retrouve TDF, opérateur de la diffusion hertzienne de la télévision et de la radio, autrement dit le spécialiste de la diffusion par les ondes, qui s'appuie sur un réseau de 9 200 sites. Pascale Varnière, qui dirige sa branche audiovisuelle, évoque une « étape importante » avec la nouvelle du jour. Elle y lit la mobilisation de ses équipes, mais aussi l'engagement des éditeurs, c'est-à-dire des stations de radio elles-mêmes, à développer la radio numérique. Après les 26 émetteurs allumés en juillet, la carte du DAB+ continue de se completer, pièce après pièce.

articles.title: AI automation hinges on portability, says Cloudera analyst - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cloudera bets portability, not agents, will set it apart in enterprise AI
Enterprises racing toward AI automation are finding that where their models and data run matters as much as what the models can do. Regulatory pressure, rising token costs and fear of lock-in are pushing companies to demand more control over their AI workloads.
That demand is shaping how data platform providers pitch their next act. Cloudera Inc. started out in the Hadoop market and later moved to a unified data layer that spans clouds and on-premises infrastructure. It is now positioning itself as an anywhere cloud for AI, according to Paul Gillin (pictured, right), enterprise editor of SiliconANGLE Media Inc.
“I think big companies decided a long time ago. They didn’t want to be beholden to a single cloud provider and that’s sort of baked into the landscape now,” Gillin said. “I think what’s different about Cloudera is that they’re strong proponents of on-premises infrastructure, of sovereign clouds, of companies being able to run their workloads wherever they want and move from one to another.”
Gillin spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight (left) at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI automation and provided analysis of the event’s keynote speech. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereign AI and purpose-built agents drive AI automation
Sovereign and private AI came up frequently in the EVOLVE26 keynote. Surveys point to regulation as the main reason enterprises want to keep AI inside their own walls. Open-weight models give them a way to do it, having grown from about 20% of token use two years ago to more than 80% today, according to Gillin. Cloudera is also adding agentic workflows across its data services. General-purpose agents are more of a consumer phenomenon, he explained.
“They’re more of an office worker tool, but the Cloudera agents are tuned to managing data,” Gillin said. “To managing workloads, optimizing GPU capacity, the types of things that really concern CIOs, because they’re paying the bills for these very high training costs.”
Simply having an agent is no longer an edge, so Cloudera is doubling down on its long-standing multiplatform play. It is extending the portability enterprises wanted from their clouds to their AI models, according to Gillin. Before trusting that pitch with AI automation, CIOs will want to know how agents are controlled, what audit trails they leave behind and how agent decisions can be documented for regulators, he noted.
“This is a very big issue with agents right now,” Gillin said. “It’s still a wild west out there with agents.”
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of EVOLVE26.

La sortie de l'iPhone Duo, le tout premier smartphone pliable d'Apple, n'est pas de tout repos pour la firme à la pomme. Outre des retours négatifs du côté logiciel et nos premiers retours mitigés (en attendant le test complet), un problème plus grave semble affecter plusieurs acquéreurs.
Comme d'autres produits technologiques un peu fragiles avant lui, l'iPhone Duo doit affronter une polémique en “gate”, à savoir le CrackGate. Ce nom a surgi d’un problème de charnière qui semble faire craquer l'un des écrans du terminal. Photos à l'appui, les premières plaintes ont eu lieu ce week-end, parfois quelques heures seulement après l'achat. Apple a fini par réagir ce lundi 26 octobre.
CrackGate de l'iPhone Duo : un problème matériel limité, selon Apple
À plusieurs médias étasuniens, la firme de Cupertino a déclaré que “les retours des premiers utilisateurs de l’iPhone Duo sont extrêmement positifs. Nous voyons émerger des initiatives très enthousiasmantes du côté des développeurs, qui mettent rapidement à jour leurs apps pour tirer parti de ce format singulier. Nous avons connaissance d’un problème affectant l’écran interne sur un petit nombre d’iPhone Duo. Si des utilisateurs rencontrent des soucis avec l’écran de leur iPhone Duo, ils doivent contacter AppleCare pour obtenir un remplacement.”
Si la firme de Cupertino indique bien être au fait du problème, il n'est en revanche pas question de s'étendre sur le sujet, et encore moins de lui donner une explication technique.
Il faudra pour le moment se contenter du conseil habituel de contacter AppleCare en cas de pépin pour un remplacement du produit, tandis qu'Apple tente de minimiser le nombre d'appareils concernés.
Malgré les différents témoignages, dont les clichés montrent des écrans abîmés généralement en bas de la dalle de droite, face à la charnière, il reste difficile aujourd'hui de savoir dans quelle mesure ce problème est réel et répandu. Certaines images peuvent être générées par l'IA pour susciter du buzz, tandis qu'il peut aussi s'agir de mauvaises manipulations de la part des utilisateurs.
L’expertise d'iFixit relance la piste du défaut de fabrication
Cependant, le spécialiste de la réparation iFixit a démonté l'appareil, y détectant plusieurs causes possibles à ce problème de charnière. Un défaut de fabrication sur un petit lot d'iPhone Duo, plutôt qu'un souci de conception général, n'est donc pas à écarter.
Avec un nombre croissant d'acheteurs d'iPhone Duo attendus dans les jours à venir, nous devrions rapidement être fixés concernant l'ampleur de la situation.

articles.title: AI isn’t replacing thinking; it’s changing where we need to think
articles.text:
AI isn’t replacing thinking; it’s changing where we need to think
AI’s value depends on data, governance and human judgement
One of AI’s biggest attractions is its ability to take time and effort out of everyday work. Tasks that would once have demanded hours of attention, such as turning meetings into notes or producing a first draft of a piece of content, can now be completed in minutes. These practical benefits help explain why AI has moved so quickly from experimentation into everyday business use.
Chief Strategy Officer at Qlik.
Yet, as AI becomes more established in the workplace, a more complicated picture is emerging. AI is changing where thinking happens. When a system can produce an answer almost instantly, the challenge shifts from creating the output to deciding what to do with it.
Employees are no longer spending as much time getting to a first answer, but they are spending more time checking whether the output is accurate, and critically, good enough to inform a decision. This creates a different kind of cognitive burden, moving from production to verification.
AI-generated outputs can appear remarkably polished and persuasive, even when they are based on incomplete information. An answer can sound convincing while overlooking a crucial piece of context or relying on incomplete information. And as AI becomes increasingly better at sounding confident, mistakes may look plausible enough to escape scrutiny and feed into business decisions without being challenged.
When confidence outpaces accuracy
This is why discernment is becoming one of the most important skills in the AI-enabled workplace. The future workforce needs the ability to apply context, experience and judgment to an output that appears authoritative. Someone who understands a market or process deeply may immediately notice that something does not add up, while another person may accept the same answer because it is presented clearly and confidently.
However, the problem is that individual discernment does not scale well, and it is unrealistic to expect every employee to catch every questionable output, especially as AI begins to support more decisions across a business. Human review is indeed essential, but relying on individual vigilance is not a robust or sustainable operating model.
The challenge clearly magnifies with the growth of agentic AI. When AI moves from suggesting to doing, the consequences of a wrong answer become more serious because the error can travel quickly into a real business process. That makes robust governance increasingly important as agentic AI becomes more embedded in how businesses operate.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Better inputs lead to better decisions
Many businesses are investing heavily in making data available to AI, but availability is not the same as readiness. This is where many AI projects begin to struggle. Organizations too often focus on the model because it is the most visible part of the technology, while overlooking the quality of the information beneath it.
The reality is that most organizations will soon have access to similarly capable models. Consequently, what will increasingly differentiate them is not the AI itself, but the quality of the data, governance and operational discipline that sit behind it.
Making data work for AI means ensuring that information is current, trusted and structured in a way that allows AI to generate outputs that reflect how the business actually operates. Without those foundations, organizations spend more time validating AI than benefiting from it.
Poor data pushes additional work back onto employees, who need to spend more time checking outputs and resolving inconsistencies - weakening any productivity case. And the data backs this up. Whilst 74% of frontline employees are now regular AI users, 41% of those report increased cognitive load alongside productivity gains.
Making governance part of everyday operations
This is also why AI governance needs to move beyond policies and principles. If organizations want AI to deliver business value, they need to answer a series of practical questions, such as: Who owns an AI-assisted decision? And where should human judgment remain in the loop?
As AI adoption grows, those questions will increasingly bring the CFO into the conversation. Finance leaders will be asked not only to control spending but also to demonstrate that AI investment is producing profitable value. That will ultimately require greater visibility into where AI is being used, how decisions are being made and whether the costs of validation, oversight and correction are being properly accounted for.
It will also mean recognizing that governance is becoming a lever for cost efficiency. When AI systems are grounded in well-structured, trusted enterprise data, they can find the right information more efficiently, potentially reducing token consumption while improving the quality and consistency of outputs. In other words, strong governance can help lower the cost of running AI tools at scale and improve the return on AI investment.
The competitive edge is still human judgement
As AI becomes a standard part of how businesses operate, simply having access to the technology will no longer be enough to stand out. Instead, the greater advantage will come from how organizations are able to bring together reliable data, strong governance and human judgment to make better decisions.
AI can accelerate the route to an answer, but it cannot decide how much weight that answer should carry. That responsibility still belongs to people, supported by the right data, governance and decision frameworks.

articles.title: Siete días metiéndose en agua a 14 °C: lo que de verdad dice (y lo que no) el último estudio del “cold plunge”
articles.text:
La inmersión en agua fría era algo que parecía reservado para deportistas que necesitaban tener una buena recuperación física tras un esfuerzo considerable, como ocurre, por ejemplo, en futbolistas. Pero esto es algo que ha pasado a convertirse en un ritual para cualquier persona con el objetivo de mantener los tejidos sanos y sobre todo jóvenes. Aunque la pregunta que de verdad nos debemos hacer es: ¿sirve para algo estar bajo agua fría durante mucho tiempo?
Un estudio publicado en la revista Advanced Biology hace unos años quiso responder a esta pregunta, reclutando a 10 chicos jóvenes de unos 23 años y físicamente activos. Con esta muestra, comenzaron a sumergirlos en agua fría para analizar qué ocurría en sus células mononucleares que viajan por todo su organismo. El problema es que no hubo ningún tipo de grupo control para poder hacer una comparativa real.
Aquí lo que se buscaba era observar la batalla que había entre dos procesos celulares que son fundamentales, como son la apoptosis, es decir, la muerte celular programada, y la autofagia, que es el sistema de reciclaje y limpieza de nuestro cuerpo.
Los resultados mostraron que la aclimatación es real, pero no inmediata, ya que en los primeros cuatro días el cuerpo sufre por estar bajo una temperatura mínima. Y sufría porque se detectaron signos de una autofagia que no estaba funcionando correctamente y también se vio un aumento de la caspasa-3 escindida, que es un marcador que nos habla de que las células están muriendo por estrés.
Sin embargo, el día 7 todo cambió, puesto que las células aprendieron a defenderse. De esta manera, el sistema de limpieza fue más eficiente y la destrucción celular volvió a sus niveles basales. En cuanto a la inflamación si que hubo un poco de decepción, puesto que los marcadores clásicos como la interleucina-6 no variaron mucho entre estar fuera de un baño de agua fría o dentro. Es por ello que la conclusión a la que llegaron fue que la exposición repetida al frío solo mejoraba la tolerancia celular a bajas temperaturas.
La fuente de la juventud todavía parece estar dentro de los libros más fantasiosos porque aún no la hemos encontrado. Este estudio no llegó tan lejos, y solo podemos sustentarnos en las declaraciones de una de las autoras que extrapoló los resultados a una supuesta prevención del envejecimiento celular, aunque en ningún momento se midió alguna de las variables que nos hablaran de esto.
Lo que sí sabemos. Pero si nos salimos de la necesidad de ser prácticamente eternos, sí que encontramos beneficios para poder darse un baño de hielo. Uno de los más evidentes nos lo da una revisión publicada este mismo año que confirma que sumergirse en hielo ayuda con la recuperación rápida, reduciendo las agujetas. El problema es que, si se usa este sistema de manera constante después de entrenar, se está perjudicando a las ganancias de fuerza y también al crecimiento muscular.
Si pensamos en los beneficios psicológicos, la verdad es que a día de hoy no hay evidencia que nos permita afirmar que el agua fría mejore el estado de ánimo o reduzca el estrés, puesto que muchos de los estudios que hay tienen un sesgo muy elevado.
El verdadero peligro. Más allá de que los beneficios antienvejecimiento no estén contrastados, meterse en agua helada no es un juego inofensivo. Aquí hay que tener en cuenta que, en el momento de tocar el agua helada, el cuerpo responde con una hiperventilación y una taquicardia que busca compensar la disminución de la temperatura corporal. Un efecto que es conocido como 'cold shock response'.
Y esto es un problema, puesto que hablamos de un riesgo cardiovascular importante que puede llevar a la muerte en el caso de darse estos baños en aguas abiertas o sin supervisión.

articles.title: Microsoft lanza un parche de emergencia por una falla crítica en Brotli que afecta a .NET
articles.text:
Microsoft publicó un parche de seguridad de emergencia para corregir una vulnerabilidad crítica en Brotli que afecta a .NET 8, .NET 9, .NET 10 y .NET 11 Release Candidate 3. La compañía emitió la actualización fuera de su calendario habitual, un domingo, después de confirmar que el fallo puede permitir la lectura o corrupción de memoria dentro de un proceso.
La corrección importa para desarrolladores, empresas y administradores de sistemas que utilizan aplicaciones .NET en Windows, Mac y Linux. La vulnerabilidad, identificada como CVE-2026-111497, está vinculada al procesamiento de datos comprimidos con Brotli, un algoritmo creado por Google y utilizado para reducir el tamaño de archivos que circulan por internet.
El fallo puede provocar filtraciones, bloqueos y ejecución de código
Rahul Bhandari, gerente sénior de programas de Microsoft .NET, confirmó que la vulnerabilidad fue descubierta el 22 de octubre y que corresponde a un desbordamiento de búfer. Este tipo de error ocurre cuando un programa intenta almacenar más información de la que puede manejar un área de memoria determinada.
Según la advertencia difundida por Microsoft, un atacante no autenticado podría leer o corromper la memoria de un proceso afectado. Las consecuencias potenciales incluyen divulgación de información, denegación de servicio y escalada de privilegios.
La falla también podría permitir la ejecución de código arbitrario mediante un flujo comprimido con Brotli manipulado. Esto significa que un actor malicioso podría intentar aprovechar datos especialmente preparados para alterar el comportamiento de una aplicación vulnerable.
El Centro de Respuesta de Seguridad de Microsoft clasificó el problema como crítico. Aunque la vulnerabilidad ya fue divulgada públicamente, la empresa indicó que no tiene pruebas de explotación activa. Sin embargo, su análisis de riesgo considera que la explotación es “más probable”.
Brotli permite comprimir datos sin perder información
Brotli es un algoritmo de compresión sin pérdida desarrollado por Google en 2015. Su función consiste en reducir el tamaño de datos como texto, código o imágenes sin modificar su contenido original. De esta manera, los archivos pueden trasladarse con mayor rapidez por internet.
El sistema utiliza un diccionario interno de palabras, frases y elementos de código. En lugar de repetir una secuencia completa de caracteres, puede reemplazarla por una referencia más corta que permite reconstruirla al descomprimir el archivo.
También identifica repeticiones dentro del contenido comprimido. Si una frase o bloque de información vuelve a aparecer, Brotli puede sustituirlo por una referencia en vez de enviarlo de nuevo completo. Esta lógica permite ahorrar espacio y mejorar la transferencia de datos.
Brotli puede ser cerca de un 20% más eficiente que sistemas de compresión anteriores, como Gzip. Esa ventaja explica su presencia en aplicaciones, servicios web y herramientas que necesitan procesar grandes volúmenes de información.
Las aplicaciones ASP.NET Core y HttpClient pueden estar expuestas
Microsoft advirtió que las aplicaciones pueden verse afectadas si procesan datos comprimidos con Brotli en varios escenarios. Entre ellos se encuentra la descompresión de solicitudes en ASP.NET Core, la descompresión automática de respuestas mediante HttpClient y el uso de las interfaces de Brotli incluidas en System.IO.Compression.
El riesgo aparece cuando una aplicación recibe y descomprime contenido manipulado. Por ello, la recomendación de la compañía es instalar las actualizaciones disponibles lo antes posible en todos los entornos afectados.
La medida alcanza a proyectos en desarrollo, servidores de producción y equipos que ejecuten versiones vulnerables de .NET. En organizaciones con múltiples aplicaciones, la revisión debe incluir tanto los sistemas expuestos a internet como los servicios internos que procesen archivos o respuestas comprimidas.
Microsoft también corrigió un fallo en Authenticator para Android
La actualización de .NET coincide con otra corrección de seguridad reciente de Microsoft. La empresa publicó un parche para una vulnerabilidad en Microsoft Authenticator para Android que podía permitir que una aplicación maliciosa instalada en el mismo teléfono obtuviera tokens de acceso de una cuenta laboral.
El fallo, identificado como CVE-2026-80097, afectaba versiones anteriores a la 6.2606.4246. Para aprovecharlo, una aplicación dañina debía estar instalada previamente en el dispositivo, por ejemplo, tras una descarga desde una fuente no confiable.
En el caso de Brotli, la prioridad es actualizar los entornos .NET afectados. En el de Authenticator, los usuarios deben comprobar la versión instalada desde Google Play Store y evitar aplicaciones descargadas fuera de tiendas oficiales.

articles.title: Qualcomm Snapdragon X Series to Power Anduril's US-Made "BlueChip" Laptops
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Qualcomm Snapdragon X Series to Power Anduril's US-Made "BlueChip" Laptops
Anduril Industries and Qualcomm have announced the "BlueChip" laptops that will be manufactured in the United States. That's the stated goal of Anduril, the company founded by Palmer Luckey, the creator of Oculus VR. He says that around 90% of the first laptop's components will come from the United States or allied countries. The first "BlueChip" laptops will use the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Series chips that are manufactured at TSMC's newest Arizona facility. The processor is the same you can find in other Snapdragon-powered laptops like the Microsoft Surface. Moving further, Anduril intends to assemble circuit boards at its Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio. The company, however, has plans to extend beyond just the final assembly. In the meantime, it will develop US production capabilities for enclosures, battery components, and other hardware components. 
Functional prototypes are ready, with preorders planned for 2027, but exact specifications and pricing remain undisclosed. Palmer Luckey, however, estimates that it will cost roughly 20% more than typical high-end consumer PCs. Keep in mind that the "BlueChip" laptops are mainly designed for security, government, and military use scenarios. That means you will not find them on your usual PC retail store shelves. At least not the first generations. According to TechCrunch, Luckey stated his intention that, in the future, Anduril will produce U.S.-made consumer-oriented laptops.

articles.title: SFR augmente encore ses tarifs : vous risquez de payer jusqu’à 5 € de plus par mois
articles.text:
Nous vous en parlions début octobre, SFR, RED et Prixtel ont décidé d’augmenter certains de leurs forfaits. Peu de temps après, des abonnés de SFR ont bel et bien rapporté une augmentation de prix de 1,49 € à presque 5 €, en fonction de l’abonnement en cours. Le plus dur serait passé pour les clients de SFR ? Il semble que non. Selon AlloForfait, l’opérateur annonce à certains de ses clients, chez SFR, RED by SFR ou Prixtel, de nouvelles augmentations de prix.
De nouvelles augmentations de prix pour les abonnés SFR
Une nouvelle fois, les hausses peuvent aller de 1 euro à 5 euros par mois. Les forfaits mobiles et Internet sont concernés. Par conséquent, la peine peut être double. Une famille peut voir son abonnement Internet augmenter, tout comme ses forfaits mobiles. Un utilisateur du réseau social X fait par exemple état d’une augmentation de 15 euros « en 2 mois pour une box et 3 mobiles ».
Les hausses atteindraient 4,99 euros par mois pour la box et 3,99 euros par mois pour certains forfaits mobiles. Ces augmentations, cumulées au sein d’une famille, peuvent donc sensiblement alourdir la facture globale d’un foyer. Si l’on considère une augmentation totale de 20 euros par mois pour un forfait fixe et trois forfaits mobiles, la facture annuelle d’un foyer augmente donc de 240 €. À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, nous ne pouvons pas dire combien d’abonnés SFR sont concernés, ni lister les offres touchées par ces augmentations de prix.
Comme le souligne BFMTV, SFR pourrait vouloir augmenter ses tarifs avant son rachat, les régulateurs étant susceptibles de limiter les hausses de prix une fois l’opération finalisée.
Il est possible de résilier son abonnement SFR sans frais
Si vous ne consentez pas à une hausse de prix, il est possible de résilier son abonnement en cours sans frais et sans pénalité, grâce à l’article L.224-33 du Code de la consommation. Comme l’opérateur l’explique lui-même : « vous avez la possibilité de résilier votre contrat sans frais et sans pénalité si vous n’acceptez pas ces nouvelles conditions contractuelles. Cette résiliation peut être effectuée dans un délai de 4 mois à compter du présent courriel ». Les personnes concernées disposent donc de 4 mois à partir de la réception du courrier les informant d’une hausse de prix.
SFR précise par ailleurs qu’il existe trois façons de résilier un abonnement concerné par une hausse de prix : par courrier (en indiquant que vous refusez cette modification contractuelle), depuis votre espace client en ligne (en indiquant le motif suivant : « Refus des modifications contractuelles/Motifs légitimes ») et, enfin, en cas de changement d’opérateur avec portabilité du numéro.

articles.title: ANYbotics begins delivery of legged inspection robot built for explosive atmospheres - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ANYbotics begins delivery of legged inspection robot built for explosive atmospheres
ANYbotics AG, a leading provider of four-legged inspection robots for heavy industry, today announced it’s shipping the world’s first legged robot designed to operate in dangerous environments where a spark or fire could trigger an explosion.
The new robot, named ANYmal X, is a dog-like robot that can patrol and inspect equipment where specialist technicians otherwise move between heavy equipment wearing dampened gear and avoid situations that might trigger an explosion.
The platform is now shipping to several oil, gas and chemical industry leaders, including multinational energy company Equinor ASA and Swiss-Dutch specialty chemical company DSM-Firmenich AG.
“Four years of pioneering engineering with more than ten patents went into ANYmal X,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Péter Fankhauser. “Many experts thought a legged robot could never be made safe for explosive atmospheres. Oil, gas and chemical plants are among the most hazardous and most costly places to operate.”
Energy and chemical industry leaders BP p.l.c., Equinor, Shell plc, Petroliam Nasional Berhad, Petróleo Brasileiro S.A., BASF SE and SLB N.V. began testing the ANYmal robots in 2023 across hundreds of onshore and offshore facilities through ANYbotics early access program. They used the data and knowledge from their participation to refine the platform into the industrial-grade robot being shipped today.
Making a legged robot safe around flammable gases is not simply a matter of giving it a tougher shell. It means controlling potential ignition sources throughout the machine so its electrical components and hot surfaces cannot set off the surrounding atmosphere.
Legged robots are made up of complex components, which must be isolated from the atmosphere. As a result, they are banned from oil, gas and chemical refineries and other hazardous atmospheres where explosions can happen. In these environments, preventable downtime can translate into massive profit losses.
Autonomous inspection robots target a growing industrial market, with research firms estimating global oil-and-gas inspection robotics revenue at roughly $800 million to $1 billion annually, according to Fortune Business Insights. The broader opportunity includes chemical plants and spending on conventional inspection services, although published estimates do not consistently isolate that combined market.
Undetected equipment failures can cost companies roughly $1.4 trillion each year in downtime, according to ANYbotics. In the oil and gas sector alone, Siemens AG reported a single hour can translate to almost $500,000 and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health reported that historically extraction workers in the United States face dangerous conditions, creating fatality rates seven times the national average.
Robots to go where no human should
“We asked one question over and over: Which credible event in the life of a walking robot could create an ignition source, and how do we make sure it never does?” said Chief Technology Officer Andrea Corda.
Companies make fixed equipment compliant by housing it in heavy, explosion-proof enclosures, with limited exposure to the outside environment. Legged robots are a completely different endeavor, with exposed cameras and sensors required for navigation and ports needed for docking. Every component must be certified explosion-proof so it won’t ignite a spark, or, if it does, it will prevent heat sources or combustion from spreading to outside environments — all while maintaining payload capacity, agility and operating speed.
The company said it engineered ANYmal X from the ground up to comply with oil, gas and chemical industry safety standards. ANYbotics performed comprehensive ignition risk assessments and implemented safeguards for every potential ignition source.
“Today, more than 50 power, metals and materials customers use this system to run over 120,000 autonomous inspections every month,” said Chief Revenue Officer Thierry Obédé.

articles.title: iPhone 18e deve manter tela de 60 Hz mesmo com novo chip • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone 18e deve manter tela de 60 Hz mesmo com novo chip
Celular de entrada da Apple é esperado com chip A20 de 2 nanômetros. Modelo deve trazer avanços em câmera frontal e desempenho.
Novos rumores apontam que o iPhone 18e pode ganhar melhorias importantes em desempenho e na câmera frontal. Ao mesmo tempo, continuaria com uma tela de 60 Hz, mantendo a limitação da série “de entrada” da Apple.
As informações foram divulgadas nesta terça-feira (27/10) pelo conhecido leaker chinês Digital Chat Station. O iPhone 18e é esperado para o primeiro semestre de 2027, quando deve ser apresentado ao lado do iPhone 18 e do iPhone Air 2.
A principal mudança prevista para o novo celular é o processador, que acompanharia o chip do iPhone 18 convencional, o Apple A20.
Assim como a versão Pro, presente nos topo de linha lançados neste ano, o componente deve ser fabricado em um processo de 2 nanômetros, contra os 3 nm do A19 do iPhone 17e. Essa mudança, vale lembrar, tende a permitir ganhos de desempenho e eficiência energética.
Outro avanço pode aparecer na câmera frontal. O vazamento menciona um novo sensor de 24 megapixels, contra 12 MP no iPhone 17e, mas continuaria com uma única câmera de 48 MP.
A tela, por outro lado, deve permanecer praticamente igual. Segundo o leaker, o aparelho terá um painel OLED LTPS de 6,12 polegadas de 60 Hz, seguindo as especificações das últimas gerações. Até celulares mais baratos, como o Galaxy A37, que pode ser encontrado por volta de R$ 1.700, tem tela em frequência superior.
Além dos vazamentos do Digital Chat Station, rumores também indicam um leve aumento na quantidade de memória RAM, de 8 GB para 9 GB, segundo o MacRumors. Mesmo com o avanço, o aparelho ficaria abaixo dos 12 GB que algumas funções mais avançadas da Apple Intelligence exigem.
Memória, aliás, é um assunto delicado na situação atual do mercado. Com a alta nos preços dos componentes, não se espera um grande avanço nesse sentido em aparelhos que tentam ser mais baratos.
Independentemente, analistas estimam que o iPhone 18 e 18e fiquem de US$ 100 a US$ 200 mais caros nos Estados Unidos. No Brasil, a linha iPhone 18 Pro teve alta de R$ 500 nas versões mais básicas. O iPhone 17e foi lançado no Brasil por R$ 5.799, com 256 GB de armazenamento, mesmo valor inicial cobrado pela geração anterior no país.

articles.title: GPT, Claude et Gemini dans une seule app : 1min.AI Pro à vie à 23€ en ce moment (-89 %)
articles.text:
Passer d’un assistant à l’autre selon la tâche finit par coûter plusieurs abonnements mensuels, alors que les modèles d’OpenAI, d’Anthropic et de Google sont aussi accessibles depuis des plateformes tierces. Le plan Pro de 1min.AI s’affiche à 24,97 $ à vie chez StackSocial, un paiement unique pour un service que notre test réservait plutôt à un usage ponctuel.
1min.AI réunit dans une même interface des modèles d’OpenAI, d’Anthropic et de Google, mais aussi de Mistral, DeepSeek ou xAI, avec des outils d’image, d’audio et de vidéo. Le service fonctionne par crédits, sans abonnement à chaque modèle. Chez StackSocial, le plan Pro de 1min.AI en accès à vie passe à 24,97 $ au lieu de 234 $, soit 89 % de remise, avec 1 000 000 de crédits rechargés chaque mois.
Le prix est affiché en dollars : le montant débité en euros dépend du taux de change. L’offre vise surtout ceux qui veulent plusieurs IA sous la main sans multiplier les comptes, moins ceux qui vivent dans un seul assistant.
Le plan Pro de 1min.AI passe à 24,97 $ au lieu de 234 $ chez StackSocial, en paiement unique pour un accès à vie et 1 000 000 de crédits par mois.
Pourquoi choisir le plan Pro de 1min.AI ?
- Plusieurs familles de modèles : GPT, Claude et Gemini cohabitent avec Mistral, DeepSeek ou Grok. Vous choisissez le modèle selon la tâche, sans changer d’application ni de compte.
- Des réponses à confronter : la fonction Multi AI Chat envoie la même requête à plusieurs modèles à la fois. Pratique pour comparer deux rédactions ou repérer une réponse qui diverge des autres.
- Un coût annoncé avant chaque requête : la plateforme estime les crédits consommés avant l’envoi. Vous savez ce qu’une image ou l’analyse d’un document va retirer de votre quota mensuel.
Rédiger, résumer, illustrer : où partent les crédits
Le million de crédits mensuels se partage entre tous les outils, du chat à la retouche d’images en passant par la transcription audio ou la discussion avec un PDF. Le texte en consomme peu, l’image et la vidéo beaucoup plus : ce volume correspond à environ 161 images ou 12 vidéos générées. 1min.AI ajoute 15 000 crédits chaque jour où vous ouvrez l’application web, soit jusqu’à 450 000 de plus par mois. Le service existe sur le web, en extension Chrome, sur iPhone, Android, Mac et Windows.
Ce fonctionnement convient à qui rédige, résume ou traduit régulièrement et veut garder plusieurs modèles sous la main pour comparer. Dans notre test de 1min.AI, nous lui avions attribué 7/10, en saluant une interface moderne et l’étendue des outils, mais en relevant l’absence de mémoire entre les conversations et l’arrivée tardive des modèles les plus récents. Nous le jugions plus adapté à un usage ponctuel ou de secours qu’à un outil de travail principal.
Face aux abonnements de ChatGPT, Claude et Gemini
1min.AI ne remplace pas un abonnement souscrit directement chez OpenAI, Anthropic ou Google : il passe par sa propre interface et par un quota de crédits. Les fonctions propres à chaque assistant, comme les projets ou la recherche web intégrée, restent du côté des offres natives. En échange, vous passez d’un modèle à l’autre sans multiplier les comptes. Pour savoir quel assistant mérite un abonnement à lui seul, notre comparatif des meilleures intelligences artificielles classe ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Mistral et Gemini.
✅ Les points forts
- Modèles d’OpenAI, d’Anthropic, de Google et d’autres éditeurs dans une seule interface
- Paiement unique, sans renouvellement
- 1 000 000 de crédits par mois, plus 15 000 par jour de connexion
- Coût en crédits affiché avant chaque requête
- Applications web, mobiles et de bureau
❌ Les limites
- Prix en dollars, montant en euros soumis au taux de change
- Pas de mémoire entre les conversations lors de notre test
- Crédits vite consommés par l’image et la vidéo
- Données conservées jusqu’à un an, à éviter pour les contenus sensibles
La licence 1min.AI Pro à 24,97 $ s’active dans les 30 jours suivant l’achat, et StackSocial accepte son retour contre un avoir tant qu’elle n’est pas activée.
À 24,97 $, le plan Pro de 1min.AI retrouve une remise que StackSocial lui applique régulièrement : nous l’avons relayé entre 21 et 27 € ces derniers mois. Le prix de 234 $ affiché en référence par StackSocial sert surtout de point de comparaison : l’éditeur facture lui-même ce plan 6,50 dollars par mois en formule mensuelle. Pour interroger GPT, Claude et Gemini depuis une même application, avec un quota confortable pour du texte, le paiement unique reste modeste.
L’offre s’adresse à ceux qui veulent tester plusieurs modèles, comparer leurs réponses ou garder une solution de repli quand leur assistant habituel flanche. Si vous travaillez chaque jour avec un seul assistant et tenez à sa mémoire ou à ses projets, l’abonnement natif vous servira mieux. Même réserve pour les documents confidentiels, vu la durée de conservation des données. Pour un usage d’appoint, en revanche, le million de crédits mensuels laisse de la marge.

articles.title: Logitech Yeti 2 is one of the best mics for streaming I've ever used – it's just a shame about the higher price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Logitech Yeti 2 is one of the best consumer desktop mics on the market, with improved sound quality and a fistful of thoughtful additions that should put it near the top of your list.
Reasons to buy
- + Exceptional audio quality
- + Solid build quality
- + Automatically adjusts the polar pattern as needed
- + Auto-gain is a useful extra
Reasons to avoid
- - All-in-one dial can be a bit finicky
- - More expensive than the original Yeti
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Logitech Yeti 2 two-minute review
It’s been 17 years since Blue launched the original Yeti, and it didn’t take long for it to become fan a favorite in the world of consumer desktop mics. There have been tweaks and touch-ups here and there, but few major changes, even after Logitech bought Blue in 2018. Until now, that is.
I’ve been using the first Yeti for years, so I was intrigued to know how the new model compared. The good news is that while there’s plenty to love about the original Yeti — it became a household name for a reason, after all — the Yeti 2 is even more impressive. It’s one of the best microphones for streaming available right now.
Put the two microphones on a desk together and you’ll see that the Yeti 2 is very slightly more compact, yet it still retains the distinctive Yeti aesthetic. More noticeable when you pick them up is the weight — at 995g (2.19lbs), the Yeti 2 is almost 50% lighter than the 1.4kg (3.09lbs) Yeti.
Another thing that immediately catches your eye is the Yeti 2’s built-in LED display, which sits above a singular dial that can be pushed in like a button. This display is a new addition and, in combination with the dial, essentially replaces the volume, mute, gain and polar pattern controls on the old Yeti.
This lets you change the mic’s settings and monitor its audio levels on the display, all without needing Logitech’s G Hub app. It’s a handy feature if you want to make quick adjustments on the fly, although we found the push-in dial to be a little finicky at times, where pressing it would occasionally not do anything. Still, it’s useful for quick changes if you don’t fancy diving into the G Hub app.
If you do want to do that, though, there are plenty of audio presets to choose from, including those for interviews, singing, speech to text, different instruments, and more. You can make manual adjustments to equalizer levels, enable the gate, compressor and more, and work through input gain settings, then save your settings to the app or one of five on-board profiles. Those profiles can be set to automatically activate when specific games launch, too.
That said, G Hub is probably not the most in-depth experience you’re likely to find. For beginners, though, switching polar patterns and adjusting the built-in noise cancelation is about all you’ll need.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The most important part of any microphone, of course, is its audio quality. And here, the Yeti 2 really delivers. Compared to my long-serving Yeti, the Yeti 2 sounded much crisper and clearer. The Yeti was by no means bad, but the latest model shows strong signs of improvement, no doubt helped by the improvement from 16-bit to 24-bit audio and the addition of software noise cancelation.
Part of that is thanks to the new Auto Tracking polar pattern that detects where your sound is coming from and automatically adjusts the pickup area accordingly, ensuring the input is optimized, wherever you’re sat. You can still set a manual polar pattern if you like, but Auto Tracking is effective enough that it will be the best option for most people.
Another useful aspect of this voice proximity sensor is its impact on gain. Now, the Yeti 2 can automatically decrease or increase the gain as you move closer to or further away from the mic, ensuring your input volume remains level throughout. This feature isn’t perfect — I noticed my voice picked up more echo the as I moved away — but it’s much better than what you got with the first Yeti, where you’d just get quieter as you moved away.
As you’d expect from Blue/Logitech, the Yeti 2’s build quality is top notch. The main body is made of metal and feels rock solid. The included metal stand has a soft padded base to keep it from slipping, while the lugs that hold the mic screwed into the base are rubberized to minimize bumps and shakes while you’re recording. This thing looks beautiful and feels like it’s made to last.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
There’s a thread on the bottom for attaching the Yeti 2 to a boom arm, in case you’d rather use it that way instead of upright in its stand. The display can also be flipped 180 degrees, which makes reading it an awful lot easier when it’s mounted this way.
There’s not a lot to dislike about the Yeti 2. The single push-in dial didn’t seem to be the most reliable feature and merging several buttons into one means it takes a little longer to scroll through the settings than dedicated dials would. We’re also disappointed to see the price has increased versus the original Yeti. But that’s all blown away compared to thing you care about most with a microphone — namely, its audio quality — which is as good as it gets in a consumer mic.
Logitech Yeti 2 review: Price & release date
- Available to buy now
- Priced at $159.99 / £139.99 / $249.95 AUD
The Logitech Yeti 2 is available now from Logitech’s website or from third-party retailers. It’s priced at $159.99 / £139.99 / $249.95 AUD.
It’s more expensive than the original Yeti, which was most recently sold for $139.99 (and is currently on sale for $109.99 on Logitech’s website), but the Yeti 2 is not unreasonably expensive. It also offers an awful lot for the price.
Logitech Yeti 2 review: Specs
| Polar patterns | Auto Tracking, stereo, cardioid, figure8, omni, hypercardioid, supercardioid, custom | 
| Frequency range | 20Hz – 20kHz | 
| Connectivity | USB-C | 
| Audio bit rate | 24-bit | 
| Sample rate | 48kHz | 
Should I buy the Logitech Yeti 2?
| Logitech Yeti 2 scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | The clever new LED display makes adjusting settings quick and easy | 5/5 | 
| Performance | Pitch-perfect audio makes this the consumer mic to beat | 5/5 | 
| Design | The Yeti 2 looks sleek and understated while being built to last | 5/5 | 
| Value | The slight cost increase is disappointing, but it’s still fairly priced | 4/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want a plug-and-play mic
The auto-gain and automatic polar pattern tracking features make managing your voice easier than ever.
You want something that’s built to last
This is no cheap plastic affair — the Yeti 2 is almost all-metal, and it feels like it could take a beating and keep on trucking.
You don’t want to break the bank
Sure, the price has gone up, but the Yeti 2 remains in the consumer price bracket without venturing into pro territory.
Don’t buy it if…
You want a professional mic
There’s no XLR connectivity and other options have more studio-appropriate features.
You want dedicated controls
Everything is combined into a single dial, which might mean it takes a little longer to adjust your settings.
You’re on a tight budget
With the price creeping upwards, this isn’t the cheapest microphone on the market.
Also consider
Elgato Wave:3
A serious contender for the title of best streaming mic around, the Elgato Wave:3 sounds just as good as it looks. It only has one polar pattern, but with audio quality as impressive as this, that might not matter.
Razer Seiren V3 Pro
Razer’s Seiren V3 Pro is aiming high with its inclusion of 32-bit float and XLR connectivity. It’s fairly pricey, but offers a lot of bang for your buck.
How I tested the Logitech Yeti 2
- I tested the mic’s performance during games and on calls with friends. I also made test recordings and compared it to the original Yeti
- I also spent time putting the microphone’s software features through their paces in the Razer G Hub app
I spent a week testing the microphone on my PC. I called friends to test its performance during gaming sessions and made audio recordings where I directly compared its audio quality with that of the original Yeti mic.

As well as TechRadar, Alex writes for iMore, Digital Trends and Creative Bloq, among others. He was previously commissioning editor at MacFormat magazine.
