articles.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
articles.text:
Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro. Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago.
The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage.
There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM, but can go to 4TB of storage.
It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers.

articles.title: Here's everything new with Apple's iOS 27.2
articles.text:
Recently, Apple launched the iOS 27.2 update with a bunch of new features. To update, check your Settings > General > Software Update.
Firstly, Siri AI is getting two big updates, one of which is great for French Canadians. Siri AI is now available in beta in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. Though it doesn’t specifically mention Canadian French, you’ll see ‘Ma copine’, not ‘Ma blonde.’
Siri AI can recall past conversations now, so you can ask Siri about something you told it before. It can also draw information from more sources, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, and even your voicemails. That’s right, voicemails! You can now say “Hey Siri, summarize my last voicemail.” However, it’s not entirely clear how Siri can access voicemails, so we’ve asked Apple about it and will update this post when we know more.
Suggestions in Messages let you take actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from conversations.
FaceTime now supports adding a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call. Plus, you can use Dual Capture to stream both your front and rear cameras during FaceTime calls.
Shared Albums in Photos now lets users edit captions and comments to help avoid duplicate photos and can show a reminder before an album expires.
Multiview is coming to iOS, so you can now watch up to four live sports streams at the same time, and it works with events that come to Apple TV.
And Apple TV profiles are coming to iOS, iPadOS and the web. So you can now set up unique profiles for family and friends who don’t have an Apple account; they have their own tailored experience, and you can manage content ratings for kids.
For iPhone Duo owners, the Apple Pencil (USB-C) now supports iPhone Duo. The Edge Light video effect is also coming to the Duo, so it’ll illuminate your face like a ring light when you’re on a video call.

articles.title: 'Ali G: Who I Iz?' is coming to Prime Video just days after debuting in theaters —and the new Amazon movie will set an unwanted record when it's available to stream
articles.text:
Ali G: Who I Iz? makes Prime Video history as new Amazon comedy movie starring Sacha Baron Cohen lands streaming release date less than a week after theatrical debut
Ali G: Who I Iz? is about to set to a major — and likely unwanted — new record on Prime Video.
The comedy flick, which sees Sacha Baron Cohen reprise his role as the infamous character, will make its debut on Amazon's streaming platform on Wednesday, October 28.
Why is that such a big deal? Because Who I Iz? was only released in cinemas on Friday, October 23. As such, it'll be the first film in history to make its streaming debut less than a week after its initial theatrical launch when it drops on one of the world's best streaming services.
Amazon hasn't explained why Who I Iz? will make its premium video on demand (PVOD) so soon after landing in theaters. In fact, the only individual who's commented on the imminent Prime Video arrival of one of 2026's many new movies is Cohen himself, with the comedian taking to Ali G's various social channels to announce the news.
I've reached out to Amazon for an official comment on this unprecedented release date decision, but nobody had responded by the time of publication. If I receive a reply, I'll update this article.
Ali G: Who I Iz? marks the first time in almost 20 years that Cohen has portrayed the titular character, with Cohen having retired his most famous creation in 2007.
Defending the decision to bring back the controversial character in a Time magazine essay, Cohen wrote: "Why does my new movie bring back that phony and unfunny guy, which some have criticized as 'microwaving a relic from a generation ago'?

"The fact that Ali G is outdated and problematic is the very reason I resurrected him. The world he’s returned to is, in many ways, worse than the one he left 20 years ago. All the prejudices my characters are designed to expose haven’t just lingered — they’ve metastasized... Twenty years ago, Ali G would sit next to world experts spouting absurdities. Today — fed a steady diet of disinformation and conspiracy theories by social media influencers and TikTok news — we have created an entire world where ignorance reigns and truth is inverted.
"I made this latest film for the same reason I’ve always done this work," he added. "Not only to make people laugh, but also to bring them face-to-face with the danger of fanaticism and conspiracy theories."

articles.title: AI success depends on business outcomes, not usage vanity metrics
articles.text:
AI success depends on business outcomes, not usage vanity metrics
Tokenmaxxing leaderboards miss the mark
Imagine a NASCAR team where leadership decides the winner is the car that burns the most fuel. The crew chief tunes every engine to run rich and wasteful. Drivers ride the gas and the brake at once. The telemetry shows record fuel consumption. The car finishes dead last.
For a stretch this year, wasteful consumption metrics drove AI measurement programs. Companies stood up internal leaderboards ranking employees by how many tokens they burned. A Meta employee built one, crowned the top "token legends," then quietly took it after the numbers leaked externally. By spring the trend had a name: tokenmaxxing.
By the start of summer the inevitable backlash arrived, with companies like Uber acknowledging they’d already spent their entire AI budget for the year in a matter of months.
CTO, ActivTrak.
More recently, the inevitable swing toward using the minimal number of AI tokens (tokenminning) leads to the same problem. If leadership defines winning as using the least amount of fuel, the winning car would never leave the starting line.
Burning or saving tokens should never be the end goal. The objective is shipping more products, at higher quality, with the same or fewer people. The job of a leader is to define the most strategic path toward the finish line, and based on that definition, build metrics that support it.
Why leaderboards miss the mark
A vanity metric is any number that looks great on a slide, leaderboard or dashboard but doesn't change how you run your business. In the AI space, even highly technical and complex metrics can become vanity metrics.
Here’s a couple I’ve seen lately, each a different way to look busy GPU utilization rates that brag about how much raw compute you’ve hoarded, regardless of whether it's solving real problems. AI features shipped per quarter, where leadership slaps a sparkle-emoji text summarizer on every legacy product to pad the release notes.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Metrics like these can feel rigorous, but they're detached from the end work itself. When leaders don’t relate metrics to end goals, engineers may race toward the nearest countable item.
The missing race map
Work completed only matters if it’s the right work. When leadership celebrates "95% adoption" of GitHub Copilot because the licenses are deployed, they can mistake superficial access for deep engagement. They assume productivity is skyrocketing. They're measuring who adopted the tool, not who is effectively using it to improve outcomes.
Developers might be generating more code faster, but if the tool isn't deeply integrated into a refined process, PR sizes inflate and the bottleneck simply shifts to human code review. Cycle time stays stagnant, or worse, bug rates go up because humans are rubber-stamping AI hallucinations.
Close the disconnect: tie depth of use directly to outcomes and business goals. If you have 95% "adoption" but your cycle time hasn't dropped by 30% or your rework hasn't decreased, you don't have high use. You just have an expensive new software distribution.
How to set the finish line
A single number rarely tells a story. If I can produce twice as much code but it takes twice as long to ship, I haven't gained efficiency. I've created more work. The right question isn't how much AI you're using — it's whether the work is actually getting better.
For engineering teams with more established workflows, start with the outcome you want to move, then use a framework like DORA or SPACE to check whether you got there. The framework is the instrument, not the goal. DORA tracks the health of your delivery pipeline — how often you deploy, how long changes take, how quickly you recover from failures, how often changes cause incidents.
SPACE tracks the full picture of developer productivity across five dimensions, including outcomes and satisfaction. Neither was designed for AI, which is exactly why they're useful: they’ll help you measure whether AI made the work better, not whether AI got used.
Pair one of those frameworks against your AI tool usage and your business outcomes like cycle time, rework rate, cost per change. A 25% increase in AI adoption that correlates with a drop in delivery stability isn't a win. The 2025 DORA report found that's exactly what many teams got when they deployed AI into underprepared systems. The tools amplified what was already there. Good engineering foundations got better, fragile ones got more fragile.
For roles outside engineering — marketing, finance, operations — build from first principles. Start with one outcome you're already trying to move: response time, pipeline conversion, forecast accuracy. Establish the finish line before AI enters the workflow. Measure toward that same outcome after. If it moved, figure out whether AI caused it and whether you can repeat it. If it didn't, you've learned something too. Picture a support team that wants to cut first-response time.
They baseline it at nine hours, then let agents draft replies with an AI assistant. Two months later response time is down to three hours, and reopen rates haven’t budged — so the speed isn’t costing them quality. That’s an outcome they can name, measure and repeat. It never needed a leaderboard.
Keeping the finish line in sight
The goal of a metric is to manage toward an outcome. If you're doing more work on the metric than on the outcome, you're upside down. You're looking at the gas tank, not the finish line. So before you stand up your next AI metric, ask one question: what outcome would move if this number did? If you can’t name it, you’re not measuring progress — you’re watching the fuel gauge. Define the finish line first; everything else is just telemetry.

articles.title: LG transforme son nouveau vidéoprojecteur 4K en chef d'orchestre d'un home cinéma sans fil
articles.text:
Avec son CineBeam HU925V, LG ne mise pas uniquement sur l'image. Ce vidéoprojecteur 4K à ultra-courte focale et triple laser intègre Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, une technologie capable d'adapter le son à l'emplacement des enceintes sans fil. À condition, toutefois, d'investir dans les modèles compatibles de la marque.
Déjà commercialisé en Corée du Sud, le CineBeam HU925V doit arriver au Japon à partir de fin octobre, pour un prix estimé à 616 000 yens, soit environ 3 500 euros. Son principal atout réside dans sa capacité à devenir le centre d'une installation home cinéma sans fil, sans nécessiter d'amplificateur AV.
Dolby Atmos FlexConnect : des enceintes sans placement imposé
Avec Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, le vidéoprojecteur peut coordonner jusqu'à quatre éléments compatibles de la gamme LG Sound Suite. Le système détecte leur position et adapte la restitution sonore à la configuration de la pièce, sans imposer leur disposition traditionnelle autour du spectateur.
Plusieurs associations sont possibles, notamment quatre enceintes M5 ou M7, ou trois enceintes de la série M accompagnées du caisson W7. L'installation nécessite au minimum deux M5 ou une M7, un réseau Wi-Fi et l'application LG ThinQ.
Le HU925V possède également ses propres haut-parleurs stéréo, mais LG ne précise pas s'ils participent à la restitution multicanale. FlexConnect reste par ailleurs indisponible lorsque le projecteur est installé au plafond ou en rétroprojection.
Une image 4K triple laser, avec 3 000 lumens ANSI
Côté image, le HU925V associe une puce DLP de 0,47 pouce à une source lumineuse triple laser RGB. Il affiche une image 4K par décalage de pixels, avec une couverture annoncée de 94 % du DCI-P3.
Son ultra-courte focale permet d'obtenir une image de 90 pouces à 5,6 cm du mur, de 100 pouces à 9,8 cm et de 120 pouces à 18,3 cm. LG annonce également une durée de vie de 20 000 heures pour la source lumineuse.
La luminosité atteint 3 000 lumens ANSI, contre 3 700 pour le HU915QE de 2022. Le constructeur proposait toutefois une autre variante, le HU915QB, déjà annoncée à 3 000 lumens ANSI. Le projecteur embarque par ailleurs le processeur α8 AI 4K Gen3, webOS 26 et trois ports HDMI, dont un compatible eARC.
Un home cinéma sans fil qui a un coût
Le HU925V est affiché à 4 799,99 dollars canadiens, mais LG n'a communiqué ni prix ni date de disponibilité pour la France. Il devra notamment se faire une place face aux vidéoprojecteurs triple laser à ultra-courte focale de XGIMI, Hisense et AWOL Vision.
À ce tarif déjà élevé s'ajoute celui des enceintes nécessaires pour profiter de FlexConnect. En Europe, LG annonce les M5 à 249 euros l'unité, les M7 à 399 euros et le caisson W7 à 599 euros.
L'installation minimale revient donc à 399 euros avec une seule M7, ou à 498 euros avec deux M5. Pour un ensemble comprenant trois M5 et le caisson W7, il faut compter 1 346 euros supplémentaires, aux prix publics italiens.
FlexConnect promet ainsi de rendre le home cinéma multicanal plus simple à installer, sans pour autant le rendre plus abordable. Reste à voir si ses performances acoustiques justifient cet investissement face à une barre de son haut de gamme ou à une installation traditionnelle.

articles.title: Lessons in Chemistry: 5 Takeaways from Bonnie Garmus’ Novel
articles.text:
Lessons in Chemistry: 5 Takeaways from Bonnie Garmus’ Novel
Discover five powerful lessons from Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus about equality, ambition, independent thinking, and self-worth.
Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus is a thought-provoking novel about ambition, gender inequality, motherhood, and the courage to challenge social expectations.
Set in the 1960s, the story follows Elizabeth Zott, a brilliant chemist whose professional ambitions are constantly challenged by a society that believes women belong in the kitchen rather than the laboratory.
When Elizabeth unexpectedly becomes the host of a cooking television show, she uses the opportunity to teach more than recipes. Through science, she encourages women to think independently, question established beliefs, and recognise their own abilities.
The novel offers several meaningful lessons about self-worth, equality, and the importance of refusing to let society define who we can become.
5 Powerful ideas in Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus
1. Never let society define your potential
One of the most important lessons in Lessons in Chemistry is that your potential should never be determined by society's expectations.
Elizabeth Zott is an exceptionally talented scientist, but she faces discrimination because she is a woman working in a male-dominated field. Instead of being judged solely on her knowledge and abilities, she repeatedly encounters people who underestimate her because of her gender.
Her experiences highlight how social stereotypes can prevent talented individuals from reaching their full potential. Elizabeth refuses to accept these limitations as the truth about herself. She continues pursuing her interests and challenges the assumptions that attempt to hold her back.
The lesson is simple: your abilities are not limited by what others believe you can achieve. Whether in your career, education, or personal life, you deserve the opportunity to explore your potential without being restricted by outdated expectations.
2. Question everything instead of accepting it blindly
Elizabeth approaches life with the curiosity of a scientist. She believes in examining evidence, asking questions, and understanding why things happen rather than accepting conventional wisdom without thinking.
This mindset becomes particularly important when she begins hosting her cooking show, Supper at Six. Although the programme is designed around cooking, Elizabeth introduces scientific explanations and encourages her audience to understand the processes behind everyday tasks.
Her approach transforms an ordinary television show into an opportunity for women to learn, think critically, and develop confidence in their own intelligence.
The novel reminds readers that questioning established ideas is not necessarily an act of rebellion. Sometimes, it is the first step towards progress.
In everyday life, this means examining the beliefs we inherit, questioning unfair traditions, and making decisions based on reason rather than fear of judgement. Independent thinking allows us to recognise when something needs to change.
3. Women deserve equal opportunities and respect
Gender inequality is a central theme throughout Lessons in Chemistry. Elizabeth encounters professional discrimination, unequal treatment, and assumptions about what women should do with their lives.
Her experiences reflect a broader social problem: women's achievements have often been overlooked simply because they do not fit traditional expectations.
Through Elizabeth's journey, Bonnie Garmus illustrates how exhausting it can be to prove one's competence in an environment where others are unwilling to offer equal opportunities. Elizabeth must work harder to have her knowledge recognised, even when her qualifications speak for themselves.
However, the novel also demonstrates the importance of women supporting one another and recognising their shared potential.
The lesson extends beyond the workplace. Equality means respecting women's choices, valuing their contributions, and allowing them to pursue careers and ambitions without being forced into predefined roles.
A person's capabilities should determine their opportunities, not their gender.
4. Intelligence and confidence can change the way people think
Elizabeth's transformation into a television personality demonstrates that knowledge can be a powerful tool for challenging social attitudes.
Rather than abandoning her scientific background to fit the expectations of a cooking show, she brings science into the kitchen. She explains cooking through chemistry and treats her viewers as intelligent individuals capable of understanding complex ideas.
Her approach challenges the assumption that domestic responsibilities and intellectual pursuits must exist separately. It also gives women a platform to engage with science in a way that traditional institutions have often denied them.
Elizabeth's confidence is not about proving that she is better than everyone else. It comes from knowing the value of her knowledge and refusing to make herself smaller to satisfy other people's expectations.
This lesson encourages readers to embrace their expertise, communicate their ideas clearly, and trust their ability to make a difference.
Sometimes, changing people's perspectives begins with one person who is willing to challenge the familiar and present a different way of thinking.
5. Family and personal identity can exist beyond traditional roles
Another meaningful lesson from Lessons in Chemistry is that people should be allowed to define family and identity on their own terms.
Elizabeth's life challenges conventional ideas about motherhood, relationships, and women's responsibilities. Her experiences show that being a mother does not mean abandoning one's ambitions, just as pursuing a career does not make someone less capable of caring for a family.
The novel explores how people navigate grief, parenthood, relationships, and the expectations placed upon them. It presents a more nuanced understanding of what it means to build a fulfilling life.
Elizabeth refuses to accept that she must choose between being intellectually ambitious and being a devoted parent. Instead, she creates a life that reflects her circumstances, values, and priorities.
For readers, the lesson is that there is no single formula for a meaningful life. People have different ambitions, responsibilities, and definitions of happiness.
Rather than measuring ourselves against conventional milestones, we can focus on building lives that align with our own values and allow us to grow.
Final thoughts
Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus is more than a novel about a scientist navigating a world that underestimates her. It is a story about challenging inequality, embracing curiosity, and refusing to let other people's assumptions determine your future.
Through Elizabeth Zott's experiences, readers are reminded that intelligence deserves recognition, women deserve equal opportunities, and personal ambition should not be sacrificed to satisfy society's expectations.
The five lessons from the book encourage us to question outdated beliefs, trust our abilities, and create lives that reflect who we truly are. Whether you are navigating your career, questioning social norms, or discovering your own identity, Elizabeth's journey offers a powerful reminder that you do not have to fit into someone else's definition of success.
Ultimately, Lessons in Chemistry encourages readers to approach life with curiosity, courage, and the confidence to challenge what they have been told is possible.

articles.title: Apple lance le MacBook Pro M6 : prix, date de sortie, fiche technique....voici tout ce qu'il faut savoir
articles.text:
Ce mardi 27 octobre, Apple a levé le voile sur son nouveau MacBook Pro de 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme. Sans keynote, le géant de Cupertino a annoncé la machine par un simple communiqué de presse. La principale nouveauté se cache sous le capot du PC portable. Il s’agit de la puce M6, inaugurée cet été par le Mac mini. Dans la foulée, Apple a annoncé un nouvel iMac animé par la même puce.
Qu’est-ce qui change sur le nouveau MacBook Pro ?
Sans surprise, la puce M6 constitue la principale nouveauté. C’est la première puce d’Apple gravée en 2 nanomètres par TSMC. Plus la gravure est fine, plus Apple peut loger de transistors sur une même surface, ce qui se traduit par plus de puissance, et une consommation d’énergie moindre.
Comme l’explique Apple, la puce M6 embarque un CPU de 12 cœurs et un GPU de 12 cœurs, soit deux de plus que la M5. Le groupe assure par ailleurs que les performances graphiques grimpent de 30 % par rapport au MacBook Pro M5. Le Neural Engine, la partie de la puce dédiée à l’IA, est désormais deux fois plus important et se montre jusqu’à 1,9 fois plus rapide. Dans les détails, chaque cœur du GPU intègre désormais un accélérateur neuronal, et la bande passante mémoire grimpe jusqu’à 170 Go/s.
La machine passe aussi au Wi-Fi 7 et au Bluetooth 6. Elle conserve 16 Go de mémoire vive de base, extensible jusqu’à 32 Go en ressortant votre portefeuille. Grâce à la puce, l’autonomie annoncée par Apple atteint les 24 heures. Apple met aussi en avant la recharge rapide. La batterie remonte à 50 % en 30 minutes, à condition d’utiliser un adaptateur USB-C plus puissant, comme celui de 96 W, vendu par Apple.
Côté design, Apple ne change rien du tout. Le MacBook Pro M6 reprend le châssis en aluminium du MacBook Pro M5, hérité du modèle de 2021. On retrouve l’écran mini-LED avec son encoche, le clavier avec Touch ID et la même connectique. L’écran Liquid Retina XDR de 14,2 pouces culmine toujours à 1 600 nits en HDR. Apple mise à nouveau sur une dalle nano-texturée, ce qui limite fortement les reflets. Elle est proposée en option, moyennant un nouveau passage à la caisse. La connectique se compose de trois ports Thunderbolt 4, d’un port HDMI, d’un lecteur de cartes SDXC, d’une prise casque et d’un connecteur MagSafe 3.
Prix et date de sortie du MacBook Pro M6
En France, le MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6 est proposé à partir de 2 299 euros. Les précommandes ouvrent le mercredi 28 octobre à 18 h 10. L’ordinateur portable sera disponible dans les magasins le vendredi 6 novembre. Comme son prédécesseur, le Mac est livré sans adaptateur secteur. Voici les tarifs en France :
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6 (CPU 12 cœurs, GPU 12 cœurs), écran standard : 2 299 euros
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6 (CPU 12 cœurs, GPU 12 cœurs), écran nano-texturé : 2 464 euros
Sur tous les modèles, l’écran nano-texturé, qui réduit les reflets, est facturé 165 euros de plus. Pour rappel, le MacBook Pro M5 a été lancé au prix de 1 799 euros l’an dernier, en octobre 2025. Depuis, la flambée du prix de la mémoire a poussé Apple à revoir plusieurs de ses tarifs à la hausse. Ce n’est pas le seul ordinateur portable dans les cartons d’Apple dans l’immédiat. Ce mercredi 28 octobre, Apple devrait lever le voile sur les MacBook Pro avec écran OLED tactile, une première pour la marque. L’annonce est attendue à 18h.

articles.title: ChatGPT et Claude bannis en Suède à cause d’usages jugés problématiques, leur IA remplaçante est aussi américaine
articles.text:
ChatGPT et Claude bannis en Suède à cause d’usages jugés problématiques, leur IA remplaçante est aussi américaine
Le gouvernement suédois interdit désormais à ses employés d’utiliser ChatGPT et Claude sur leurs ordinateurs professionnels, invoquant de sérieux risques pour la sécurité des données sensibles.
Depuis le lundi 26 octobre 2026, les agents du gouvernement suédois n’ont plus le droit d’accéder aux versions web de ChatGPT (OpenAI) et de Claude (Anthropic) depuis leurs postes de travail. Cette décision radicale fait suite à un audit interne mené plus tôt cette année au sein de l’Administration suédoise des transports. Les conclusions de cet examen ont mis en lumière de sérieuses dérives dans le partage d’informations sensibles et le traitement des réponses générées lors de la gestion des dossiers d’État.
La crainte du Shadow IT et la fuite d’informations hors des frontières européennes
Le cœur du problème rapporté par le gouvernement suédois est simple : l’absence de contrat d’entreprise encadrant la protection des informations. Les autorités redoutent ainsi logiquement que les données confidentielles saisies dans ChatGPT et Claude ne soient renvoyées aux développeurs américains pour entraîner leurs futurs modèles. Ce phénomène d’utilisation de logiciels non homologués, connu sous le nom de Shadow IT, complique la traçabilité des échanges au quotidien et expose l’État à des transferts illégaux de données protégées par le RGPD vers des serveurs situés aux États-Unis.
Pour Mikael Wettercrantz, directeur de la numérisation et responsable de l’information (CIO) auprès des services gouvernementaux suédois, le recours à des plateformes dépourvues d’accords de sécurité stricts pourrait avoir des “conséquences pour la sécurité de l’information de la Suède”. Selon la radio publique Sveriges Radio, l’Agence suédoise des impôts et le Conseil national des soins institutionnels (SIS) ont également appliqué ces restrictions, tandis que l’Autorité suédoise de recouvrement étudie la question.
Les fonctionnaires ne sont toutefois pas totalement privés d’intelligence artificielle. Le gouvernement recommande désormais l’usage exclusif de Microsoft Copilot, qui a passé avec succès les contrôles de sécurité et bénéficie d’un accord officiel avec Stockholm, même si son accès fait désormais l’objet d’une surveillance renforcée. Un nombre très restreint d’agents pourra continuer à solliciter ChatGPT et Claude, mais uniquement via une “plateforme spéciale pour les assistants d’IA” développée en interne par les autorités.
ChatGPT et Claude rejoignent ainsi DeepSeek sur la liste noire suédoise. La semaine dernière, le département de la Sécurité intérieure des États-Unis a lui-même banni tous les produits de la start-up chinoise à l’échelle fédérale, affirmant que la plateforme pouvait contenir des “logiciels malveillants et d’autres vulnérabilités de sécurité” au profit de Pékin.

articles.title: Un agente de IA no es un chatbot más: te puede ahorrar mucho tiempo al día. Y este no llega a 7 euros al mes
articles.text:
Llevo meses utilizando mucho la IA en mi día a día y, como la mayoría de personas, lo hago haciéndole preguntas. Realmente, lo hago incluso sin sacar el móvil del bolsillo: utilizo Gemini desde mi reloj. Eso ha hecho que me pique el gusanillo por investigar e ir probando cosas nuevas, como generar textos, resumir documentos o proponer ideas. En general, todo se resume en tareas que nos ahorran mucho tiempo.
Lógicamente, eso tiene un nivel más: los agentes de IA. Estos van más allá de los chatbots y son capaces de encargarse de tareas de todo tipo sin que tengamos que estar pendientes. Uno muy interesante es Hostinger Agent que, además, está de oferta: si elegimos su plan de 12 meses, su precio es de 6,99 euros al mes (en lugar de 9,99 euros al mes).
Hostinger Agent - Plan de 12 meses
Un agente de IA pensado para ahorrarnos mucho tiempo al día
Un agente de IA no se limita a contestar peticiones. Lo bueno que tienen estos es que permiten organizar tareas, ejecutar determinadas acciones y utilizarlos con ciertas herramientas conectadas. Con Hostinger Agent, por ejemplo, podemos conectar Gmail, Slack o Notion. Esto ayudará al agente a poder investigar y organizar contenido sin tener que empezar desde cero cada vez. Aunque claro, siempre viene bien echar un ojo al resultado para comprobar que todo es correcto.
Vamos a ver la utilidad de uno de estos agentes más fácil con un ejemplo. Imagina que tienes un negocio y quieres hacer una pequeña inversión en anuncios locales. Puedes utilizar Hostinger Agent para que recopile información sobre otros negocios de la zona, identifique qué tipo de mensajes utilizan y cree una propuesta inicial para ayudarnos a distribuir nuestro presupuesto.
De hecho, podemos ir un paso más allá. También podemos recurrir a un agente de IA para que nos ayude directamente a preparar un borrador de artículos, organice información para una campaña o trabaje el SEO básico de una web. Es importante entender que todas estas tareas no nos van a dar un resultado definitivo, pero sí un primer paso que nos servirá de punto de partida y nos ahorrará tiempo.
También nos puede echar una mano en esas tareas tediosas del día a día que hay en cada jornada. Ahí podemos meter respuestas a preguntas frecuentes o hacer resúmenes diarios de información para tener un seguimiento activo de la jornada. Además, si conectamos el agente a otras aplicaciones, podremos reducir de esta forma pasos intermedios que nos suelen robar muchos minutos del día.
Ahora bien, ¿eso quiere decir que se le puede delegar cualquier tarea a un agente de IA? La respuesta es que no. Hay ciertos ámbitos que requieren que revisemos cada paso del proceso, como pueden ser temas fiscales, asuntos legales u operaciones delicadas que impliquen datos sensibles. La IA nos puede echar una mano, pero no es una herramienta infalible a la que debamos confiarle cualquier cosa sin supervisión.
Como ya hemos explicado un poco más arriba, la forma más económica de tener Hostinger Agent ahora mismo es apostar por su plan de 12 meses. El precio total del mismo es de 83,88 euros y con ello tendremos 1.000 créditos al mes para gastar. Es importante señalar que esto no equivale a 1.000 tareas, sino que cada tarea consume un número determinado de créditos (va en función de su complejidad).

articles.title: php2shell: Angreifer nutzen die Lücken jetzt aus – 4 Millionen deutsche Dienste veruwndbar
articles.text:
php2shell: Angreifer nutzen die Lücken jetzt aus – 4 Millionen deutsche Dienste veruwndbar
Angreifer nutzen die php2shell genannten Sicherheitslücken in PHP inzwischen erfolgreich aus. Das bestätigte die US-Cybersicherheitsbehörde CISA, die die Schwachstellen in ihren Katalog bekannter ausgenutzter Lücken aufgenommen hat. Über die Lücken lässt sich Schadcode einschleusen und ausführen. Die PHP-Entwickler hatten in der Woche des 19. Oktobers dringende Updates veröffentlicht.
Vom Versuch zum Treffer
Nach dem Bekanntwerden der Lücken registrierten Infrastrukturanbieter wie Amazon und Cloudflare Millionen von Angriffsversuchen. Erfolgreich war davon lange keiner. Das änderte sich am Wochenende, als erste Treffer auf Honeypots auftauchten – also auf absichtlich verwundbaren Servern, die Angriffe protokollieren.
Adel Karimishiraz, Leiter für Detection and Response beim KI-Unternehmen Perplexity, betreibt solche PHP-Honeypots und wertet sie mit Perplexity-KI aus. In den ersten 26 Stunden nach Veröffentlichung der Lücken beobachtete er zahlreiche Angriffsversuche: 30 Mal ging dem System der Arbeitsspeicher aus, in elf Fällen stürzten Worker-Prozesse ab, die Anfragen abarbeiten. Ausgeführten Schadcode konnte er zunächst nicht nachweisen, wie er auf X schrieb.
Vier Millionen Dienste melden alte Versionen
Am Abend des 23. Oktober meldete Karimishiraz dann einen möglichen Treffer. Auf GitHub legte er anschließend eine Analyse vor: Über die php2shell-Lücken gelangte Schadcode auf seine Honeypots und wurde dort ausgeführt. Insgesamt dokumentiert er 35 gestartete Shells – also Kommandozeilen-Zugänge – auf drei Honeypots mit PHP 8.4.26. Die Angriffe kamen von zwei IP-Adressen.
Zahlreiche Organisationen hatten ihre Webseiten in der Woche des 19. Oktobers vorsorglich vom Netz genommen, um die Patches einzuspielen. Die meisten sind wieder online. Trotzdem bleibt die Lage unübersichtlich: Der Schwachstellenscanner der IT-Sicherheitsfirma Censys fand am Freitag rund 4,2 Millionen anfällige PHP-Instanzen allein in Deutschland. Am Morgen des 27. Oktobers waren es laut Censys immer noch mehr als vier Millionen Dienste, die sich mit der Versionsnummer einer verwundbaren PHP-Ausgabe melden. Wer eigene PHP-Installationen betreibt, sollte die Updates umgehend einspielen. Offizielle Infos gibt die PHP Foundation.

articles.title: Researchers set a real-time fiber record: 3.2 petabits per second over 10.3 kilometers
articles.text:
So Much Internet P0rn: Demand for data processing is surging, and traditional communication standards are no longer up to the job. Thanks to a novel engineering approach, a Chinese team is developing fiber-optic technology that might solve the data speed problem for a while, and then some.
A joint initiative by Chinese researchers and engineers has set a new record for real-time fiber-optic communications. The team sent 3.2 petabits per second (Pbps) through a single optical fiber, topping the 2.5 Pbps mark the same group set earlier this year. The figure reflects bidirectional transmission, with traffic flowing in both directions at once.
One petabit equals 1,000 terabits, which means a 3.2 Pbps connection could download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second. The researchers said the feat means one fiber-optic cable could, in theory, serve the gigabit broadband needs of 3.2 million households.
The record comes from researchers at CICT's National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technologies and Networks, Peng Cheng Laboratory and FiberHome Fujikura. They reached 3.2 Pbps using a 24-core optical fiber over a distance of 10.3 km.
The optical signal was engineered to use thousands of parallel channels across three wavelength bands. The team relied on optical modules it developed in-house, aiming for real-time transfers that could meet current commercial standards.
Lab tests have previously reached much higher speeds on similar 24-core fiber setups, but those efforts depended on experimental equipment and signal-processing devices.
The researchers said petabit-level data channels may be essential to keeping the AI industry moving forward. Single-mode optical fibers are nearing their capacity limit as new AI data centers drive ever more traffic back and forth.
Beyond AI and data centers, the technology could benefit other high-performance connectivity scenarios, including linking massive computing centers and powering backbone networks for 6G wireless services. The work was selected for the 2026 Optical Fiber Communication Conference, and the researchers have been invited to publish their results in a scientific journal.
Finally, CICT noted that the record arrives in the year that marks the 50th anniversary of China's "practical" optical fiber infrastructure. In 1976, the country's research focused on "glass filaments" just 0.2 millimeters wide. Today, China is setting world-level records as it pursues full self-reliance in the IT business.

articles.title: OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de IA que usa la computadora y cuesta la mitad
articles.text:
OpenAI lanzó el 26 de octubre GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de gama media pensado para trabajo de oficina en la computadora. Sus precios para desarrolladores son un 50% menores que los de GPT-5.6 Terra, su antecesor, y los de GPT-6.1 Sol, un modelo superior de la misma empresa.
Según el anuncio de la compañía, Terra combina razonamiento visual, uso preciso de la computadora y una redacción más natural. Entre las tareas que menciona están redactar propuestas, interpretar planos técnicos, completar formularios y editar videos.
Ya está disponible para los usuarios de los planes Plus, Pro, Enterprise y Edu en ChatGPT Work y en Codex, la herramienta de programación de OpenAI. Los desarrolladores pueden usarlo en la API (la conexión para integrarlo en otras aplicaciones) con el nombre gpt-6.1-terra. El anuncio no menciona el plan gratuito.
USD 1 por millón de unidades de texto de entrada
El precio estándar es de USD 1 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 5 por millón de salida, según la documentación oficial. Los tokens son las unidades de texto que procesa y cobra un modelo. La firma Artificial Analysis, que mide modelos de IA, informó que GPT-5.6 Terra costaba USD 2 y USD 12, respectivamente.
El modelo acepta texto e imágenes, y responde solo con texto. Tiene una ventana de contexto de 1.050.000 tokens, es decir, la cantidad de información que puede manejar en una sola consulta, y su conocimiento llega hasta el 1 de junio de 2026.
En las pruebas comparativas que publica OpenAI, con esfuerzo de razonamiento medio, Terra obtiene 15 puntos porcentuales más que GPT-5.6 Terra en Agents’ Last Exam, un examen de tareas profesionales, a cerca de un tercio del costo. La empresa afirma que iguala a GPT-6 Astra, su modelo más capaz, con una décima parte del precio por token.
En programación, el modelo resolvió el 50,3% de las tareas de Terminal-Bench 4.0 con el máximo esfuerzo, frente al 21,5% de GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI recomienda GPT-6.1 Sol o GPT-6 Astra para los trabajos de programación más complejos.
Cifras que provienen de la propia empresa
OpenAI también comparó el modelo con Claude Opus 5.5, de Anthropic. Con el máximo esfuerzo, dice, Terra es más de tres veces más eficiente en tokens y cobra una cuarta parte por token, lo que supone un costo por tarea unas nueve veces menor.
En una prueba interna con preguntas diseñadas para provocar errores, la tasa de fallos factuales bajó de 53,6% a 16,7% con esfuerzo bajo, y a 4,3% con el máximo. Esas cifras son de la empresa y ningún tercero las confirmó, señalaron Decrypt y Quartz.
Artificial Analysis sí midió el modelo por su cuenta: con el máximo esfuerzo, Terra suma 6 puntos más que GPT-5.6 Terra en su índice de inteligencia, con un costo por tarea de USD 0,40 frente a USD 1,40. En su índice de programación con agentes, que son asistentes de IA que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta, obtuvo 48 puntos, seis menos que GPT-6.1 Sol.
El analista Simon Willison comparó a Terra con Sonnet, el modelo intermedio de Anthropic, y señaló que una opción más barata sirve para tareas repetitivas y automatizadas. Ted Sanders, empleado de OpenAI, escribió en Hacker News que para los suscriptores no es una gran novedad: si alcanzan los límites de uso, les puede rendir un poco más.
Para los planes de ChatGPT, OpenAI indica que la misma cuota de uso cubre más tareas con Terra que con GPT-5.6 Terra, y bastantes más que con Sol o Astra. El anuncio no precisa cuántas más.

articles.title: SAP advances its autonomous enterprise push with smarter, governed Joule agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SAP advances its autonomous enterprise push with smarter, governed Joule agents
SAP SE today announced a set of artificial intelligence innovations at its annual TechEd conference for developers, enhancing its Joule assistant solutions and Business AI Platform, including tabular data foundation models.
New capabilities in Joule Work will help AI agents become more efficient and interoperate with open protocols. In this case, the Model Context Protocol and Agent 2 Agent allow Joule, the company’s agentic AI assistant, to gather context, make decisions and execute multistep business workflows across the enterprise, while also bringing in third-party data or services.
However, every time an agent goes to work, it needs to be governed by a central authority just like an employee; it needs access and it must execute on tools with permissions. “Open protocols need governed doors,” Ted Way, vice president and chief product officer of SAP business AI product engineering, told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
Way explained that SAP would like customers’ own agents to collaborate with its business agents across company systems. The proposition is that opening those interconnections also requires a controlled entry point where organizations can enforce and oversee activity. This is where a new orchestration layer will come in, enabling assistants and agents to invoke Joule Agents through a governed gateway.
In addition, a recent update will allow agents to trigger n8n workflows, an important connector through Joule Studio. N8n is a node-based workflow automation platform that connects different apps and uses deterministic automation; this means that AI agents can trigger it, but unlike generative AI, n8n uses event-based and trigger-based logic for decision-making. It cannot hallucinate; it is not random and will follow exact rules from start to finish.
That means n8n is suitable for highly regulated or sensitive work that depends on exact needs.
“It needs to do these five steps in this order exactly like this every single time,” Way explained, so in that case, n8n is the go-to.
SAP’s approach combines flexible, natural-language agentic triggers with a prescribed workflow. An agent may help determine when it is needed, while compliance-sensitive procedures can still require an exact sequence of steps.
SAP builds on cloud data to ground the autonomous enterprise
The company today announced the expansion of SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager in SAP Data Cloud, or BDC, to provide an AI-native authoring experience for businesses by giving agents an understanding of how applications relate to one another. It does so by defining relationships between company facts, allowing agents to reason more accurately and make decisions across enterprises.
SAP’s acquisition of Reltio, recently announced at SAP Connect, brings on board multidomain data management to BDC. That helps unify customer, supplier and product records across SAP and third-party systems into trusted data products for applications and agents.
The new product is designed to complement the company’s existing Knowledge Graph, which provides rich business context from SAP data.
Additionally, the company said, it’s expanding its lakehouse capabilities with Dremio, another acquisition, by adding native support for Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris and a high-performance, federated query engine that enables unified data access without moving or copying data.
Bringing AI models to tables
“Not every enterprise problem is a language problem,” Way said, explaining that although much of the AI approach has focused on natural language, much business data is stored in tables.
To handle this, SAP announced its latest tabular AI model, SAP-RPT-2.0, which expands beyond classification and regression to support anomaly and outlier detection, providing AI-powered analysis through embeddings. It will give multitable capabilities to reduce manual engineering and deliver faster, deeper insights from structured data.
The company also launched a new SAP-RPT-TS model, which will help customers predict values across time-indexed metrics for key forecasting. It uses SAP Business Planning without custom business machine learning, allowing less technical users to deploy the model on their systems.
In a partnership with Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., SAP announced it’s deploying SAP-RPT on the International Space Station. The aim is to assist with predicting issues before failures escalate, reconstruct missing sensor values from historical data, and generate explainable mission health reports for astronauts and ground teams, all without sending data back to Earth before analysis.

articles.title: Apple anuncia MacBook Pro e iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6; veja preços • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple anuncia MacBook Pro e iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6; veja preços
Novo MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas promete ainda até 24 horas de autonomia. Já novo iMac de 24 polegadas traz sete opções de cores.
A Apple escolheu esta semana para fazer uma série de anúncios de produtos. Começou com o iPad Mini com tela OLED. Agora, nesta terça-feira (27/10), a companhia revelou dois Macs com chip M6: um MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas e um iMac de 24 polegadas. No Brasil, os preços começam em R$ 17.999.
O Apple M6 é um chip com até 12 núcleos de CPU e 12 núcleos de GPU, sendo que estes últimos são complementados com aceleradores de inteligência artificial. Também para lidar com tarefas de IA, o chip conta com uma implementação do Neural Engine com dois blocos de 16 núcleos.
Eis o efeito: o M6 oferece até 30% mais desempenho gráfico, bem como até 25% mais desempenho em IA em relação ao M5. Isso deixa claro que o MacBook Pro continua apto a lidar com tarefas que demandam altas cargas de trabalho.
Isso sem abrir mão da autonomia: ainda de acordo com a Apple, o MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas conta com uma bateria que dura até 24 horas com uma recarga completa. Trata-se do maior tempo de autonomia já registrado na linha. Para completar, a carga pode chegar a 50% de capacidade com apenas 30 minutos de tomada.
Falando dos demais recursos, o novo MacBook Pro também conta com uma tela Liquid Retina XDR (LCD com mini-LED) de 14 polegadas que alcança brilho de pico de 1.600 nits em HDR e, opcionalmente, com vidro “nano-texture”, que reduz os reflexos para melhorar a percepção de qualidade de imagem.
A frente também abriga uma câmera de 12 megapixels com tecnologia Center Stage, que usa IA para manter o usuário centralizado na imagem durante chamadas de vídeo.
Outros atributos de destaque incluem:
O novo iMac de 24 polegadas traz o mesmo chip M6 do novo MacBook Pro, podendo ter dez ou 12 núcleos de CPU e GPU, o que significa que desempenho também é um ponto forte do modelo, principalmente no âmbito da inteligência artificial.
Mas, talvez, o maior destaque fique para a tela, que consiste em um painel Retina (LCD) de 24 polegadas com resolução 4,5K. O componente suporta ainda até 500 nits de brilho e mais de 1 bilhão de cores. A câmera de 12 megapixels com Center Stage está por lá. O vidro “nano-texture” também é uma opção aqui.

articles.title: Micron Plans 400-Layer 3D NAND with Wafer-to-Wafer Bonding in 2027
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Micron Plans 400-Layer 3D NAND with Wafer-to-Wafer Bonding in 2027
Micron is actively working on bringing its next-generation G11 NAND Flash technology to production, as the company has announced that G11 will be its first 3D NAND Flash. With the current G9 technology shipping across Micron's product portfolio, the company has created NAND Flash storage modules using over 200 layers of scaling. However, as the current technology reaches its limitations, the next phase involves exploring vertical stacking. With G11, Micron aims to use wafer-on-wafer 3D NAND stacking to double the capacity of NAND modules. Micron is now officially following in the footsteps of Chinese NAND giant YMTC, which has been making 3D stacked NAND for some time using Xtacking technology.
This is achieved by splitting each wafer into separate components. One is designed as a memory cell wafer, while the other contains peripheral logic circuits. These are combined using hybrid bonding technology in wafer-to-wafer stacking. Hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that fuse together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together. In this way, Micron plans to ship 400-layer NAND in the second half of 2027, which is less than a year away, and we are about to see more commercialization of 3D silicon.For capacity and speed, Micron advertises that G11 will double the density per square millimeter. From 21 Gb/mm² for G9, the G11 generation is targeting 42 Gb/mm². Other improvements include a much faster I/O speed, increasing from 3,600 MT/s in G9 to 5,400 MT/s with G11, while efficiency is expected to be significantly improved with 25% lower energy transfer per bit. Real-world performance will depend on the number of these 3D NAND chips in the SSD, as well as the controller, firmware, and interface that the SSD uses to communicate with the host system. Therefore, we don't yet know what kind of speeds consumers can expect, but rest assured, we will be benchmarking them in the future.

articles.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
articles.text:
Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country’s occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely — or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir. But as vaccination rates have slipped nationwide in recent years and outbreaks grow bigger and more frequent, domestic travel now poses a greater risk than international incursions.
In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread.
South Carolina’s measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania’s ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it.
The study in Washington relied heavily on epidemiological data, linking cases among contacts and exposure sites. But also key to the work was whole genome sequencing, which made clear that cases didn’t just stem from one single introduction of the virus from South Carolina that then spread among Washington residents; instead, it revealed five separate introductions.
“As public health jurisdictions prepare to respond to increased measles importations linked to domestic measles outbreaks, while remaining vigilant for international importations, timely whole-genome sequencing can supplement epidemiologic information to help differentiate distinct importations from local transmission and inform outbreak response,” the authors conclude.
Importations
In their analysis, health officials identified the first importation in a resident who fell ill with the telltale rash on January 12 after returning from a trip to South Carolina, where they were exposed to a person sick with measles. Genome sequencing found that the virus closely matched sequences from South Carolina cases. One close contact of the Washington case fell ill and was isolated. No other cases were linked to this importation.

articles.title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastructure. Worries abound that, in the short term, the energy crunch could lead to surging electrical bills and, in the long term, may eventually lead to outages or other technical problems.
At TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this month, industry insiders tempered much of this criticism with optimism about how the flood of new energy connections could actually be opening the door for grid modernization. Apoorv Bhargava, founder and CEO of Weavegrid, Tim Heidel, CEO of Veir, and Kristen Eberhard, VP of policy at Rewiring America, said that though the grid faces new challenges, there are also plenty of new opportunities as well.
“It’s a very different electric grid, right?” said Bhargava. “We’re dealing with a ton of new variables, including renewable energy. We’re dealing with a ton of new load in the form of electric vehicles and data centers and heat pumps, and the ability to manage and orchestrate is fundamentally what utilities are now grappling with.”
While all of those new connections are driving an ever larger amount of stress to the grid, Bhargava’s company hopes to provide the kind of load orchestration and management that helps utilities maximize the potential of the current system. Weavegrid’s software can help organizations efficiently deploy energy while also optimizing connections to reduce utility payers’ bills, the founder said.
Heidel, on the other hand, runs a company that is working to build out and expand the physical infrastructure of the grid, while also making it run much more efficiently. Veir sells superconductive power lines that promises to transfer energy at a much more efficient rate than traditional ones. Veir’s cables can carry power five times further than traditional cables while also requiring 20 times less space, the company has said. Earlier this month the startup raised $110 million in a series C funding round.
“The scale of the investment in AI infrastructure is driving a tremendous amount of innovation,” said Heidel. “There’s a ton of new technologies that are coming off the shelves and starting to get to scale that, pulled together, can actually really make sure that data centers are the best community neighbors and citizens be right.”
He added: “I think that we really need to look at ways that we can really adopt all of that as fast as possible to ease this next stage of growth.”
Eberhard, whose organization advocates for household electrification, also said that while the surge in data center energy demand has spurred a new urgency to the modernization cause, it has also created an environment where industries are ready to try new things.
“I feel like this era of AI and load growth is a very improv era,” Eberhard said. “There’s a lot of yes-and-ing going on. So yes, we need more transmission lines. Yes, we need more centralized power plants, and we also need to make sure that we’re taking advantage of all this other stuff that we had previously been leaving on the table when we didn’t have this urgency of the AI demand.”

articles.title: Israeli ad tech firm tied to suspected Starlink tracking effort, report claims — researchers say it outbid everyone for Starlink-linked ads in 100+ countries, including where the service is banned
articles.text:
Israeli ad tech firm tied to suspected Starlink tracking effort, report claims — researchers say it outbid everyone for Starlink-linked ads in 100+ countries, including where the service is banned
Israeli ad-tech firm linked to suspected surveillance campaign exploiting online advertising auctions across sensitive networks.
Discover-Tech, an Israeli advertising technology company, has reportedly been linked to a suspected surveillance effort aimed at Starlink users, according to Reuters. The report, which cites six people familiar with the matter, claims the firm was the top bidder for ad space tied to Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries. Researchers suspect the aggressive bidding was meant to reveal where users are located or to enable further monitoring — though the findings do not show that anyone was actually tracked.
The data comes from TrendAI, the research arm of Trend Micro. Its October 15 report referred to the activity as ‘Shadow-Earth-79’ without naming a company, but the report claims the codename belongs to Discover-Tech. TrendAI says its attribution process is designed to avoid ‘hype-driven labels’ that could mislead security teams. “Our approach reduces the risk of misattribution, hype-driven labels, and unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions.” The report says.
The method exploits how online ads are sold with advertisers bidding in real-time auctions for space on websites and in apps, and each bid request can carry details about the person on the other end. Collected over time and combined with other data, that information could be used to identify people, follow their activity across the web, or select targets for spyware.
The geography is what raised eyebrows. Shadow-Earth-79 was reportedly the largest ad buyer in Syria, Libya, Yemen, and South Sudan, and the second largest in Afghanistan, while also claiming unusually large shares of bids in Hungary, Israel, Egypt, Azerbaijan, and Venezuela. TrendAI says the pattern points to ‘targeting and tracking infrastructure rather than a commercial advertising operation.’ That is plausible, given how little legitimate Western advertising demand exists in sanctioned or war-torn markets.
Notably, Discover-Tech was already under scrutiny. On the same day as TrendAI’s report, Citizen Lab and ad security firm Confiant separately named the company, alleging that it used ad auctions to collect data on users across sensitive networks, including those tied to media organizations, governments, and tech firms. “The malicious advertisements were purchased by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a legitimate advertising company, but which we found operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners.” Citizen Lab wrote.
Google and Comcast have since said they removed Discover-Tech from their advertising platforms, while the report says that a major U.S. technology company and an international organization have opened internal inquiries into whether the firm’s ads targeted their employees.
For Starlink, the stakes are obvious — the service works outside conventional telecom networks, which makes it a lifeline where governments restrict internet access, and makes its users an attractive target for those same governments. In April, Iran’s nationwide internet blackout passed 1,000 hours, with authorities reportedly going after Starlink terminals and imposing severe penalties for possessing one. Earlier this month, SpaceX also limited Starlink service for Ukraine’s high-speed military drones, which Ukrainian officials say complicates logistics and operations.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Advertising and consumer tech have been abused for tracking before. A backdoor was previously found in a popular iOS ad library that could collect device-location data and capture screenshots, while Chrysaor, Android spyware linked to the Pegasus family, was discovered by Lookout and Citizen Lab on a small number of devices. More recently, a researcher claimed to have found extensive data collection, including ad-related telemetry, inside a Samsung smart TV’s Tizen operating system, though those findings are still being investigated.
That said, it is still unclear if Discover-Tech actually used Starlink-related data to single out specific subscribers remains unverified, and neither the company nor SpaceX has commented.

His interest in technology started early, taking apart things around the house to see how they worked, often to his dad’s frustration. His curiosity sometimes got the better of him, including a few failed attempts to fix laptops, one of them a gifted Dell XPS. articles.title: Samsung launches clip-on Galaxy Buds On that work on either ear
articles.text:
Samsung has released the new Galaxy Buds On earbuds, its first clip-on Galaxy Buds. Though the earbuds are officially only in South Korea, I expect a global release to follow.
Samsung says the Galaxy Buds On lets you listen to what’s going on around you while listening to music or having a conversation. Because of the design, it puts less strain on the ears during extended use. The company said it analyzed data from different ear shapes so that it can optimize the position of the speakers and battery.
The Buds On also sports ‘TwinBoost speakers’ designed to offer better low-frequency performance, along with automatic volume control that adjusts to the environment. There’s also an Audio Leakage Reduction feature to help prevent people from hearing what you’re listening to. And when you’re setting up the earbuds, they don’t have a right and left side. The Buds On can automatically detect which side they’re in and adjust the audio channels accordingly.
Spec-wise, the Buds On use the Snapdragon S7 Gen 1 Sound platform with a high-efficiency Class-D amplifier for up to 9.5 hours of continuous music playback on a single charge.
In addition to three microphones, the Buds On have a bone conduction-based vibration sensor that detects vibration when a person speaks and uses machine learning to separate the user’s voice and reduce background noise.
When you wear the Buds On and say “Hey Google, let’s talk live,” Gemini Live launches, so you can talk to the AI in a natural conversation.
There are also Head Gestures to answer or end calls, dismiss alarms, or read message notifications. On Galaxy devices, you can adjust the volume and equalizer by just heading over to your device’s settings instead of heading to the Galaxy Wearable app.
The earbuds are priced at KRW₩299,000, which converts to roughly C$316.94, so if the Buds On come to Canada, expect them to be in the mid-$300 range.

articles.title: Google Cloud’s Gemini voice AI wants to do more than just talk
articles.text:
Google Cloud’s Gemini voice AI wants to do more than just talk
What if AI could do more than answer the phone? At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Naren Kachroo showed Gemini voice AI handling bookings, sales negotiations and multilingual conversations.
Imagine asking an AI assistant to find a customer, negotiate a price and help close a sale, all without typing a single prompt. Voice AI is moving beyond answering questions to taking on tasks, and Google Cloud wants businesses to put it to work.
At TechSparks 2026, Naren Kachroo, Head of AI Go-to-Market at Google Cloud, demonstrated how Gemini’s voice AI capabilities could help businesses handle customer conversations, restaurant bookings and sales negotiations.
From talking to taking action
Until now, much of the AI experience has revolved around asking questions and getting answers. Kachroo said the next step is AI that can access information, use tools and take action on a user’s behalf.
“We don't want to focus on voice AI just being an experience to talk to AI,” he said. “We want voice AI to be powered through agentic experiences where the task is actually accomplished with AI.”
To show what that means, Naren Kachroo played a demonstration of an AI assistant booking a restaurant table for eight. The assistant answered questions about bringing a birthday cake, identified a dish from an image, discussed vegetarian options and switched between English and Spanish during the conversation.
In other words, it did more than take a booking. It handled the questions that came with it, too.
Kachroo also introduced Gemini Live voice capabilities, alongside models for text-to-speech, speech-to-text and translation. He showcased Live Avatar, which combines voice interaction with a visual AI presence.
Meet the AI sales assistant
The standout demonstration involved a fictional safety equipment business with 500 helmets sitting in its inventory. Its owner, Rajesh, wanted to sell them quickly and instructed an AI voice agent to find a suitable lead, contact the customer and negotiate a price above Rs 400 per helmet.
The assistant checked the business’s leads, identified a construction company that needed 500 helmets and initiated a call in Hindi. When the prospective buyer pushed for a lower price, the AI negotiated while sticking to the owner’s pricing instruction.
It was a glimpse of how AI could help small businesses manage sales without handling every step themselves. The agent could draw on internal business information, speak to a customer and respond to objections, rather than simply recommend what the owner should do next.
Kachroo said the demonstration showed how the agent maintained context as it moved from internal information to a customer conversation.
Why India needs voice AI
Voice could be particularly useful in India, where people speak many languages and have different levels of comfort with typing or navigating digital interfaces.
“I believe that India and Indian consumer is continuing to go as voice first,” Naren said.
He highlighted Google’s work on Indian languages, accents and cultural nuances, and pointed to Equal AI, an Indian company building voice assistants that can handle calls on users’ behalf.
For Kachroo, the goal is to make voice AI useful in everyday business processes, not just impressive in a demo. That means building systems that understand context, handle interruptions and follow instructions while completing tasks.
The real test, then, is not whether AI can hold a conversation. It is whether it can get the job done. And for businesses exploring voice AI, that could be the difference between another chatbot and a genuinely useful assistant.

articles.title: Le Xiaomi Smart Band 11 arrive enfin en Europe, mais pas encore dans tous les pays
articles.text:
Après un lancement en Chine au début du mois de septembre, le Xiaomi Smart Band 11 pose ses valises sur le sol européen, plus précisément en Espagne où le bracelet connecté est déjà référencé à partir de 59,99 euros dans sa version de base.
Un design plus fin et un écran très lumineux
Le Smart Band 11 se distingue du Xiaomi Smart Band 10 par plusieurs aspects, notamment par son épaisseur. En effet, le boîtier mesure seulement 9,99 mm d’épaisseur pour un poids plume de 15,58 g (sans le bracelet). Côté affichage, le constructeur chinois a intégré une dalle AMOLED oblongue de 1,72 pouce dotée d’une définition de 212 par 520 pixels, portée par une impressionnante luminosité de 2 000 cd/m2 qui garantit une lisibilité parfaite en extérieur.
Découvrez : Les meilleures montres connectées pour le sport en 2026
Le bracelet tourne sous HyperOS 4, et embarque plusieurs capteurs pour assurer un suivi plus précis de la fréquence cardiaque et de la saturation en oxygène dans le sang (SpO2). Les sportifs pourront également compter sur plus de 150 modes d’entraînement préinstallés. Enfin, le bracelet est protégé par une étanchéité certifiée jusqu’à 5 ATM, soit une résistance à l’immersion équivalente à 50 mètres de profondeur.
Prix, versions et autonomie du Xiaomi Smart Band 11
Affiché à 59,99 euros dans sa version standard, le bracelet voit son prix grimper à 79,99 euros pour la variante équipée de la puce NFC, bien que Xiaomi n’ait pas encore confirmé tous les détails concernant la prise en charge des paiements sans contact. Si une édition en céramique est mentionnée sur le site officiel espagnol, elle n’est pour l’instant pas disponible à l’achat.
L’autonomie reste l’un des gros points forts de cette génération : la batterie de 233 mAh promet d’atteindre jusqu’à 21 jours d’utilisation sur une seule charge (dans un scénario idéal, probablement moins en usage réel). Entièrement compatible avec l’écosystème iOS et Android, le bracelet se décline en plusieurs coloris : noir, argent et rose.
Pour l’instant, seul le Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active est disponible sur le site de Xiaomi France à 39,99 euros. Compte tenu de la proximité de nos voisins espagnols, il n’y a pas de raison que le Xiaomi Smart Band 11 et sa variante NFC n’arrivent pas en France dans les jours ou semaines à venir. articles.title: Anthropic, en su S-1: "Tenemos un historial de pérdidas y es posible que no generemos ingresos suficientes en el futuro"
articles.text:
La esperadísima salida a bolsa de Anthropic, la primera de un laboratorio frontera de la inteligencia artificial, ha generado un sinfín de reacciones. Las cifras apabullan: la compañía ha generado 16.000 millones de dólares durante los primeros seis meses de este año, registrando pérdidas de 80.000 millones en el mismo periodo de tiempo. Pese a todo, declara un margen del 10%, por primera vez positivo desde su nacimiento en 2021.
De forma resumida, Anthropic ya está ganando dinero en su operativa diaria en términos ajustados. Su gran problema es la revalorización de los bonos convertibles con los que se financió, la mayoría en manos de Amazon, y que aumentan conforme la empresa lo hace; y su verdadero lastre son los compromisos de compra firmados con los hiperescaladores, unos 265.600 millones de dólares a 30 de junio de 2026, con plazos de hasta 20 años.
Todo esto y mucho más aparece en su S-1, el folleto que toda empresa estadounidense debe publicar antes de salir a bolsa.
Seguramente en noviembre sabremos cómo interpretan los mercados las cuentas de Anthropic. Hasta entonces, lo que tenemos son fragmentos más o menos viralizados del documento. Si uno es un entusiasta de la IA, resaltará la gran diversificación de ingresos de Anthropic —más de 11.900 clientes con más de 100.000 dólares de gasto anual, muy lejos de la concentración pregonada anteriormente; según el NYT, ningún cliente supera el 10% de la facturación anual de Anthropic—.
¿Y si uno es un doomer, un pesimista de la IA? Tendría la tentación de compartir este párrafo incluido en la página 64 del S-1. Copiamos y pegamos literalmente, incluyendo las negritas:
Si no logramos gestionar de forma eficaz el crecimiento de nuestro negocio y de nuestras operaciones, es posible que no podamos mantener controles internos, sistemas de información y procesos de cumplimiento normativo eficaces, que nos enfrentemos a un mayor escrutinio regulatorio y que se dañe nuestra marca y nuestra capacidad para captar y retener clientes. Como consecuencia, nuestro negocio, nuestra situación financiera y nuestros resultados de explotación podrían verse afectados negativamente.
Tenemos un historial de pérdidas netas y es posible que no generemos ingresos suficientes para alcanzar o mantener la rentabilidad en el futuro.
Hemos registrado pérdidas netas todos los años desde nuestra fundación, con una pérdida neta de 1.500 millones de dólares en 2023, 8.300 millones en 2024 y 42.000 millones en 2025, y de 80.700 millones de dólares en los seis meses terminados el 30 de junio de 2026. Es posible que no logremos ni mantengamos la rentabilidad en el futuro.
Dentro captura:
La frase, sin duda, es llamativa. Cuando una empresa con pérdidas superiores a los 80.000 millones de dólares en apenas medio año incluye un disclaimer de esas características, merece la pena tomárselo en serio. Sucede que es algo habitual en todas las salidas a bolsa de las grandes empresas estadounidenses, en especial de las tecnológicas.
Un repaso al S-1 de Uber, al F-1 de Spotify y al S-1 de SpaceX, tres empresas de menor capitalización a la prevista por Anthropic —2 billones de dólares en el supuesto más optimista— pero de proporciones gigantescas igualmente, devuelve frases similares en sus respectivos documentos. Uber, en concreto, declaraba haber "incurrido en pérdidas significativas desde su creación"; Spotify admitía que quizá "no sería capaz de generar suficientes ingresos para ser rentables".
Son fórmulas calcadas a la empleada por Anthropic y no es casual. Su S-1 incluye 94 páginas de riesgos asociados a la compra de sus acciones. Esto sí es excepcional, dado que duplica las precauciones sugeridas por otras empresas en sus salidas a bolsa, pero obedece a un mismo patrón: protegerse legalmente ante hipotéticas demandas de inversores en caso de que la empresa no sea rentable a medio plazo. En esencia, el S-1 advierte a los futuros inversores que si pierden dinero con Anthropic no es culpa de Anthropic, ellos avisaron.
La naturaleza explosiva de las empresas tecnológicas, con operativas a pérdidas durante años y sostenidas por inversores privados en líneas de crédito infinitas, resalta lo que, por otro lado, son los riesgos inherentes a meter tu dinero en bolsa. Algo siempre puede salir mal. Anthropic, como Uber y Spotify antes, no es rentable ahora mismo; su valor reside en la tecnología que maneja y en sus capacidades futuras, tanto desde un punto de vista técnico como financiero.
Siguiendo el ejemplo de Uber: fundada en 2009, no declaró beneficios operativos hasta 14 años después; solo en 2023, cuatro años después de salir a bolsa, salió de los números rojos. El riesgo existía, pero a largo plazo era una apuesta ganadora.
La descomunal dimensión de la industria IA magnifica los riesgos inherentes a toda salida a bolsa. Y el discurso polarizado en torno a su viabilidad económica también, de ahí la viralización de un oscuro párrafo estándar en el S-1 de Anthropic. El gran paso de la empresa dirigida por Dario Amodei debería resolver una de las grandes preguntas de la IA: ¿estamos ante una burbuja que camina inevitablemente hacia la ruina o nos encontramos ante el negocio más rentable de todos los tiempos?
Por si el fin del mundo llega, su folleto se pone la venda antes de la herida.

articles.title: La Huawei Watch 6 se fait plus discrète au poignet comme sur la facture grâce aux 50 € de réduction appliqués par Amazon
articles.text:
La montre connectée Huawei Watch 6 propose de nombreuses fonctionnalités dédiées au suivi sportif et à la santé. Son prix passe de 449,99 € à 399,99 € chez Amazon, qui en assure la livraison gratuitement.
Si Huawei est connu pour ses smartphones, ses montres connectées sont, quant à elles, une autre porte d’entrée dans la santé connectée. La Huawei Watch 6 s’adresse aux personnes qui souhaitent suivre leur activité physique et leur bien-être sans s’encombrer : elle est actuellement disponible à 399,99 € chez Amazon. Cela correspond à une réduction de 50 € par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours affiché par le marchand pour ce modèle de 42 mm.
La Huawei Watch 6 de 42 mm est à 399,99 € au lieu de 449,99 € chez Amazon, une offre à durée limitée.
Pourquoi choisir la Huawei Watch 6 ?
- Pour son format compact : son boîtier pèse environ 38 g sans le bracelet, ce qui permet de l’oublier quand on la porte.
- Pour son écran AMOLED : la dalle de 1,38 pouce bénéficie d’une luminosité qui atteint jusqu’à 3 000 nits selon Huawei.
- Pour sa connectivité : le GPS intégré est idéal pour le suivi sportif en extérieur, et il est possible d’y configurer une eSIM avec une offre opérateur compatible.
Une montre adaptée au quotidien et aux entraînements
Course à pied, vélo ou marche : la Huawei Watch 6 se montre très utile pour réaliser des mesures durant un grand choix d’activités physiques. Elle dispose de capteurs qui lui permettent également de suivre le sommeil et la fréquence cardiaque. Son capteur X-TAP permet de lancer Panorama santé, une synthèse de plusieurs indicateurs de bien-être réalisée en une minute, après avoir posé un doigt sur le capteur. Les sportifs bénéficient également d’une analyse de leur récupération, utile dans un programme sur mesure. Enfin, cette montre fonctionne avec Android et iOS.
Un petit format qui demande des recharges régulières
Cette version de 42 mm privilégie la discrétion et sa petite taille implique une petite batterie. En mode standard, Huawei annonce jusqu’à trois jours d’autonomie, contre quatre jours et demi pour la version de 46 mm. Si vous optez pour l’affichage permanent, l’autonomie annoncée passe à deux jours dans ce même mode : mieux vaut garder son support de recharge sur vous si vous partez durant le week-end. Le mode économie d’énergie permet toutefois de grappiller un peu d'autonomie supplémentaire.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran AMOLED protégé par un verre saphir.
- GPS intégré et suivi de plusieurs activités sportives.
- Boîtier de 42 mm pesant environ 38 g sans bracelet.
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie limitée à deux jours avec l’affichage permanent en mode standard.
- L’utilisation de l’eSIM est conditionnée par votre opérateur.
