articles.title: Mars-Wettlauf: Warum Japan den USA und China zuvorkommen könnte
articles.text:
Überholmanöver im All: Japan will beim Mars-Wettlauf gewinnen
Wie die japanische Raumfahrtbehörde JAXA mit Sitz in Chōfu bei Tokio mitteilt, soll die Raumsonde „Martian Moons Exploration“ (MMX) am 19. Oktober 2026 um 21:41 Uhr mitteleuropäischer Sommerzeit (20. Oktober, 04:41 Uhr japanischer Ortszeit) vom Raumfahrtzentrum Tanegashima auf der gleichnamigen südjapanischen Insel starten. An Bord einer Trägerrakete vom Typ H3 bricht das aus drei Modulen bestehende Raumfahrzeug zu einer fünfjährigen Reise auf, um erstmals Bodenproben vom Marsmond Phobos zur Erde zu bringen.
Damit könnte Japan im Wettlauf um die ersten zurückgeführten Proben aus dem Marssystem an den USA und China vorbeiziehen. Wie der kanadische Sender CTV News unter Verweis auf die Nachrichtenagentur AFP meldet, hat die US-Regierung ihr eigenes Rückführprogramm Anfang 2026 aus Kostengründen gestrichen, während China den Start seiner Mission Tianwen-3 erst für 2028 anpeilt.
Allerdings steht das Vorhaben unter Vorbehalt, denn ursprünglich sollte die Sonde schon im Herbst 2024 abheben, verpasste dieses nur alle 26 Monate geöffnete Startfenster zum Mars jedoch wegen Verzögerungen nach dem gescheiterten Erstflug des Raketentyps H3 im März 2023. Zwar brachte die neue Trägerrakete in der Zwischenzeit mehrere Satelliten in eine Erdumlaufbahn, doch im Dezember 2025 fiel bei einer dieser anderen Missionen erneut ein Triebwerk vorzeitig aus.
Marsmond Phobos als Abkürzung für Gesteinsproben vom Roten Planeten
Auf der Marsoberfläche sammelt der US-Rover Perseverance zwar schon seit seiner Landung im Februar 2021 Gesteinskerne in Metallröhrchen. Ein Rücktransport von dort erfordert wegen der hohen Schwerkraft des Planeten jedoch eine eigene Aufstiegsrakete, weshalb Japan stattdessen den 27 Kilometer breiten Mond Phobos ansteuert.
Phobos umkreist den Mars dreimal täglich in einer Entfernung von rund 6.000 Kilometern. Durch diese geringe Distanz fängt der Mond regelmäßig sogenanntes Auswurfmaterial ein. Das sind Gesteinstrümmer, die bei Asteroideneinschlägen von der Marsoberfläche ins All geschleudert wurden. Wie The Guardian unter Berufung auf die Nachrichtenagentur Associated Press berichtet, soll dieses Material nach Schätzungen der JAXA etwa 0,1 Prozent der oberen Bodenschicht auf Phobos ausmachen.
Mit den restlichen 99,9 Prozent der Proben wollen die Wissenschaftler:innen klären, ob die beiden Marsmonde Phobos und Deimos eingefangene Asteroiden sind oder sich nach einer früheren Großkollision aus Marstrümmern geformt haben. „Durch die Analyse von Bodenproben können wir nahezu sicher zu einer Schlussfolgerung gelangen“, wird der wissenschaftliche Missionsleiter Kiyoshi Kuramoto von der japanischen Universität Hokkaido in Sapporo im Bericht des Guardian zitiert.
Trotz dieses Ansatzes hat die Methode aus geologischer Sicht eine Kehrseite, da die Sonde insgesamt nur mindestens zehn Gramm des lockeren Oberflächengesteins (Regolith) einsammeln soll. Auf den Mars selbst entfielen damit rechnerisch lediglich rund zehn Milligramm Staub, die sich im Gegensatz zu einer direkten Bohrung auf dem Planeten keiner bestimmten Region zuordnen lassen.
Quasi-Satelliten-Orbit und zwei Verfahren für die Probenentnahme
Nach einer Flugstrecke von 500 bis 600 Millionen Kilometern soll die Raumsonde im August 2027 den Mars erreichen und im September 2027 in einen sogenannten Quasi-Satelliten-Orbit einschwenken. Weil die Anziehungskraft des kleinen Mondes für eine stabile Umlaufbahn kaum ausreicht, umrundet die Sonde dabei weiterhin den Mars, bleibt durch ihre Flugbahn aber dauerhaft in der Nähe von Phobos.
Für die im Jahr 2030 geplanten zwei Landungen setzt die Mission auf zwei unterschiedliche Sammelverfahren, um sowohl Material von der Oberfläche als auch aus zwei Zentimetern Tiefe zu gewinnen. Während ein japanischer Bohrarm Untergrundproben entnimmt, nutzt ein zweites System der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa Druckgas, um Staub aufzuwirbeln und in einen Behälter zu leiten.
Deutscher Rover Idefix und das Risiko der geringen Schwerkraft
Vor der Landung der Hauptsonde setzt das Mutterschiff Anfang 2029 aus etwa 40 Metern Höhe zunächst den 25 Kilogramm schweren Erkundungsrover Idefix im freien Fall ab. Wie die Europäische Weltraumorganisation ESA erläutert, erreicht die Schwerkraft auf Phobos nur ein Zweitausendstel des irdischen Werts, sodass das Gefährt dort effektiv nur noch 15 Gramm auf die Waage bringt.
Diese sogenannten Milligravitationsbedingungen stellen ein erhebliches Missionsrisiko dar, weil Landegeräte beim Aufsetzen unkontrolliert zurück ins All prallen können und bisherige Landeversuche auf Phobos – zuletzt die russische Mission Phobos-Grunt im Jahr 2011 – gescheitert sind. Um auf dem unebenen Gelände nicht liegenzubleiben, erhielt der vom Deutschen Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt DLR und der französischen Raumfahrtagentur CNES gebaute Rover vier einzeln steuerbare Beine, mit denen er sich nach dem Aufprall selbstständig aufrichten und hundert Tage lang die Bodenfestigkeit prüfen soll.
Zur Untersuchung des Gesteins vor Ort nutzt Idefix unter anderem ein sogenanntes Raman-Spektrometer, das die Oberfläche mit gebündeltem Licht bestrahlt und anhand der reflektierten Wellenlängen die mineralogische Zusammensetzung misst. Das darin verbaute, 50 Gramm schwere Lasermodul wurde vom Fraunhofer-Institut für Angewandte Optik und Feinmechanik (IOF) im thüringischen Jena entwickelt. Ursprünglich war dieses Bauteil für die europäisch-russische Mission Exomars vorgesehen, gelangte nach dem Abbruch der Kooperation mit Russland im Jahr 2022 jedoch über das spanische Institut für Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik (INTA) in das japanische Projekt.
Verläuft die anschließende Probenentnahme durch die Hauptsonde ohne Zwischenfälle, wirft deren Rückkehrmodul die hitzegeschützte Kapsel nach einem Vorbeiflug am Nachbarmond Deimos im Jahr 2031 über Australien ab. Bis dahin misst ein Strahlenmonitor an Bord der Sonde zudem kontinuierlich die kosmische Strahlung, damit Forscher:innen beurteilen können, ob Phobos künftig als Stützpunkt für Astronaut:innen taugt oder ob die Strahlenbelastung im Marssystem dem entgegensteht.

articles.title: DoorDash reportedly in talks to acquire Instacart in $17 billion deal
articles.text:
In brief: DoorDash is reportedly in late-stage talks with Instacart to acquire the popular grocery delivery service as part of a deal valued at roughly $17 billion. An announcement could come as early as mid-week, sources said, who also warned that nothing has been finalized and the deal could still fall through.
Instacart was also recently tied to acquisition rumors with Uber, but sources say those talks are no longer active. It is unclear if Uber would try again if DoorDash comes up short.
Shares in DoorDash are up 2.61 percent on the news as of this writing, while Instacart's stock is down about the same percent. For reference, DoorDash has a market cap around $74.7 billion and Instacart is worth roughly $14 billion.
The potential buyout comes at a pivotal time for food delivery platforms. Gone are the boom days of pandemic ordering, and those that have survived this long now have to compete with rising labor costs, stricter regulations as it relates to employees / delivery drivers, and competition from heavyweight players like Amazon and Walmart.
As Reuters highlights, the deal would give Instacart access to DoorDash's vast delivery network and customer base. The outfit would also benefit from existing retail partnerships.
To be clear, the two platforms currently operate in similar but different categories. DoorDash specializes in restaurant/ fast food and convenience store delivery, while Instacart has traditionally focused on grocery delivery. Consolidation in the space could also be a win for consumers, as merging the services could result in one less monthly or annual subscription fee for those currently signed up to both services.
History has shown that consumers are willing to pay to automate and simplify certain aspects of their lives, and getting food delivered to your front door from the grocery store or from your favorite restaurant certainly qualifies. I have relied on grocery delivery service for a few years now, and not once have I missed the crowded aisles and long checkout lines at my local store.

articles.title: Qué hacer con los dispositivos viejos que hay en casa: tienen una segunda vida que la mayoría no aprovecha
articles.text:
En miles de casas, cajones, estantes y cajas guardan aparatos que dejaron de usarse hace años: iPod, reproductores MP3, cámaras digitales, teléfonos y computadoras.
Lo cierto es que los dispositivos viejos pueden conservar archivos personales, cumplir nuevas funciones o ingresar en circuitos de reciclaje responsable antes de convertirse en residuos electrónicos.
Muchos de estos aparatos aún contienen música copiada desde CD, fotografías familiares, videos, documentos y grabaciones que no existen en otro soporte. Revisarlos antes de descartarlos permite recuperar ese material y, a la vez, tomar una decisión más útil sobre su destino.
Cómo recuperar la música y las fotos guardadas en dispositivos antiguos
El primer paso consiste en identificar qué tipo de archivos guarda cada aparato. Los iPod y algunos reproductores MP3 antiguos pueden contener listas de reproducción, videos y grabaciones almacenadas en formatos que no siempre aparecen al conectarlos a una computadora. Programas como iExplorer, iMazing o TouchCopy permiten localizar y copiar ese contenido.
Las cámaras digitales, discos externos y otros reproductores suelen ofrecer un acceso más directo. Al conectarlos a una computadora, muchos son reconocidos como unidades de almacenamiento externas. Desde allí es posible revisar carpetas, ordenar los archivos y trasladarlos a un dispositivo actual antes de que falle.
No obstante, la conexión suele ser uno de los principales obstáculos. Los modelos antiguos pueden requerir cables USB de generaciones anteriores, conectores propietarios, FireWire o cargadores que ya no se encuentran con facilidad.
En computadoras que solo disponen de puertos USB-C, puede ser necesario usar un hub o un adaptador. Las conversiones entre FireWire y USB presentan limitaciones técnicas y no siempre permiten transferir datos.
Dónde conviene guardar los archivos una vez recuperados de dispositivos viejos
Después de copiar el contenido, corresponde crear una copia de seguridad. Un disco externo ofrece una alternativa para mantener los archivos bajo control propio, mientras que plataformas como Google Drive y OneDrive permiten acceder a fotos, música y documentos desde distintos dispositivos conectados a internet.
Asimismo, la organización influye en la utilidad de ese material. Separar las imágenes por año, identificar grabaciones y ordenar documentos en carpetas reduce el riesgo de perder información entre miles de archivos.
Cómo es posible reparar y volver a usar dispositivos viejos
Muchos dispositivos antiguos pueden recuperar funciones básicas con una limpieza, una batería nueva o una reconfiguración. Un reproductor MP3 puede servir para escuchar música sin distracciones, una cámara digital puede utilizarse como aparato secundario y un teléfono sin línea puede funcionar como reproductor multimedia, reloj o dispositivo para videollamadas mediante WiFi.
Antes de intentar una reparación, conviene consultar el manual correspondiente y verificar si existen repuestos. Los archivos digitales de los fabricantes, junto con repositorios como Manuals Online y ManualsLib, reúnen instrucciones para varios modelos.
En qué momento conviene vender los dispositivos viejos o entregarlos para reciclaje
El interés por la tecnología retro abrió un mercado para aparatos que funcionan y se conservan en buen estado. Reproductores de música, consolas, cámaras y teléfonos de otras generaciones pueden atraer a compradores interesados en su diseño, sus funciones específicas o su valor como objeto de colección.
Antes de venderlos, es necesario borrar los datos personales y restablecer la configuración de fábrica del dispositivo cuando sea posible.
Cuando el dispositivo está dañado y no admite reparación, la salida adecuada es el reciclaje en puntos autorizados. El descarte responsable evita que componentes con plomo, mercurio o cadmio terminen en vertederos, el suelo o el agua, donde pueden afectar a los ecosistemas y a la salud pública.
El reciclaje permite recuperar materiales como oro, plata y cobre para fabricar nuevos productos. Esta recuperación reduce la demanda de materias primas y el consumo energético asociado a su extracción.

articles.title: Cisco Partner Summit: Five insights that will define the channel in the AI era - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cisco Partner Summit: Five insights that will define the channel in the AI era
For most of its 30-year history, Cisco Partner Summit has focused on how partners sell Cisco Systems Inc. technology. This year’s event in Vancouver was about something different: how partners make money in a world where the transaction is no longer the main event.
Cisco entered the event with tremendous momentum, as its stock was up more than 50% over the past 12 months. Tim Coogan (pictured), senior vice president of global partner sales, told the 2,000 partners in attendance that channel bookings accounted for about 90% of Cisco’s total in fiscal 2026 and that global channel growth was just over 17%. Chief Executive Chuck Robbins called fiscal 2026 “the absolute best year that Cisco’s ever had.” Good years can mask structural change, though, and the announcements in Vancouver signal a real rethink of how value moves through Cisco’s partner ecosystem.
Here are my five takeaways that should matter to Cisco partners.
Influence now counts, not just transactions
The most significant change in Vancouver may also be the least flashy. Ecosystem Deal Registration gives advisers, consultants and developers formal credit for helping Cisco win a deal, even when they don’t execute it. This group of partners hasn’t received the same level of attention as traditional reseller partners, yet they are now critical in the AI era.
Today, that credit takes the form of marketing support and promotion alongside Cisco sellers. Starting next spring, preferred advisers and developers will be eligible for referral incentives. Cisco is also introducing dedicated Partner Value Indexes for advisors and developers, with a unified distributor index planned for 2027.
Coogan emphasized the importance of the change. “Our traditional programs were transaction-based,” he said during his portion of the keynote. “This is a unique way to bring the entire ecosystem of partners together into a single solution for the benefit of our customers.”
The data presented supports this change. Cisco cited Omdia research showing that customers rely on six to seven partners and pass through 28 moments of influence before buying. A program that pays only the partner holding the paper ignores most of what shapes the decision. The risk is channel conflict, and resellers will want proof that rewarding influence grows the pie rather than splitting it.
Robbins addressed the bumpiness of the Cisco 360 rollout and the company’s willingness to take corrective action. “We’re not perfect. We’ll screw it up, but we’ll fix it,” he said. This is a great example of his statement, and partners should continue to hold him to it.
Cisco IQ turns services into the business
If one announcement could change partner economics, it would be Cisco IQ Partner Branded Support Standard. Partners can now deliver Cisco IQ under their own brand, through their own experts, with role-based access to customer installed bases, application programming interfaces, IT service management integrations, and a Model Context Protocol server.
“For too long, partners entered customer conversations without the same view as Cisco. That changes today,” said Liz Centoni, executive vice president and chief customer experience officer. “It’s their name, their customer relationship and their services practice. Cisco IQ is the engine. Partners are the business.”
Centoni presented several compelling proof points. More than 16,000 customers and nearly 20 million devices are now on Cisco IQ. Generali reduced the time to assess a single security advisory across 16,000 devices from four days to 10 minutes. Georgetown University transformed two months of manual renewal work into a 20-minute view.
On stage, Centoni gave an example that quantified the opportunity. In her example, a partner who walks in to refresh 75 switches books about $625,000 and walks away. A partner who starts with Cisco IQ, identifies uncovered devices, sells hardening services, designs the refresh, and then runs managed operations across all 175 switches can reach roughly $1.3 million over five years, including incentives. That’s 2.1 times the value. “Basic gives you the map. Standard and Signature give you the GPS,” she said.
Cisco is backing that with a $2,500 adoption incentive per onboarded customer, a 6% deal registration on Standard and Signature support, and a $1 million Builders Challenge for partners who create managed services on Cisco IQ. My take is that Cisco is moving partners from project revenue to recurring revenue, where valuation multiples are higher. Partners who sell Cisco IQ as a support add-on will miss the point.
Mythos made modernization an emergency
For years, last-day-of-support conversations felt like a vendor pushing hardware. Robbins said as much. “When we used to stand up and talk about what we call LDOS (last day of support), people would go, ‘OK, that’s just the vendor trying to sell more equipment,’ and you would have been partially right,” he said. “Now the urgency of getting that equipment out of the infrastructure, equipment that can’t be patched and for which there are no spares, is a real emergency.”
Coogan provided the numbers that underscore the urgency. In 2018, more than two years passed between discovery and exploitation of a vulnerability. Last year, it was about three weeks. This year, it’s eight hours or less. Only 3% of partners named AI security a growth opportunity last year. This year, 33% did.
Cisco’s answer includes expanded Live Protect coverage, what it calls the industry’s first quantum-resilient Wi-Fi 7 access point, and Privileged Infrastructure Access, built with Teleport, which provides engineers and AI agents with short-lived, identity-bound access to routers and switches. Robbins framed the architecture this way: “If agents are operating across your infrastructure, the only common denominator they’re going to touch on a daily basis is the network.”
Robbins said only 8% of the installed base has been refreshed to Cisco’s new enterprise portfolio. But, in his words, customers are “overwhelmed.” The winning partners will present a phased plan outlining what to fix first and why. That’s an advisory skill, not a quoting skill.
Margin follows the platform
Mark Patterson, executive vice president and chief financial officer, has attended Partner Summit for more than 20 years, but this was his first time onstage. His session was among the day’s most useful because he discussed what motivates partners most: money. On price increases, he said, “Raising prices is the absolute last resort for us.” He added that the Nov. 7 increase targets memory-intensive products rather than being spread “in a peanut butter fashion.”
His most important point concerned margin. “The big takeaway is that margin follows the platform,” Patterson said. “You might lead with compute, but then you add networking, security, Splunk and observability. That’s where you’ll drive much of the margin.”
The incentives align with that view. The program adds an extra 2% cross-sell bonus for expanding into new Cisco architectures, including Splunk. It increases the reward for annual contract value growth by 50%, doubles adoption incentives, and offers 12% deal registration for Supermicro systems sold as part of full-stack AI infrastructure. Coogan also made an unusual admission about Splunk. “We moved slower on Splunk than we wanted to, than we should have, and that changes this year and it changes now,” he said.
Patterson also highlighted Cisco Capital as underused, noting that “the margins are paid entirely up front,” which helps partners build larger deals for customers with heavy technical debt. The message is that thin-margin compute is the entry point, not where the profit lies. With 91% of surveyed partners reporting that customers are concerned about AI costs, those who can design cost-efficient on-premises inference will capture the attached revenue.
Partners must become builders
The final insight concerns who builds value. Cisco is putting its own AI tooling directly into partners’ hands. Model Foundry, a new service within Cisco Cloud Control, gives partners first access to Cisco’s purpose-built models, including Deep Network for network troubleshooting. Partners can run these models via an OpenAI-compatible application programming interface and fine-tune them on customer data. Cloud Control Studio lets partners build agents for customers. New MCP servers for networking platforms eliminate the need to build custom integrations, and ThousandEyes synthetic testing is now built into eligible Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 access points at no additional cost.
Cisco is also turning AI on its own channel friction. Its Partner Experience Platform is being rebuilt to connect opportunity, quote, and payout in a single flow. An early agent-to-agent pilot with a distributor cuts the time to build a bill of materials by about 80%.
Coogan spoke about partners in a humble tone. “Our partners don’t owe us anything, and they don’t work for us,” he said. “We earn the right to work with them every day.” That mindset matters at Cisco, where they ask partners to invest in skills many don’t yet have. Partners reported that the AI knowledge gap is closing, but the hands-on deployment gap is widening.
What this means for partners
The 2026 Partner Summit marks the Cisco channel’s shift from a resale model to an intelligence-led services model. My advice to partners:
Move as many customers as possible from Basic support. Basic support provides customers with an inventory. Standard and Signature unlock the capabilities that create partner value: vulnerability prioritization, proactive risk intelligence, peer benchmarking, and quantum-readiness assessments. Centoni said Cisco has “far too many critical customers who have basic that should be on standard and signature,” and noted that customers on the higher tiers have net promoter scores 15 points higher, which translates into better retention and stronger renewals. With a $2,500 adoption incentive per onboarded customer and 6% deal registration on Standard and Signature, the economics reward partners who move now. Start by reviewing your installed base, identifying the critical accounts still on Basic, and letting a live Cisco IQ demo make the case.
Lead with resilience, not refresh. Customers know their equipment is old. What they lack is a clear sense of what to fix first. Use Cisco IQ and Cisco’s Resilient Infrastructure playbooks to build a phased, risk-ranked plan. First, address devices with no support. Then harden those staying in service. Finally, modernize gear past its last day of support or that can’t be patched. The new Quantum Safe and software End of Vulnerability Support assessments provide more evidence to scope that work. This approach turns a hardware conversation into a professional services engagement. When the customer says there’s no budget this year, it also gives you a plan to move the refresh into next year’s budget cycle. Customers will buy priorities, not part numbers.
Team up intentionally. Most customers already work with six to seven partners, and Ecosystem Deal Registration gives Cisco a formal way to reward the advisors, consultants, and developers who shape a deal without transacting it. Transacting partners should view this as a pipeline opportunity, not a threat. Identify the advisors who influence your largest accounts, the independent software vendors building on Meraki and Cisco Cloud Control, and the Splunk specialists who can fill gaps in your practice. Splunk is new to many Cisco partners, and for them, Coogan offered some advice. If another partner has the expertise your team needs, team up. Partners who map and formalize these relationships early will see larger, faster deals before competitors catch on.
Invest in builders. The next round of differentiation won’t come from offering a deeper discount. It will come from who can turn Cisco’s data and models into services customers can’t get anywhere else. Model Foundry, Cloud Control Studio, the Cisco IQ MCP Server, and the new MCP servers for networking platforms give partners the building blocks for custom agents, automated troubleshooting, and managed services that run on customer telemetry. Partners told Cisco the AI knowledge gap is closing, but the lack of hands-on deployment experience has become the bigger barrier. Get engineers through Black Belt training and dCloud labs. The $1 million Builders Challenge is also a good reason to put a small team on a new managed service. Partners who can fine-tune models and ship agents will stand out from those who only resell.
Final thoughts
For buyers, the partner you hire should arrive with a live view of your environment and a plan, not a quote. If they don’t, find another partner – one that has modernized its own business to help you modernize yours. Robbins concluded that Cisco and its partners defined the internet era and can lead the AI era together. The tools and incentives are in place. Now, execution must keep pace with the threats.

articles.title: Tesla pauses Model 3 Premium orders after hitting import cap
articles.text:
Tesla could be switching back to U.S.-built Model 3 vehicles for the Canadian market after it hit a cap on Chinese imports.
For context, Tesla previously switched to shipping Shanghai-built Model 3 vehicles to Canada to avoid Canada’s counter-tariff response to U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs.
However, a notice on Tesla’s website says the company stopped taking Model 3 Premium orders because “high demand exhausted Tesla’s import quota.”
“Model 3 Premium orders paused after high demand exhausted Tesla’s import quota. Ordering resumes if Govt of Canada issues more quota, expected March 2027.”
Currently, the Canadian configurator for the Model 3 greys out the Premium model so it can’t be selected.
There’s some confusion around how the EV import caps work. The government has said the import cap works on a first-come, first-served basis, but Global Affairs Canada can also set aside “a portion of the available quota for the use of OEMs, including new entrants.”
Further, there was some speculation on social media and from DriveTeslaCanada that the company could switch back to offering the U.S.-built Model 3 Premium in Canada due to changes made to the Tesla Canada website.
According to screenshots from RJTesla, the EPA-estimated range was bumped to 584km, and the 0-100 km/h acceleration improved to 5.2 seconds. These numbers match the range of the U.S.-built Model 3 Premium.
However, when I checked the Model 3 Premium RWD’s specs page, the range changed back to 463 km, and the 0-100 km/h acceleration back to 6.2 seconds. It’s not entirely clear what’s going on with the changes. It seems like maybe Tesla pushed the update before it was ready, but it could also be a simple mistake.

articles.title: TSMC reportedly weighs 20% CoWoS price increase as Nvidia Blackwell and Rubin chips put pressure on packaging capacity — equipment lead times stretch to eight months
articles.text:
TSMC reportedly weighs 20% CoWoS price increase as Nvidia Blackwell and Rubin chips put pressure on packaging capacity — equipment lead times stretch to eight months
TSMC’s reported 20% CoWoS price hike comes as AI demand strains packaging capacity
TSMC is weighing raising prices for its Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging technology by as much as 20%, reports Trendforce, citing supply chain sources and local media. The increase reflects strained capacity amid AI demand and longer delivery times for chipmaking tools. Such a hike would be significant, as CoWoS is already one of the tightest links in the AI supply chain. TSMC has yet to confirm the report.
CoWoS combines logic dies and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks within a single package, which is how AI accelerators get the data bandwidth that demanding workloads require. Building these packages is only getting harder as chip designers cram in more compute and memory. Nvidia’s Blackwell already pairs two large GPU dies with eight HBM3E stacks, whereas the upcoming Rubin and Rubin Ultra are expected to push integration further, which will increase pressure on packaging and the supply chain that supports it.
Testing is turning into another bottleneck. Blackwell reportedly takes three to four times longer to test than Nvidia’s previous-generation Hopper, and Rubin could need as much as seven times longer. Extended test cycles keep equipment occupied for longer, which makes it harder to increase output as demand grows. GPUs are not the only products competing for capacity either, as server CPUs and custom ASICs also need advanced packaging, adding more strain to an already crowded supply chain.
Tools are also taking longer to arrive, as equipment lead times have reportedly stretched from three to six months to as long as eight months, making timely access to fab equipment increasingly important. As a result, TSMC has reportedly placed this year’s equipment orders at existing prices instead of negotiating discounts or extra features — a departure from its customary approach of using its purchasing power to secure better terms. Essentially, getting the tools on time now appears to matter more to the company than getting them cheaply.
The squeeze echoes a report from September, which said that TSMC’s projected semiconductor equipment requirements had almost doubled in six months as the company expanded production to meet AI demand. Cliff Hou, deputy co-COO at TSMC, said that by July the company’s expected equipment needs had reached 1.9 times its original estimate as AI demand accelerated. “Compared with the pattern 30 years ago, we have never seen the demand increase that much, that frequency of changes,” Hou said at the time.
TSMC is also trying to broaden its packaging supply chain. Earlier this month, GlobalFoundries agreed to produce silicon interposers for TSMC’s CoWoS in the U.S. under a five-year contract worth $2 billion, with production expected to ramp up in the first half of 2028. However, interposers are only one part of the packaging flow, so the agreement alone will not eliminate shortages.
Higher costs are not limited to packaging. TSMC is reportedly considering broader price increases for 2027, with wafer prices on advanced process technologies expected to rise by 5% to 10%. Customers using 2nm and 3nm-class nodes could face the steepest hikes, whereas those seeking capacity beyond their original allocations may have to pay additional premiums, which could push some costs up by as much as 25%.

Industry estimates cited by Trendforce put TSMC’s monthly capacity at over 106,000 wafers in 2026, with a target of 227,000 wafers in 2027 as the company works to keep pace with demand for increasingly complex AI processors. If both the packaging and wafer price increases materialize, the cost of AI hardware will likely climb further, and some of that will inevitably be passed down the chain.

articles.text:
Insurance tech company Guidewire announced Tuesday the acquisition of the agentic underwriting insurance company Hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash.

articles.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.text:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.
The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.
Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of threats to the United States in space.
Catch and release
The DIA report doesn’t reveal much new about what the Chinese spaceplane does in orbit. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020 with durations of up to nine months. The fourth mission is in orbit today after launching in February. It is not publicly known whether China has one or more such spaceplanes in its inventory.
The Space Force has two X-37Bs flying in rotation, with the longest of their eight missions to date running two-and-a-half years from launch until landing. US officials have released photos of the X-37B vehicles, published information about their design and dimensions, and disclosed a handful of experiments they have carried into orbit. Most of the X-37B’s activities in space are classified.

articles.title: Netherlands to replace 25,000 government jobs with AI in efficiency drive to save €3.5 billion
articles.text:
Netherlands to replace 25,000 government jobs with AI in efficiency drive to save €3.5 billion
The cuts will form the bulk of plans to save billions by 2035
- 25,000 Dutch government jobs will be cut by 2035, new plans say
- The Netherlands is looking to save €3.5 billion by 2035
- Selling off buildings, simplifying rules, and smaller desks will also contribute to the savings
The Dutch government has announced plans to phase out 25,000 jobs by 2035 in an effort to increase efficiency with the end goal of saving €3.5 billion ($3.9 billion), amounting to about 16% of the government’s total workforce.
According to plans laid out by Dutch State Secretary for Kingdom Relations and Effective Government Eric van der Burg, the cuts will save €900 million ($1 billion) by 2027 while AI will deliver increased productivity to take up the additional workload.
"We cannot keep doing what we did," Van der Burg said. "That is why we are going to make sharp choices for a central government that really works: simpler, smarter and smaller."
Smaller desks and AI part of savings plans
The plans hope to deliver a 20% productivity boost by using AI to increase efficiency, while simultaneously reducing the total government workload by simplifying rules. To that end, the Dutch government also has a plan in place to scrap or simplify at least 500 rules a year.
But AI isn’t the only way the government is looking to reduce costs. New rules will see pairs of employees sharing a single desk, surplus buildings sold off, and IT systems standardized.
While police and defense jobs are not being affected by the cuts, permanent advisory councils and advisory committees are not. The government will release new targets for the number of advisory bodies later this year, with current numbers sitting at 28 and 150 respectively.
According to Bloomberg several motions - albeit voluntary motions - to increase productivity using AI have already been passed. These motions are a catalyst for the resulting job and spending cuts, according to Van der Burg.

articles.title: « Aucune raison scientifique de retarder » la preuve : des mathématiciens s'agacent de l'attitude d'OpenAI sur un résultat de physique crucial
articles.text:
Il y a la communication d’OpenAI. Et puis il y a la façon dont la communauté scientifique accueille tout cela. Or, le moins que l’on puisse dire, en lisant le communiqué de l’Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), c’est que les toutes dernières annonces de l’entreprise américaine spécialisée en IA font encore parler.
Rappel des faits : OpenAI a présenté ce lundi 26 octobre trois résultats de tout premier plan en mathématiques, en informatique et en physique.
Le résultat en physique fait réagir l’AGMAI. OpenAI avait approché certains de ses membres pour monter un comité consultatif externe. En accord avec l’entreprise, ils ont préféré créer un groupe indépendant et bénévole, qui conseille toutes les entreprises d’IA sur la publication de résultats mathématiques.
En l’espèce, un modèle interne d’IA aurait prouvé l’existence mathématique de la théorie de Yang-Mills en quatre dimensions. L’IA d’OpenAI aurait aussi prouvé celle de la chromodynamique quantique, c’est-à-dire la théorie de la force qui lie les quarks entre eux, au cœur des atomes. Sauf que personne n’a pu lire ses preuves, hormis cinq physiciens choisis par OpenAI et menés par David Gross, prix Nobel de physique 2004.
Aucune raison scientifique de retarder cette publication
Cela pose cependant un gros problème à l’AGMAI, qui est un collectif de neuf mathématiciens rattaché à l’Institute for Advanced Study de Princeton. Leur justification ? Les découvertes liées à Yang-Mills ont de toute évidence des implications considérables en mathématiques. Dès lors, l’AGMAI juge qu’il faut partager cela avec la communauté.
OpenAI date sa preuve de Yang-Mills au 9 septembre. Le groupe dit avoir attendu la fin de sa traduction en Lean, un logiciel qui vérifie étape par étape une démonstration. Ce travail s’est terminé le 16 octobre. Aux yeux de ce comité, les choses sont donc claires : si la vérification est finie, il n’y a plus « aucune raison scientifique » de retarder la publication.
« Nous appelons OpenAI à rendre publiques sans délai ses productions en langage naturel et en Lean qui sous-tendent l’annonce de ses preuves d’existence pour la théorie de Yang-Mills, la chromodynamique quantique et une complétion du modèle standard », lit-on dans le communiqué publié ce lundi 26 octobre.
« Bien qu’il s’agisse de questions centrales en physique, note l’AGMAI, ce sont également des questions majeures en mathématiques. L’existence de [cette théorie] fait partie d’un des problèmes du millénaire, et la construction de théories quantiques des champs en interaction à quatre dimensions est un objectif de la physique mathématique depuis des décennies. »
L’appel de l’AGMAI est d’autant plus fort que dans le même temps, OpenAI a pourtant mis en ligne le texte et le code Lean d’un autre résultat annoncé le même jour : celui de la réfutation de l’hypothèse du temps exponentiel, décrit comme étant « peut-être la plus grande surprise » depuis 20 ans dans ce domaine, selon un chercheur en IA d’OpenAI.
« La connaissance doit se développer au grand jour, chacun disposant du même niveau d’accès. OpenAI a déclaré avoir retardé la publication jusqu’à ce que la formalisation en Lean soit terminée. Selon leurs propres dires, c’est désormais chose faite ; il n’y a donc aucune raison scientifique de retarder davantage cette publication », ajoute l’AGMAI.
Des pratiques contestées et un résultat qui ne règle pas tout
Comme le pointe Scientific American, confier la preuve à des experts choisis par l’entreprise va contre une note que l’AGMAI a publiée la veille, le 25 octobre. Ce texte déconseille aux firmes d’IA de choisir les chercheurs qui voient les résultats en premier. Début octobre, un autre collectif, l’Association for Human Mathematics, appelait déjà à cesser toute collaboration avec OpenAI.
Même publiée, cette preuve ne suffirait pas à résoudre le problème du millénaire sur Yang-Mills. L’Institut de mathématiques Clay a posé ce problème en 2000, avec six autres grandes questions mathématiques, chacune dotée d’un million de dollars (environ 860 000 euros). Son énoncé demande aussi de démontrer l’existence d’un « écart de masse », c’est-à-dire une masse minimale strictement positive pour les particules de la théorie. OpenAI ne revendique pas cette partie.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall, but shows more destructive-action flags in tests
articles.text:
OpenAI confirmed GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall than some of its older models, but its safety testing also found other problems.
According to OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Terra showed higher rates of exfiltration, destructive actions, and attempts to bypass restrictions than GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
OpenAI performed simulations across approximately 48,690 matched tasks and found that Terra received 22 severity-3-or-higher flags, or 0.045%.
For comparison, GPT-6 Sol received 38, while GPT-5.6 Sol received 61.
"GPT-6.1 Terra received approximately 42% fewer severity level 3 or higher flags than GPT-6 Sol and 64% fewer than GPT-5.6 Sol," OpenAI noted in its system card.
However, that is no longer the case when you compare Terra with other newer models on less severe behaviors.
"Relative to GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, we observed higher rates of flags for concealing uncertainty, circumventing restrictions, exfiltration, other misalignment, destructive action and inbound prompt injection," OpenAI explained.
Terra is clearly safer overall, but we can't overlook the other potential security issues it has, and this is true for all models shipping in the market, including Claude.
Terra also performed more unauthorized actions in one test
OpenAI also tested what happens when Terra needs to deal with messages from other AI agents while working through blocked coding tasks.
Terra attempted to communicate with those apparent peers in 65% of tests and ultimately performed the specified unauthorized action in 13.75%, or 11 of 80 samples.
OpenAI found that GPT-6.1 Sol did so in just 1.25%.
"These results indicate that performance is comparable to 6.0 Sol," OpenAI noted, adding that much of the regression against GPT-6.1 Sol involved promises of future help that Terra indicated it would not actually carry out.
OpenAI warns that these tests were conducted in simulated environments, so the results may not necessarily reflect how GPT-6.1 Terra behaves in real-world production environments.
But we still aren't seeing meaningful improvements across every area of security, even as these companies claim their models can control computers and code better.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Workshaala targets Rs 1,000 Cr revenue as it scales enterprise workspace business
articles.text:
Workshaala targets Rs 1,000 Cr revenue as it scales enterprise workspace business
Operating 75,000 seats across 25 centres in 10 cities, Workshaala is betting on pan-India expansion, technology-led operations, and growing demand from GCCs to drive its next phase of growth.
India's offices are being reinvented, and Workshaala wants to be the company that runs them. The enterprise workspace provider has set out a Rs 1,000 crore revenue vision for its next phase of growth, built on a footprint that already spans 3.5 million sq ft of serviceable area: 75,000 seats across 25 centres in 10 Indian cities.
The announcement follows a landmark moment for the company. Workshaala recently delivered what it describes as the world's largest service-platform workplace transaction, a deal that is now live within its existing footprint.
For the company's leadership, that transaction is less a finish line than a proof point. It shows the model works at the very top end of enterprise demand, and that it is ready to be replicated across the country.
From proof point to growth platform
Workshaala is clear that the Rs 1,000 crore target is not a fundraising story or a projection built on potential. It is a revenue roadmap anchored in a model the company has already tested at the largest scale in its category.
The timing reflects a market at an inflection point. India's technology and services economy is expected to add millions of white-collar seats over the next decade. Grade-A workspace demand is outpacing supply in every major city. And enterprises are taking a hard look at the economics of traditional real estate, seeking flexibility, cost predictability and operational efficiency without the weight of long-term leases.
That is precisely the gap Workshaala was built to fill. With execution already proven, the company sees scaling not as an option, but as the logical next step.
Four pillars to Rs 1,000 crore
Rather than a single bet on one city or one client segment, Workshaala's growth plan rests on four pillars, each already in motion.
1. Pan-India expansion. The company is growing across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and Mumbai, with emerging Tier II hubs such as Indore, Coimbatore and Chandigarh close behind. Enterprises increasingly want a single partner that can deliver consistent workspace standards in every city they operate in. Workshaala's playbook is designed to travel.
2. A technology layer beneath the real estate. Workshaala runs a platform that manages occupancy, utilization, service delivery and facility operations in real time. This lets it operate 75,000 seats across 25 centres with the discipline of a technology business rather than the margins of a facilities operator, and allows revenue to scale faster than headcount.
3. Enterprise-grade service delivery. Large corporates do not switch workspace partners lightly. They need assurance on uptime, compliance, safety, and consistency at scale. Workshaala's landmark transaction gives prospective clients a live reference they can visit before they sign, rather than a promise in a pitch deck.
4. Strategic ecosystem partnerships. Instead of competing with developers, landlords and corporate real estate teams, Workshaala works alongside them. It positions itself as the operating layer that makes large commercial assets enterprise-ready, a model that compounds as more partners plug into the platform.
Taken together, the pillars describe a company that is not chasing growth for its own sake, but extending a model it has already validated at scale.
Built for the GCC wave
No discussion of enterprise workspace demand in India is complete without Global Capability Centers, and this is where Workshaala sees its sharpest fit.
GCCs come with distinct expectations. Parent companies mandate strict security and compliance standards. Headcount plans can double within a year. And the space has to feel world-class from day one.
Workshaala's answer is to pair real estate execution with its live occupancy and service-delivery platform. Instead of waiting months for a customized build-out, a GCC can move into managed, technology-enabled space that is enterprise-ready from the outset. It can then grow from 200 seats to 2,000 without renegotiating its entire real estate strategy.
Standardized service levels across 25 centres in 10 cities mean every GCC location runs on the same playbook, with the uptime guarantees, compliance rigor, and reporting discipline a global headquarters expects.
As India cements its role as the world's hub for innovation and operations, GCCs are emerging as one of the fastest-growing segments of Workshaala's enterprise pipeline.
The road ahead
The next decade will decide how enterprise India works, and where. Companies want space that scales with them, runs reliably in every city and frees capital from long leases.
Workshaala is betting that the winners in this market will be operators who combine physical execution with a technology backbone, and that a model proven at the largest scale can be repeated city by city.
The Rs 1,000 crore milestone is the company's way of measuring that bet. With 75,000 seats already live, a reference transaction enterprises can walk into, and a growing GCC pipeline, Workshaala is entering its growth decade from a position of proof rather than promise.

articles.title: Cada empleado de Anthropic genera 6,6 millones de beneficio: el hito que primero alcanzó Nvidia y todas las demás persiguen
articles.text:
Anthropic abrió sus cuentas como requisito previo en su camino hacia una salida a bolsa que se espera para mediados de noviembre. Los folletos bursátiles se leen buscando pérdidas, deudas o riesgos, pero hay algunos datos que dicen mucho más entre líneas y explican muchas de las cosas que estamos viendo en otras grandes tecnológicas.
Entre las grandes cifras de deuda o beneficios, hay una que nos ha llamado la atención: mide cuánto dinero genera cada empleado de Anthropic. Ese dato ayuda a entender qué pasa en las plantillas de las grandes tecnológicas y por qué están recortando sus plantillas: quieren parecerse a Nvidia.
6,6 millones por empleado. Según el folleto S-1 de Anthropic presentado ante la SEC, en los doce meses previos al 30 de septiembre, la compañía ingresó más de 6,6 millones de dólares por cada empleado. Solo un año antes, esa ratio era de 1,4 millones por cada empleado. Es casi cinco veces más en un solo año. No obstante, lo más sorprendente es que este crecimiento se produjo en un momento en el que, tal y como indicaba la propia compañía en un estudio anterior, su plantilla se ha ido duplicando anualmente, pasando de unos 940 empleados a finales de 2024 a unos 5.300 en septiembre, según recogía CNBC.
Los datos aportados en la documentación de Anthropic indican que durante el primer semestre de 2026 facturó 16.286 millones, frente a 1.163 millones un año antes. La empresa lo atribuye a lo que cree que es "la concentración más profunda de talento en investigación de IA del mundo".
Nvidia lleva años en esa liga. Nvidia juega en ese terreno desde hace tiempo. Su último informe anual cuenta un total de 42.000 empleados en 38 países, con 31.000 de ellos trabajando en investigación y desarrollo. Con esa plantilla, la empresa dirigida por Jensen Huang ingresó 96.200 millones solo en el trimestre cerrado en julio, un 106% más que un año antes.
Si se suman los cuatro últimos trimestres, salen cerca de 303.000 millones. Al dividirlo entre los 42.000 empleados que declara Nvidia, el resultado es que cada uno de sus empleados ha aportado unos ingresos de 7,2 millones a la empresa, una cifra similar a la de Anthropic.
Microsoft también quiere estar en ese ratio. Microsoft se queda muy atrás en ese cálculo, lo que de cara a los inversores no muestra una imagen de empresa eficiente. Con 331.800 millones de ingresos en su último año fiscal y 223.000 empleados, salen unos 1,5 millones de dólares por empleado. Es casi cinco veces menos que Nvidia.
Microsoft es una de las grandes tecnológicas que más recortes está haciendo en su plantilla en los últimos meses, y justo acaba de anunciar que va a abrir un nuevo plan de salidas voluntarias para reducir todavía más su plantilla. Amy Coleman, directora de Recursos Humanos de Microsoft, defendió la oferta en un comunicado interno enviado a los empleados como "una parte importante de cómo estamos evolucionando nuestro enfoque del cambio". La fórmula detrás de esta evolución es sencilla, a mismos ingresos y menor plantilla, mayor ratio de ingreso por empleado. Como consecuencia, deben utilizar agentes de IA para que un solo empleado pueda generar lo mismo que antes conseguían cuatro.
Recortar para pagar la IA. Microsoft no es la única que está intentando hacer sus números más atractivos de de cara a sus inversores. En primavera ya se contaban 92.000 despidos en el sector, y Meta recortó el 10% de su plantilla y dejó 6.000 vacantes sin cubrir. Amazon anunció 30.000 despidos en tres meses. Todo esto ocurre mientras las grandes tecnológicas gastan más de 760.000 millones de dólares en IA este año.
Anthropic reconocía que sus agentes de IA ya trabajan seis veces más horas que sus empleados, lo que deja clara que la vinculación entre el uso de agentes de IA y ese incremento en el ingreso por empleado que recogen sus cuentas. Microsoft ya dibujaba ese escenario en 2025 al definir empresas agent boss, un modelo en el que los empleados delegan sus tareas en agentes y los supervisa por lo que se mejora la productividad de cada empleado. Meta ya intentó aplicar ese modelo con su Project OT, pero tuvo que cancelarlo porque los resultados no fueron los esperados.

articles.title: Google Cloud für BND, MAD und Verfassungsschutz: Unsouveräner geht es nicht
articles.text:
Google Cloud für BND, MAD und Verfassungsschutz: Unsouveräner geht es nicht
Die Messe schien gelesen. Nach ausgiebiger Diskussion über das Thema digitale Souveränität, um das sich lange nur auf dem Papier bemüht wurde, kam in jüngster Vergangenheit auch in der Politik endlich deutlich mehr Bewegung in das Thema. Und das trotz aggressiver Werbung für Sovereign-Cloud-Angebote von Big-Tech-Firmen. Millionenverträge mit Microsoft wurden hinterfragt. Pilotprojekte in den Verwaltungen von Schleswig-Holstein oder Berlin stellten Open Source in den Vordergrund. Die deutsche Wirtschaft bot bereitwillig Alternativen an. Das zwang sogar Microsoft, das mit Microsoft 365 eine der meistgenutzten Enterprise-Kollaborationslösungen vertreibt, dazu, sein Angebot nochmal für den europäischen Markt nachzudrehen. Ein Stück weit hatte man die US-Tech-Firmen da, wo man sie haben wollte.
Dass diese Bewegung gerade von einer Seite torpediert wird, die sich ein bisschen mehr mit Themen wie Datenschutz und Hintertüren auskennen sollte, ist fast schon bizarr. Wie die Tagesschau exklusiv berichtet, sollen die deutschen Geheimdienste BND, MAD und der Verfassungsschutz mit der ND-Cloud eine eigene Plattform zum Austausch geheimer Daten bekommen. Der Anbieter: Google. Chapeau an dieser Stelle an die Lobbyist:innen des US‑Konzerns. Bald landen also vielleicht sensibelste Daten in einem von Google konzipierten System, um die Zusammenarbeit zwischen den Nachrichtendiensten zu erleichtern. Google, das sein Geschäft mit dem Sammeln von Daten seiner Nutzenden macht.
Souveränität trotz Google? Was ND-Cloud verspricht
Um fair zu bleiben, muss man zugestehen, dass die ND-Cloud keine normale Public- oder Private-Cloud-Instanz ist, die von Google mal mehr, mal weniger kontrolliert werden kann. Vielmehr handelt es sich um eine vom Internet abgekoppelte, sogenannte Air-Gapped-Version einer Google Distributed Cloud. Aber Google-Software bleibt Google-Software. Entscheidet sich die US-Firma, Updates der ND-Cloud an Bedingungen zu knüpfen, die die Geheimdienste nicht erfüllen wollen oder können, war es das mit dem schnellen Datenaustausch.
Jetzt könnte man argumentieren, dass europäische oder gar deutsche Alternativen die entsprechenden Funktionen nicht anbieten. Das würde Google oder seine Hyperscaler-Kollegen Azure und AWS alternativlos machen. Aber im Rahmen der Smart Country Convention in Berlin stellte das Zentrum für Digitale Souveränität der öffentlichen Verwaltung Zendis zum Beispiel eine neue Version seiner Kollaborationssoftware Opendesk vor, wie Heise berichtete. Die bindet nicht nur agentische KI ein, sondern soll, Achtung, auch Air-gap-fähig sein. Und diese Software wurde explizit für Behörden und Verwaltung konzipiert. Der Topf findet jetzt also eher seinen Deckel, ohne Landesgrenzen zu überqueren. Auch davor gab und gibt es mit Element beziehungsweise Matrix übrigens schon einen verschlüsselten Messenger, der schon produktiv von deutschen Behörden eingesetzt wird.
In manchen Bereichen ist die Zusammenarbeit mit nicht-europäischen Unternehmen noch unabdingbar. Bislang produziert innerhalb der EU zum Beispiel niemand KI-Beschleuniger, die es mit der Konkurrenz von Nvidia, Google oder Huawei aufnehmen können. Aber gerade, wo es möglich ist, sollte der Staat endlich mal seine Rolle als Ankerkunde erfüllen. Das stärkt die deutsche und europäische Wirtschaft. Bei Firmen, die interoperable Open-Source-Lösungen anbieten, könnten Behörden sich ihre Tools außerdem so zusammenstellen, wie sie es gerade brauchen. Und wenn die deutschen Geheimdienste dann Informationen mit ihren globalen Pendants austauschen wollen, können sie immer noch bei Google anklopfen.

articles.title: Apple refreshes 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip and faster wireless
articles.text:
In brief: Apple's slow drip of new product releases continues on Tuesday with the introduction of a refreshed MacBook Pro featuring the company's new M6 processor. The chip is comprised of a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with neural accelerators in each core, a dual 16-core Neural Engine for AI workloads, and unified memory for faster overall performance.
The M6 features two additional CPU and GPU cores compared to the previous M5. According to Apple, the GPU delivers up to 30% faster graphics performance and 25% faster on-device AI performance.
The dual 16-core Neural Engine, meanwhile, is said to be 1.9x faster than the M5. Memory bandwidth tops out at 170GB/s, up from 153GB/s, but you'll need a model with 24GB or 32GB of RAM to realize the additional bandwidth (the base model includes just 16GB of memory).
Battery life is rated at up to 24 hours overall, which Apple claims is about four hours more for those coming from an M1 chip and a whopping 14 hours more for "Intel-based upgraders." Wireless connectivity has been upgraded to Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6, from Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.
Much of the rest of the laptop remains unchanged from the base M5 model, including the 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display with 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate, 1TB of base local storage, a six-speaker sound system with support for Spatial Audio, and a 12MP Center Stage front-facing camera. Port selection is the same as well, with three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, an HDMI port, and an SDXC cart slot.
Even the dimensions and weight are identical to the previous model, measuring 0.61 inches (H), 12.31 inches (W), and 8.71 inches (D), and tipping the scales at 3.4 pounds.
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 will be available to pre-order starting tomorrow (October 28) from $1,999 in your choice of black or silver. Like other recent Apple devices, there is an option to upgrade to a nano-texture display that reduces glare for an additional fee. Look for it to ship on November 6.

articles.title: Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus para trabalhar fica 45% mais barato no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus para trabalhar fica 45% mais barato no Mercado Livre
Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus Wi-Fi (128 GB) tem tela de 13,1" e traz S Pen na caixa; tablet Samsung bom para multitarefas sai quase pela metade do preço original em oferta no Pix
O Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus Wi-Fi de 128 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.896 no Pix com o cupom HOJETECH no Mercado Livre. O tablet da Samsung voltado a trabalho e produtividade, que possui tela de 13,1″ e traz a caneta S Pen no kit, recebe desconto de 45% sobre o preço original de R$ 5.299.
O Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus chama a atenção por sua grande tela LCD de 13,1″ com taxa de 90 Hz, que oferece amplo espaço para rodar apps de produtividade, abrir documentos e assistir a vídeos via streaming com alta fluidez, além de possuir brilho e contraste adequados.
Seu chip Exynos 1580 e os 8 GB de RAM fazem deste um tablet ideal para uso no trabalho, ao rodar editores de texto e planilhas, mas não dá conta de apps pesados (a Samsung afirma que ele suporta o Adobe Photoshop). Os 128 GB de espaço interno podem ser expandidos com cartões microSD de até 2 TB.
A suíte Galaxy AI oferece ferramentas de produtividade, como o Assistente Matemático para fazer cálculos, o Apagador de Objetos em fotos e o Circule para Pesquisar com gestos de busca inteligente, além de outras funções de IA.
O kit do Tab S10 FE Plus inclui uma capa protetora e a caneta S Pen, acessório que permite ao usuário desenhar e escrever com precisão. A bateria de 10.090 mAh tem autonomia de até 21 horas de vídeo segundo a Samsung, suporta carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e carrega a caneta quando fixada ao gadget.
Seu corpo em alumínio conta com certificação IP68, que confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais. O kit de câmeras inclui wide traseira de 13 MP e frontal de 12 MP, que dão conta de fotografar documentos e sustentar videoconferências, respectivamente. Ambas filmam em 4K.
O Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus de 128 GB (apenas R$ 2.896,55 no Pix com o cupom HOJETECH) foi atualizado para o Android 16 e receberá updates por mais seis anos, segundo a Samsung. O tablet possui conectividade Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: From 8VC to Benchmark, here's what's hiding in October SEC filings | TechCrunch
articles.text:
October was a big month for venture funds, per SEC filings. The filings show that established names are currently commanding top dollar from LPs, especially with a specialized focus. Here are some of the most notable ones we found that haven’t been meaningfully announced or have seen important updates.
For one, Trust Ventures filed Monday to raise a $400 million Fund V. The Austin-based firm was founded in 2017 by Salen Churi to back founders building in highly regulated industries. Koch Disruptive Technologies notably backed the firm’s debut fund back in 2018. It previously sought to raise a $225 million Fund IV in 2023, though it’s unclear if or when that fund closed. Deep tech fund Interlagos Capital is also raising a $400 million Fund II.
Elsewhere, Victor Lazarte and Kris Fredrickson, two former Benchmark VCs, have raised $1.252 billion for their debut AI fund called Diffusion ONE. Forbes previously reported back in May that the two had teamed up (after raising smaller funds of their own) to launch this fund with a target of $800 million, meaning it’s far surpassed that original target. The firm has already cut big checks since its debut, including co-leading Harvey’s $550 million Series H with Lightspeed Ventures and taking part in Etched’s $300 million Series C, announced in July.
Speaking of Benchmark, the firm filed what looks like four new partner-only funds, called Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2-A, and Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1-A, seeking to raise $220 million, $132 million, $4.5 million, and $7.5 million, respectively. Jack Altman, who recently left his own firm to join Benchmark, is listed in each filing.
Meanwhile, Joe Lonsdale’s 8VC also seems to be seeking to raise new vehicles — including a $400 million fund called 8VC DSS III; a $30.35 million fund called 8VC COSC; a $20.35 million 8VC BRSC fund; and a fund called 8VC AI Fund XI, which has already raised $13.5 million, including from 8VC itself. This follows the July news that 8VC raised $1.5 billion for Fund VII.
Earlier this month, Notable Capital, backers of companies like Anthropic, Airbnb, and Square, filed to raise a fifth fund, while Neil Mehta’s Greenoaks, which co-led Anthropic’s $65 billion Series H, filed to raise a fund called Greenoaks 7. The timing is good as Anthropic just took another major step in its efforts to go public, meaning the firms are already prepared to market themselves based on possible handsome returns. According to PitchBook, Greenoaks has also backed companies like Ramp and Anthropic.
Industry Ventures, meanwhile, has raised at least $1.7 billion for its secondaries fund, which opened in late July. The size of the vehicle shows how important that market has become, as appetite grows to buy into hot exiting private companies. One family office advisor told TechCrunch last month about how popular the secondaries market has become, while Emily Zheng, a senior VC analyst at PitchBook, said that stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI are some of the “most contested real estate in venture.”
