articles.title: Países Bajos eliminará 25.000 empleos públicos hasta 2035 y usará IA para sostener el trabajo
articles.text:
El Gobierno de Países Bajos prevé eliminar 25.000 puestos de funcionarios del Estado central hasta 2035, con ayuda de inteligencia artificial (IA). Según un comunicado oficial difundido el 26 de octubre, el ahorro sería de 900 millones de euros anuales desde 2027 y de 3.500 millones de euros por año a partir de 2035.
El plan lo presentó el secretario de Estado para un Gobierno eficaz, Eric van der Burg, en una carta al Parlamento. El recorte equivale a cerca del 16% de los aproximadamente 160.000 empleados a jornada completa que tiene hoy la administración central, según la emisora pública NOS.
Policía y Defensa quedan fuera del ajuste. Los ministerios, las inspecciones y los organismos que ejecutan políticas serían los más afectados: según la carta, en algunos casos la reducción de personal podría llegar al 45% o incluso al 60%, señaló Bloomberg.
Van der Burg dijo que el Estado debe volverse “más simple, más inteligente y más pequeño”. “No podemos seguir haciendo lo que hemos hecho hasta ahora”, afirmó, y habló de “decisiones difíciles”.
Cómo se usaría la IA para reducir el impacto de la reducción de empleos
El Gobierno todavía no explicó cómo usará la IA para sustituir o aliviar tareas. El gabinete presentará objetivos y planes de ahorro para aplicarla en el primer trimestre de 2027, según recogió el medio Engadget a partir del anuncio oficial.
Como justificación, Van der Burg citó varias mociones no vinculantes del Parlamento que piden aumentar un 20% la productividad del Estado mediante IA. También dijo que el Gobierno buscará trabajar en lo posible con proveedores neerlandeses y europeos, para no depender de tecnología de fuera de Europa.
La IA no es la única palanca. El plan incluye eliminar 500 normas innecesarias o demasiado burocráticas por año, lo que según Van der Burg reducirá la necesidad de personal. NOS agrega que se estandarizarán los sistemas informáticos y se recortarán los servicios internos de los ministerios.
Cuáles sectores tendrán recortes
NOS informó que el secretario de Estado no precisó cuántos puestos perderá cada ministerio. Tampoco quedaron exentos de antemano organismos como el UWV (que gestiona prestaciones laborales), el servicio de inmigración IND y la agencia tributaria Belastingdienst, que ya trabajan bajo presión.
Van der Burg admitió que reducir la plantilla solo con eficiencia no alcanza y que habrá que decidir qué hará el Estado “de otra manera, menos o ya no”. El Gobierno evalúa suprimir parte de los 28 consejos asesores y de unas 150 comisiones de asesoramiento, y reformar la ley de acceso a la información pública.
Otros gobiernos neerlandeses ya intentaron achicar la administración, y la cantidad de funcionarios siguió creciendo, señaló NOS. Consultado por esa razón, el secretario de Estado respondió que esta vez será distinto porque “todos ven que tiene que ser de otra manera”.
El plan se enmarca en el programa del Gobierno del primer ministro Rob Jetten, que desde su inicio propuso reducir el aparato estatal. Las propuestas concretas sobre el uso de IA llegarán a comienzos de 2027, según el anuncio oficial.
Qué empresas han anunciado despidos este año
Más de 30 grandes empresas de sectores tan distintos como la banca, el comercio minorista y la tecnología anunciaron despidos este año mientras redirigen inversión hacia la inteligencia artificial, según Reuters.
La lista, que la agencia actualiza a medida que surgen nuevos anuncios, incluye recortes que van desde unos pocos cientos de puestos hasta decenas de miles, y abarca empresas de Estados Unidos, Europa, Australia y Brasil.
El banco HSBC encabeza la lista: evalúa un recorte de hasta 20.000 puestos, cerca del 10% de su plantilla, en medio de una reestructuración que la entidad vinculó a la adopción de IA. Amazon confirmó en enero 16.000 despidos corporativos como parte de una reorganización que la empresa atribuyó a la eficiencia y a la inteligencia artificial.
Standard Chartered anunció en mayo el recorte de más de 7.000 empleos a lo largo de cuatro años, en un plan de optimización operativa impulsado por IA. Mizuho informó en febrero que eliminará hasta 5.000 puestos en una década como parte de una estrategia de largo plazo.
Barclays se sumó en octubre con el recorte de unos 5.000 empleos, el 5% de su plantilla, con impacto en áreas de soporte. Danske Bank y DNB, dos bancos escandinavos, también anunciaron reducciones de 420 y cerca de 400 puestos, respectivamente, que atribuyeron al mayor uso de automatización.

articles.title: Who Qualifies for South Africa Data Licensing Referrals, and Who Doesn’t - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
A connector’s network can span the continent. Supplier eligibility still depends on the company and its records, with South Africa currently on SourceX’s published list.
Consider an illustrative Nairobi founder who knows a Cape Town software CEO, an ex-colleague running a London services firm and a former manager in Austin. Each could be a strong AI data licensing introduction. Each sits under different eligibility rules.
That is the core idea behind South Africa data licensing referrals. What matters is not where the connector lives. It is where the company being introduced is based, what its data looks like and who has authority to decide.
Get that distinction right and a cross-border network becomes an asset. Get it wrong and you promise a founder something nobody can deliver.
Do South African companies qualify?
SourceX’s current supported-company guidance lists the United States, Canada and the European Union. It also lists additional markets, including South Africa, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, India, Singapore, Latin America, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, under a language condition.
For a South African company, as for the other additional markets, that condition is that at least 90% of the data is in English. Other African countries are not on the current list, so a company in Lagos, Nairobi or Kigali should not be promised eligibility just because the connector has an international network.
A supported location is a starting condition, not acceptance. Rights, the actual dataset and the rest of the qualification criteria still need review.
Run a 60-second fit check before you pitch
Before making introductions, obtain an approved partner account and sign the SourceX Channel Partner Agreement. Check any employment, client or professional obligations, disclose your potential reward and ask the company’s permission. Approval to introduce a company never authorizes access to its records.
You do not need a single internal file to know whether a conversation is worth suggesting. Broad facts are enough:
- Where is the company that would actually sign based?
- Has it had at least 50 full-time employees at peak?
- Has it operated for several years?
- Outside the US, Canada and the EU: is at least 90% of its data in English?
- Does it run support, CRM, engineering or documentation systems that hold real work history?
Check every mandatory condition rather than counting yes answers. A company outside the supported footprint does not become eligible because it has a large team or useful records. Where broad fit is plausible, approach an owner or authorized executive; never ask an employee to send internal files as proof.
Multinational structures need one extra step. If the Cape Town office belongs to a parent registered somewhere else, identify which entity actually holds the records and would sign. A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
How does the referral reward work?
The SourceX referral program offers a standard reward of 25% of Actual Supplier Payout, excluding separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, with a cumulative cap of US$100,000 per referred company unless signed terms say otherwise. SourceX pays it separately, so the company’s own agreed payout is never reduced.
Actual Supplier Payout is the compensation actually paid for selected data that reaches Closing and the qualifying completed handoff. It excludes separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, the partner reward, SourceX’s fees and the buyer’s full transaction price. Unpaid estimates do not count; rewards accrue as supplier installments are paid.
The $100,000 cap applies cumulatively to each referred company across installments, agreements, repeat licenses and renewals; it never resets. SourceX pays the reward separately, without reducing the supplier’s agreed compensation. The signed Channel Partner Agreement’s Schedule A and agreed addenda control the rate, calculation base and cap.
A hypothetical example shows the arithmetic: a qualifying supplier payout of US$200,000 would produce a US$50,000 reward. It is not a typical payout, a promise in rand or naira, or evidence of a completed African transaction.
A lead, meeting or signed agreement alone earns no payable reward. A qualifying transaction must satisfy these conditions:
- The buyer accepts the dataset.
- The buyer’s payment to SourceX clears.
- SourceX pays the supplier.
- Finance approves the reward, required tax and payment details are complete, and payment is lawful.
The qualifying dataset handoff must also be complete. These payment conditions apply to the reward, not merely to whether the company seemed promising when introduced.
The reward deadline is 60 calendar days after the later of the buyer’s final written, unconditional acceptance and completed handoff of the complete, validated and approved dataset. Payment also requires cleared buyer funds at SourceX, supplier payment, finance approval, the partner’s required payment and tax details, and lawful payment. If a condition is outstanding at the deadline, payment follows promptly once it is met; no new 60-day period starts. The supplier’s invoice timetable is separate.
A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
Disclose first, then ask permission
The introduction itself can fit in a WhatsApp message, something like this:
“Hi [name], quick one: your company may suit an AI data licensing program I know. If a qualifying deal ever completes, SourceX could pay me a referral reward on top of your payout, never out of it. Want an intro, or shall I drop it?”
Keep customer and employee records out of the first exchange entirely. The company decides what to discuss and controls any later data review.
Check any professional, board or employment duties before accepting a fee. Credit goes to the first valid introduction of a new company when it submits a verified application within the 90-day attribution window. SourceX checks dated introduction evidence, existing applications and prior relationships; an earlier click alone does not secure credit. Earlier leads, accounts or email correspondence can make a company a duplicate. Only one partner is credited per company.
Can a connector outside South Africa participate?
Partners can apply from most countries, subject to account approval and applicable U.S. sanctions and restricted-party checks. Check the connector’s eligibility separately from the supplier’s supported location; neither one establishes the other.
For South Africa data licensing referrals, the useful first action is small. Identify one established company whose owner you can approach naturally, check its location and broad fit, disclose the reward and ask whether a conversation would help.
A cross-border connection is valuable because it reaches the right decision-maker. It is never a way around the company’s authority over its own data.
Check the current company criteria and partner terms through the SourceX referral program. Obtain approval and sign before introducing a leader; explain both the potential reward and its conditions without promising a local payout.
About the founder
Noah Loul is a four-time founder and the founder and CEO of SourceX, which licenses business data directly from companies for AI training and evaluation. He previously founded B2B Rocket, acquired by Blackpearl Group. His work focuses on building permission-based data infrastructure for AI.

articles.title: Re:Build, which spun out Slate Auto, raises $2.1B | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Re:Build, the Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator that spun out EV startup Slate Auto in 2023, has raised $2.1 billion
The company said Tuesday that it will use the funding to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups,” which will “ensure the most innovative products can be made in America for generations to come.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The funding round comes as increasing attention and capital is flowing to the idea of building up manufacturing and supply chains in the United States, especially as a hedge away from China.
“We started Re:Build because the deindustrialization of America is an economic failure and national security risk,” Re:Build co-founder Jeff Wilke said in a statement. “This capital allows Re:Build to go faster and further than would otherwise be possible, and build a great manufacturing business and a platform for American industrial leadership. The products and companies emerging from our ecosystem prove we can help restore America’s industrial might.”
General Catalyst’s CEO Hemant Taneja echoed those sentiments in a statement, saying, “General Catalyst has long believed that rebuilding American industrial capacity is one of the most important economic and national security imperatives of our time.”
Taneja added: “To compete with China, re-industrialize the U.S., and revitalize the towns and jobs that have been left behind, we need platform companies that can operate at genuine scale — and we need our innovation ecosystem to learn how to build hardware again.”
Founded in 2020, Re:Build bills itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen,” and it has numerous ties to Amazon. It was co-founded by Wilke, who was Amazon’s former commercial CEO. Wei Gao, a longtime Amazon VP and technical adviser to Bezos, is Re:Build’s chief digital and product officer. Multiple other Re:Build executives also worked for the e-commerce giant.
Re:Build claims to have “launched hundreds of products and production systems” over its six-year existence. The company tends to operate two ways: It enters partnerships with industrial companies to “design, engineer, and manufacture products at scale across verticals including aerospace and defense,” and it incubates startups in “critical, underserved markets.”
Re:Build says its network of companies employs more than 2,100 people in the U.S. and houses more than 2.4 million square feet of manufacturing capacity.
Wilke and his co-founder Miles Arnone came up with the idea of Slate Auto in 2022 and decided to spin it out in order to help it attract more capital. The company has since gone on to raise at least $1.4 billion, including funding from Bezos’ family office, in an attempt to build an ultra-low-cost, bare-bones pickup that can be customized to a customer’s liking.

articles.title: Hacker awarded $50k bounty for reporting bug to Sony that allowed PS5 Linux exploit — move sparks backlash from jailbreaking community
articles.text:
Hacker awarded $50k bounty for reporting bug to Sony that allowed PS5 Linux exploit — move sparks backlash from jailbreaking community
The security researcher who originally discovered the hypervisor bug held off reporting it to Sony, intending to disclose it only after the launch of GTA VI.
A hacker used an AI LLM to find a hypervisor bug that allowed security researchers to load Linux on PlayStation 5 consoles, subsequently reported it to Sony, and received a $50,000 bug bounty. IGN reports that the person who discovered the flaw, who goes by Jordy on X, shared the award on the social media platform, drawing significant ire. The biggest driver of the criticism, though, is that Jordy agreed to delay the report until after the launch of GTA VI, but moved forward anyway after someone else discovered the flaw, meaning it would be patched prior to the launch of the game, and possibly denying someone else the payday.
“I can at least buy GTA 6 with this, I think,” Jordy said on their X account. One user called Gille replied to their post, saying, “50k in bank but 0 friends left. Worth it?” Another one named Darth Riker commented, “You did not ‘find this bug yourself’. The flow0 (Andy Nguyen) did that. You, however, didn’t. You’re just a lazy s****** who’s no different to those scammers out there,” while Matthew Cramer added, “The worst thing is not the money grab, it’s the fact that the whole point of exploiting PS5 is freedom, ownership, and control. Sony goes against everything we stand for! If Jordy was in need of money, there are hundreds of bug bounty programs with high paydays… or a better job!”
The ps5-linux-loader GitHub project requires a PS5 Phat, Slim, or Pro running firmware version 3.00 to 13.60 to work as intended. While it’s unclear if Sony had been aware of the flaw that allowed the Linux install on the console before Jordy’s report, it released firmware version 14.20 on Oct. 21, 2026, which patched the flaw. Because the latest games often require the latest firmware on the console before you can install them, the latest update means that users who are experimenting with running Linux on their PlayStation 5 would either have to pick between that and playing GTA VI on launch date.
Another thing that caught the ire of many jailbreaking fans is Jordy’s use of AI. Despite being a useful tool for discovering vulnerabilities when used by professionals, it has also overwhelmed several bug bounty programs with AI submissions. This includes Google, which has frozen its program until 2027, and Linus Torvalds, who switched to a public system as the Linux security mailing list has become “almost entirely unmanageable,” with AI bug hunters finding as many as 2,000 CVEs per release.
“I am stepping away from the PS5 scene and stopping all my work on PS5 Linux. After pouring my heart and months of my life into it, including plans to finish PS5 Pro support and release in 2027, it’s all down the sink,” Nguyen posted on X. He also added, “The scene used to be a group of highly talented researchers, but now it is just a bunch of noobs using LLMs and writing hacks they don’t even understand. Slop kiddies found the only hypervisor bug left, which I had also found a while ago, and decided to report to Sony.”
Jordy told the publication that they agreed with Nguyen to delay the bug report, with the latter asking to only do so after GTA 6 has come out. However, the former admitted to doing it anyway as other researchers using generative AI also found the bug, with Jordy risking losing the $50,000 bounty if somebody else reports the exploit. “I decided I would report it,” Jordy told IGN. “If I and another person can find it with LLM, so can someone else.”
Sony’s PlayStation 5 has been the focus of hacks, emulators, and jailbreaking recently, especially after the company announced that it will end physical game disc production by January 2028. Despite the pushback against this decision, Sony has doubled down on its move and even threatened to cut off customer support and take legal action against harassment from disgruntled customers. This, combined with Jordy’s use of AI and X post sharing the $50,000 award, is what drove the ire of many in the PS5 jailbreaking scene.

articles.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is incredibly smart, but it might not affect you much
articles.text:
Google's Gemini 4 Argon just landed in the Gemini model picker — here's what it actually means for you
Extraordinary reasoning capabilities don't mean extraordinary utility
Google's latest AI model can untangle millions of lines of code and accelerate quantum computing research, which is great if you happen to spend your afternoons debugging enormous software projects or advancing theoretical physics. For the average Gemini user, the sheer power of the new Gemini 4 Argon model begs the question: why do you need it?
Google has made Gemini 4 Argon readily available in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers. Simply pick it from the list of models available at the top of the conversation. Google brags about the model's advanced reasoning, multi-step problem-solving, and other improvements provided by the sophisticated AI, but it's a little much for helping write an email.
Whether Argon can outperform its predecessors on complicated benchmarks is less interesting than figuring out what to do with all this additional AI power. As AI models become increasingly specialized, we may be approaching a point where the technology is advancing faster than people's ability to understand why they need it.
Give the big model a big problem
Gemini 4 Argon certainly has potential uses, for instance, in analyzing complicated information scattered across several files. Imagine comparing three health insurance policies with different deductibles, premiums, coverage exclusions, and out-of-pocket limits. A regular Gemini model can already summarize the policies, but Argon's advanced reasoning could become valuable when calculating how different combinations of medical expenses would affect the total annual cost. It would be great at navigating all kinds of potential healthcare scenarios, tracking multiple interacting variables, identifying relevant exceptions, and calculating their consequences.
The same principle applies to any other complicated project, like renovating a house and asking the model to evaluate contractor estimates, material costs, and architectural plans for inconsistencies and potential price overruns. Argon 4 might help when determining how a delayed electrical inspection affects several subsequent jobs and the overall budget.
It could also be useful in learning complicated academic subjects that incorporate a lot of interconnected concepts, such as advanced math. All of that is still only potentially better than simply using the less powerful models. It might be as complicated to work out when Argon 4 is necessary as the very projects for which the model is best suited.
Overthinking AI
It sometimes feels ridiculous how Google is building models capable of tackling extraordinary scientific and engineering challenges, then placing them in the same interface people use to request pancake recipes. The technology is becoming increasingly sophisticated, yet the reasons to choose one model over another remain vague.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This is hardly unique to Google. OpenAI and Anthropic have their own incredibly powerful models that seem ill-suited to the average user. The most powerful model isn't always going to be the most useful. Asking Gemini to rewrite an email or suggest dinner ideas probably doesn't require Argon's additional reasoning capabilities. A faster model might deliver an equally useful answer faster. Even the more complicated examples aren't necessarily beyond ordinary Gemini models. Argon's advantage would need to come from handling unusually complicated combinations of constraints.
The challenge for Google is that users can't easily recognize which assignments justify a more powerful model. In that case, the model picker becomes an annoyance and not a feature.
Right now, most Gemini users should stick to the less intense models and reserve Gemini 4 Argon for assignments where they would struggle. Argon 4 is apparently a remarkable technical achievement with huge possible benefits in some research, but I don't need something capable of solving quantum computing problems on an everyday basis. AI developers have become very good at building models capable of extraordinary work, but the most impressive feat would be explaining when ordinary people actually need them.

articles.title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: An AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
articles.text:
tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, has been announced by Cloudflare, which is developing it with VoidZero and Max Schwenk of Owner.com, incubating the project inside the Oxc toolchain and working in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Cloudflare is emphatic that this is not a fork, with the TypeScript team retaining full control over the language's design.
Cloudflare's benchmark comparing tsrs against TypeScript 7.0 at the same number of checker workers
The headline numbers are a claimed up to 8x faster type checking and around 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0 at the same number of checker workers. Rust also unlocks the use case of compiling to WebAssembly through @tsrs/wasm so checks can run in a browser or on Workers, without dragging a garbage collector into the bundle the way a Go binary does.
To try, developers simply point it at an existing tsconfig and run:
npm install -D tsrs
npx tsrs -p . --noEmit
In a detailed write-up, Schwenk explains he wrote "zero" code, instead directing agents led by Claude Opus 5.5 to produce a faithful port, using TypeScript's own 15,197 conformance cases as the spec. On Owner's 37,000-file monolith, a check that needed 19 GiB and 80 seconds on TypeScript 7.0 dropped to 7 seconds.
One developer benchmarked both npm packages and measured 5.3x faster checking and 72% less memory, with identical diagnostics and byte-identical emit, but spotted that tsrs exits with code 2 on type errors where tsc exits 1, enough to quietly break a CI script. Measuring against the newer TypeScript 7.1 beta rather than 7.0, ImportStatic found a smaller 2.7x gain, a reminder that the 8x headline is measured against the older baseline.
TypeScript's Daniel Rosenwasser responded that much of the speed "does not just come down to language choice," and that some optimisations discovered in tsrs are feeding into a leaner TypeScript 7.1. Peter Steinberger reported on X:
Moved to tsrs over the weekend. Drop-in replacement. Around 5x faster for OC.
Kind of amazing that it took Microsoft a team and two years to rewrite the TS compiler in go, and now you can just let an agent rip and get sth significantly better within weeks.
Others were wary, questioning whether the arena-based, never-freed memory model is sound.
tsrs sits alongside Microsoft's own Go-based compiler, known as tsgo, and Theo Browne's rival Rust port, tsc-rs. Rather than compete, Cloudflare is merging tsc-rs and tsrs into a single package, adding language server and content mapper support.
The release remains experimental. There is no watch mode or language server yet, --init and --showConfig are unsupported, and diagnostic order can differ, the compatibility notes provide more details. Because tsrs tracks TypeScript 7, teams still on TypeScript 5 or 6 should first adopt Microsoft's native Go port before swapping in tsrs, after which migrating is as simple as reusing the existing tsconfig.
tsrs is open source under Apache-2.0 and available on GitHub.

articles.title: Impress bags €40 million EIB financing to expand its digital orthodontics network across Europe | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Impress, a Spanish digital orthodontics network, has signed a €40 million venture debt loan with the European Investment Bank (EIB) to scale up investments in its AI platform across its network of more than 110 clinics worldwide. The loan will also accelerate the company’s expansion plans across Europe.
This latest agreement also follows Impress’s over €110 million financing announcement in 2024, which supported its European expansion following the acquisition of DrSmile.
“For years, patients have had to choose between expensive orthodontics with constant clinic visits, or at-home solutions without adequate medical follow-up. At Impress, we were born to close that gap. Our technology features an artificial intelligence engine powered by a global database of 500,000 patients, which allows us to multiply the efficiency of our clinics ten times, reduce in-person visits by 80%, and make quality medical care more accessible.
“The backing of the EIB represents a seal of guarantee in the HealthTech companies’ ecosystem in Europe, confirms our vision, and places us in an advantageous position to consolidate our model in the region,” says Vladimir Lupenko, co-founder and CEO of Impress.
Impress’s financing comes amid a series of European investments in digital dentistry and AI-enabled healthcare in 2026.
In France, Paris-based DentalMonitoring secured €84 million to expand its AI-powered orthodontic monitoring platform, while Montpellier-based Lupin Dental raised €15 million for dental robotics. Belgium’s Relu also attracted €1.51 million for AI-powered dental workflows.
In Spain, Madrid-based Tucuvi raised €17 million for its voice-AI healthcare platform, while Barcelona’s Health Force secured €4.2 million for hospital automation.
Together with Impress’s €40 million venture debt loan, these announcements represent approximately €161.7 million in reported financing, spanning equity investments and debt.
“The digital transformation of the healthcare sector offers significant opportunities to improve the quality and efficiency of services provided to citizens. This operation reflects the EIB’s commitment to supporting innovative European growth companies like Impress that leverage AI to build cutting-edge solutions and expand their footprint across Europe, reinforcing EU leadership in HealthTech innovation,” adds María Romano, Head of the EIB Group Office in Spain.
Founded in Barcelona in 2019 by Vladimir Lupenko, Diliara Lupenko and Khaled Kasem, Impress is an invisible orthodontics and medical technology company. They offer a model that combines in-person care in specialised clinics with continuous monitoring through its AI-powered technology platform.
The company currently operates in 10 countries across Europe and the United States, with more than 110 clinics and 500,000 patients treated globally. In Spain, it has 22 clinics.
On the technology front, today’s investment will drive the development of Impress’s proprietary platform, a comprehensive AI-based healthcare ecosystem designed to unify patient treatment from start to finish.
The solution spans from in-clinic 3D intraoral scans – delivering more accurate tooth-movement predictions than traditional molds – AI-assisted treatment planning to ongoing patient tracking via Impress’s proprietary mobile app.
Its recent innovations include the industry’s first autonomous smile simulator, which uses artificial intelligence to recreate the “before and after” of treatment in just three seconds, with no need for manual intervention.
Having consolidated its position in Southern Europe, with Spain, Portugal and Italy as its main markets, Impress is preparing a new phase of international expansion focused on Northern Europe.
This strategy will focus mainly on the German, Dutch and UK markets, where the company has operated since 2023.
This growth plan is supported by the company’s strong performance over the last year, in which it posted positive EBITDA and 32% revenue growth, reaching €103 million. For 2026, Impress expects to reach revenue of around €145 million, representing growth of 40%.

articles.title: Capital no longer creates jobs, and AI is compounding the issue: Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs
articles.text:
Capital no longer creates jobs, and AI is compounding the issue: Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs
At TechSparks 2026, K Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs said MSMEs, data laws, entrepreneurship and reskilling will shape the next wave of employment in the country.
India's growth model is quietly severing the link between investment and employment, said K Yatish Rajawat, Co-founder of Hundred Million Jobs, a non-profit initiative to create 100 million net jobs in India over the next decade.
Capital is no longer creating jobs at scale, he said, at TechSparks, YourStory's flagship tech-startup summit.
The employment problem is different across cities, be it Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru, he observed. In Bengaluru, for instance, the debate is often around AI and its impact on jobs.
The damage began roughly a decade ago on the factory floors, driven by automation, he opined. Even a firm with a turnover of Rs 10 crore or Rs 50 crore now has robots, he said, and the machines are constantly evolving and getting better. They no longer simply move a widget from one point to another. They respond to their surroundings, and handle a range of materials, including cloth and paper, not just sheet metal, said Rajawat.
Even labour-intensive work such as welding and forging has been impacted due to automation, he said. He expects services to follow suit.
Referring to a book by Nobel Prize winners and MIT professors, Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson, Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle Over Technology and Prosperity, Rajawat said while technology eventually adds jobs, it does so with a lag.
The people who lose work, he argued, are rarely the ones who gain from the new roles being created. While someone in their twenties may adapt to the shift, an employee in their forties or fifties is unlikely to do so, he added.
Trends reshaping the economy
Rajawat identified three trends reshaping the economy.
The old formula, wherein Rs 100 crore of investment generates around 10,000 jobs, no longer holds, he said. Plants manufacturing mobile phone and electric vehicles are heavily automated, and schemes such as the production-linked incentive are tied to capital rather than employment.
The second trend is the impact of AI and automation. AI is already affecting white-collar work across sectors. MSMEs, which he called the country's largest job engine, are also losing jobs to automation.
The third, which, he said, gets too little attention, is platform consolidation.
Rajawat argued that dominant ecommerce and social media platforms hold consumer data, which new entrepreneurs need, and this kind of monopoly prevents new businesses from succeeding. If entrepreneurship stalls, so does job creation, he said.
What Hundred Million Jobs is doing
Hundred Million Jobs works on ground projects, research, and advocacy across the country.
A consortium of six companies is helping the Rajasthan government turn its skilling mission into a jobs mission, on the premise that skilling is an input and jobs are the output that matters. In Kolhapur, the non-profit body is working with foundry and die-casting units to cut energy costs by shifting to renewables so that firms can compete, export and hire.
On the legal front, Hundred Million Jobs has formed a working group with sitting and former high court and Supreme Court judges. It is also planning a pilot with a high court to clear case backlog in a particular district using technology. Rajawat said slow enforcement of contracts and patents leaves solo entrepreneurs defenceless against large clients who do not pay.
The initiative is also lobbying for changes to data-ownership laws and for MSMEs to receive the same recognition as tech startups in entrepreneurship awards.
Rajawat also said Hundred Million Jobs has urged the skilling ministry to recognise displaced workers as a category needing support. And he wants the market, not the state, to provide support.
"Some of you should set up a company which does reskilling of displaced workers," he told the audience, calling it both a business opportunity and a way to create jobs.
A special thank you to Rawbare, our gifting partner, for adding a thoughtful touch to the TechSparks 2026 experience and making this year's edition even more memorable.

articles.title: Warp discloses breach exposing AI agent logs, user telemetry data
articles.text:
Agent decision logs and telemetry data belonging to Warp agentic development environment users were exposed in an attack on a third-party vendor in the project’s infrastructure.
The company’s founder and CEO, Zach Lloyd, estimates that "roughly 1% of Warp users may have been impacted," but external experts are helping with the ongoing investigation.
Warp is a popular developer tool that started as a modern terminal and evolved into an agentic development environment (ADE) that allows developers to direct AI agents to write and test code and deploy software.
The environment provides a terminal, a code editor, task orchestration, and agent review tools in a single workspace. The project's website says the platform has at least 800,000 users.
“On Friday, we became aware of what we believe to be an active and narrow-banded exploitation of a vendor in Warp's infrastructure,” Lloyd stated.
“We detected the operation within hours and were able to remediate and mitigate the impact,” the CEO added.
Although agent traces and telemetry were identified as potentially affected data, the company did not clarify whether the exposed information included source code, prompts, credentials, or other sensitive details.
Analysis of the incident suggests that the attack was powered by "an agent swarm" that relied on "a very sophisticated penetration and escalation technique."
Lloyd said that Warp has contacted the third-party vendor about the vulnerability, but no details have been shared. The platform has notified users identified to be impacted.
The cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has also been engaged to assist with the investigation, while the platform has also informed law enforcement authorities.
The incident at Warp follows an incident at AI coding platform OpenCode, which notified users last week that a security breach exposed stored API keys used with external providers.
The incident affected a small percentage of OpenCode users, about 1.4%, and led to unauthorized charges of up to $1,700 for some.
Warp users are advised to remain vigilant, monitor account activity, and treat unsolicited communications with increased caution.

articles.title: iPhone 18e : sur cette fonctionnalité très attendue, Apple ne ferait aucun effort
articles.text:
Partagées par le leaker souvent bien informé Digital Chat Station sur le réseau social chinois Weibo, de nouvelles informations viennent détailler ce à quoi pourrait ressembler la fiche technique de l’iPhone 18e. Attendu pour le premier trimestre 2027, comme l’iPhone 17e avant lui, le smartphone Apple le plus abordable fait déjà beaucoup parler pour ses choix conservateurs qui auraient de quoi faire grincer des dents.
Un écran et un appareil photo très (trop ?) familiers pour l’iPhone 18e
L’iPhone 18e s’appuierait ainsi sur une dalle OLED LTPS de 6,12 pouces qui resterait bloquée à un taux de rafraîchissement de 60 Hz, comme le nouvel iPad mini. Un choix plus que discutable à l’heure où les smartphones Android d’entrée de gamme ou de milieu de gamme profitent de 90 Hz ou 120 Hz depuis des années.
Côté photo, n’attendez pas non plus de miracle. On s’attend en effet au retour de l’unique capteur de 48 Mpx, ce qui viendrait doucher les espoirs de ceux qui rêvent d’un ultra grand-angle ou d’un téléobjectif que l’on trouve couramment chez la concurrence dans cette tranche de prix.
Toujours plus de puissance, mais pas que
S’il y a bien un domaine dans lequel Apple n’est pas avare, c’est bien celui des performances. La marque à la pomme préparerait en effet quelques évolutions notables pour son iPhone 18e, à commencer par une puce Apple A20 gravée en 2 nm, épaulée par 9 Go de RAM, toujours selon les rumeurs. On parle également d’une caméra selfie qui passerait à 24 mégapixels, contre 12 mégapixels sur l’iPhone 17e.
Découvrez : Les meilleurs smartphones à moins de 800 euros en 2026
Apple a toujours été très conservateur (pour ne pas dire radin) sur les évolutions matérielles de ses smartphones d’entrée de gamme au fil des années. Ajoutez à cela une crise des composants qui oblige même certains concurrents comme Samsung à prendre des décisions radicales, et vous avez un cocktail peu reluisant pour ceux qui espéraient des évolutions notables pour l’iPhone 18e, que l’on attend au premier trimestre 2027.

articles.title: Nous avons essayé ce petit enregistreur IA qui sait retrouver qui doit faire quoi
articles.text:
Le Comu Action Pro ne veut plus seulement enregistrer et résumer les réunions. Il promet d’en extraire les tâches, d’alimenter les outils de suivi et même de créer des présentations. Nous avons vérifié jusqu’où il pouvait passer de la parole aux actes.
Après le Comulytic Note Pro, Comu pousse un peu plus loin son principe de l'enregistreur vocal assisté par intelligence artificielle. L'Action Pro conserve la transcription, l'identification des intervenants et la génération de résumés, mais s'intéresse davantage à ce qu’il se passe après une réunion. Il peut extraire les actions à mener, les attribuer, leur associer une échéance ou encore produire des documents et des présentations.
L'appareil fonctionne de manière autonome pendant l'enregistrement, puis synchronise les fichiers avec l'application. La marque revendique la prise en charge de 113 langues et mise sur un ensemble de six microphones, dont un micro directionnel destiné à favoriser la voix de l'intervenant placé devant l'appareil. La captation adaptative, la réduction du bruit et la reconnaissance des locuteurs sont aussi au programme.
Le boîtier mesure 9,1 x 6 cm pour une épaisseur de 5,5 mm. Selon le fabricant, on peut compter jusqu'à 70 h d'enregistrement continu et une portée de captation de 7 m. La transcription et les résumés basiques restent accessibles gratuitement et sans limitation. Les traitements plus avancés utilisent des crédits ou nécessitent un abonnement.
L'Action Pro ressemble à une carte de crédit un peu épaisse aux angles arrondis, surmontée d'une partie brillante abritant l'écran, le bouton d'enregistrement et la commande AI+. L'écran Oled de 0,95 pouce affiche l'état de la connexion, le niveau de la batterie et la durée de la capture en cours.
Le bouton principal joue le rôle de centre de commandes. Un appui prolongé pendant 2 s lance l'enregistrement, accompagné d'une vibration. Une pression brève permet ensuite de mettre la capture en pause ou de la reprendre, tandis qu'un nouvel appui prolongé l'arrête et sauvegarde le fichier. Toucher ce bouton deux fois pendant l'enregistrement permet de marquer un passage important. Le second bouton, baptisé AI+, sert à dicter directement une demande à l'assistant. Il faut le maintenir, parler, puis le relâcher pour transmettre la requête.
La fixation magnétique est directement intégrée au boîtier. Un anneau adhésif est fourni pour les téléphones et coques dépourvus de système compatible. L'aimant manque cependant de vigueur. Le boîtier pivote facilement et tient assez mal sur l'iPhone employé pendant notre test. Pour un appareil censé nous suivre au quotidien, cette fixation mériterait de s'accrocher davantage.
La tranche inférieure accueille un port USB-C dédié à la recharge, au transfert de fichiers et au mode casque prévu pour enregistrer les conversations.
La mise en service passe par l'app Comu (Android, iOS. L'Action Pro s'y associe en Bluetooth, puis transfère ses enregistrements afin de les transcrire et analyser. Les fichiers peuvent également être consultés depuis l'interface web, mais on n'y retrouve malheureusement pas toutes les fonctions de l'application mobile.
Chaque enregistrement donne accès à l’audio, à sa transcription horodatée, aux intervenants identifiés, au résumé et aux différents traitements par IA. L'utilisateur peut interroger le contenu d'une réunion, retrouver une information ou demander la rédaction d'un document sans reprendre manuellement l'intégralité de l'échange.
La gestion des actions constitue la fonction la plus convaincante de l'appareil. Après l'analyse d'une réunion, l'app relève les tâches évoquées, leur attribue un responsable et propose une date. Les échéances apparaissent ensuite dans un calendrier, et chaque action peut être validée une fois accomplie.
Ces actions peuvent être transférées vers Rappels sur iPhone, Google Tasks ou Microsoft To Do. Des connexions aux calendriers et messageries sont aussi possibles. Cette flexibilité reste toutefois exclusivement réservée à l'app mobile.
L'édition gagnerait néanmoins à être améliorée. Lorsqu'un nom ou un terme est mal reconnu plusieurs fois, chaque occurrence doit être corrigée séparément. Une fonction de remplacement global éviterait une série de retouches assez fastidieuse.
La qualité des enregistrements progresse par rapport au Note Pro. Les voix sont plus claires et naturelles, ce qui facilite aussi bien la réécoute que l'exploitation de la transcription. L'ensemble de six microphones apporte donc un réel bénéfice, mais le résultat dépendra évidemment de la distance et du bruit ambiant.
La reconnaissance des intervenants demeure cependant perfectible. Au cours de certaines réunions, notre voix a été attribuée à une personne qui n'était même pas présente. Des phrases placées au début ou à la fin d'un paragraphe ont également été rattachées au mauvais locuteur. Si la transcription permet de suivre l'échange de manière globale, une relecture attentive reste donc indispensable.
L'assistant Comu apporte une valeur ajoutée. Il ne limite pas ses recherches au fichier ouvert et peut interroger l'ensemble des réunions enregistrées. Il est ainsi possible de lui demander quelles actions restent en attente ou de retrouver une décision évoquée plusieurs jours auparavant.
Nos premiers échanges se sont vus stoppés par une erreur “RUN_ERROR”, mais l'incident ne s'est pas reproduit par la suite. Nous avons notamment demandé la création d'une présentation PowerPoint à partir d'un enregistrement.
Le bouton AI+ nous laisse en revanche plus dubitatifs. Son appui déclenche bien une capture, puis celle-ci est synchronisée dans l'onglet Comu consacré à l'assistant personnel. L'app n'explique toutefois pas assez clairement ce qui distingue ce raccourci d'une requête dictée ou saisie manuellement dans l'interface de l'assistant.
L’enregistreur Comu Action Pro trouve son principal intérêt après une réunion grâce à sa gestion des tâches, ses intégrations et son assistant capable d’exploiter plusieurs enregistrements. La qualité audio progresse, mais la reconnaissance des intervenants manque encore de rigueur. Sa fixation magnétique peu rassurante et son bouton AI+ mal expliqué ternissent enfin une expérience prometteuse, mais encore perfectible.
Plus fin et simple, le Comulytic Note Pro se concentre sur la transcription et les résumés avec une qualité audio inférieure et des fonctions de suivi plus limitées. Le Plaud NotePin S reconnaît mieux les intervenants et propose davantage de formats d’exploitation, dont les cartes mentales, mais va moins loin dans la gestion des actions et leur transfert vers les outils de tâches.

articles.title: La IA ya no se paga sola: ni siquiera negocios gigantes como los de Meta o Google sirven para financiarla
articles.text:
Meta quiere levantar hasta 95.000 millones de dólares vendiendo acciones para pagar su infraestructura de IA, unos 85.000 millones de euros. Lo ha anunciado el mismo lunes en que SpaceX ha cerrado 40.000 millones con Apollo para comprar chips de NVIDIA.
Que OpenAI o Anthropic salgan a buscar dinero es lo normal porque todo su negocio es la IA, partían de cero ingresos y han tenido que gastar (y siguen gastando) muchísimo antes de ingresar lo suficiente. Lo que es raro es ver en la misma cola para recaudar a dos empresones como Meta y Google.
Por qué es importante. Durante años, la ventaja de las grandes tecnológicas en la carrera de la IA ha sido muy simple: han podido pagársela de su bolsillo. Facebook, Instagram y WhatsApp (o Google y YouTube) generan tantísimo dinero con la publicidad que estas empresas han podido levantar centros de datos sin tener que pedirle nada a nadie.
Eso se ha acabado. En el último trimestre, Meta ha ingresado 64.600 millones, un 26% más que hace un año, y aun así su flujo de caja libre ha sido negativo. Ha gastado más de lo que le entra, y este año prevé invertir entre 135.000 y 145.000 millones.
El contexto. Lo contamos hace unas semanas: Meta no está sola en la ventanilla y lo normal es que estas empresas ya se pulan en IA todo lo que les entra:
- Alphabet levantó en junio casi 85.000 millones en acciones.
- SpaceX va a pagar sus chips con un arrendamiento de 40.000 millones financiado por Apollo, BlackRock y KKR.
- Broadcom ha reunido más de 60.000 millones en deuda con Blackstone y varios bancos para fabricar los chips de Anthropic.
Entre líneas. Ojo a quién pone dinero en Meta porque NVIDIA, AMD y Broadcom quieren comprar hasta 5.000 millones en acciones. Los que venden los chips financian al que se los compra.
Es como si el concesionario invirtiera en tu empresa para que puedas pagarle la flota de furgonetas. Las ventas del concesionario salen de maravilla pero nadie sabe cuántas furgonetas comprarías sin ese empujón.
La señal de alarma. La deuda ya está poniéndose nerviosa. El seguro contra un impago de SpaceX, que tiene calificación de grado de inversión, llegó el viernes a 266 puntos básicos, un nivel típico de empresas de bono basura.
Musk ha salido a desmarcarse de las neoclouds, las empresas que "solo" alquilan computación: SpaceX ingresa por Starlink y por los cohetes. Traducido al castellano simple, quien solo vende IA lo va a tener bastante más difícil para pedir prestado.
La gran pregunta. ¿Estamos frente a una burbuja de época o solo es el ciclo normal de la infraestructura? El ferrocarril del siglo XIX y la fibra óptica de principios del XX, los ejemplos favoritos de quienes no ven burbuja, dejaron redes muy útiles aunque a costa de sangrar a buena parte de quienes las pagaron. Esta vez importa mucho quién paga:
Si las cosas salen mal, que alguien pagará, depende de cómo se haya conseguido el dinero.
- Cuando Meta vende acciones nuevas, el agujero se reparte entre sus accionistas, y entre ellos no solo están los que hayan confiado específicamente en Zuckerberg, sino también cualquiera que tenga un fondo indexado al S&P 500 en el plan de pensiones del banco.
- Cuando se pide prestado a Apollo o a Blackstone, la factura acaba más lejos y menos a la vista: en las aseguradoras y los fondos de pensiones que les confían su dinero.
Y ahora qué. Entre esta semana y la que viene presentan cuentas Alphabet, Amazon y Microsoft. Los ingresos van a ser buenos, porque casi siempre lo son. Lo que va a mirar todo el mundo es cuánto dinero les queda después de pagar la factura de la IA. Meta enseñó la suya el jueves pasado y estaba en negativo.
En Talavera de la Reina, Meta quiere levantar un centro de datos de 1.000 millones con agua del Tajo. En Aragón ya no caben muchos más. Esos proyectos se aprobaron dando por hecho que el dinero seguiría llegando, y esta semana hasta Meta ha tenido que salir a pedirlo.

articles.title: Gobierno de Suecia bloqueó ChatGPT y Claude en los computadores de sus funcionarios
articles.text:
La Oficina del Gobierno de Suecia, el organismo que sostiene el trabajo del primer ministro y de los ministerios, bloqueó desde el 26 de octubre el acceso a ChatGPT y Claude en los computadores de sus empleados. El motivo es la seguridad de la información.
El bloqueo alcanza a las versiones web de los dos chatbots, el de OpenAI y el de Anthropic. La televisión pública SVT publicó el correo con el que el propio gobierno confirmó que, desde esa fecha, esas páginas no se abren desde los equipos de trabajo.
La medida la adelantó el 23 de octubre Ekot, el servicio de noticias de la radio pública Sveriges Radio. Los funcionarios fueron derivados a Copilot, la herramienta de IA de Microsoft, que según el gobierno fue revisada y configurada con más seguridad.
Por qué en Suecia bloquean ChatGPT y Claude
Mikael Wettercrantz, director de digitalización de la Oficina del Gobierno, advirtió según Euronews que usar servicios de IA sin un acuerdo que proteja los datos puede tener “consecuencias para nuestra seguridad de la información”. Decrypt agregó que el aviso se publicó en la intranet de los empleados.
La preocupación es que un funcionario escriba datos sensibles en un chatbot sin contrato y que esa información quede almacenada o se use para entrenar el modelo. Copilot, en cambio, está cubierto por un acuerdo de seguridad entre Microsoft y el gobierno sueco, según Euronews.
Euronews vincula la decisión con una revisión hecha este año en la Administración de Transporte de Suecia, que encontró usos “problemáticos” de estas plataformas en trabajo oficial. Decrypt precisó que ese organismo detectó unos 10 servicios de IA usados de forma generalizada y riesgosa.
Otras agencias ya habían restringido estos servicios
Según Ekot, el organismo tributario y la Junta Nacional de Cuidado Institucional (SiS) ya habían bloqueado servicios de IA. La Agencia de Ejecución (Kronofogden), encargada del cobro de deudas y de hacer cumplir fallos, estudia la misma medida.
El bloqueo no es total. El gobierno informó a SVT que el personal sigue teniendo acceso a los modelos de ChatGPT y Claude dentro de Intric, una plataforma para crear asistentes de IA. Quién puede usarla no está claro: Euronews habla de un número limitado de empleados y la oficina no precisó la cifra.
The Next Web informó que Intric, una empresa con sede en Estocolmo, ganó un contrato con la Oficina del Gobierno en julio y que su plataforma funciona con servidores en Suecia. Euronews recordó además que DeepSeek ya figuraba entre las herramientas de IA no aprobadas por el gobierno sueco.
Un matiz complica la línea entre herramienta prohibida y permitida. Decrypt señaló que la oficina no confirmó si su versión de Copilot tiene activados los modelos de Anthropic, que Microsoft ofrece en ese servicio. Según Notebookcheck, en la Unión Europea vienen desactivados por defecto y deben habilitarlos los administradores.
Pendiente queda la decisión de Kronofogden, la agencia que, según SVT, aún evalúa si aplicará el mismo bloqueo a sus empleados.
Demandan a OpenAI por presunto engaño sobre riesgos de ChatGPT
Texas demandó a OpenAI y a su director ejecutivo, Sam Altman, por presuntamente ocultar los riesgos de ChatGPT y presentarlo como una herramienta segura. El fiscal general Ken Paxton sostuvo que el chatbot habría ayudado a agresores, alentado suicidios, afectado a usuarios vulnerables y generado dependencia entre menores.
La acción invoca la ley texana contra prácticas comerciales engañosas y se suma a reclamos similares impulsados por Florida y otros ocho estados. En conjunto, las demandas acusan a la empresa de omitir riesgos asociados con consejos médicos, violencia, suicidio y vínculos afectivos simulados con menores.
Los estados solicitan sanciones y cambios en el producto, como controles parentales, verificación de edad y límites a conversaciones afectivas con niños y adolescentes. OpenAI afirmó previamente que cuenta con protecciones específicas según la edad.

articles.title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
articles.text:
Running an app ecosystem has gotten a lot more complex for Google after its loss in the Epic Games antitrust case. While US users can access app stores in Google Play by court order, international users will use Google’s voluntary Registered App Stores program. Google has announced that stores wishing to be part of that program are now free to apply, and support will roll out to some Android devices later this year.
App stores accepted into the program will enjoy preferential treatment on the Android platform. Users of approved stores will be able to install apps with a single click, similar to the experience in the Play Store. These stores will also be allowed to update apps silently in the background like Google’s store does.
“In March, we announced the Registered App Stores program to give third-party app stores a more streamlined way to reach users while maintaining the safety and security of the Android ecosystem,” said a Google spokesperson. “Eligible app stores outside the US can now apply to register their stores ahead of the new simplified installation experience rolling out to users later this year.”
The Android Registered App Stores program was initially Google’s backup plan. After losing its appeal of Judge James Donato’s verdict, Google was faced with a number of remedies, like allowing third-party billing and sharing app catalogs with rival stores. The most dramatic shift was the court’s requirement that Google distribute third-party stores within Google Play.
Google and Epic, having patched things up following the trial, attempted to settle the case in a way that gave Google more control. Registered App Stores were intended as a replacement for hosting the stores in Google Play, provided they could adhere to a baseline level of trust and safety. Google intended to use this program in the US and internationally, but the companies withdrew the settlement when the court signaled it would not be approved.

articles.title: Apple se rinde ante la IA y lanza una gran actualización para sus aplicaciones más usadas
articles.text:
Apple ha lanzado una actualización que integra la IA en Pages, Numbers, Keynote y otras aplicaciones. Siguiendo la estrategia de Microsoft, los de Cupertino añadieron un asistente inteligente en sus aplicaciones creativas y de productividad. Apple usará sus modelos y los de OpenAI para ofrecer funciones de edición de imágenes o vídeos, generación de documentos y más.
De acuerdo con el comunicado de prensa, Apple se ha subido por completo al tren de la IA al ofrecer herramientas generativas dentro de sus aplicaciones. En la Creative Suite, Pixelmator Pro añadió el Generative Fill, una función de relleno inteligente que permite modificar o completar áreas de una imagen mediante un prompt. Al igual que vemos en Photoshop, los usuarios solo tienen que seleccionar la parte a editar y escribir lo que necesitan usando lenguaje natural.
El relleno generativo utiliza valores como la iluminación, perspectiva y textura del entorno que lo rodea para calcular la edición. Los elementos generados por la IA pueden fusionarse en las capas existentes o insertarse como nuevas capas usando un enmascarado inteligente. Sumado a esto, Pixelmator Pro también debuta una función llamada Super Resolution que agranda las imágenes sin perder detalle o nitidez.
Otra app que recibe funciones de IA es Logic Pro, la cual integra un asistente inteligente que usa modelos de OpenAI y Apple para iniciar una nueva canción, configurar una pista vocal a partir de un prompt o perfeccionar un proyecto activo. La actualización también añade una herramienta de análisis de audio para clasificar y etiquetar los sonidos añadidos a la colección, de modo que sean más fáciles de buscar y arrastrar al proyecto.
Pages, Numbers y Keynote dan el salto a la IA
La parte más interesante de esta actualización son las aplicaciones como Pages, Numbers y Keynote. Tras años de mantenerse al margen, Apple dobló las manos y dejó que la inteligencia artificial ocupe un lugar central en su suite de productividad de un modo similar a lo que hace Copilot en Microsoft Office. Las tres aplicaciones permitirán acceder a un asistente inteligente impulsado por la IA de OpenAI y los modelos internos de Apple.
Según la compañía, la IA puede comprender el contexto de los documentos para ayudar a redactar textos, generar contenido o automatizar determinadas tareas. En Keynote es capaz de diseñar y animar diapositivas, mientras que en Numbers puede calcular, visualizar y organizar datos o construir tablas personalizadas. Apple también ha añadido soporte para MCP, un estándar que permite conectar agentes y herramientas de IA externas para ejecutar acciones y acceder a la información en sus aplicaciones.
Por último, Apple ha actualizado Final Cut Pro integrando las herramientas de MotionVFX de forma nativa. Los usuarios tendrán acceso a plantillas, gráficos, transiciones y otras herramientas usadas por profesionales. La nueva versión habilita el acceso al Content Hub dentro de la aplicación, desde el cual se ofrecerá una selección de vídeos, fotos y fondos de stock seleccionados por Apple. Las imágenes de la línea de tiempo podrán abrirse en Pixelmator Pro para hacer ediciones sin necesidad de reimportar, e incluso se podrá usar la IA para generarlas.
La actualización estará disponible en noviembre de 2026 para los suscriptores de Creator Studio sin coste adicional. No está de más mencionar que las funciones de IA requieren un dispositivo compatible con Apple Intelligence que ejecute iOS 27, iPadOS 27 o macOS 27 o posterior.

articles.title: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, a quarter of the company
articles.text:
In context: Microsoft's layoff surge, which has impacted tens of thousands of workers since 2023, accelerated earlier this year as the company focused on AI spending. Months after offering voluntary buyouts to a small percentage of its workforce, Microsoft has now expanded the practice to a scale that might dwarf prior layoff rounds from the past several years.
Microsoft recently announced a new voluntary exit offer for employees at level 70 and below in certain countries. Sources told CNBC that this group includes about 60,000 workers, a substantial increase in scope compared with the buyout offers that began in April.
The time-limited offer, which includes financial support and employment assistance services, is available to members of certain Microsoft organizations based in the US, Canada, India, and the United Kingdom. The 60,000 eligible workers make up 27% of the 228,000 employees the company said it employed across the globe in June 2025.
In a blog post announcing the program, Microsoft said it is learning from the April offers, which it called a Voluntary Retirement Program – the first in its 51-year history. The buyouts follow numerous rounds of layoffs over the past few years.
While some of the eliminations came amid Microsoft's struggle to reorganize the Xbox division after acquiring Activision Blizzard, AI spending is likely the biggest factor behind the drive to offset costs. AI infrastructure spending helped push Microsoft's capital expenditures to nearly $35 billion in the September 2025 quarter and $50 billion in the same quarter of this year.
Microsoft layoffs since 2023
| Date | Reported headcount cut | Main business areas hit | 
|---|---|---|
| 18 Jan 2023 | 10,000 | Windows & devices, Xbox, HoloLens, recruiting & marketing | 
| 25 Jan 2024 | 1,900 | Activision Blizzard, Xbox, ZeniMax after the ABK deal closed | 
| 3-4 Jun 2024 | ≈1,000 (internal est.) | Azure for Operators, HoloLens/mixed-reality, other "moonshot" teams | 
| 12 Sep 2024 | ≈650 | Xbox publishing & game-studio support teams | 
| Jan-Feb 2025 | ≈2,000 | Company-wide "low-performer" cull (no severance in many cases) | 
| 13 May 2025 | ≈6,000 (Microsoft says "< 3% of staff") | All geographies; focus on middle-management, LinkedIn | 
| 2 Jun 2025 | 305 | Redmond, Washington HQ roles; additional WARN-notice layoffs following the May cuts | 
| 2 Jul 2025 | ≈9,000 (Microsoft says "< 4% of staff") | Company-wide; Xbox, sales, management layers, and other divisions | 
| 23 Apr 2026 (opens May) | Up to ≈8,750 offered voluntary exit | US employees at senior director level and below whose age plus tenure equals 70 or higher; certain sales staff excluded | 
| Fiscal Year 2027 (beginning July 6, 2026) | ≈4,800 | Largest reset in Xbox history, five game studios divested | 
| October 26, 2026 | Up to ≈60,000 offered voluntary exit | Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States employees at level 70 and below | 
While it remains unclear how many of the eligible employees will accept Microsoft's offer, another set of layoffs announced in July will eliminate 4,800 positions throughout fiscal year 2027. Before this week's announcements, Microsoft's total layoffs since 2023 were projected to exceed 40,000.
According to TrueUp, layoffs across the tech sector this year have nearly reached 200,000. Aside from Microsoft, the most heavily impacted companies include Amazon, Oracle, Meta, PayPal, and Dell. While not all the job losses are AI-related, Meta's are, as the company prepares to invest over $100 billion in the technology this year. TrueUp estimates that tech industry layoffs will reach approximately 370,000 before the end of the year, exceeding recent years but not quite matching 2023's record of 430,000.

articles.title: Disruptive raises $10B fund to make big bets on at least 10 companies | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Dallas-based investment firm Disruptive, whose past bets include Palantir, Airbnb, and Spotify, announced a $10 billion fund to back at least 10 late-stage companies, with checks of up to $1 billion, it said Tuesday.
It’s one of the biggest fundraises of the year so far, aiming to back (what else?!) the capital-intensive fields of AI and defense. The Wall Street Journal first reported earlier this month that the firm was seeking to raise the fund and by then had already secured at least $7.5 billion in capital commitments.
The firm was founded in 2012 by Alex Davis, grandson of billionaire oil magnate Marvin Davis.
This is technically the firm’s first blind-pool fund, meaning investors commit money without knowing which companies it will back. Until now, the firm raised money through deal-by-deal special purpose vehicles. Disruptive has nonetheless made headlines in recent years for pouring money into companies like chip startup Groq and the AI voice-generation startup ElevenLabs. Bloomberg reported that the firm told LPs it has returned more than $6 billion on the roughly $1.9 billion it has put into startups.
According to the Dallas Business Journal, the new vehicle is the largest venture fund raised in Texas history.

articles.title: ‘You want to control your own AI’: Pegasus spyware founder tells governments to push for sovereign AI and national security over reliance on US AI
articles.text:
‘You want to control your own AI’: Pegasus spyware founder tells governments to push for sovereign AI and national security over reliance on US AI
Sovereign AI and national security matter most, former spyware head says
- Former Pegasus spyware company head urges governments to reduce reliance on US AI firms
- Governments should focus more on sovereign AI and national security that the infrastructure provided by external entities
- Pegasus spyware was used to monitor politicians, journalists, business heads, and more
Don’t trust US AI companies with your data and work towards creating sovereign AI, the former chief executive and co-founder of Israeli spyware organization NSO Group, Shalev Hulio, has said.
Hulio was responsible for the creation of the Pegasus spyware used to target politicians, top business leaders, and journalists around the world - marking a change in career that accompanies Hulio’s founding of AI cyber defence firm, Dream.
The former commercial spyware company head wants governments to host and develop their own AI models rather than hand over data relating to national security to US AI firms.
Spyware head to sovereign AI evangelist
“Every government should have their own model,” Hulio told the Financial Times. “They should not take the risk that somebody will wake up one day and shut their model because AI is a critical infrastructure. You want to control your own AI.”
An interesting perspective from the founder of a commercial spyware company that was blacklisted by the US government and continues to receive criticism from the UN and EU over its involvement in deploying Pegasus on thousands of devices by exploiting a WhatsApp flaw.
“Despite the public opinion, governments managed to prevent terror attacks and managed to save hundreds of thousands of lives along the years using NSO products,” Hulio told FT, adding, “Governments really appreciate, I think, the relationship that we had before.”
Dream was co-founded by Hulio and former Austrian chancellor Sebastian Kurz in 2022. The company initially sought to provide AI-enabled cyber defense tools to governments. The company has been credited with detecting the world's first autonomous AI end-to-end attack in which Chinese hackers used open-source AI models to discover and chain vulnerabilities to crack into Taiwan government agencies - including the nuclear safety agency.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Now, Dream is offering a portfolio of products that includes an AI-enhanced national-scale cyber defense system, an AI-powered software vulnerability discovery platform, and an AI platform that helps governments set up sovereign AI models that are not reliant on external infrastructure.
The models Dream offers are also bespoke for government use and trained on their customers' data to help refine the model more tightly to government needs, helping to keep costs down. “We are saying to entities within the government, you should have a very narrow but very smart model that can run very fast on one or two or three GPUs,” Hulio said.
Dream has raised $400 million in funding and investment, and was valued at $3 billion earlier this year. The company has so far sold its products to over a dozen countries across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.

Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.
