articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 27, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (October 27, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, October 27, 2026.
YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Featured stories
Naiyya Saggi on building EDT
Naiyya Saggi, founder of consumer appliance and beauty-tech startup EDT (Everyday Design & Technology), is reimagining everyday products for Indian consumers. Founded in 2025 with co-founder Vyasateja Rao, the startup offers a range of devices for the home, kitchen and beauty segments. Its products include Luma, a programmable glass air fryer; Flow, a temperature-controlled glass kettle; and SUKI, a hair dryer designed to minimise hair damage.
Saggi, who previously founded parenting platform BabyChakra and co-founded the Good Glamm Group, says EDT aims to address market gaps by combining thoughtful design with technology tailored to Indian consumers.
Sarvam AI signs five-year agreement with Defence Ministry to develop AI technology
Indian AI startup Sarvam AI has signed a five-year agreement with the Ministry of Defence to develop artificial intelligence (AI) technology for the armed forces. The partnership aims to strengthen India's indigenous AI capabilities for defence applications and reduce dependence on foreign technology for sensitive military operations.
Founded by Pratyush Kumar and Vivek Raghavan, Sarvam AI develops AI models and tools tailored to Indian languages and contexts. Its defence work comes amid the government's push to build homegrown AI systems for military applications, including intelligence analysis, surveillance, reconnaissance, and operational decision-making. The collaboration could help integrate indigenous AI capabilities into India's defence ecosystem.
Funding news
Live2.ai raises Rs 130 Cr to expand AI-led social commerce platform
Bengaluru-based Live2.ai, which uses artificial intelligence (AI) to connect social media intelligence with marketing and commerce, has raised Rs 130 crore ($14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by venture capital firm IvyCap Ventures. The round includes fresh capital to fund expansion and a secondary component that gives early shareholders partial liquidity.
Founded by J Venkat and Neha Suyal, Live2.ai helps brands monitor conversations across social media platforms, analyse trends, audit influencer content, publish campaigns and measure performance.
Maasi raises Rs 6 Cr to build a reliable nanny service for Indian parents
Bengaluru-based childcare startup Maasi has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Better Capital, alongside Antler India. Angel investors, including Rapido veteran Rishikesh SR, Shadowfax’s Vaibhav Khandelwal, Xoxoday’s Sumit Khandelwal, Siddhant Goyal, and Sanjay Ramakrishnan, also participated. Following its public launch on October 20, the startup says it attracted a waitlist of more than 4,000 parents within five days and has served over 1,200 parents through a network of more than 500 caregivers.
Founded by Aashu Manchali, Gargi Pandey, and Reshov Roy, Maasi aims to solve the challenge of finding reliable childcare by offering verified, trained nannies.
Mochatrade raises $5.5M to expand US markets trading platform for Indian users
Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in total funding for its US markets trading platform targeting Indian users. The funding was led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures, Zero Knowledge Ventures and other investors. Earlier backers include Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund. The platform aims to make trading linked to US-listed companies such as Nvidia and Tesla more accessible to Indian users.
Mochatrade lets users fund accounts through UPI and track margins, profits, and losses in rupees. Its platform offers long and short positions through perpetual futures contracts linked to US company prices, without requiring users to open a US brokerage account or own the underlying shares. These contracts have no fixed expiry, and leverage lets traders take larger positions with less upfront capital, increasing both potential gains and losses.
CopperPilot raises $390K to build AI design agent for electronics hardware
CopperPilot, an AI-powered design agent for electronics hardware, has raised $390,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Neon Fund, with participation from US-based angel investors. The startup also announced the release of the first version of its design agent, codenamed Epsilon, which is now available to hardware engineers. CopperPilot says its weekly active users have grown 25-fold since August 2026, and it has run more than 6,000 design tasks, or artefacts, on the platform to date.
The startup aims to simplify electronic circuit board design by automating tasks such as reading component datasheets, selecting parts, drawing schematics and routing circuit boards. These processes can take engineers several weeks and cost thousands of dollars before they have a first prototype. CopperPilot aims to reduce this timeline to hours, helping hardware teams accelerate product development and reduce engineering workloads.
dubdub raises $1.3M seed round led by 3one4 Capital, others
dubdub, a swipe-based trivia and puzzle app, has raised $1.3 million in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris Venture Partners. Founded by second-time entrepreneurs Kaustubh Priye and Supan Shah, who previously built and sold health-tech company Aldun to Care.Fi, the startup plans to use the funds to expand its product and engineering teams, introduce new interactive formats and improve personalisation.
Launched in March 2026, dubdub has crossed 20,000 downloads. The app aims to replace passive scrolling with interactive content, including questions, puzzles and mini-games across more than 20 categories, such as cricket, Bollywood, pop culture, mythology, general knowledge and logical reasoning. It uses AI and user interactions to personalise challenges, while letting users compete with friends, compare scores, and share their experiences.
Nova Spectral AI Raises Rs 21.15 Cr in seed round
Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Nova Spectral AI has raised Rs 21.15 crore in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors. The company is developing a quantum dot-based short-wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chip designed for drones, surveillance systems, robots, autonomous vehicles and other physical AI applications. Its technology uses indium arsenide quantum dots and CMOS-compatible manufacturing processes to target sensor costs up to 100 times lower than conventional indium gallium arsenide technology.
The startup aims to reduce India's dependence on imported infrared sensors while making advanced imaging more affordable. Co-founder and CEO Anish Priyadarshi said the funding would support team expansion and development of a field-ready prototype within 18 months.
Tensrai Secures investment from Finvolve and India Accelerator
Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has secured an undisclosed investment from venture capital fund Finvolve and India Accelerator. The company will deploy the capital towards technology development, engineering, customer deployments and market expansion. Founded in 2022, Tensrai is developing a unified autonomy platform that enables industrial and commercial robots and vehicles to perceive, navigate, learn and perform physical tasks. Its technology combines AI-based localisation, intelligent navigation and mission planning, including operations in GPS-denied environments.
The startup is also developing capabilities that allow robots to learn tasks through human demonstrations. Its applications include material movement, cleaning and robotic manipulation across factories, warehouses, hospitals and commercial campuses. Tensrai's business model includes robot sales, retrofitting, Robot-as-a-Service and customised solutions.
Other news
Aleph appoints Medhavi Singh as India Country Head
Global digital advertising and fintech solutions company Aleph has appointed Medhavi Singh as its Country Head for India. The appointment reflects the company's focus on India's digital economy and the country's growing importance in the Asia-Pacific region.
Singh brings over 15 years of experience across digital advertising, retail media, quick commerce and revenue strategy.
She joins Aleph after nearly nine years at Criteo, where she most recently served as Country Head for India and helped grow the company's business in the market.
Before Criteo, she spent nearly five years at Google in account strategy and analytical leadership roles across India, the UK, and the US.
She holds a degree in computer science engineering and an MBA.
Protectt.ai acquires majority stake in Bosch-incubated AIShield
Cybersecurity company Protectt.ai Labs has made a strategic investment in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), becoming its majority shareholder. The investment comprises a primary share issuance and a secondary purchase from existing investors. Following the transaction, AIShield will operate as an independent entity, AI Shield Private Limited (AISW), under Protectt.ai.
The capital will support AIShield's research and development, international expansion and development of sovereign AI security capabilities as organisations increasingly seek to secure AI systems against emerging cyber threats.
Skydo gets IFSCA authorisation to expand cross-border payment services
Cross-border payments platform Skydo has received final authorisation from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate as a Payment Service Provider (PSP) at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) International Financial Services Centre (IFSC). The approval follows the in-principle authorisation granted in May 2026 and enables the company to develop a broader range of cross-border payment products.
Skydo plans to introduce multi-currency accounts, merchant acquiring and collections, and payment infrastructure for exporters, investment platforms and trade finance companies operating in the IFSC. One proposed offering is a multi-currency account that will allow eligible Indian exporters to collect and hold foreign currency, use it to pay overseas suppliers, or convert it into rupees when required, subject to regulatory requirements.
TagMango partners with ClickFunnels to launch Backstage Pass for creators
TagMango, a Y Combinator-backed creator monetisation platform, has launched Backstage Pass in partnership with ClickFunnels, a sales-funnel platform whose users have generated over $11 billion in sales.
TagMango works with more than 10,000 creators and has reached over 15 million users, while ClickFunnels has a community of more than 150,000 customers. Unveiled at Funnel Hacking Live in Las Vegas, Backstage Pass will initially target the US market before expanding to India.
The platform aims to help creators engage and monetise their audiences directly, without relying on social media algorithms for visibility.
Mudrex report maps India's real-world asset tokenisation landscape
Crypto investment platform Mudrex has released The Builder’s Guide to RWA Tokenization in India, a report examining the state of real-world asset (RWA) tokenisation across seven asset classes: commodities, currencies, bonds, equities, real estate and land, credit, and energy. The report finds that India has established much of the public infrastructure required for tokenisation, with the next phase of growth depending on businesses developing solutions using these existing systems.
According to the report, bonds and energy have seen government-led pilots, while Maharashtra has committed to introducing a land-tokenisation law. In credit, market participants have explored blockchain-based warehouse-receipt lending and invoice tokenisation through the Reserve Bank of India's sandbox. However, commodities, currencies and equities remain largely untapped opportunities.
The report highlights the potential for innovations such as blockchain-based gold tokens backed by physical gold, cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) transactions and regulated tokenisation of listed shares.
Amazon to deploy 3,000 Tata electric trucks across India
Amazon and Tata Motors have announced a collaboration to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon's transportation network in India. The deployment, described as the largest electric-truck rollout by an e-commerce company in the country, will extend Amazon's fleet electrification efforts beyond last-mile delivery. The trucks will transport customer shipments between facilities, across cities and along national freight corridors. The first batch of vehicles was flagged off in Delhi in the presence of Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel HD Kumaraswamy and senior executives from both companies.
Under the arrangement, Tata Motors will supply the electric trucks, while Amazon's carrier partners will own and operate them. The initiative combines Amazon's logistics network and freight demand with Tata Motors' vehicle manufacturing, engineering and servicing capabilities. The companies aim to accelerate the adoption of electric freight transportation in India and demonstrate the potential of zero-tailpipe-emission trucks for large-scale logistics operations.
BikeWo Green Tech partners with Green Drive Mobility to scale electric logistics
BikeWo Green Tech Limited has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Green Drive Auto Services, also known as Green Drive Mobility, to jointly develop and expand electric logistics operations across India. The partnership will focus on last-mile, mid-mile and long-haul freight transportation, with the companies aiming to build a green logistics platform with a fleet of at least 5,000 electric trucks over the coming years.
Green Drive Mobility currently operates more than 350 electric trucks and approximately 8,000 electric two-wheelers. Its truck logistics clients include More Retail, DHL and Gati. The company also provides ONDC-enabled last-mile logistics services, supporting quick-commerce businesses through its electric two-wheeler fleet. The collaboration aims to expand electric-vehicle use across India's freight and logistics sector.
US wealth management firm AssetMark opens Hyderabad GCC
US-based wealth management platform AssetMark has opened a Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Hyderabad, with capacity to accommodate approximately 500 employees. The centre will strengthen the company's global technology and business operations while expanding its presence in India. AssetMark has operated in the country through an outsourcing model for nearly a decade. The new facility will bring dedicated operations and technology teams in-house to support its wealth management platform, including artificial intelligence initiatives. Led locally by Joshi Alaparthi, Vice President and Head of India GCC, the team will collaborate with US-based colleagues on engineering, operations and product management. Hiring is underway across experience levels, with the company planning to recruit 10–15 graduates from Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology as its first campus recruitment cohort.
Bounteous expands Bengaluru office to strengthen enterprise AI capabilities
AI services firm Bounteous has inaugurated an expanded office in Bengaluru as it scales its enterprise AI capabilities and global delivery operations. The facility will provide additional workspace for collaboration among engineering, data and technology transformation teams serving clients worldwide. Bounteous has operated in India for more than two decades and serves over 70 Fortune Global 2000 clients. In June 2026, the company joined Anthropic's Claude Partner Network as a launch Preferred Services Partner. Since then, it has built a team of more than 1,000 certified Claude architects to help enterprises integrate AI into their workflows. Its proprietary Bounteous Arc platform supports the design, development and deployment of AI agents. The company has more than 5,000 employees globally, with operations in Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, and Hyderabad.
IIM Calcutta Innovation Park, AIM train incubation professionals
IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP) and Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), under NITI Aayog, have conducted a three-day residential capacity-building programme for 20 incubation and innovation professionals from institutions across India. Held at the IIM Calcutta campus, the AIM-AiPEX programme aims to strengthen the capabilities of professionals supporting startups and entrepreneurship.
The initiative addresses the growing need for skilled incubation managers as India's ecosystem expands to more than 1,200 incubation centres. Participants received practical training in startup sourcing and selection, programme design, enterprise support, go-to-market strategies, fund management, legal compliance, governance and performance monitoring.
The programme included expert-led sessions, practical exercises and interactions with mentors and entrepreneurs. IIMCIP said the initiative would help participants apply their learnings to strengthen startup support in their respective institutions.
The Func. Lab launches creatine-based hydration and protein products
Indian functional nutrition brand The Func. Lab has introduced two creatine-based product lines, CREASalts and Crea Protein, designed to integrate supplementation into everyday hydration and protein routines. CREASalts combines 3g of creatine monohydrate with electrolytes and taurine per serving. It is available in four flavours, with prices starting at Rs 500 for 15 servings.
The protein range combines 3g of creatine with either plant-based protein or whey protein and comes in multiple flavours. Plant Protein + Creatine is priced from Rs 600 for a travel pack, while Whey Protein + Creatine starts at Rs 1,500. The company said the products aim to simplify daily supplementation by combining commonly used nutrition products. Founded by Sohrab Khushrushahi, Sahil Kukreja and Daneesh Davar, the brand targets consumers seeking performance and functional nutrition solutions.
GetCompanion expands in-person companionship services to Delhi
GetCompanion, a human presence platform, has expanded its in-person companionship services from Gurugram to Delhi. The startup connects users with trained, verified companions for conversation, shared interests, and everyday activities, including walks, shopping, restaurant visits, games, and hospital visits. The company clarified that its services do not include therapy, medical advice, caregiving or physical assistance.
Founder and CEO Shradha Chaturvedi said the expansion aims to make human connection more accessible to people living away from family, adjusting to new cities or seeking company during personal transitions. To ensure safety, meetings are restricted to verified residences or secure public locations, such as parks, malls and cafes. Companions undergo identity and background checks, police verification, psychometric assessments and specialised training. GetCompanion plans to expand into additional Indian cities.
COTRAV BLACK enters premium live entertainment market
COTRAV BLACK, an ultra-premium live-experiences platform, has announced its entry into India's luxury entertainment market. The brand will offer invite-only VIP enclosures at concerts, sporting events and cultural occasions, targeting business leaders, entrepreneurs and high-net-worth individuals. Its debut is scheduled for A.R. Rahman's concert at Mumbai's Jio World Centre on November 1, 2026.
The experience will include curated guest lists, private viewing areas, personalised hospitality and premium food and beverage services. The initiative comes amid growth in India's organised live-events industry, which expanded 44% to Rs 14,500 crore in 2025 and is projected to reach Rs 19,600 crore by 2028. Backed by the group behind travel management company COTRAV, the platform also envisages selective partnerships with brands and financial institutions.
Powerplay reports up to fourfold growth in platform spending after AI Adoption
Construction technology platform Powerplay has reported up to fourfold growth in platform spending over approximately 18 months among customers adopting its AI agents. The Bengaluru-based company offers an AI Purchase Executive to help contractors compare supplier prices, track material requirements and check purchase orders against budgets. Its AI Credit Analyst helps organise project information and financing documents for loan applications through lending partners. Powerplay said its annualised marketplace transaction volume increased from approximately Rs 36 crore to around Rs 100 crore over the past year.
Financing volume facilitated through lending partners grew more than eightfold from a small base, across four cities. The platform represents more than 40,000 construction firms and 85,000 projects. Founded by Iesh Dixit and Shubham Goyal, Powerplay is expanding its AI-led procurement and financing capabilities.
Digi Yatra begins international passenger trials across seven Indian airports
Digi Yatra has commenced trials to extend its digital identity platform to international air travel at seven Indian airports: Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar.
Running from October to December 2026, the three-month trial will allow Indian nationals holding e-passports and travelling on Air India and IndiGo international flights to use Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints, including terminal entry, security areas, and boarding gates, subject to infrastructure availability. The trials cover all international destinations served by Air India and select destinations served by IndiGo.
Eligible passengers can create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential through the Digi Yatra app by scanning their passport’s Machine Readable Zone, reading its embedded chip using a compatible smartphone’s NFC capability, and completing a selfie-based verification process. The passenger's device stores the credential in their Digi Yatra wallet, where they can use it at enabled touchpoints during the trial.
Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete mandatory airline document checks, immigration and other travel formalities. Trial feedback is expected to inform plans for a wider rollout in 2027.

articles.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro: Wie das Open-Weight-Modell Sicherheitsrisiken eindämmen soll – und wo der Haken ist
articles.text:
Kimi K3.1 Pro: Wie das Open-Weight-Modell Sicherheitsrisiken eindämmen soll
Das chinesische KI-Startup Moonshot AI hat mit Kimi K3.1 Pro ein neues Open-Weight-Modell vorgestellt, das den Druck auf US-Labore wie OpenAI und Anthropic weiter erhöht. Laut Unternehmensangaben kann es bei Programmierung, 3D-Modellierung und Finanzanalysen mit Spitzenmodellen wie Claude Opus 5.5 und GPT-6 Astra mithalten. Unabhängige Tests von Artificial Analysis bestätigen: K3.1 Pro ist derzeit das stärkste Open-Weight-Modell. Aber wie sicher ist das neue Modell aus China?
Der KI-Wettlauf geht in die nächste Runde
Lange Zeit lagen die USA bei der KI-Entwicklung vorn, aber chinesische Modelle haben deutlich aufgeholt. Laut dem AI Index Report 2026 der Stanford University betrug der Vorsprung im März 2026 nur noch 2,7 Prozent. Schon die Veröffentlichung des Vorgängers Kimi K3 löste in den USA deshalb Panik aus: Laut Fortune hatten Analyst:innen nicht damit gerechnet, dass China schon ein Modell auf dem Niveau von Anthropics Fable 5 veröffentlichen würde.
Noch im Juni hatte die US-Regierung das KI-Modell von Anthropic aufgrund von Sicherheitsbedenken sperren lassen. Das Thema steht aktuell im Fokus der Debatte – allerdings sind es jetzt die KI-Labore selbst, die eine strengere Regulierung fordern. Präsident Donald Trump bezeichnete Warnungen hingegen als „Schwindel” und sagte, dass eine Entwicklungspause China einen Vorsprung verschaffen könnte. Inzwischen hat er eine „Super Intelligence Force“ gegründet, die unter anderem sicherstellen soll, dass die USA ihre Vorreiterrolle ausbauen können.
Kimi K3.1 Pro hält mit der Konkurrenz mit
Das neue Modell ist eine nachtrainierte Version von Kimi K3. Bei Terminal-Bench 4.0 erzielte es 65,7 Prozent und liegt damit über GPT-6 Astra, aber leicht unter Claude Opus 5.5. Auch im Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index erreichte das Modell 55 Punkte und – deutlich über dem Durchschnitt vergleichbarer Modelle. „Kimi K3.1 Pro gehört zu den führenden Modellen in Sachen Intelligenz […]. Es ist zudem auffallend langsam und sehr ausführlich“, heißt es im Bericht der unabhängigen Benchmarking-Plattform. „Bei der Bewertung des Intelligenz-Index generierte es 150 Millionen Token, was im Vergleich zum Medianwert von 81 Millionen sehr umfangreich ist.“
Die Preise liegen bei zwei Dollar für eine Million Eingabetoken und zehn Dollar für eine Million Ausgabetoken. Damit ist Kimi K3.1 Pro deutlich günstiger als die Spitzenmodelle von OpenAI und Anthropic. Da es sich um ein Open-Weight-Modell handelt, plant Moonshot AI, die vollständigen Gewichte bis zum 4. November 2026 zu veröffentlichen. Das KI-Startup gibt an, die Fähigkeiten des Modells im Bereich der offensiven Cyberfähigkeiten eingeschränkt zu haben. Die allgemeine Programmierfähigkeit soll dadurch erhalten bleiben. Diese Maßnahme mindere zwar die von dem Open-Weight-Modell ausgehenden Risiken, könne sie aber nicht komplett ausschließen.
Welche Risiken bergen Open-Weight-Modelle?
Wenn ein Open-Weight-Modell wie Kimi K3.1 Pro an der Spitze mitspielt, erhalten Unternehmen und Entwickler:innen Frontier-Leistung, ohne von einem einzelnen API-Anbieter abhängig zu sein. Bei Closed-Weight-Modellen bleiben die Parameter dagegen beim Anbieter.
OpenAI steht Open-Weight-Modellen zwar generell offen gegenüber, veröffentlicht für seine Pioniermodelle aus Sicherheitsgründen aber ebenfalls keine Gewichte. Da die spätere Verwendung schwer abzuschätzen sei, wäre es sicherer, neue Modelle zunächst per API bereitzustellen.
Für Kimi K3.1 Pro bedeutet das: Sind die Gewichte erst einmal öffentlich zugänglich, könnte das Modell auch für Cyberangriffe verwendet werden. Moonshot AI hätte dann keine Möglichkeit mehr, potenziellen Missbrauch zu überwachen oder durch Sicherheitsupdates zu begrenzen.

articles.title: Micromania annule l'événement de lancement de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.text:
Micromania comptait célébrer la sortie du remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time en ouvrant plusieurs de ses magasins en nocturne, dans la nuit du 4 au 5 novembre 2026. La fête aurait été belle, puisque les clients ayant précommandé le jeu dans les magasins participants devaient repartir, dans la limite des stocks, avec une réplique de la boîte Nintendo 64 de l’époque. On peut y ranger le jeu, exclusif à la Switch 2.
L’enseigne a dû revoir ses plans. Dans un message publié sur son compte X ce mardi 27 octobre, Micromania annonce : « Au vu des récents événements, nous sommes malheureusement contraints d’annuler les nocturnes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time… » 14 magasins étaient concernés par l’événement, disséminés dans plusieurs grandes villes (Paris, Lille, Nice, Caen, Rouen…). Aucun n’ouvrira comme prévu initialement.
Les répliques de la boîte Nintendo 64 de Zelda: Ocarina of Time tirées au sort
Que les fans se rassurent, la réplique de la boîte Nintendo 64 pourra toujours être obtenue. Mais les modalités changent, et la boîte n’est plus uniquement réservée aux clients des magasins participants. Ce sera désormais un tirage au sort, et il suffit de précommander le jeu chez Micromania jusqu’à ce dimanche 1er novembre inclus pour participer. « Vos chances sont doublées pour les clients Premium / Ultimate », précise Micromania. 5 000 exemplaires sont à gagner, il n’y en aura donc pas pour tout le monde.
« Toutes les précommandes sont concernées (sur le site, en magasin et depuis l’ouverture des précos) », ajoute le compte officiel. Les gagnants seront prévenus par e-mail avant la sortie du jeu, afin de pouvoir récupérer leur cadeau le jour du lancement. Si jamais votre magasin venait à être fermé, votre commande sera disponible dans un autre magasin proche, selon la liste suivante.
La décision de Micromania est prise alors que plusieurs de ses magasins ont été pillés le samedi 17 octobre, en marge des manifestations. À Lille, où devait se tenir une nocturne, les vitrines ont été brisées. Des images du Micromania de l’avenue Jean-Médecin, à Nice, ont fait le tour du web notamment en raison de la réaction de son gérant, Pierre Collin, qui a tenu tête aux casseurs.
Micromania préfère éviter de nouveaux débordements dans un contexte déjà très tendu. Dommage pour celles et ceux qui avaient noté la nuit du 4 au 5 novembre dans leurs agendas, en pensant se réunir entre amis pour découvrir la remise au goût du jour de l’aventure culte de Link.

articles.title: Vous n’arrivez pas à vous connecter à LCL ? La banque est frappée par une panne ce matin
articles.text:
Depuis le début de la matinée, une panne LCL empêche de nombreux clients d’accéder à leurs comptes. L’application comme le site de la banque affichent des messages d’erreur, et les signalements se multiplient.
Une panne LCL perturbe l’accès aux comptes en ligne ce mardi 27 octobre, aussi bien sur l’application mobile que sur le site de la banque. Les signalements se sont multipliés depuis environ 9h00 sur des plateformes comme TotalBug et Downdetector, ainsi que sur les réseaux sociaux. Un incident qui, hélas, survient quelques jours après une panne historique sur le réseau mobile de l'opérateur Orange.
LCL est en panne ce mardi, impossible d’accéder à ses comptes sur l’appli et le site
Sur l'application LCL comme sur l'espace client en ligne, le problème est le même. La page rame, et l'accès au compte est finalement impossible. « Nous ne pouvons donner suite à votre demande pour le moment », est l'un des messages remontés ce matin par les clients. Un autre évoque un laconique « problème technique ». Il n'est pour l'heure par possible de consulter son solde, passer une opération, ou ouvrir sa messagerie. Tout est à l'arrêt, sur téléphone comme sur ordinateur.
Chez les clients, l'agacement l'emporte, car l'alerte n'est pas la première cette année. Le 1er avril, il avait été impossible de se connecter au site comme à l'appli pendant un moment. Le 12 mai également. Et le 9 juin, d'après l'historique, il avait fallu patienter jusqu'à la fin de matinée pour retrouver un service normal. LCL est « plus souvent en panne que les banques gratuites », déplore un client peut-être un brin de mauvaise foi.
Il est évidemment inutile de réinstaller l'application ou de marteler le bouton de connexion, car on le redit, les site et appli flanchent en même temps, chez de nombreux utilisateurs. La cause et la durée de l'incident restent pour l'heure inconnues. Le numéro du service client est le 09 69 36 30 30. Et prudence avec les e-mails ou SMS qui proposent de débloquer votre compte, car les escrocs raffolent de ces matinées noires.

articles.title: Cross-border payments startup Taja surpasses 50,000 users across 7 African markets - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Pan-African fintech startup Taja has surpassed 50,000 users and is now processing millions of dollars in transaction volume each month, two years after launching its cross-border payments platform.
Launched in 2024, Taja has built a platform that allows individuals and businesses to send, receive, convert and spend money globally. It offers multi-currency wallets and accounts, international collections, cross-border payouts, real-time currency conversion, virtual cards and digital-asset settlement capabilities.
The startup is live in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Senegal, South Africa, Benin and Ivory Coast, connecting users to major global currencies and payment networks in the United Kingdom and United States.
“We built Taja because moving money across borders shouldn’t feel like navigating a labyrinth,” said David Orovwiroro, the startup’s CEO.
“Surpassing 50,000 users and processing millions of dollars in monthly transaction volume demonstrates the growing demand for accessible, borderless financial infrastructure. We remain committed to ensuring that African creators, freelancers and business owners have the financial tools they need to participate and compete in the global economy.”
The startup said it plans to continue expanding across Africa and into international markets, with a focus on strengthening its payment infrastructure.

articles.title: Tailscale warns of SSH flaws allowing root privilege escalation
articles.text:
The Tailscale security team is working to patch almost a dozen security vulnerabilities that could be exploited to steal credentials, crash servers, gain root privileges, and more.
Tailscale develops a software-defined mesh virtual private network (VPN) built on WireGuard that lets users connect computers, servers, and cloud instances from anywhere to the same encrypted mesh network ("tailnet") via direct peer-to-peer (P2P) connections.
Cyberdione Labs discovered 11 flaws (collectively known as Tailworm) that still lack patches during a security audit of Tailscale 1.104.2 and the self-hosted headscale v0.29.5 control server.
"All findings were verified by reproduction in a lab environment on unmodified, released software (tailscale v1.104.2, headscale v0.29.5)," said Erica Windisch, founder of Cyberdione Labs, who reported the flaws to Tailscale and publicly released the details.
"It is the opinion of the researchers that rapid awareness of these flaws will expediate remediation across impacted devices. These vulnerabilities were not introduced by the researchers, but were discovered, and discovered with low effort."
The table below classifies the security issues by the component they affect. The most critical issue is in Tailscale's SSH server and could let authorized attackers gain code execution with root privileges through Unix-socket forwarding on a targeted tailnet.
| Component / feature | Mechanism (what breaks) | Attacker requirement | Principal outcome | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Tailscale SSH (tailscaled's embedded SSH server, running as root) | Unix-socket forwarding ( ssh -R/-L) performs path checks and file operations as root; races and missing privilege drop let an ordinary session replace, dial, or delete privileged resources | One approved device + one SSH policy rule (forwarding granted automatically on headscale; per-rule on SaaS) | Root execution on target servers; capture of enrollment keys; arbitrary root-file deletion | 
| Tailscale app connectors (conn25, experimental) | Connector translates traffic to attacker-chosen destinations with no validation; network ACLs are never consulted for the true destination | A device granted the connector capability | Reach cloud metadata (credential theft), internal LANs, and — in Kubernetes — every cluster service | 
| headscale control server (self-hosted deployments) | Unauthenticated resource exhaustion (memory growth, cache eviction) | Internet reachability; no account | Control-server crash loop; blocking of new-device onboarding org-wide | 
| Tailscale DERP client (relay connection in every agent) | Unbounded read of a malicious relay's response | Ability to position/point a client at a hostile relay | Client-agent memory exhaustion | 
| tailscale serve (local service exposure) | TCP-forward to a unix socket lacks a guard present on the HTTP path; plus a race in per-mount authorization | Operator configures the forward (or a peer races the mount check) | Remote administrative-API access to the node; minority of requests bypass app authz | 
On Monday, the Tailscale team said it received Cyberdione Labs' report and was working on patches to address these security issues by the end of today.
The developers also confirmed that the reported flaws are "serious" as they could let threat actors with permissions on targeted systems take actions with escalated privileges.
"Most of the Tailscale SSH issues we've identified concern privilege escalation. In some circumstances, someone already authorized to connect over Tailscale SSH may be able to perform actions beyond the permissions of their configured local user, including potentially gaining elevated privileges," Tailscale said.
"These are serious security issues, and we're treating them accordingly. Exploitation depends on the permissions granted to the connecting user or device, the system's configuration, and other conditions. We're continuing to verify the full scope of the findings and which configurations may be affected."
However, despite the severity of the issues, Tailscale said it doesn't recommend that users disable the Tailscale SSH feature.
"If you want to jump to the most important part, based on our current assessment, we're not recommending that everyone disable Tailscale SSH," said Mike Shaver, VP of Engineering at Tailscale.
Instead, the Tailscale team shared measures that should mitigate some of these flaws:
- Review SSH access policies. Limit access to the users and devices that need it.
- Disable SSH forwarding if you don't need it. Set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restart the service. This disables SSH forwarding without disabling Tailscale SSH entirely, and mitigates several of the more serious findings.
- Review access to sensitive systems. Consider temporarily tightening your Tailscale SSH access policies while we investigate, so that only the specific users and devices that need access can connect.
The Tailscale devs aim to push a new version that fixes these issues by the end of Tuesday, October 27, and urged users to prepare to update and "apply the patched Tailscale client release when it becomes available."

articles.title: Un ChatGPT moins cher et plus puissant : le nouveau modèle GPT-6.1 Terra d'OpenAI a trouvé sa recette
articles.text:
Le modèle Terra d’OpenAI était resté jusque là sur la génération GPT-5.6 (arrivé en juillet dernier). Désormais, il passe à GPT-6.1 et devient plus puissant, mais surtout deux fois moins cher. Ce modèle est vu par OpenAI comme capable de travailler sur plein de tâches différentes, et il est déjà disponible.
GPT-6.1 Terra est là : qu’est-ce qui change vraiment ?
Sur la page dédiée à ce modèle, OpenAI explique que GPT-6.1 Terra est un modèle dit intermédiaire (pas le moins cher, mais pas le plus puissant) conçu pour analyser ce qui s’affiche sur votre écran, puis agir. Cliquer, saisir du texte, remplir un formulaire, passer à un autre logiciel… il peut à peu près tout faire. Il succède donc à GPT-5.6 Terra, dont la sortie avait été suspendue par l’administration Trump au nom de la sécurité nationale. Seuls quelques partenaires sélectionnés avaient pu le tester. Un système nécessaire puisqu’il y a encore quelques jours, deux agents IA d’OpenAI ont effectué des actions surprenantes. Quelques jours plus tard, le modèle était enfin sorti.
GPT-6.1 Terra est taillé pour le travail professionnel, avec des usages variés : rédiger un mail, interpréter un plan technique, extraire les données d’une facture pour les saisir dans un logiciel comptable, assister un montage vidéo, etc. OpenAI le présente donc comme un modèle associant raisonnement visuel détaillé et utilisation précise d’un ordinateur.
Sur le benchmark Agent’s Last Exam, cette version est 15% plus performante que la version précédente (sur un exercice de transformation de plans architecturaux en modèles 3D et en analyse d’un film d’animation). GPT-6.1 Terra est d’ores et déjà disponible dans ChatGPT Work et Codex. Mais pour le moment, il est réservé aux abonnés à ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise et Edu.
Un modèle d’IA deux fois moins cher que sa version précédente
Aujourd’hui, la gamme de modèles d’OpenAI compte quatre niveaux, du moins cher au plus puissant : Luna, Terra, Sol et Astra. Terra est donc dans une position intermédiaire, entre le plus accessible qu’est Luna et des modèles plus coûteux comme Sol et Astra. GPT-6.1 Terra est annoncé à 1 dollar par million de tokens en entrée et 5 dollars par million de tokens en sortie. Pour rappel, sur GPT-5.6 Terra, c’était deux fois plus cher.
Au regard de la grille tarifaire d’OpenAI, ce modèle est dix fois plus cher que le modèle le moins cher, à savoir GPT-6 Luna. Mais il est dix fois moins cher que le modèle le plus puissant, GPT-6 Astra, tout en ayant des performances qui s’en rapprochent. OpenAI semble donc en faire un modèle avec le meilleur rapport performances-prix possible.

El Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete es un robot aspirador de gama alta y se nota en los detalles: tiene batería para rato, que se pierda es casi una misión imposible, se esmera en el fregado, su app es completísima. No obstante, para mí donde es verdaderamente diferencial precisamente es cómo ve y elimina las manchas secas gracias a su tecnología con IA, el agua caliente con detergente y su gran rodillo. En este sentido, me parece una estupenda opción para gente tecnológica con una casa grande y/o complicada.
Eso sí, no es un robot aspirador para todo el mundo: su aplicación puede ser liosa para gente que no se apañe con la tecnología (pienso en mi madre, por ejemplo) y pese a ser un modelo que supera holgadamente los mil euros, no es el más exhaustivo con el pelo de mascotas. Y quizás ahí también esté su gran hándicap: siendo un robot aspirador ambicioso, no lo es tanto en el global de la experiencia frente a otros candidatos más asequibles (atendiendo a PVP).
roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete Robot Aspirador Succión Extrema de 36000 Pa, Negro
Nuestra experiencia con el Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete
Un diseño que vence pero no convence. Con una base elegante y sufrida donde guarda el agua sucia, el agua limpia, el detergente y el depósito de suciedad y un robot con un diseño bastante estándar, hay que hilar filo para ver qué tiene de especial. A favor: la txapela retráctil es útil para que pueda meterse a limpiar por debajo de muebles, el rodillo de fregado va de lado a lado y hay dos cepillos laterales, uno a cada lado. Eso sí, he echado en falta que el rodillo central para el aspirado sea más largo o sea doble y que los laterales salgan hacia los lados para llegar mejor a las esquinas. Sí, uno de ellos es capaz de girar a un lado y al otro, pero no es tan eficaz como esos bracitos para llegar a las esquinas.
Te reto a que lo pierdas. Hace tiempo que no solo no despejo la casa cuando paso el aspirador sino que además, hay días que vivo un poco en el caos de seguir adecentando mi casa nueva. Pues bien: este robot aspirador, que para moverse usa una cámara, un visor láser y algoritmos de reconocimiento nunca se ha perdido y como puede verse en la app, ha recorrido toda mi casa con una excepción obvia: aquellos lugares donde no cabe. O donde tienen a bien tumbarse las perras, porque ni siquiera las molesta. La pletina que separa la cocina del salón (de apenas un centímetro de altura en la zona central) no ha sido un problema porque de hecho puede subir bastante más gracias a la estructura de sus ruedas.
Un fregado superlativo. Tengo un piso pequeño, dos perras grandes y soy un poco torpe. Conclusión: mi casa tiende a tener manchas y pelo, mucho pelo. A lo largo de estos días lo he puesto a diario (varias veces al día, de hecho) en todas sus configuraciones y va sobrado de potencia en aspirado. Así, poniéndolo en el modo medio se traga el típico diente de ajo travieso que se te cae mientras cocinas. También ha dejado impecable la alfombrita fina. ¿Y si la alfombra es más gorda? Pues probablemente escale, pero para evitar mojarla con el rodillo de fregar, este se sube 1,5 centímetros y además viene con un protector para evitar el roce. En pocas palabras: no te la juegas a mojarla.
En general, los pelos y otra suciedad fina también se las traga bien porque la potencia de succión no es un problema: donde vas a tener que sacar la escoba es en las esquinas o sitios de difícil acceso. Allí es donde se termina acumulando la suciedad y allí es donde se echa en falta esos brazos extensibles (una vez los pruebas, no hay vuelta atrás) para alargar los cepillos laterales y que sí tiene el rodillo de fregar. El fregado es lo que el Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete borda: en cuanto "ve" una mancha, les mete mano para retirarlas. ¿Y si es una de café sequísimo? Pues incide si no se va, aunque esta es una opción que se puede activar en la app.
Tremenda batería. La ficha técnica no le hace justicia a la experiencia porque en una frase: tiene pila para rato. Poniéndolo solo a aspirar a máxima potencia en mi piso de 55 metros cuadrados ha consumido un 20% de batería. A modo normal en aspirado y fregado, un 30%. Vamos, que si tienes una casa de varios pisos no se te va a quedar corto y además, recuerda dónde está y qué ha limpiado ya, por lo que en caso de quedarse a medias, lo retoma cuando se ha cargado lo suficiente.
Mantenimiento bajo mínimos. Aquí voy a terminar muy rápido: llevo unos 15 días probándolo y lo único que he hecho ha sido llenar el depósito de agua y vaciar el de agua sucia aproxidamente una vez a la semana y eso con dos perras en casa tiene mérito. El proceso por cierto es fácil y limpio: extraer y volcar/poner bajo el grifo. Me ha llamado la atención lo poco que se atasca el pelo, gracias a la forma de los cepillos laterales y a ese rodillo central partido en dos que gira en sentidos opuestos, lo que facilita el tragarse el pelo y que no se haga bola.

Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete, la opinión de Xataka
Mi sensación al terminar la review de este robot aspirador es que me ha dejado un poco a medias. Me explico: la clase media se ha puesto las pilas, sirva como ejemplo su hermano pequeño el Roborock QV 35A, y cuesta encontrar argumentos para justificar gastarse bastante más de mil euros en uno. Antes de nada, un disclaimer: el Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete es un robot aspirador que ronda el notable alto - sobresaliente en todo.
Es cierto que este modelo es superlativo en el fregado, de hecho está entre los mejores que he probado, pero de un modelo de gama alta tan ambicioso toca ser quisquillosa e ir a los detalles y en este caso, creo que la aspiración tiene todavía cierto margen de mejora por dos motivos: la extensión del cepillo lateral es más efectiva que mover la suciedad de un lado a otro y el rodillo central debería ser más grande o incluso dos. Y si ya cuenta con una versión de la app simplificada, con menos opciones, menos textos y mensajes más claros para gente no tecnológica, mejor que mejor.
¿Lo recomiendo?
Si cumples varias de estas premisas, de cabeza: tener una una casa grande con algún que otro desnivel, ser una persona techie y sobre todo, deseas un robot aspirador que además de aspirar, friegue mucho y bien, el Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete es caballo ganador. Eso sí, siempre y cuando el presupuesto no sea un problema.

articles.title: French VC Aquiti closes €60 million fund for founders outside of traditional venture hubs | EU-Startups
articles.text:
French VC Aquiti announces the final close of their AVA1 fund at nearly €60 million in order to back founders building across the Greater Southwest of France from pre-Seed onwards.
Through its AVA1 fund, Aquiti invests at pre-Seed and Seed, with initial investments ranging from €100k to €3 million and substantial reserves for follow-on rounds. They intend to build a portfolio of 25 to 30 companies.
“Founders should not have to choose between building where they want to live and accessing the capital, network and ambition they need to go far. With AVA1, our goal is simple: be the first partner for the best founders in the Greater Southwest, and stay alongside them as they scale,” says Jean-François Cochy, General Partner at Aquiti and Head of AVA1.
Aquiti’s AVA1 final close comes amid a series of European early-stage venture fund announcements in 2026.
In France, Paris-based Newfund closed its €60 million HEKA fund to support BrainTech startups, while 360 Capital announced an €85 million close for its Poli360 2 DeepTech fund and Elaia closed its third DeepTech Seed fund at €134 million.
Elsewhere, Germany’s Vanagon Ventures completed a €20 million pre-Seed fund, while Lithuania’s FIRSTPICK launched a €25 million vehicle focused on Baltic founders. Together, these fund announcements represent €324 million in disclosed fund capital, rising to nearly €384 million including AVA1.
Aquiti’s regional approach also builds on earlier investment activity, with EU-Startups previously identifying the firm among the backers of Bordeaux-based TreeFrog Therapeutics and CardNexus.
“We chose Aquiti because the relationship went far beyond capital. From our first discussions, we found a team that combines a genuinely close human relationship with experience in investing and supporting tech companies as they scale. Most importantly, we share the same level of ambition: to make RelaiSanté a category-defining company and transform the way patients access care and support after hospitalisation,” adds Étienne Boix, co-founder and CEO of portfolio company RelaiSanté.
Aquiti Gestion is a French private equity firm that has been supporting businesses across Southwestern France for over 25 years, managing over €230 million in assets across regional SMEs and corporate buyouts. To expand into the fast-growing startup ecosystem, the firm launched a dedicated, modern venture capital arm in 2018, known simply as Aquiti or Aquiti Ventures.
This specialised, five-investor venture team focuses strictly on pre-Seed and Seed-stage investments in breakthrough technology, healthcare, and climate startups, pairing the institutional stability of a 25-year-old asset manager with the agile, tech-focused mindset of a fund founded in 2018.
Aquiti has built a team of five investors and backed 13 companies, from AI-powered materials discovery at Synboli to new models of care coordination at RelaiSanté.
They look to work alongside founders to establish the right governance, make key hires, prepare for future funding, and open doors to potential new customers.

articles.title: Developers Reporting Double-Digit Weekly Time Savings from AI Fell from 68% to 26%
articles.text:
The share of developers reporting ten or more hours saved each week through AI fell from 68% to 26% in a year, according to Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026. Adoption over the same period became close to universal, with 95% of developers and 96% of engineering leaders saying their organization actively uses AI in engineering.
The report draws on 1,155 individual contributors and 405 engineering leaders surveyed during 2026. Atlassian is unusually direct about what that means, stating that its findings "reflect self-reported experience and perception, not system-level telemetry such as deployment frequency, cycle time, or revenue impact," and that associations in the data "should not be interpreted as causal proof."
Taroon Mandhana, Atlassian’s CTO for AI and Teamwork, summarised the shift as one where "the bottleneck has moved to managing AI’s work."
Local benefit has not gone away. Eighty-seven percent of developers say AI helps them ship faster and 80% say it helps them deliver more without longer hours. What has not followed is relief from everyday obstacles. Only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI, while 50% report about the same amount, which the report describes as friction "of a different type than before AI."
Some of that difference is AI itself. Forty-nine percent of developers now spend four or more hours a week managing AI tools, and 65% say they spend time correcting AI-generated work that missed the original intent. Both figures run higher among engineering leaders, at 57% and 72%. Twenty-nine percent name reviewing or managing AI-generated code as a source of friction outright.
The rest of the list has barely moved in three years. Finding information leads at 51%, followed by meetings at 50%, context switching at 45% and technical debt at 44%. Finding information also topped the 2025 list and placed second in 2024. Coding has never appeared on it.
Measurement is where the report is most pointed. Sixty percent of developers say AI use is treated as a productivity signal in their organization, 41% say they sometimes use AI more than necessary because they feel expected to, and only 42% of leaders say they have the right metrics to separate real gains from activity.
Responding to Mandhana, Shan Huang, who builds production AI agents for enterprise workflows, connected two of those figures:
If people are using AI more than necessary because they feel expected to, part of that 49% spending 4+ hours a week managing AI output is not a tooling problem, it is a metric problem. Call it performative throughput: the usage gets counted as productivity, and the cleanup lands on somebody else’s calendar.
Taylor Johnson of Athena Intelligence proposed a replacement in one line:
AI activity is not impact; measure accepted work, not usage.
Organizations with a stated position are rare and appear to fare better. Seventeen percent of developers and 23% of leaders report a clear, actively implemented AI strategy across the software delivery lifecycle. Among developers who do, 41% report noticeably less friction than before AI, against 22% of those describing an inconsistent or poorly communicated strategy. Andrew Boyagi, Atlassian’s head of DevOps evangelism, calls that gap the differentiator, though the report itself cautions that the association is not causal.
One trend has run the same way for three years. The share of developers saying leadership does not fully understand the challenges they face was 44% in 2024, 63% in 2025, and 66% in 2026.
Cam Turner, a designer and former AWS staffer, put the practical question that neither the report nor the thread answered: "68 to 26 in a year says the work moved from making to reviewing. Is anyone designing the review step yet, or are teams just absorbing it?"
Two caveats sit on the headline figure. This is vendor research from a company selling developer tooling, landing on a conclusion that favors formalizing AI delivery. The comparison base also changed, from 3,500 developers and managers across six countries in 2025 to 1,560 respondents this year, and neither edition publishes fieldwork dates.
Self-reported hours are soft in both directions, which commenter Harshit Jain raised directly: is the drop about review load, or about higher expectations? The report does not separate them.

articles.title: Intel's leaked 28-core Nova Lake CPU beats the Core Ultra 9 285K and Ryzen 9 9950X3D in single-thread testing
articles.text:
Highly anticipated: What appears to be another leak of Intel's upcoming Nova Lake-S desktop processors has hit the internet. A PassMark benchmark lists results for a 28-core chip, and its single-thread score is higher than that of the Core Ultra 9 285K and Ryzen 9 9950X3D.
A VideoCardz reader found the entries through PerformanceTest 11.1's Manage Baselines feature. Listed as "Intel 0000," the processors appear in submissions dating back to September.
The fastest 28-core result reaches 5,210 points in the single-thread test, with another scoring 5,191. For comparison, the individual baselines selected by VideoCardz scored 5,059 for the Core Ultra 9 285K, 4,805 for the Ryzen 9 9950X3D, and 4,635 for the Core i9-14900KF. That gives the Nova Lake-S sample leads of around 3%, 8.4%, and 12.4%, respectively. The publication selected comparison systems whose overall CPU Mark results were close to the processors' published averages.
The overall CPU Mark result is less impressive: 61,509 points against 67,274 for the 285K and 72,066 for the 9950X3D. It still beats the 14900KF's 58,074, though. Separately, the eight-core entries score between 9,004 and 23,478 points, a wide spread that could reflect differences in test conditions or development configurations.
The highest Memory Mark score shown is 2,523.4, around 25% below the selected 285K system's 3,349.6. These are system-level results, so the gap can't be attributed to the processor alone.
The screenshot lists approximately 16GB of RAM, a reported CPU speed of roughly 3.3GHz, and turbo readings near 4.8GHz for both 28-core entries.
The eight-core entries, listed as using an embedded platform, top out at 5,085 single-thread points. The fastest result narrowly exceeds the Core Ultra 9 285K baseline of 5,059, a lead of about 0.5%.
It's important to remember that these are unverified results from unidentified pre-release samples. Unknown test conditions and unfinished hardware or firmware mean they may not reflect retail performance.
Earlier this month, a lineup leak listed a Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC with eight performance cores, 16 efficiency cores, and four low-power efficiency cores. The leak listed a 125W TDP and integrated graphics with 32 execution units. BFC appears to identify the large-cache models – the acronym likely took inspiration from the iconic Doom weapon.
The standard 4950K reportedly retains that 28-core configuration without the big cache. Its original table omitted the four LP-E cores, which leaker Jaykihn said also feature in standard models. The benchmark entries don't identify a retail model or establish whether the tested chip carries the additional cache.
Further down the leaked stack, the 65W Core Ultra 9 4900 BFC combines 6P+12E+4LP-E cores, while the 125W Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC uses 8P+12E+4LP-E. Both list 32-EU graphics. The 125W Core Ultra 5 4650K and 4650KF list 6P+12E cores before adding the reported LP-E quartet; the KF drops integrated graphics.
| Model | Cores (P+E+LP-E) | Big cache | TDP | iGPU | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC | 8+16+4 | Yes | 125W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 9 4950K | 8+16 | No | 125W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 9 4900 BFC | 6+12+4 | Yes | 65W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC | 8+12+4 | Yes | 125W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 7 4850K | 8+12 | No | 125W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 5 4650K | 6+12 | No | 125W | 32 EU | 
| Core Ultra 5 4650KF | 6+12 | No | 125W | None | 
The family is expected to require LGA 1954 motherboards and 900-series chipsets, while larger configurations with up to 52 cores are tipped to arrive later.

articles.title: Windows 11 añade una opción para mejorar el rendimiento del sistema: comprueba si está disponible en tu PC
articles.text:
Las versiones de prueba de Windows 11 incorporan un nuevo interruptor llamado Advanced Performance Extensions (APX), con el que el sistema operativo podrá aprovechar una tecnología diseñada para mejorar el rendimiento del procesador. Sin embargo, la opción depende de una característica física del chip y, por ahora, no está disponible en los procesadores de consumo que se venden actualmente.
APX aparece en la Build 29695, distribuida a través del programa Windows Insider. Microsoft todavía no ha anunciado cuándo llegará a la versión estable de Windows 11 ni ha publicado resultados de rendimiento propios. Aunque la compañía describe la función como una forma de conseguir “mejor rendimiento”, activar el interruptor solo tendrá efecto en un equipo con un procesador compatible.
Cómo comprobar si tu PC puede usar APX
La opción se encuentra en fase de pruebas y su disponibilidad depende del procesador instalado. Si el chip no incorpora APX, el interruptor aparecerá inactivo o no producirá ningún cambio. Una actualización de Windows no puede añadir esta capacidad a un procesador que carece de ella físicamente.
En el mercado de consumo, la documentación de GCC apunta a Intel Nova Lake como la primera familia de procesadores que incorporaría APX. Estos chips aún no están a la venta. Para servidores, Intel ha confirmado la compatibilidad de Diamond Rapids, una familia Xeon destinada a centros de datos.
Por ahora, ninguna de las familias Intel Alder Lake, Raptor Lake, Meteor Lake, Lunar Lake, Arrow Lake o Panther Lake es compatible. Tampoco hay una fecha confirmada para la llegada de APX a procesadores AMD. Robert Hormuth, responsable de la división de clientes de AMD, ha mencionado la tecnología en el contexto de la colaboración entre ambas compañías, pero no se ha anunciado ningún modelo Ryzen compatible.
Más registros para reducir los accesos a memoria
APX es un conjunto de instrucciones que Intel añadió a la arquitectura x86 en 2023. Su cambio principal consiste en duplicar de 16 a 32 los registros de propósito general del procesador. Los registros son espacios de almacenamiento muy rápidos dentro del chip, donde se guardan temporalmente los valores que necesita un programa mientras se ejecuta.
Al disponer de más registros, el procesador puede mantener más datos cerca y reducir los accesos a la memoria RAM, que es más lenta. Las nuevas instrucciones también están pensadas para mejorar la ejecución de ciertas operaciones y ayudar a reducir errores en la predicción de los pasos de un programa.
Intel afirma que, en pruebas con un prototipo, el código compilado para APX realizó un 10 % menos de cargas y más de un 20 % menos de almacenamientos que el mismo código compilado para una base Intel 64. También se detectó una reducción del 10 % en el número total de instrucciones.
Esas cifras no significan que Windows 11 vaya a funcionar un 10 % o un 20 % más rápido en el uso cotidiano. Los resultados proceden de pruebas preliminares y describen cambios en el código procesado, no una mejora general garantizada para cada aplicación o tarea.
El software también debe adaptarse
La presencia de un procesador compatible y del interruptor en Windows no basta para acelerar automáticamente todos los programas. Según Intel, los desarrolladores tendrán que recompilar sus aplicaciones para que puedan aprovechar los registros adicionales. La empresa sostiene que no será necesario modificar el código fuente, aunque cada programa deberá pasar por su proceso de actualización y pruebas.
Las aplicaciones que no se recompilen seguirán funcionando con normalidad, pero no aprovecharán las ventajas específicas de APX. Por eso, incluso cuando lleguen los primeros procesadores compatibles, el beneficio dependerá también de que el sistema operativo y el software estén preparados.
Por ahora, APX es una función en pruebas orientada a futuras generaciones de procesadores. En los equipos actuales, activar opciones de Windows no permitirá obtener esta mejora si el chip no es compatible. La disponibilidad efectiva dependerá de la llegada de procesadores compatibles, del lanzamiento de la función en Windows 11 y de la adaptación de las aplicaciones.

articles.title: Ex-CEO do GitHub lança Entire, plataforma rival feita para IA e humanos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Ex-CEO do GitHub lança Entire, plataforma rival feita para IA e humanos
Thomas Dohmke, ex-CEO do GitHub, lançou a plataforma Entire para competir com a sua antiga empresa.
Já mencionamos Thomas Dohmke aqui no Tecnoblog. A razão é simples: ele foi CEO do GitHub entre 2021 e 2025. O executivo está de volta, mas agora na condição de fundador da Entire, uma empresa de hospedagem e colaboração Git que surge para competir justamente com o GitHub.
A Entire foi apresentada em julho, mas o seu lançamento oficial se deu nesta semana. No anúncio de lançamento, o serviço foi descrito da seguinte forma:
A Entire está lançando a primeira plataforma Git criada para que agentes e humanos trabalhem juntos, uma alternativa ao GitHub que oferece a velocidade necessária para que as equipes integrem alterações tão rapidamente quanto os agentes de programação as criam.
Repare que a descrição acima menciona “agentes”. Trata-se de uma forma de dizer que a Entire foi projetada não só para o trabalho de desenvolvedores humanos, como também para tarefas executadas por agentes de inteligência artificial. Na prática, isso significa que a plataforma foi preparada para suportar as altas cargas de trabalho que esses agentes podem demandar.
Mas as diferenças com relação ao GitHub não acabam aí. No lugar de pull requests, que são recursos comuns no GitHub que permitem ao usuário informar a outros desenvolvedores sobre alterações no repositório de determinado projeto, a Entire usa Trails.
Trails são uma forma de registrar e comunicar mudanças em código de modo que outros desenvolvedores possam não só entender o que mudou, mas também como e por quê. Não por acaso, a Entire compara a interface dos Trails à visão que um piloto tem do painel de um avião (não no sentido de complexidade, mas de acompanhamento da operação).
Dohmke e sua turma enfatizam que o desempenho é outro diferencial da plataforma: “a Entire é construída em um novo servidor de controle de versão compatível com Git, com pushes até 89 vezes mais rápidos do que o GitHub e seis vezes mais rápidos do que o Cursor Origin”, descreve o comunicado oficial.
Sim. Pelo menos nesta fase de lançamento, a Entire não cobra nada pelo uso da plataforma para repositórios de código e Trails. Porém, o usuário precisa comprar créditos para o uso de agentes de IA. A boa notícia é que cada conta criada no serviço recebe um crédito de US$ 100 como “boas-vindas”.
O site oficial é entire.com.
