articles.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
articles.text:
Protein design tools may be getting increasingly sophisticated, but you still need a sophisticated understanding of protein structure for them to work. This can include knowing enzyme mechanisms down to the positions of specific amino acids, as well as the water molecules that also occupy the area where catalysis takes place. Once you specify these, the tools can build the rest of a protein around this target.
A large collaboration of researchers based in China, however, decided to bring protein design to the masses, making a tool that can take natural language prompts and use them to produce proteins with the function you specify. If your measure for success is a working protein, then the success rate may not be great. But they still manage to get the job done. And, in a separate announcement, Hugging Face shared that it’s now hosting a tool that does similar things on the DNA level.
The equivalent of vibe coding may have come to protein design—at least if you have access to a lab where you can sort the good designs from the dozens of failed ones.
Focusing on function
Some of the best protein design tools we have available right now work through a two-step process. First, you specify a set of constraints, such as the need to bind another molecule or to have a specific arrangement of amino acids. One AI tool then generates a protein shape that meets those constraints. Once that’s done, a separate tool populates that shape with a specific sequence of amino acids that can ensure the protein folds into the appropriate configuration to match the shape.
Obviously, doing that often requires a fair bit of technical knowledge. If you’re designing a catalyst, for example, then you not only need to know what amino acids are critical to get a chemical reaction to happen, but you have to know where they should be located within a 3D space. That, not surprisingly, requires a fairly sophisticated understanding of protein chemistry and the ability to express that understanding in whatever form that the protein design tools require.
The thing is, if two experts were talking to each other, they wouldn’t need to get that specific. If one said “serine protease,” for example, the other would know a lot of what was implied by that in terms of the specifics of the reaction mechanism. We need to get specific when communicating with an AI tool because, while our current generation of tools are great at working through the 3D arrangements of amino acids, they’re kind of stupid about the functions that those 3D arrangements enable.
In the work of the team behind the new tool, called Pinal, this doesn’t necessarily have to be the case. We have databases full of millions of protein sequences tagged with notes about the functions those proteins perform. With the proper training, the researchers reasoned, it should be possible to just use the same terminology in those tags to get a system that outputs a sequence that performs exactly like what you’re looking for.
Proteins plus language
Pinal, on some levels, works quite like the standard tools, following a two-step process of building a backbone for the protein and then filling in the details of the amino acids that populate that backbone through a separate process. But there are very significant differences—beginning with what you need to do to start the process.
Rather than specifying some details of a few amino acids in the design product, you simply tell the system what you want. “The first stage is handled by T2struct, a text-to-structure module that translates a natural language prompt into a structural blueprint,” as the system’s developers describe it. T2struct doesn’t output a 3D shape, either; it simply produces a linear array of tokens that correspond to the spatial relationship between each amino acid and its nearest neighbors and assign a probability to each.
That gets handed off to a system called SAProt-T, which uses a combination of the original text and the output to T2struct to construct the sequence of amino acids in the final protein design. Here, the probabilities generated earlier matter, since SAProt-T performs a global re-evaluation. According to the authors, this avoids the risk of “overlooking a slightly less probable structure that can accommodate a far superior functional sequence.”
How do you develop a system that can do all of this? The researchers decided the best way was to use massive amounts of data. For each set of tags that describe a protein’s function, they fed the tags into an LLM and had it provide a plain-language description and used both the tags and the description as part of the training. They used protein sequences from three different databases, paired with structural information predicted by AlphaFold; just one of these databases contained 800 million keyword–protein pairs.
It’s noteworthy that AlphaFold is not 100 percent accurate in its predictions, so if you’re trying to generate something related to a relatively obscure protein, this could be a problem. But many common proteins have structural data available, which presumably would ensure AlphaFold made informed predictions.
In any case, apparently enough of the structural data was right for the training to work.
Functional proteins
To test Pinal, the researchers asked it to design four very different proteins: a fluorescent one, two enzymes, and one that takes part in a large multi-protein complex. While the details vary a bit from case to case, there was a similar process for each; we’ll use the fluorescent protein as an example.
The classic example of a fluorescent protein, which won its discoverer a Nobel, is GFP, the green fluorescent protein. Pinal was asked to produce 50,000 proteins that could fluoresce like GFP. This massive list was then filtered down by a number of criteria. For starters, the researchers rejected anything with a sequence that looked like a known fluorescent protein. But they selected for a couple of key features found in GFP: the ability to form a barrel-like structure, and the presence of a key amino acid that can be chemically modified to enable fluorescence.
In short, they wanted it to be a bit like GFP in general, but not very similar in terms of the specific amino acid sequence. That filtering left them with a high-priority list of just 29 candidate proteins, all of which were made in E. coli. A grand total of one of them fluoresced.
All the other examples were done similarly: start with a massive list, narrow it down computationally, then test a few dozen designs, of which only a few would work.
It would be tempting to dismiss this as a horrifically low success rate. But remember that a lot of the suggestions that were most likely to work would look a lot like known GFP proteins, and so be weeded out. The researchers also didn’t even bother to test whether things that didn’t form a structure similar to GFP might work, so they may have rejected a huge range of alternative fluorescent proteins based on that.
Not just proteins
Last week also saw the introduction of something very similar but focused on DNA sequences. A collaboration of the AI company Hugging Face, the Zhongguancun Academy, and the University of Naples “Federico II” introduced what they’re calling Carbon X, an open-weight model that can run on local hardware. It is based on a human-language model called Qwen3-14B but was retrained using DNA, followed by reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning.
The re-training (technically termed mid-training) required a careful balancing act: “A low learning rate preserves English but leaves DNA at chance, and a high one learns DNA but forgets English.” But the result is a single model that can speak both DNA and English and translate between them. So, like large genome models, you can prompt it with a DNA sequence, and it will attempt to predict sequences that might come after it in a typical genome. But you can also prompt it with a mix of DNA and natural language, asking it things like “what would the consequence of changing this G to an A be?”
While the team has not released a publication describing the behavior of the system, their internal performance suggests it’s quite good, being competitive with large, specialized commercial models like GPT-6.1 Sol. That said, it also includes a few cautions. The system is not especially good at noting specific positions, especially on longer sequences. It can also be prone to hallucinations if the prompt isn’t specific enough. So, the usual cautions when using an AI tool definitely apply.
Hugging Face points out two major reasons why Carbon X might be a better option than commercial models, even for tasks where the commercial models tend to perform a bit better, both of them related to the fact that Carbon X can be run locally. The first is simply cost; the company’s demonstration video was done using a MacBook, so it can be run repeatedly on relatively affordable hardware. The second is that there are many situations where, for proprietary or privacy reasons, people will not want to share the inquiries they’re making with a commercial entity.
Keeping it plain
It’s easy to think this is dumbing biology down so anyone with the slightest bit of knowledge can start making custom proteins and viruses. That’s not entirely accurate. They can easily get the sequences out of the tool. But they will then likely need to use a lot of specialized tools to screen through these in order to find sequences that are more likely to be functional. And then there’s the issue of testing them, which requires a well-equipped biology lab and trained specialists.
Biologists have clearly not been taken out of the equation.
In many cases, this may solve ongoing issues faced by experimental biologists. In the post-genome era, there have been lots of questions that are best answered via computers. But a lot of tools made to get these answers were made by bioinformaticians who did not go out of their way to make their tools approachable. Many biologists can understand a relatively English-ish phrase like “find me all the enhancers that control the expression of this gene.” But far fewer will know which combination of tools are needed to answer that question, much less how to configure them.
Giving those biologists a tool that can answer these questions without the need to consult multiple software manuals has potential to accelerate research. But it may take a few years before it becomes clear that biologists find this capability useful.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute.
As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH.
However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released.
MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.”
However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999.
Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work.
“Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch.
Are you down with P versus NP?
The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P versus NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P).
A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful.
However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.”
That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle.
The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.
“Every computer scientist should probably put a little more weight on the plausibility of P = NP, but one’s weight may vary,” Williams said. “I do think that it kind of calls into question a lot of the intuitions that we thought we had about … how tractable [hard NP problems] are. I also think that this is probably not the final answer either. I don’t think that OpenAI’s algorithm could possibly be the best algorithm you can get.”
The work ahead for computer scientists
The durability of ETH has lead to it being included in many scientific papers over the past decade that will need to be revisited if the AI labs claims that they’ve proven it wrong holds up, Williams said.
“This is partly why I was asking or pushing OpenAI to support a conference on this — it’s going to affect many researchers’ works, and we need to figure out, okay, what happens next besides understanding the algorithms. We need to understand, how should the foundations change compared to what we had before?” he said.
Before scientific concerns, there are cybersecurity questions. Williams said that an improved algorithm could imply that cryptographic systems relying on certain key sizes could be considered broken. So one of the first questions he asked OpenAI science lead Dan Roberts “was if they had checked that this affects any crypto systems … is anything insecure now? And apparently, they checked, and they were reasonably confident that this didn’t … imply any breaks.”
This new AI paradigm of scientific discovery is still a work in progress, but Williams says he is optimistic despite real concerns, particularly about training the next generation of scientists. Being a computer scientist who does high level math has perhaps made the adjustment easier for him than for pure mathematicians.
Still, he says AI is “forcing people to be a little more ambitious about the kind of work that they do, and to think more deeply about, okay, if all the things I used to work on are now low-hanging fruit for AI, how can I raise the bar for the kind of scientific questions I want to ask?”

articles.title: Roblox accused of downloading 145GB of 3D assets, including adult content, for AI training purposes during scraping spree — 1,000 files scraped by automated crawler that ignored Open3DLab's site rules
articles.text:
Roblox accused of downloading 145GB of 3D assets, including adult content, for AI training purposes during scraping spree — 1,000 files scraped by automated crawler that ignored Open3DLab's site rules
Another crawler vacuuming up the internet for undisclosed reasons
Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab has publicly warned that a web crawler, linked to the gaming platform Roblox, mapped "almost every project" on its website, along with sister sites SFMLab and SmutBase, downloading 145.5GB of data in the process. In a blog post, Open3DLab reports that "complete copies" of 1,027 files from 712 projects were sourced in the process, which it believes were taken for "AI training purposes."
The blog post goes into the specifics of the incident, along with some changes that Open3DLab has made since to try and avoid a repeat. According to the post, Open3DLab's staff noticed a crawler "making a large number of requests to our sites and download infrastructure" on October 18. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address. The crawler didn't respect the site's robots.txt file or Terms of Service, which explicitly forbid scraping. It also, according to the report, ignored creator licenses for the projects, which prohibit non-commercial use.
The crawler read "practically [its] entire catalogue" of 18,926 projects in a span of 34 hours over a total of 26,429 requests. Once it was done, the crawler downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects before it "suspended operations." Files downloaded include 364 files, or 54.8GB worth, from 224 projects hosted on SmutBase, OpenLab's sister site focused on adult content. A further 345 projects of adult-marked SFMLab projects, or 62.6GB worth, were also taken.
According to Open3DLab, the crawler's "main limiting factor" was its use of free download servers that capped speed and concurrent downloads. The scraping was detected on the same day, and blocked by the following morning. Further download attempts were detected on October 19, "neatly within office hours, only briefly pausing for an hour around lunchtime," and despite being blocked, "did not reduce its download attempts."
A final attempt on October 20, with requests tapering, "likely in an effort to test... rate limiting," was made, with requests stopping completely later that day. Open3DLab made another request at this point for comment, although without reply.
The Roblox user agent mentions "3D foundation model research." As Open3DLab's blog post notes, Roblox has been building such a model since March 2025, when it introduced Roblox Cube, its "core generative AI system" for 3D modeling for character rigging, with characters and avatars listed as future goals. Further AI tech that could build in-game models using natural language prompts, called "4D generation," was beta launched in February 2026. The email address listed in the user agent matches one of the researchers listed on the Roblox Cube research paper, according to Open3DLab, although it redacted the name here.
Noting Roblox's "track record," Open3DLab's "most likely explanation" is that the crawler was collecting "training or evaluation data" for its 3D foundation model, although it notes that it can't prove it.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Roblox is a gaming platform and game creation system with over 33 million users and billions of "game experiences" for its player base, 40% of whom are reportedly aged under 12 years old. Open3DLab is clear to state that it "doesn't think Roblox set out to collect adult content" but that "as far as [its] logs show, nobody checked," which, it believes, is "not a good position" for Roblox to be in.

articles.title: Google presenta Genie 4: su IA para crear mundos interactivos es más bestia que nunca
articles.text:
Google ha dado un nuevo paso para la creación de mundos interactivos hiperrealistas de la mano de Genie 4. La más reciente actualización de la citada IA llega con importantes mejoras, marcando un salto de calidad muy notorio en comparación con la versión previa que se presentó hace poco más de un año.
La primera optimización notoria que trae Genie 4 respecto de su predecesor está en la simulación humana. Ahora es posible crear simulaciones con personas que se ven mucho más realistas que antes. Además, la IA tiene una mejor comprensión física del mundo, lo que permite crear situaciones con un resultado final mucho más parecido a lo que vemos en la vida real al lidiar con colisiones, aerodinámica y más.
Otra novedad que trae Genie 4 es que puede generar audio de forma nativa. Esto significa que la inteligencia artificial soporta la creación de diálogos, sonido ambiente, efectos y música en tiempo real. Lo que Google tiene entre manos es realmente prometedor y se construye sobre la base de otros modelos ya disponibles, como Gemini 3.8 Flash y Gemini Omni.
Si bien generaciones previas del modelo parecían destinadas a generar escenarios interactivos similares a un videojuego, Genie 4 lo lleva a otro nivel. La nueva IA brinda la posibilidad de crear situaciones que van desencadenando otras acciones con más naturalidad, y todo lo que el usuario se imagina se puede ir añadiendo o modificado sobre la marcha a través de un prompt.
Google presenta Genie 4, una nueva generación de su IA para crear simulaciones interactivas
Google sostiene que Genie 4 puede servir para que un cineasta genere el borrador de una escena que prepara para una serie o película. Así, por ejemplo, es posible ajustar la iluminación, los ángulos de cámara o la acción en tiempo real. La empresa también dice que estudios de videojuegos pueden prototipar un concepto de diseño antes de ponerse manos a la obra con su desarrollo. Y hasta menciona la opción de crear escenarios interactivos a partir de una imagen fija ya existente.
Por supuesto que Genie 4 tiene sus limitaciones. Desde Google advierten que el modelo aún no puede sostener la consistencia de ciertos elementos cuando la simulación es demasiado grande o se extiende por demasiado tiempo. Lo mismo, cuando se realizan múltiples modificaciones y todas tienen un nivel de complejidad importante.
"Las interacciones físicas complejas, la precisión del audio en tiempo real, la representación de texto legible, la precisión espacial y la coherencia a largo plazo son áreas de investigación activa", advierten los californianos en tal sentido. Así que no esperes que algún trasnochado intente montar una película o un videojuego completo a partir de Genie 4.
Genie 4 por lo pronto está limitado a un grupo de testers de confianza, pero la idea de Google es abrirlo al público general pronto. Eso sí, prepárate a pagar. En principio se ofrecerá solo a los suscriptores de Google AI Ultra, el plan que cuesta hasta 219,99 euros al mes.

articles.title: Mehr Erfolg bei der Jobsuche: So nutzt du KI als deinen persönlichen Karriere-Coach
articles.text:
4 KI-Prompts für den Traumjob: So überzeugst du Recruiter
Wer auf Stellensuche ist, hat es zurzeit nicht leicht: So vermeldet das Institut für Arbeitsmarkt- und Berufsforschung im Vergleich zum Vorquartal einen Rückgang von 11 Prozent bei den Stellen, die zwischen April und Juni ausgeschrieben wurden. Auf 100 von den Unternehmen ausgeschriebene Stellen kamen durchschnittlich 291 arbeitslos gemeldete Personen. Auch die Stellenangebote für Jobeinsteiger:innen sind laut einer Analyse der Jobplattform Indeed seit 2022 stark zurückgegangen.
„Wir haben gerade nicht das, was man einen Arbeitnehmermarkt nennt. Hinzu kommt: Vieles ist sehr disruptiv, unter anderem auch durch KI. Viele Menschen haben wirklich Mühe, da mitzuhalten, und zweifeln an ihren Fähigkeiten“, fasst Marcel Zimmermann seine Beobachtungen über die derzeitige Lage auf dem Arbeitsmarkt zusammen.
Der heutige Unternehmensberater saß in seiner Funktion als Vizepräsident für den Bereich globales Marketing beim Messtechnikunternehmen Mahr jahrelang selbst Bewerbenden gegenüber und entschied darüber, wer eingestellt werden sollte. Mittlerweile hat sich Zimmermann selbstständig gemacht. Er berät Firmen unter anderem bei ihrer KI‑Strategie. Das Thema mit den Bewerbungen hat ihn trotzdem nicht losgelassen: Kürzlich hat Zimmermann mit seiner Co-Autorin Silke Grotegut auch ein Buch darüber geschrieben, wie man KI bei Bewerbungen am besten einsetzt.
Folgende Dinge sollten Bewerber:innen beachten, wenn sie KI für ihre Bewerbungen einsetzen wollen:
- Zugriff auf alle Artikel von t3n.de
- t3n Magazin und MIT Technology Review in digitaler Form
- Reduzierte Werbung
- Wöchentlicher Newsletter

articles.title: Ce que les Français demandent vraiment à ChatGPT au travail : les chiffres réservent quelques surprises
articles.text:
Correction de documents, création de visuels, marketing ou programmation : les usages professionnels de ChatGPT sont plus variés qu’on pourrait le croire. Grâce aux nouvelles données publiées par OpenAI, il est désormais possible d’identifier les activités les plus fréquentes en France, avec quelques résultats surprenants.
Vous utilisez ChatGPT pour reformuler un mail, corriger un document ou résoudre un problème informatique ? Vous êtes loin d’être seul. Depuis son lancement, le chatbot d’OpenAI a trouvé sa place dans de nombreuses activités professionnelles, mais il restait difficile de savoir précisément lesquelles occupaient le plus les utilisateurs. Une nouvelle publication permet d’y voir plus clair, grâce à des données couvrant 165 catégories d’activités dans près de 100 pays. Et en France, une tâche domine largement les conversations professionnelles avec l’intelligence artificielle.
En France, la correction de textes écrase toutes les autres activités
Dans cette nouvelle étude publiée le 26 octobre, OpenAI analyse les activités professionnelles associées aux messages envoyés à ChatGPT entre début 2025 et septembre 2026.
Les données françaises du troisième trimestre 2026 placent la correction et la révision de documents en première position, avec 17,1 % des messages professionnels classés. C’est plus de deux fois la part de la deuxième activité, la création de visuels et de compositions graphiques, qui représente 6,7 % des échanges.
Le marketing arrive ensuite, avec 4,3 % des messages consacrés à la conception de supports promotionnels. Plus inattendu, les conseils juridiques et réglementaires occupent la quatrième place avec 4,2 %, devant les questions liées à l’éducation et à la formation (3,9 %).
La programmation informatique n’apparaît qu’en neuvième position, avec 2,8 % des messages, derrière notamment les recherches sur des produits et services, le dépannage informatique ou les calculs financiers.
Les chiffres montrent également que les habitudes évoluent rapidement. Début 2025, la correction de documents représentait encore 24,4 % des messages professionnels français classés. Sa part diminue donc nettement, tandis que celle de la création graphique a plus que doublé en un peu plus d’un an.
Attention, cela ne signifie pas nécessairement que les Français corrigent moins de textes ou programment moins avec l’IA. Ces pourcentages représentent des parts relatives, qui peuvent diminuer alors que le nombre d’utilisateurs de ChatGPT ne cesse de grimper.
Des usages plus variés, mais pas forcément des salariés plus efficaces
Cette diversification se retrouve à l’échelle internationale. Dans les 74 pays suivis sur toute la période, les dix activités professionnelles les plus fréquentes représentaient en moyenne 56 % des messages classés début 2025, contre 51,1 % au troisième trimestre 2026.
Une évolution qui montre que ChatGPT ne se cantonne plus à quelques tâches, même si la rédaction conserve une place importante.
En septembre 2026, 34,8 % des messages professionnels français relèvent ainsi de la grande catégorie « Writing », qui englobe notamment la rédaction, la correction et la traduction. À l'échelle mondiale, cette proportion atteint 32,6 %.
Ces chiffres doivent toutefois être interprétés avec précaution. OpenAI analyse les messages de comptes individuels, et non l’ensemble des échanges réalisés dans les entreprises. Les conversations des comptes Enterprise et les usages de Codex sont notamment exclus, ce qui peut sous-représenter certaines activités techniques, en particulier le développement.
Autre limite : les catégories sont attribuées par des modèles automatisés. Elles décrivent les intentions supposées des utilisateurs, pas les résultats réellement obtenus.
Un message demandant à ChatGPT de corriger un document ne prouve pas que la correction est réussie. Et encore moins que son auteur a gagné du temps. Les bénéfices réels de l’IA sur la productivité restent d’ailleurs débattus, notamment lorsque les résultats nécessitent d’importantes vérifications.
Les données publiées par OpenAI permettent désormais de comprendre quelles activités les utilisateurs confient à ChatGPT. Elles ne permettent pas encore de déterminer si le chatbot réalise ces tâches mieux ou plus rapidement qu’un humain.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: Live2.ai raises Rs 130 Cr to expand its AI-led social commerce platform
articles.text:
Live2.ai raises Rs 130 Cr to expand its AI-led social commerce platform
The pre-Series B round, led by VC firm IvyCap Ventures, comprises fresh capital for business expansion and a secondary component for partial liquidity to early shareholders.
Bengaluru-based Live2.ai, which uses artificial intelligence (AI) to connect social-media intelligence with marketing and commerce, has raised Rs 130 crore ($14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by venture capital firm IvyCap Ventures.
The round combines fresh capital for business expansion and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.
Live2.ai plans to invest the capital in its AI agent platform, expand enterprise deployments, strengthen cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, and recruit engineers, data scientists, and customer success staff.
“Brands today are drowning in signals and starved of action,” said J Venkat, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, Live2.ai. The funding, he added, would help bring detection, decision-making, and activation into a single governed workflow for global enterprise customers.
The platform monitors conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X, and review websites. It integrates trend analysis, influencer-content audits, campaign publishing, and performance measurement. It also converts content cleared for commercial use into shoppable experiences across websites, retail outlets, customer relationship management systems, and online marketplaces.
The investment reflects a wider shift in how brands use social media to understand consumer behaviour and drive sales.
“Social has become a key channel for how consumers discover, evaluate, and buy, yet brands still rely on fragmented and manual tools to understand and act on it,” said Vikram Gupta, Founder and Managing Partner of IvyCap Ventures. He said Live2.ai was building an AI-native operating system to turn real-time cultural signals into commerce, with the security and governance required by global brands.
Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer Neha Suyal said the challenge is to turn intelligence into timely, measurable action at scale.
Live2.ai says it serves more than 200 brands across the United States, Europe and Southeast Asia, including Henkel’s Schwarzkopf, Titan Brands, and Shiseido. Revenue grew fourfold over the past 12 months, according to the company, with 90% generated outside India.
The investment comes at a time when funding into Indian AI businesses is growing. Recent rounds include voice-AI startup Navana.ai’s Rs 40 crore Series A fundraise in September and enterprise software company Kapture’s $10 million pre-Series B funding in June.
Policy is evolving alongside the industry. The government’s IndiaAI Mission has an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years to develop computing infrastructure, support domestic AI capabilities, and promote responsible adoption.
Governance guidelines issued in February this year propose national institutions for AI policy coordination and safety. Separately, consumer-affairs guidance requires clear disclosure of paid or barter influencer endorsements.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Madica raises $6 million for Africa's early-stage startups
articles.text:
Madica, the pre-seed investment programme backed by US venture firm Flourish Ventures, has received $6 million in fresh capital from Flourish to back 25 to 30 more African startups over the next three years.
Each startup will still get up to $200,000, plus 18 months of mentorship, executive coaching and investor-readiness support. All $6 million will go into new pre-seed and seed deals, and none is set aside for follow-on rounds, Madica said in a statement shared with TechCabal on Tuesday. The company said a separate budget pays for founder support but did not disclose the figures.
Madica’s new backing comes as early-stage funding becomes harder to secure. African startups raising between $100,000 and $1 million fell from 179 in the second half of 2025 to 100 in the first half of 2026, a 44% decline, according to Africa: The Big Deal, a funding tracker.
Yet, most of the money that does flow stays in four countries. Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa took 82% of startup funding in 2025, though they are home to about 30% of Africa’s people. Madica’s $200,000 cheques are in the range investors are pulling back from, and it goes looking for founders outside those four markets
When Flourish launched Madica in October 2022, it set aside $6 million to back 25 to 30 startups over three years, with an equal amount for founder support. Madica has backed 18 startups in 10 countries so far, and its first investments came in 2024.
“Three years have given us valuable lessons and encouraging early signals, but building enduring companies and assessing venture outcomes takes longer,” said Emmanuel Adegboye, Head of Madica.
Madica says its portfolio companies have gone on to raise, on average, twice its investment from other investors. On a $200,000 cheque, that is about $400,000 in follow-on funding per company, signalling its early-stage bets are drawing the follow-on capital that most African pre-seed startups struggle to find.
In its statement to TechCabal, Madica described this as a portfolio average, so some companies have raised less, and the figure says nothing about investment returns.
Every company in the portfolio is majority African-owned. More than half have at least one female co-founder, and 39% have a female CEO. In September, Madica made its first investments in Algeria and Cameroon. Adegboye told TechCabal at the time that Madica now co-invests in most deals because a $200,000 cheque alone often isn’t enough.
Madica said it will judge the extension by whether its startups turn early traction into lasting growth and show they can deliver venture returns. It wants other investors to copy what works. If they do, more early money could reach founders outside Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa, where 40% of Madica’s applications already come from.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Google Photos change l'interface de l'onglet « Collections », il va falloir retrouver ses réflexes — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le relooking des applications Google, nous y sommes habitués à force. La firme de Mountain View bouscule alors nos habitudes avec des changements d’interface plus ou moins radicaux, et plus ou moins réussis suivant à qui vous demandez un avis. Dans tous les cas, il faut faire avec.
Exemple avec Google Photos, qui déploie en ce moment une nouvelle version de l’onglet « Collections ». C’est lui qui regroupe vos albums, mais aussi les images et vidéos présentes sur votre smartphone.
Nous avons constaté la nouvelle interface sur la version 7.97.0.1003140569 de Google Photos sur Android. Le Play Store indique une date de mise à jour de l’application au 20 octobre 2026. Les changements par rapport à l’ancienne mouture sont assez marqués, mais ils ont le bon goût d’être paramétrables.
Voici à quoi ressemble l’onglet « Collections » de Google Photos désormais
Avant, « Collections » affichait une grille de 2 cartouches par 2, avec les Favoris et la Corbeille en haut. Les deux autres étant choisis en fonction de vos usages les plus fréquents. En dessous venaient deux grandes cartes pour les Albums et les images Sur cet appareil, puis une liste du reste (Captures d’écran, Vidéos…).
Maintenant, vous êtes accueilli par des cartouches verticaux Épinglés. Par défaut Favoris, Captures d’écran et Corbeille, mais vous pouvez appuyer sur Modifier pour ajouter/retirer ceux de votre choix, tout en changeant leur ordre d’apparition si besoin. C’est ce que vous voyez sur la capture au milieu de l’image ci-dessous.
Viennent ensuite les catégories Sur cet appareil, Albums, Personnes et Lieux. Notez que ces deux dernières s’affichent même si vous n’avez pas activé les paramètres nécessaires à leur fonctionnement. Enfin, les Autres collections se trouvent tout en bas de la page, sous forme de liste.
Le bouton Commander à nouveau peut surprendre. C’est un bug puisqu’il devrait s’appeler Réorganiser et masquer (ou simplement Réorganiser, selon le choix que Google fera lors de la correction de l’affichage).
Il permet d’agencer l’onglet « Collections » comme bon vous semble. Par exemple en supprimant les éléments Épinglés ou les catégories qui ne vous servent pas. Il suffit de décocher les cases associées. C’est aussi là que vous pouvez changer l’ordre de ces catégories.

articles.title: "Puede devorar hasta 30 kg de pescado al día": el temor de los municipios catalanes ante la reintroducción de una criatura perdida hace 50 años
articles.text:
En Cataluña han dado luz verde al regreso de una criatura que desapareció de sus costas hace más de medio siglo. El plan parece simple: traer focas monje desde África y devolverlas al Mediterráneo, empezando por algunos enclaves de la Costa Brava. La iniciativa promete recuperar una especie amenazada y restaurar parte del equilibrio ecológico perdido. El problema está en su apetito: según los pescadores y las autoridades locales, cada ejemplar adulto puede llegar a consumir hasta 30 kilos de pescado al día.
Dos municipios ya han dejado claro que no van a asumir las consecuencias.
Un regreso después de 50 años. La Generalitat quiere recuperar la foca monje del Mediterráneo (Monachus monachus), una especie que antiguamente habitaba las costas catalanas y cuya presencia fue disminuyendo durante el siglo XX. La caza, las capturas accidentales, la persecución por parte de pescadores y la transformación del litoral contribuyeron a su desaparición.
Uno de los últimos avistamientos documentados en el cabo de Creus se produjo en 1973, entre Roses y Cadaqués. El secretario de Transición Ecológica, Jordi Sargatal, lleva más de veinte años defendiendo su recuperación y quiere reactivar el proyecto en 2027, con el cabo de Creus y la isla balear de Cabrera entre los principales lugares considerados.
La solución está a miles de kilómetros, en África. El proyecto contempla trasladar ejemplares procedentes de la colonia de Cabo Blanco, situada en la costa atlántica entre Mauritania y el Sáhara Occidental, uno de los principales refugios mundiales de la especie. Existe un marco de cooperación entre Mauritania, Marruecos, España y Portugal para estudiar el traslado de focas, y Sargatal ha planteado la posibilidad de movilizar entre 15 y 20 animales anuales hacia distintos programas de recuperación.
La estrategia incluye reforzar poblaciones atlánticas como las de Canarias y Madeira y favorecer el intercambio genético con las poblaciones del Mediterráneo oriental. La especie cuenta con una población mundial estimada en varios centenares de ejemplares, repartidos principalmente entre el Atlántico africano, Madeira, Grecia, Turquía y Chipre. El objetivo es crear nuevas poblaciones reproductoras y reducir el riesgo de que una enfermedad o una catástrofe ambiental afecte a una proporción importante de los animales supervivientes.
El problema son los 30 kilos de pescado. La oposición más contundente ha llegado desde El Port de la Selva, cuyo Ayuntamiento y cofradía de pescadores advierten de las consecuencias que podría tener la llegada de estos mamíferos marinos. Según el consistorio, una foca monje adulta "puede devorar hasta 30 kilos de pescado diarios", una cantidad que compara con las capturas de una embarcación durante una semana.
Una apreciación: esa cifra representa el máximo invocado por las autoridades municipales y no debemos confundirla con una ingesta diaria media científicamente acreditada. En cualquier caso, los pescadores temen que la recuperación de un depredador de gran tamaño aumente la competencia por los recursos marinos y afecte a una actividad que consideran fundamental para la economía y la identidad cultural de la localidad.
Tres calas en el centro de la disputa. Porque el Ayuntamiento de Cadaqués también rechaza el proyecto, especialmente por la posibilidad de instalar un recinto experimental en Cala Jugadora, dentro del Parque Natural del Cap de Creus. Según el consistorio, la propuesta podría afectar a tres calas y exigir modificaciones del Plan Rector de Uso y Gestión del parque, con restricciones a la navegación, el fondeo y el acceso a pie.
El municipio cuenta con más de mil embarcaciones y considera que estas limitaciones perjudicarían a la pesca profesional, las empresas náuticas, los centros de buceo y el turismo. Su alcaldesa, Pia Seriñana, ha denunciado que conocieron los detalles a través de los medios de comunicación y exige que se paralicen los trámites hasta que exista información formal y un acuerdo con los sectores afectados.
Una especie amenazada que intenta recuperarse. La foca monje es uno de los mamíferos marinos más escasos del planeta. La Unión Internacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza estima que sobreviven aproximadamente entre 800 y 1.000 individuos y, gracias a los avances de conservación, rebajó su categoría mundial de amenaza de “En peligro” a “Vulnerable” en 2023.
Dicho esto, la recuperación sigue siendo frágil: las poblaciones están fragmentadas, los animales necesitan lugares tranquilos para reproducirse y las interacciones con las actividades pesqueras continúan siendo una amenaza. Para los promotores del proyecto, devolver la especie a Cataluña permitiría recuperar un depredador que formó parte de sus ecosistemas durante siglos.
Una recuperación que tendrá que negociar con la costa. La Generalitat mantiene la iniciativa en una fase preliminar y todavía no existe una fecha definitiva para liberar las criaturas. Ante las resistencias de Cadaqués y El Port de la Selva, Sargatal ha planteado estudiar otros emplazamientos próximos a Portbou, mientras las autoridades locales reclaman información, participación y garantías sobre el futuro de sus actividades económicas.
Sea como fuere, el proyecto resume una de las grandes dificultades de recuperar especies desaparecidas: el territorio al que se pretende devolverlas ha cambiado profundamente durante su ausencia. Así, medio siglo después, el regreso de la foca monje dependerá tanto de las condiciones ecológicas como de la capacidad para hacer compatible su protección con la pesca y los usos tradicionales del litoral.

articles.title: Intel's APX offers 'better performance' in Windows 11 according to new Insider setting — Microsoft begins early enablement for Advanced Performance Extensions on Nova Lake CPUs
articles.text:
Intel's APX offers 'better performance' in Windows 11 according to new Insider setting — Microsoft begins early enablement for Advanced Performance Extensions on Nova Lake CPUs
Advanced Performance Extensions, or APX, will bring improved performance to some apps, but there are no chips that support it just yet.
A new "Advanced Performance Extensions (APX)" option has been spotted in a version of Windows 11 made available to Windows Insiders on October 23, with the feature set to enable a boost in application performance on compatible chips. At the moment, those chips don't exist. But when they do, this feature is the one that you'll want to flick on if you're using one of them. The new toggle was reported by Neowin after it was first spotted by a poster on the X social network. The feature debuted in build 29295 as an Experimental build, so it's unlikely that it will make its way to the version of publicly available Windows 11 anytime soon.
Intel announced APX back in 2023, confirming that it features 16 additional general-purpose registers and three-operand instruction formats with a new data destination register for many integer instructions. Doubling the number of general-purpose registers from 16 to 32 will allow code compiled with APX to run with 10% fewer loads and 20% fewer stores than Intel 64's baseline, says Intel. APX has been available in the GCC compiler since version 14, with subsequent versions up to GCC 17, which is targeting a 2027 code freeze, adding additional support. LLVM and MSVC have preliminary support, as well. Although enablement has been going steady for the past two years, developers will still need to recompile their applications with the proper flags for APX-capable CPUs to leverage those instructions.
Not that there's any real need to rush just yet. The fact that no APX-capable chips are on sale yet means that enabling the feature in Windows 11 build 29295 does nothing currently. But it's clear that Microsoft is getting its ducks in a row ahead of time. Intel's Nova Lake Core Ultra 400-series chips are expected to be the first to feature APX support, but they won't break cover until early 2027. Even then, it's likely that the 28-core version will debut first, with the 52-core model made to wait until later in the year. These are consumer chips, of course, with Intel's Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' bringing APX support and up to 256 cores to the data center, also in 2027.
The good news is that you might not have to buy a new chip to enjoy improved Windows 11 performance. Five years after Windows 11's debut, Microsoft has already said that it's working to make its operating system play more nicely with machines with just 8GB of RAM. But what Microsoft gives with one hand, it soon takes away: an expansion of the Windows 11 Memory Integrity feature will reduce gaming performance on some systems.

articles.title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview on Tuesday. The latest model generates the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet, allowing users to type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene. The model also generates real-time audio that matches the simulated world, including music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue.
The release of Genie 4 comes a couple of months after AI video startup Runway released its second world model, GWM Worlds 2, a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation. At the same time, the world model industry is beginning to consolidate. Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs is being acquired by AMD, Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, and Rivian just acquired Third Dimension to bring simulation capabilities in-house for self-driving testing.
Genie 4 is Google’s latest move to stay ahead in the crowded field.
Google released its predecessor, Genie 3, as a research preview a little over a year ago. Aside from being far more photorealistic and featuring audio, Genie 4 allows for free-form edits, like changing the weather or camera angle in real time or adding new people or objects. It can maintain a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double its predecessor’s limit, and offers better physics and more humanlike characters.
Gemini, Google’s AI model, is also more closely integrated with Genie 4, acting as the director that plans steps and checks frames while Genie creates the visuals. In a research experiment tied to Gemini Robotics, a Gemini 4 Argon model broke down tasks into steps that Genie 4 simulated in real time. The experiment shows a possible way to test robot scenarios in simulation before they happen in the real world.
“What we’ll increasingly see in the future are these hybrid world models, where you have a combination of Gemini writing code and text, and Genie ingesting that in real time and simulating reality at different levels of abstraction,” Tejas Kulkarni, research director at Google, said during a briefing.
As with other world models, the pitched commercial use cases include gaming, interactive learning, and robotics. One speculative example of interactive learning would be entering a painting of a historical scene and chatting to the painting’s subjects about the event portrayed.
But “trusted testers” — the people who get first access to Google’s cutting-edge products — are pointing to a possible new use: prototyping films.
“The real time aspect becomes most valuable in the areas where keeping a state of flow in the creativity space becomes incredibly useful,” Diego Rivas, a Google DeepMind engineer, said during a press briefing. “For example, in the ideation phase, in the storyboarding phase — anytime you’re kind of in need of rapid ideation.”
Google also offers Veo, its AI video-generation model that makes high-definition clips with built-in synchronized audio from text, image, or video prompts — a tool that has been growing in popularity among filmmakers.
Rivas added that users could, eventually, rely on Gemini Omni, a multimodal large language model that can generate video from images, audio, and text, to turn those prototypes into creative assets. Though those capabilities, he says, are still a ways off.
Throughout the briefing, Rivas stressed that it’s still early days for Genie 4 and that it’s not yet clear what the end-to-end product experience will be. The team also acknowledged that Genie 4 still has gaps: Details and objects can drift the longer a simulation runs, and they still haven’t quite figured out how to ensure the audio will be accurate and any in-world text will be legible.
Genie 4 is available now as a research preview for trusted testers. In the coming weeks, the model will roll out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie, Google’s AI tool for generating interactive worlds from text or image prompts, and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

articles.title: Warner Bros. drops final trailer for Dune: Part Three
articles.text:
The end of the year is fast approaching and with it, the pre-Christmas release of Dune: Part Three, the final installment in Denis Villeneuve’s acclaimed adaptation of sci-fi author Frank Herbert’s novel(s). Warner Bros. gave us a broody and haunting extended teaser in March and a July trailer jam-packed with tantalizing hints of what to expect, along with plenty of Easter eggs to delight avid book fans. Now we’ve got one last action-packed trailer setting up the final act for iconic anti-hero Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet).
(Spoilers for first two films in the franchise below.)
Previously, 2021’s Dune culminated in the brutal defeat of House Atreides by rival House Harkonnen, with Paul and his mother, Lady Jessica (Rebecca Ferguson), fleeing to the desert and taking refuge among the Fremen. Among them is Chani (Zendaya), whom Paul has been seeing in visions all along.
In Dune: Part Two (2024), Paul ingratiated himself with the Fremen, learned to ride a sandworm, and won Chani’s love. A pregnant Lady Jessica had her own plans for Paul as a messiah figure to fulfill a Bene Gesserit prophecy. Ultimately, Paul challenges the emperor, defeats his champion, and demands the Princess Irulan (Florence Pugh) as his wife. The other Great Houses reject Paul as ruler, so he launches a holy war against them. And Chani rides off on a sandworm after refusing to bow down to Paul.

articles.title: Grab 32GB of DDR5 RAM for just $151 in this 4-in-1 Newegg bundle with the 9800X3D and a 2TB SSD — start building a high-end 4K gaming PC with this combo deal that also includes an AM5 Gigabyte motherboard and a free MSI AIO liquid cooler
articles.text:
Grab 32GB of DDR5 RAM for just $151 in this 4-in-1 Newegg bundle with the 9800X3D and a 2TB SSD — start building a high-end 4K gaming PC with this combo deal that also includes an AM5 Gigabyte motherboard and a free MSI AIO liquid cooler
Four big parts for your next rig with a juicy discount
Rather than spending $450 on 32GB of DDR5 all by itself, you can save a ton of money when you pick up RAM as part of Newegg's PC component bundles, $350 in this case. In this bundle, you can pick up four parts you need for $1,180.99 in a set that includes the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D with 32GB DDR5, a Gigabyte X870E motherboard, and 2TB of SSD storage.
● Check out this deal at Newegg
The discount knocks $358.99 off the combined price for this kit, meaning you're picking up RAM for the equivalent price of just $151.01. That's a massive discount compared to the current price for 32GB of DDR5 RAM, let alone this particular kit, which would cost you $509.99 if you bought it separately.
The price is even better when you include the freebies. A year's worth of McAfee isn't much to write home about, but a free MSI MAG Coreliquid A13 240mm AIO cooler worth $72.49 certainly is. That'll help you keep the 9800X3D cool, and it's totally free with this kit, too.
This is a significant haul for the price in the current market, giving you several of the components you'd need to kickstart a new 4K gaming PC build. Whether it's $358.99 you're saving, or over $431 if you include the free AIO, you're saving several hundred dollars that you can put towards a case, peripherals, power supply, or that all-important GPU purchase.
Four significant parts for a gaming PC build are combined in this Newegg combo deal. It includes the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of Team Group T-Force Delta RGB DDR5-6000 RAM, a Gigabyte AM5 X870E Aorus Elite WiFi 7 motherboard, and a 2TB Team Group NV5000 SSD, along with a free AIO cooler from MSI worth $72.49.
The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D is one of the fastest gaming CPUs on the market right now, as you'll see in our CPU benchmark data, and it's still the top option in our best CPU guide. Other chips, like the 9950X3D2, have nudged ahead on performance, but with significantly higher power demands.
AMD dominates the market with its 3D V-cache chips: there just isn't a matching alternative from Intel. The extra L3 cache it provides, with a total of 96MB in the 9800X3D, means that your CPU doesn't have to revert to the slower system RAM. The result is better, more stable frame rates, and overall better gaming performance.
As specs go, you're getting a modern Zen 5 CPU with eight cores. All eight have access to the increased 96MB L3 cache, too. You get a clock speed of 4.7 GHz, which boosts up to 5.2 GHz, and a TDP of 120W. This is a CPU that won't struggle with the demands of 4K gaming with ray tracing, as long as you have a GPU able to match it.
This AM5 CPU needs a motherboard to match, and with this bundle, you're getting the Gigabyte X870E Aorus Elite Wi-Fi 7. This is a mid-tier board for gamers from Gigabyte, and it comes with a set of features designed with gamers in mind. You get 12 USB ports at the back here, with two USB-C ports that give speeds of up to 40 Gbps.
You can install a whole set of M.2 SSDs here, and with the 9800X3D installed, three of them are rated for PCIe 5.0 speeds. 2.5G Ethernet and Wi-Fi 7 support is included, and the board also includes support for up to 256GB of DDR5 RAM for speeds up to 8,200 MT/s.
This bundle isn't quite that good, but you do get 32GB here. Two 16GB modules of Team Group T-Force Delta RGB RAM are included, with speeds of 6,000 MT/s, with CAS and memory timings of 38-38-38-78. Good RAM for gaming, especially with customizable RGB lighting, but it's the price that beats it all. As we mentioned, the discounts applied here mean you're getting this $500+ RAM set for the equivalent of just $151.01.
Oh, and 2TB of SSD storage is included, which'll give you plenty of space for big AAA games alongside a Windows installation. The Team Group NV5000 SSD here is an M.2 NVMe SSD with Gen 4 speeds, and it'll be a good start option in a market where, like RAM, SSDs are becoming very expensive.
This $1,180.99 Newegg combo deal for the 9800X3D, 32GB DDR5, a 2TB SSD, and a Gigabyte AM5 gaming motherboard is a real steal in the market, and one that'll save you $358.99. You won't find 32GB of DDR5-6000 RAM for anything close to the equivalent $151.01 cost you're getting it here. This is a good, core set of parts that'll help you build a new, or upgrade an existing, 4K gaming PC, with that freebie AIO from MSI to help keep it cool.

Un Dual Mode pour choisir entre finesse et vitesse
Le Dual Mode est l’argument le plus pratique de cet écran. En 4K, il monte à 160 Hz pour profiter de la finesse de l’image dans les jeux solo. En 1080p, il grimpe à 320 Hz pour les jeux compétitifs où chaque image compte. Et grâce à une latence ultra-faible de seulement 0,5 ms, vous n’aurez aucun retard entre votre action en jeu et la réaction de l’écran.
Il vaut donc mieux avoir une carte graphique qui soit capable de suivre la cadence afin d’exploiter tout son potentiel. Enfin, à l’arrière on retrouve une connectique complète : deux ports HDMI 2.1, un port DisplayPort 1.4a, un port USB-C, deux ports USB 2.0 Type-A, un port USB Type-B et une sortie casque audio.
Pour tout savoir sur ce moniteur gaming, vous pouvez consulter notre test complet sur le MSI MPG 274URDFW E16M.
Si vous souhaitez le comparer à d’autres modèles en 1080p, 1440p ou 4K, jetez un œil à notre comparatif des meilleurs écrans PC gamer.

articles.title: Rachat de SFR : Orange confirme le calendrier mais dit faire très attention à un détail en particulier
articles.text:
Orange a confirmé, ce mardi en publiant ses résultats trimestriels, que le rachat de SFR reste prévu pour fin 2027. L’opérateur reconnaît toutefois attendre des décisions de justice liées aux procédures engagées par les représentants des salariés.
Le rachat de SFR par ses concurrents Orange, Bouygues Telecom et Free reste attendu au second semestre 2027, si les autorités donnent leur feu vert. C'est ce que l'opérateur historique vient de rappeler ce mardi, en marge de la présentation de ses résultats trimestriels. Le discours d'Orange est plutôt sobre, presque administratif peut-on dire, mais il tombe au moment où les représentants du personnel de SFR ferraillent devant la justice. On rappelle que ce rachat constitue une opération à 20,35 milliards d'euros, qui décidera à terme chez qui atterriront 25 millions d'abonnés.
Orange ne bouge pas d’un pouce sur le calendrier du rachat de SFR, malgré les remous
Il faut lire le communiqué financier d'Orange jusqu'à sa deuxième page pour tomber sur les trois petites phrases qui nous intéressent le plus aujourd'hui, en tout cas dans le cadre de notre article. Orange y rappelle en effet la signature, le 6 juin dernier, du protocole d'accord conclu avec Bouygues Telecom et Free pour se partager SFR, le deuxième opérateur du pays. Il aura fallu s'y reprendre à deux fois, souvenez-vous, Altice ayant éconduit une première offre de 17 milliards d'euros il y a tout juste un an. Le calendrier, lui, « reste inchangé » nous apprend Orange, avec une finalisation envisagée au second semestre 2027, sous réserve du feu vert des régulateurs. L'Autorité de la concurrence, saisie du dossier en juillet, avait annoncé au moins dix-huit mois d'examen.
Orange ajoute que des décisions sont encore attendues dans les procédures engagées par les comités sociaux et économiques d'Altice France. Le CSE central de SFR a en effet saisi la justice, contre Altice comme contre les trois repreneurs, pour obtenir davantage d'informations sur la cession. Le tribunal judiciaire de Paris devait se prononcer cette semaine, avec surtout une audience sur le fond prévue début décembre.
Ce dialogue social, auquel Orange se dit « attaché », a connu des jours plus orageux. Le 24 septembre par exemple, environ un tiers des 8 000 salariés de SFR a cessé le travail, selon les syndicats. Le consortium promet une solution à chacun, à savoir que quelque 5 000 rejoindraient les trois acheteurs, et 3 000 resteraient chez SFR le temps de piloter la migration. C'est insuffisant pour l'intersyndicale, qui réclame trois offres de reclassement par personne et des indemnités de départ plus généreuses. Après avoir présenté leur proposition de septembre comme finale, les acheteurs devaient revenir à la table le 16 octobre avec une nouvelle offre, dont rien n'a pour l'instant filtré.
Qui récupère quoi dans le grand partage de SFR ?
Pour ce qui est des 20,35 milliards d'euros, le montant devrait se répartir de façon inégale. Bouygues Telecom prendra 42 % à sa charge pour repartir avec le plus gros lot, c'est-à-dire l'intégralité de SFR Business, environ 5,9 millions de clients particuliers et le réseau mobile des zones peu denses. De quoi devenir, à terme, le numéro deux du marché. Free (31 %) héritera des 6 millions d'abonnés RED by SFR, auxquels s'ajouteraient 1,6 million de clients SFR. Orange, avec 27 %, se contentera d'environ 4,9 millions de clients, dont ceux des opérateurs virtuels Syma, Coriolis et Réglo Mobile. Concernant les magasins, seules 120 boutiques SFR seraient reprises (sur 500 environ), une quarantaine par acheteur.
Pour les clients, il n'y a pas franchement d'urgence. Dans une FAQ publiée le 19 octobre, l'ARCEP, le régulateur des télécoms, rappelle qu'aucune démarche n'est nécessaire, que chacun conserve son numéro de téléphone et que SFR est tenu à ses obligations de couverture et de qualité de service. Le sort des box et des décodeurs, en revanche, n'est pas tranché. Une fois l'opération autorisée, les repreneurs prévoient trente mois de transition, pilotés par une structure commune, avec une migration qui pourrait s'étirer jusqu'à mi-2030, avant que la marque SFR ne s'efface. Dans l'intervalle, SFR et RED by SFR relèvent certains tarifs jusqu'à 5 euros par mois, ce qui ne manque pas de faire réagir, même si l'opérateur au carré rouge laisse aux abonnés concernés quatre mois pour partir sans frais.
Les finances d'Orange, elles, se portent bien. À périmètre comparable, le chiffre d'affaires progresse de 3,6 % au troisième trimestre, à 12,2 milliards d'euros ; en données brutes, la hausse atteint 22 %, gonflée par l'intégration d'Orange España (ex-MasOrange) depuis le mois de juin. L'Afrique et le Moyen-Orient tirent la croissance (+14,2 %), tandis que la France avance à petits pas (+0,5 %), malgré des ventes nettes record, avec 146 000 lignes mobiles et 78 000 accès fixes de plus. L'EBITDAaL gagne 4,6 %, ce qui permet de relever l'objectif annuel au-delà de 4,5 %. Le groupe revendique plus de 367 millions d'accès et prévoit un dividende de 0,79 euro par action, dont un acompte de 0,30 euro versé le 3 décembre, le solde restant soumis au vote des actionnaires.

articles.title: Günstiger als Glasfaser? Wann 5G die bessere Alternative ist
articles.text:
Besser als Glasfaser? Dieser Standard wäre zumindest deutlich günstiger
Beim Ausbau von Glasfaserkabeln hinkt Deutschland im europäischen Vergleich weiter hinterher. Vor allem im ländlichen Raum gibt es noch viele weiße Flecken.
Bis die Glasfaserinfrastruktur großflächig etabliert ist, könnte das Mobilfunknetz einspringen, um Breitbandinternet zu liefern. Dies schlägt jedenfalls das deutsche Beratungsunternehmen Dialog Consult in einer Studie vor.
5G Fixed-Wireless-Access kann auf bestehende Struktur zurückgreifen
Dialog Consult setzt genauer gesagt auf 5G Fixed-Wireless-Access (5G FWA). Dabei wird Breitbandinternet über das Mobilfunknetz an einen festen Standort geliefert. Kabel müssen dazu nicht verlegt werden.
Der Vorteil: Die Infrastruktur besteht bereits. Gebäude müssten nur mit einem 5G-Router oder einer Außenantenne nachgerüstet werden.
5G als Ergänzung und Übergangslösung für Glasfaser
Die Autoren betonen, dass sie Glasfaser nicht zugunsten von 5G aufgeben wollen. Sie sehen den Standard eher als Ergänzung und Übergangslösung.
So könnte 5G die Zeit überbrücken, bis großflächig Glasfaserkabel verlegt sind. In Gegenden, in denen sich der Ausbau von Glasfasertechnologie wirtschaftlich nicht lohnt, könnte 5G FWA sogar dauerhaft eine alternative Lösung darstellen.
In Österreich kommt laut der Studie bereits im großen Stil Fixed-Wireless-Access zum Einsatz. Die Hälfte aller Breitbandanschlüsse läuft im Nachbarland über 4G oder 5G. Dies gelte vor allem für ländliche Gegenden.
5G FWA ist deutlich günstiger als Glasfaser
Ein Glasfaseranschluss kostet laut einer Analyse des Bundesverbands Breitbandkommunikation (BREKO) zwischen 1.600 und 3.900 Euro.
Der Ausbau von Mobilfunkfunknetzen hin zu 5G FWA benötige hingegen nur 72 bis 100 Euro pro Teilnehmer. Kommen dabei Millimeterwellen, bei denen die Latenzzeit kürzer ist, zum Einsatz, liegen die Kosten bei 132 bis 180 Euro.
5G FWA in drei Studien wirtschaftlicher als Glasfaser
Dialog Consult verglich in drei Fallstudien die Kosten von 5G FWA und Glasfaser hinsichtlich des Cash-Flow. Bei allen Fällen berechneten sie ein Basisszenario und ergänzten mögliche Abweichungen mit jeweils einem optimistischen und einem pessimistischen Szenario.
Alle drei Studien haben den Unternehmensberatern zufolge einen wirtschaftlichen Vorteil von 5G FWA gezeigt. Den schnelleren Rollout der Mobilfunklösungen haben sie dabei noch nicht einmal berücksichtigt.

articles.title: Noel Tata challenges resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman
articles.text:
Noel Tata challenges resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman
Noel Tata wrote to Tata Sons' company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay on Monday, challenging the resolution for the reappointment of Chandrasekaran beyond February 2027 as well, which brought the ruptures inside the over-century-old conglomerate's board out in the open.
Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata on Monday challenged the resolution to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as the chairman of Tata Sons, which was passed at the September 17 board meeting of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate.
Noel Tata wrote to Tata Sons' company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay on Monday, challenging the resolution for the reappointment of Chandrasekaran beyond February 2027 as well, which brought the ruptures inside the over-century-old conglomerate's board out in the open.
Sources privy to the development said Noel has termed the reappointment for five years as void, basing his argument on a slew of factors, including notice and the agenda for the meeting.
Noel contended that the reappointment was taken out of turn and it was not on the agenda at all for the meeting, the sources said, adding that it was limited to a debriefing from the nomination and remuneration committee.
Emails sent to Tata Sons and Tata Trusts seeking comments on the matter did not elicit an immediate response.
Noel, who heads the Tata Trusts that own two-thirds of Tata Sons, had opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment when it had been put to vote. Venu Srinivasan, the second of the Tata Trusts' directors on the board of Tata Sons, sided with the majority in favour of the reappointment.
Other directors who had voted in favour of Chandrasekaran's reappointment at the meeting included Anita George, Harish Manwani, and Saurabh Agarwal.
As per Tata Sons' Articles of Association, Tata Trusts' nominee directors have to give their affirmative vote for a resolution to be passed, Noel contended.
In the letter, Noel also sought an unedited video recording of the board meeting, according to the sources.

articles.title: Apple renueva el iMac y el MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas con los procesadores M6: el precio es el plato amargo
articles.text:
Quien avisa no es traidor, pero Apple nos ha traicionado un poco con las fechas. Sabíamos que este miércoles 28 de octubre Apple presentaría nuevos dispositivos y sabíamos perfectamente que sería el iPad Mini OLED, nuevos Mac con el M6 y el MacBook Pro con panel táctil OLED. Sin embargo, parece que Apple tiene claro que el más especial es el modelo con pantalla táctil y ha decidido dejar todos los focos del miércoles para él solito.
Así, ayer presentó el nuevo iPad Mini que, aparte de la pantalla OLED, monta el espectacular SoC A20 Pro que ya hemos puesto a prueba en el análisis del iPhone 18 Pro Max. Y hoy ha desvelado la renovación de dos de los Mac que aún no habían dado el salto al chip M6 que debutó hace unos meses con el Mac mini.
A continuación, vamos con todos los detalles tanto del MacBook Pro M6 como del iMac M6.
Nuevos Mac con M6
"Hasta 13 veces más rápido en tareas de IA que el M1". Apple se empeña en comparar todos los nuevos SoC M con el de primera generación cuando han pasado seis añazos y el M1 no estaba diseñado para eso. Dicho esto, el principal cambio de este MacBook Pro es, evidentemente, el procesador.
El M6 cuenta con una CPU de 12 núcleos compuesta por dos núcleos de alta potencia, cuatro de rendimiento y seis de eficiencia. La GPU es de 12 núcleos y parte de 16 GB de memoria RAM con un ancho de banda de 153 GB/s, pero que podemos ampliar a 24 o 32 con un ancho de banda de 170 GB/s.
El almacenamiento sigue siendo de 1, 2 o 4 TB y donde también han actualizado es en el Wi-Fi. De un Wi-Fi 6e que ya nos chirrió en el modelo del año pasado, pasamos por fin a Wi-Fi 7 para equipararse con los modelos que tienen los M5 Pro y M5 Max.
Y un detalle importante: el único MacBook Pro que cuenta con el nuevo procesador M6 es el modelo de 14 pulgadas. Si nos vamos a las 16 Pulgadas, las únicas opciones son los M5 Pro y Max, cuya renovación la veremos en algún momento de comienzos de 2027.
Si miramos el iMac M6, los cambios son básicamente los mismos. Wi-Fi 7 y la nueva versión del procesador que, en esta ocasión, sí detallan como cinco veces más rápido para tareas de IA que el iMac M4. Parte de los 16 GB de memoria RAM y de los sonrojantes 256 GB de almacenamiento.
Ahora bien, aquí sí tenemos dos versiones de M6:
- El mismo que en el MacBook Pro con 12 núcleos tanto de CPU como de GPU.
- Una versión recortada con 10 núcleos de GPU (un núcleo menos tanto de rendimiento como de eficiencia) y 10 núcleos de GPU.
La memoria en ambos casos cuenta con un ancho de banda de 170 GB/s.
Precio y lanzamiento de los nuevos iMac M6 y MacBook Pro M6
Como es habitual, es una renovación "porque toca". Ya habían metido el M6 en dos de los Mac y tocaba ir haciendo el relevo en los que quedan. Sin embargo, que Apple haya optado por actualizar sólo el modelo de 14 pulgadas nos dice que el de 16 pulgadas lo va a enfocar a un usuario más profesional que opte por los procesadores más capaces y caros.
Hablando de precios, el MacBook Pro M6 de 14 pulgadas sube 100 euros el precio respecto a la generación anterior, partiendo de 2.329 euros en su versión de 1 TB, 16 GB de RAM y sin pantalla nanotexturizada.
El iMac M6 es una victoria pírrica porque hay que celebrar que no suben el precio... más de lo que ya subieron este verano. Porque si el iMac M4 salió por 1.519 euros en octubre de hace dos años, este verano subió 300 euros para colocarse en 1.819 euros. Ese es el precio del iMac con el M6 de 10 núcleos y, si queremos el de 12 núcleos, toca dejarse 2.019 euros.
Por un PC de sobremesa que está pensado para aplicaciones creativas con... 256 GB de memoria.
Tanto uno como otro se podrán reservar a partir de este 28 de octubre y se pondrán a la venta el próximo 6 de noviembre.
