articles.title: Oxfam-Bericht: Superreiche treiben die Klimakrise an – und profitieren davon
articles.text:
Oxfam-Bericht: Milliardäre treiben Emissionen – und profitieren von Klimaschäden
Superreiche heizen mit ihrem Lebensstil den Klimawandel überproportional an und verdienen zugleich an den Folgen. Das zeigt ein Bericht der Entwicklungsorganisation Oxfam, der im Vorfeld der UN-Klimakonferenz COP31 veröffentlicht wurde.
Allein Privatjet-Flüge verursachten im vergangenen Jahr weltweit 16 Millionen Tonnen CO₂. Ein Flug mit einem Privatjet stößt im Schnitt 3,7 Tonnen CO₂ aus und damit fast so viel, wie ein Mensch im globalen Durchschnitt pro Jahr verursacht. Die reichsten 0,1 Prozent der Menschheit verantworten mehr konsumbasierte Emissionen als die ärmsten 44 Prozent, also rund 3,5 Milliarden Menschen, zusammen.
Milliardäre profitieren von der Klimakrise
Auch die Investitionen der Superreichen verschärfen die Klimakrise, betont Oxfam. Der Bericht „Disaster Divide“ analysierte die Geldanlagen von 1.000 Milliardär:innen im Jahr 2025. Die Autor:innen nutzten dafür unter anderem die Forbes-Milliardärsliste sowie Daten von Bloomberg und S&P Capital IQ. Das Ergebnis: 71 Prozent der Investitionen flossen in besonders klimaschädliche Branchen wie Öl, Gas oder Chemie. Die damit verbundenen Emissionen summierten sich auf 486 Millionen Tonnen CO₂-Äquivalente.
Auch für diesen Zusammenhang findet Oxfam einen anschaulichen Vergleich: Ein Milliardär verursacht mit seinen Investitionen in etwas mehr als einer Minute mehr CO₂ als ein Mensch aus der ärmeren Hälfte der Weltbevölkerung im ganzen Jahr. Unter den knapp 1.000 Milliardär:innen sind auch 49 Deutsche, deren Investitionsemissionen im Durchschnitt bei 704.881 Tonnen CO₂-Äquivalenten und damit laut den Oxfam-Daten weit über dem internationalen Durchschnitt liegen. Ein deutscher Milliardär verursacht allein durch Unternehmensanteile in gut sechs Minuten mehr CO₂ als ein Mensch aus der ärmeren Hälfte Deutschlands im gesamten Jahr.
Gleichzeitig wächst der Markt für den Wiederaufbau nach Katastrophen, getrieben von klimabedingten Extremwetterereignissen, von geschätzten 70 Milliarden US-Dollar im Jahr 2024 auf 92 Milliarden US-Dollar im Jahr 2029. Oxfam fasste dazu 217 börsennotierte Unternehmen im „Destroy & Rebuild“-Index zusammen: große Öl-, Gas-, Kohle- und Zementproduzenten auf der einen, Firmen aus Klimaschutz und Katastrophen-Wiederaufbau auf der anderen Seite. Die Daten zeigen unter anderem, dass große Vermögensverwalter wie Blackrock oder Vanguard gleich doppelt am Klimawandel verdienen.
Vermögensverwalter wie Vanguard, Blackrock und State Street investieren sowohl in die Verursacher als auch in die Beseitigung von Katastrophen. So investiert etwa Blackstone beim Katastrophensanierer Servpro, hält aber zugleich Anteile am Kohlekraftwerk Gavin in Ohio, einem der größten Kohleemittenten der USA. Mitunter nutzen Investor:innen Katastrophen auch, um wirtschaftsliberale Politik durchzusetzen: Nach Hurrikan Maria 2017 in Puerto Rico privatisierte man das Stromnetz, nach Hurrikan Irma entstanden in Barbuda beim Wiederaufbau vor allem Luxuswohnungen und ein Golfplatz.
Oxfam fordert gerechte Besteuerung
Oxfam zieht daraus klare Forderungen an die Politik: Wer die Klimakrise so stark befeuert, müsse auch für ihre Bewältigung zahlen, statt die Kosten auf die Allgemeinheit abzuwälzen, sagte Manuel Schmitt, Referent für soziale Ungleichheit bei Oxfam. Die Organisation verlangt neben einem konsequenten Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien eine gerechte Besteuerung großer Vermögen.
Reiche Länder sollen zumindest ihre Zusage von der Weltklimakonferenz in Belém einhalten und die Mittel für Klimaanpassung bis 2035 verdreifachen.
Das Geld könnte etwa aus Steuern für die Reichsten und aus Übergewinnsteuern für Konzerne kommen. Zudem sollen mehr Gelder für Klimaanpassung als Zuschüsse und nicht als Kredite fließen.

articles.title: Nexus Luxembourg 2027: Applications now open for Startups & Scaleups Awards (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Around 240 startups and scale-ups will pitch live in Luxembourg on 9–10 March 2027, competing for a Grand Prize worth over €125,000. Applications close on 16 November.
Most founders know the trade-off of the conference circuit: a booth that costs thousands, a pitch slot you have to pay for on top, and no guarantee the right people walk by. The Nexus Luxembourg Startups & Scaleups Awards take a different approach. If your company is selected, an all-inclusive package costs €99, VAT included.
That gets you a booth for both days, a live pitch in front of investors and corporate decision-makers and a seat at the awards ceremony. Applications are open to startups and scale-ups from anywhere in the world, until 16 November 2026 at 12:00 CET.
What selected startups & scale-ups get
The €99 package covers three things:
- A turnkey exhibition booth for both days, to meet attendees, partners and investors.
- A live pitching slot on stage, in front of a jury of experts and investors.
- A reserved seat at the Awards Ceremony on day two, 10 March.
The stakes go beyond visibility. The overall winner takes home a Grand Prize worth over €125,000. Last year’s package combined €25,000 in cash with more than €100,000 in services from Luxembourg partners, from legal, tax and cybersecurity support to co-working space, high-performance computing and media campaigns. The 2026 category winners also got a dedicated investor matchmaking session at the Luxembourg Venture Days.
Who can apply: 12 categories
The Awards are open to startups and scale-ups worldwide. Applicants pick one of 12 categories:
| Category | Typical solutions | 
|---|---|
| RegTech & LegTech | Compliance automation, KYC/AML, legal tech | 
| FinTech & InsurTech | WealthTech, banking, payments, insurance | 
| Cybersecurity & Data Sovereignty | Cloud security, cryptography, European data sovereignty | 
| Digital Society & GovTech | Public-sector digitalisation, digital identity, citizen services | 
| Enterprise AI & Workflow Automation | GenAI at work, domain-specific LLMs, RPA | 
| SpaceTech | Satellite imagery, orbital logistics, space data | 
| Industrial AI & Smart Logistics | Digital twins, supply chain AI, predictive maintenance | 
| Smart Mobility | Connected vehicles, MaaS, fleet decarbonisation | 
| GreenTech & ClimateTech | Decarbonisation, ESG reporting, circular economy | 
| Digital Health & Platforms | Telemedicine, patient monitoring, health data | 
| Clinical & MedTech Innovation | Medical devices, AI diagnostics, surgical robotics | 
| EdTech & Future of Work | Re-skilling, talent management, collaboration tools | 
Key dates
The window is short: applications close in a few weeks.
| Date | Milestone | 
|---|---|
| 16 November 2026, 12:00 CET | Applications close | 
| 10 December 2026 | Selected startups and scale-ups announced | 
| 9–10 March 2027 | Live pitches and Awards Ceremony at Nexus Luxembourg | 
Why Nexus Luxembourg is worth a founder’s two days
Nexus Luxembourg has grown fast. The June 2026 edition drew more than 9,600 attendees from over 80 countries, with 400+ speakers on five stages.
The 2027 edition runs under the theme “Building AI, Sovereignty & Growth“. That matters for founders: the focus is on European companies that build, sell and scale trusted technology, not only on regulation. Startups pitch in the Launchpad Arena, alongside the Intelligence Forum, the Fintech Sphere and the institutional hub “Luxembourg Makes It Happen“.
Luxembourg’s size works in founders’ favour. Government, the financial centre, EU institutions, corporates, founders and international investors share the same venue for two days, which makes the right meeting easier to get.
Applications close on 16 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. Apply now on the Nexus Luxembourg website.
Nexus Luxembourg 2027 takes place on 9–10 March 2027 at Luxexpo The Box, Luxembourg-Kirchberg. For questions about the awards, contact: [email protected].

articles.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
articles.text:
Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- University of Cambridge
- Summary:
- Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.
- Share:
A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.
Researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.
Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.
The researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.
A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision
Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.
To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.
"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system."
The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.
Another important advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.
A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare
To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.
When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.
The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.
The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.
"These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment."
The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.
Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough
The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.
Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.
The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.
"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible."
Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.
Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices
The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.
In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.
Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.
"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work shows that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day."
As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Original written by Michael Shuff. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:

articles.title: James Webb encontra galáxia em forma de anel que pode ter nascido de colisão rara
articles.text:
O telescópio espacial James Webb identificou a galáxia em forma de anel mais distante já observada. Batizada de GS18660, ela aparece como era cerca de 2,1 bilhões de anos após o Big Bang e pode ter se formado a partir de colisão entre duas galáxias no Universo primordial.
A estrutura chama a atenção por apresentar um anel de estrelas recém-nascidas. Segundo um estudo publicado em 8 de setembro na revista científica Astronomy & Astrophysics, diferentes evidências indicam que uma galáxia menor pode ter atravessado o centro da GS18660, desencadeando a formação do anel.
A hipótese, no entanto, ainda não foi confirmada. Os pesquisadores consideram a colisão a explicação mais provável, mas reconhecem que outras possibilidades precisam ser investigadas.
Como uma colisão pode criar uma galáxia em forma de anel?
- Quando uma galáxia menor atravessa o centro de outra maior, o impacto pode produzir uma onda de gás denso que se propaga para fora. O processo é semelhante às ondulações que aparecem na superfície da água quando uma pedra cai em um lago;
- O gás se acumula ao longo dessa onda e favorece o nascimento de novas estrelas. Com isso, a galáxia pode desenvolver uma estrutura circular brilhante;
- Esse tipo de formação é raro no Universo próximo. Embora interações entre galáxias possam ter sido comuns no Universo primordial, a criação de estruturas em forma de anel por colisões é considerada incomum;
- No caso da GS18660, os astrônomos identificaram uma galáxia companheira menor que se afasta da estrutura principal a aproximadamente 425 quilômetros por segundo. Os pesquisadores também encontraram uma ponte de gás conectando os dois objetos, com mudanças de velocidade ao longo de sua extensão;
- Esses sinais sugerem que as galáxias podem estar interagindo. A posição da companheira também é compatível com a hipótese de que ela tenha atravessado o disco da galáxia principal.
O que o James Webb descobriu?
A GS18660 foi selecionada para observação porque imagens anteriores do telescópio espacial Hubble mostravam estrutura alongada. Os pesquisadores não procuravam especificamente uma galáxia anelar.
Foi somente com as observações mais detalhadas do James Webb, utilizando o instrumento NIRSpec, que a estrutura circular ficou evidente. Os cientistas conseguiram investigar a forma da galáxia em três dimensões, acompanhar os movimentos do gás quente, analisar sua composição química e estudar a história de formação de estrelas.
Os dados também ajudaram a estimar quando a possível colisão aconteceu. De acordo com os cálculos da equipe, o evento teria ocorrido entre 17 milhões e 42 milhões de anos antes do período observado.
Os pesquisadores estimam ainda que entre 10% e 20% da massa estelar da região do anel tenha se formado nas últimas dezenas de milhões de anos. Isso reforça a possibilidade de que o impacto tenha desencadeado um episódio intenso de formação de estrelas.
Leia mais:
- Uma explosão cósmica durou 27 dias; o que a manteve ativa?
- Entenda a origem da Lua do Caçador que brilhou no céu este mês
- Simulação impressionante recria os primeiros bilhões de anos do Universo
Colisão não é a única explicação possível
Apesar das evidências, os cientistas ressaltam que nenhum dos sinais observados comprova isoladamente que houve uma colisão. A interpretação se apoia no conjunto de características da galáxia, incluindo o anel, a presença da companheira e a ponte de gás entre os objetos.
Existe outra explicação possível: uma estrutura interna semelhante a uma barra estelar poderia direcionar gás e estrelas para determinadas regiões, formando um anel sem a necessidade de uma galáxia intrusa.
A própria GS18660 apresenta uma estrutura semelhante a uma barra, que se estende de norte a sul. Ainda não está claro se ela é uma estrutura estelar real ou se também resulta de uma interação entre galáxias.
Descoberta pode mudar o que sabemos sobre o Universo primordial
A descoberta também pode ajudar os astrônomos a compreender a frequência dessas estruturas no passado. Estimativas anteriores sugeriam que galáxias anelares formadas por colisões seriam tão raras no Universo primordial quanto são atualmente, aparecendo em aproximadamente uma a cada dez mil galáxias.
Se a origem por colisão da GS18660 for confirmada, essa estimativa poderá precisar de revisão, indicando que esse tipo de evento era mais comum nas primeiras fases da história cósmica.
Independentemente da explicação definitiva, o objeto oferece oportunidade de investigar como as galáxias já estavam desenvolvendo estruturas complexas quando o Universo tinha apenas alguns bilhões de anos.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Newfoundland and Labrador tech association lays out priorities to unlock province’s budding tech sector | BetaKit
articles.text:
In recent years, Newfoundland and Labrador has solidified its reputation as a budding tech hub by producing one blockbuster exit and outclassing the rest of the country on unicorn companies per capita.
“There are great companies here that sell to other provincial governments, and they’re not selling here.”
Andrea King, TechNL
The 2020 Nasdaq purchase of local financial crime management company Verafin injected more energy into the province’s tech sector, in part because it minted dozens of local millionaires, multiple people told BetaKit. Meanwhile, emerging scale-ups like Spellbook and CoLab Software have attracted Silicon Valley backers like Khosla Ventures and Spider Capital, alongside a strong local presence on their cap tables.
Now, with a new leader at the helm of its main tech association, TechNL, Newfoundland and Labrador could be poised for policy changes that the organization believes could help drive more startup creation and scaleup growth. The provincial government, led by Premier Tony Wakeham, has signalled it’s ready to work together.
Serial entrepreneur Andrea King took over as CEO of the government-funded innovation nonprofit TechNL in August. In addition to its advocacy efforts, the organization (which has roughly 200 members) runs tech and business development skills training events, a graduate transition program, and a number of other events to help place local talent. King told BetaKit at her office in St. John’s which policy changes are top of mind for the sector.
She said the first priority is reducing red tape—including cutting down on duplicate paperwork when applying for funding or grants across multiple provincial and federal organizations—and speeding up the review process in general. The second item relates to a familiar issue for the Canadian ecosystem: procurement reform to enable more purchasing from local companies.
“There are great companies here that sell to other provincial governments, and they’re not selling here,” King said.
Wakeham, who took office a year ago, appeared open to these asks from the sector when King broached them in an on-stage conversation at the TechNL summit last week.
RELATED: Why CoLab is in the “sweet spot” of engineering software
“Our government was elected with a clear commitment to grow our economy, to create new opportunities, and to make Newfoundland and Labrador a better place to live, work, invest, and raise a family,” Wakeham said on stage, adding that it should be a place “where government works with the private sector to create the conditions for investment, innovation, and growth.”
Another ask is to make the province’s tax system more competitive. King suggested one “easy” win would be to increase the province’s investment tax credit rate from 20 percent (in the North Avalon region, where St. John’s is located) to match Nova Scotia’s 35-percent innovation tax credit.
“I’m open to anything that will improve business and create more opportunities in Newfoundland and Labrador,” Wakeham told BetaKit when asked about whether he would consider such tax changes. “Sometimes we can get hung up on how much revenue government takes in through taxation, but I believe that the more money [is] put back in people’s pockets, the government will eventually get it back.”
Wakeham also hinted at a provincial AI strategy, following the release of Canada’s national roadmap this past June. “It’s something we’re working through,” he said. “Part of all of this has to be working with the players in the industry to make it happen.”
On stage, King said getting people to move to Newfoundland and Labrador was one of the most important issues facing the industry. “We need to attract skilled, educated, and ambitious workers,” she said.
Wakeham agreed that the province needs to create more opportunities for work, but noted that there are “challenges” related to the federal government’s reduced immigration targets.
Taylor Young, chief strategy officer at CoLab, said in a recent interview with BetaKit that talent retention hasn’t been a big problem for the company: “I think the connections are so rich between people that people want to be here and they want to come back.”
Feature image courtesy TechNL. Image by Ritche Perez.

articles.title: Apple rolls out iOS 27.2 with new Siri AI languages and security fixes | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple has rolled out its latest iOS 27.2 update for iPhones and iPads, featuring expanded language support and improved memory functions for Siri AI, suggestions in messages, and Apple Pencil support for the foldable iPhone Duo.
With the new software update, Siri AI can now be used in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, in beta. Apple says the AI assistant can now remember details from past conversations and answer accordingly. The ability for AI assistants to remember a person’s preferences have been a key area of focus for AI model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, whose assistants now do a better job at recalling facts and choices related to users.
Apart from its own suggestions and answers, Siri can also tap into sources like photos attached in Messages, calendar event attendees, voicemails, Safari history, and reading lists. Users can define what apps they might want to exclude from Siri AI’s memories.
While the iPhone Duo is facing some display-related problems for early buyers, Apple is adding more features with the update. iOS 27.2 brings Apple Pencil support for the foldable in apps like Notes and Preview. What’s more, users can use the Edge Light effect to highlight their face better during video calls.
The new software version also adds features for FaceTime, including streaming via front and rear camera simultaneously through Dual Capture for group call, and the ability to add a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call.
Users on iOS 27.2 will get suggestions to add a message as an item in a reminder or an event in a calendar. Plus, users can edit captions or add comments in Shared Albums along with reminders of the expiry date of the folder.
The update also refreshes the Podcast app, which will show new episodes from the shows you follow and also the episodes that you are currently listening to.
Apple has also added Multiview to iPhone so viewers can watch up to four live sport streams simultaneously on Apple TV such as Major League Soccer (MLS), Formula 1 (F1) in the U.S., and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders during the Major League Baseball (MLB) season. Users can also view multiple feeds of F1 during the broadcast.
iOS 27.2 also packs in over 160 security fixes, according to the company’s release documentation. Many of the bug fixes were also backported so that users running the older iOS 26 software can benefit from the fixes.
Apple says that about 80% of iPhone owners are still running iOS 26.
Meanwhile, Apple backported a specific bug fix to users of iOS 18, first released in 2024, which Apple says may have been exploited “in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.” This is standard language that Apple uses when someone’s phone has been compromised by government spyware or a law enforcement forensic device, but did not provide specifics about who was exploiting it.

articles.title: Cuidado al verificar que no eres un robot: estafas con CAPTCHA falso dan control de PC a extraños
articles.text:
Una simple casilla con el mensaje “No soy un robot” puede ocultar una trampa si, después del clic, exige abrir herramientas del PC, instalar programas o seguir combinaciones de teclas.
Las estafas con CAPTCHA falso buscan que la propia víctima ejecute acciones que permiten a extraños tomar el control de su computadora y acceder a contraseñas.
ESET advirtió sobre estas maniobras, que imitan verificaciones conocidas para generar confianza. El engaño aprovecha un hábito extendido: muchas personas completan CAPTCHA a diario y pueden seguir indicaciones fuera de lo común sin detenerse a revisar qué están autorizando.
Qué alertas permiten reconocer un CAPTCHA falso
Un CAPTCHA legítimo debe resolverse dentro del navegador. Puede pedir seleccionar imágenes, identificar objetos, escribir caracteres distorsionados o marcar una casilla de verificación. Algunas versiones incluso operan en segundo plano y no requieren ninguna intervención adicional.
La alerta aparece cuando la página solicita abrir Ejecutar, PowerShell, Terminal o el Símbolo del sistema. Conviene cerrar el sitio si pide descargar un archivo, instalar una extensión del navegador, habilitar notificaciones o copiar y pegar instrucciones.
Los expertos advierten que un CAPTCHA no necesita acceso a las herramientas internas del dispositivo para confirmar que hay una persona frente a la pantalla.
Cómo funciona el engaño conocido como ClickFix
Una modalidad frecuente recibe el nombre de ClickFix. En estos casos, una página muestra un supuesto CAPTCHA o un aviso que informa de un problema inexistente en la computadora. Luego, propone una “solución” que requiere abrir una función del sistema y pegar un comando.
El sitio puede copiar ese código al portapapeles sin que la persona lo advierta. Después, las instrucciones indican qué teclas presionar y dónde pegar el contenido. Si el comando se ejecuta, puede instalar programas diseñados para robar información o un troyano de acceso remoto, una herramienta que da a un atacante control sobre el dispositivo.
Por qué esta modalidad de estafa puede ser muy convincente
Los CAPTCHA forman parte de la navegación en internet desde hace más de dos décadas. Su objetivo es diferenciar a una persona de un programa automatizado que intenta acceder a un sitio, enviar formularios o realizar acciones repetitivas.
Google reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha y Cloudflare Turnstile son algunos de los servicios que ofrecen este tipo de controles, así que esa familiaridad explica la eficacia de la estafa.
La apariencia de una ventana falsa puede ser similar a la de un sistema de verificación real, pero el riesgo aparece en el paso posterior. Si una pantalla de seguridad propone salir del navegador, instalar algo o modificar ajustes, hay que interrumpir el proceso y cerrar la página.
Cómo prevenir ejecutar CAPTCHA falso
La dirección del sitio ofrece una primera pista. Es clave observar el nombre de dominio completo para detectar faltas de ortografía, letras cambiadas o direcciones que imitan a empresas y plataformas conocidas.
Asimismo, es útil verificar si el CAPTCHA está integrado en la página o si aparece en una ventana emergente aislada. Los controles legítimos suelen formar parte del formulario o del acceso al sitio.
Pasar el cursor sobre un enlace o una casilla puede mostrar el destino al que dirige. La presencia de HTTPS protege la comunicación frente a interceptaciones, pero no confirma por sí sola que la página sea auténtica.
Qué hacer si se copiaron instrucciones, pero no se ejecutaron en el PC
Si se copió un comando al portapapeles, pero todavía no se presionó Intro ni se completó la instrucción, la pauta es no ejecutarlo. Debe cerrarse cualquier cuadro de diálogo del sistema que haya quedado abierto y reemplazarse el contenido del portapapeles con un texto inofensivo, como una frase cualquiera.
Después, conviene realizar un análisis de seguridad con la herramienta de protección instalada en el dispositivo. Es aconsejable revisar las descargas recientes y las extensiones del navegador para eliminar elementos desconocidos.

articles.title: US officials want Section 702 renewed before damaging court ruling goes public
articles.text:
Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant.
Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September.
The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year.
Wyden, the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff, the former chair of its House counterpart, say the administration owes Congress an explanation for the delay, and the names of the officials responsible, by November 6.
“If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED, “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.”
Outside Congress, Demand Progress and 22 other civil liberties and government accountability groups on Monday urged congressional leaders to refuse to reauthorize Section 702 “while the administration actively withholds legally mandated information about how the surveillance program operates.” Signatories range from the American Civil Liberties Union to the conservative-backed Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability.

articles.title: Data center gear is being hijacked in transit to the tune of hundreds of millions — grand-theft-GPU thieves hack accounts, perform hit-and-runs, spoof GPS signals, and funnel hardware to China
articles.text:
Data center gear is being hijacked in transit to the tune of hundreds of millions — grand-theft-GPU thieves hack accounts, perform hit-and-runs, spoof GPS signals, and funnel hardware to China
At least someone's turning a profit in the AI space.
Have you been watching many heist movies lately? Here's a Hollywood-ready script for a new one: Organized crime teams have taken to stealing data center gear off or with their transport trucks, to the tune of tens of millions per shipment. They employ hacking and phishing, vehicular ramming, GPS signal spoofing, and have ties to international crime networks. An extensive report on NBC sheds light on this new trend, remarking that over $100 million dollars of computing and related gear were stolen via transit interception in various guises since June 2026 alone.
This type of heist has been growing over the past couple of years, but just this year the one incident in Reno made $38 million in gear disappear. In the same city, $15m of semiconductors and Apple products got nabbed in July 2025, according to Fortune. The month of June 2026 was particularly profitable for thieves, as they made off with $13m of gear around the Mojave Desert area, and $10m worth of server rack components headed to Texas.
The stolen gear includes servers, fiber-optic and copper cabling, RAM modules, drives, routers, and other miscellaneous gear. Although NBC doesn't mention GPUs by name, stolen data center servers headed for AI buildouts are likely to have some.
Even copper wire is worth a lot these days, as one snagged trailer had $300,000 worth of the now-precious metal. As Keith Lewis from Verisk Cargonet puts it, "it's like stealing pure gold bars [...] it's so much easier to steal [data center shipments] than to rob a bank."
The methods used employ technological smarts and brutality in equal amounts. Each heist is unique, but broad patterns are apparent. Thieves gain access to online accounts of freight brokers and carriers, and from there on they can look up cargo manifests and shipping schedules, as well as impersonate shipping companies. Then they track a shipment or issue a false one, and eventually collect the truck with the precious cargo.
In a few recent cases, the heists involved thieves literally ramming escort cars so that the truck executes a trouble-free getaway. In those cases, the truck driver was likely in on the play, and probably got in the driver's seat thanks to the prevalence of AI-generated IDs coupled with poor personnel vetting practices.
And as for GPS trailer tracking, the malfeasants thought of that too: in one case, they seemingly used GPS beacon impersonation and broadcast fake coordinates so that neither human nor automated system believed anything was amiss.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The first instinct is to assume that all of the gear would end up on the second-hand market. But in an additional twist to the story, the thieves already have overseas buyers ready before the heist actually takes place.
Law enforcement officials believe that the gear is slurped up by entities operating in countries under the U.S.' tight AI export controls, including China. Verified Carrier, a platform for vetting carriers, says that this year, it's seen suspicious activity linked with U.S. cargo theft in India, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Colombia, and Moldova. Scott Cornell of TAPA Americas estimates that six to seven out of 10 stolen cargo shipments (data center gear or otherwise) end up overseas.
David Warrick, of supply management firm Overhaul, describes the scale of the problem: "These are international syndicates. They run like big corporations…They have penetrated the supply chains at all levels, in terms of drivers, in terms of warehouse operators. They know where all the high-value goods are; they know who transacts them, and they look for the weak points in the supply chain to be able to exploit those."
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.
- bigdragon So you're telling me that people would rather risk consequences with the law than work jobs according to corporate directives? Sounds like there's a systemic problem with the way people are being compensated. We have a serious problem when ripping off data center projects nets people a better quality of life than working legitimately through the system. I don't doubt that a lot of these heists are inside jobs or aided by insiders.Reply

articles.title: Over 70,000 drones light up the night sky in a record-breaking spectacle
articles.text:
71,207 drones broke world record in Texas using Chinese expertise and intriguing 'drone-in-a-box' concept — Shenzhen-based Damoda teamed with Sky Elements to bring 10000-strong dragon to life
Record-breaking light show launches over 70,000 drones
- Sky Elements and Damoda launched 71,207 drones during the record attempt
- A formation of 10,183 drones created the record-breaking blue dragon
- Each performance involved approximately 10,200 drones flying several times daily
Sky Elements teamed up with Damoda America in rural Texas to secure two Guinness World Records, launching a total of 71,207 drones within one week.
That weekly total surpassed the previous record of 55,939 launches, set earlier in 2026 by Aerial Illuminations and UVify.
On September 28 2026, the teams used 10,183 drones to form a giant blue dragon, breaking the record for the largest mythical creature depicted by multirotors.
Shenzhen engineers bring charging launch trays
Damoda supplied the hardware and sent specialists from its Shenzhen base to work alongside American operators from Sky Elements throughout the three nights.
Sky Elements sought out Damoda for both titles because the manufacturer offers launch equipment that differs from regular setups in how each aircraft gets positioned.
Crews normally place each drone by hand, whereas Damoda units arrive in trays that store and charge them and receive each aircraft after landing.
The system simplifies transport and warehousing, since every aircraft departs from one dedicated tray and returns there after completing its flight.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Their assignment was to help the Texas crews handle faults as they arose during repeated launches of a fleet that exceeded 10,000 aircraft.
The dragon glowed in electric blue and served as the centrepiece of a programme that also featured oceanic scenes, two astronauts and a lion.
The entire event unfolded at a remote farm with few residents nearby, where the crews operated the whole fleet from one site.
Every performance involved about 10,200 drones, a volume that the crews found demanding because the fleet flew several times each day.
A thunderstorm struck after the opening show on 27 September, yet the remaining performances continued and ran through the closing night on 30 September.
“This was easily one of the most challenging drone attempts I’ve adjudicated, with the weather and the sheer scale of 10,000 drones flying multiple times a day,” said Michael Empric, the adjudicator who oversaw the attempts for Guinness.
“Yet after several very long nights (and early mornings), it was great to see everything finally come together with five successful shows on the final night.”
Fleet and Dragon breaks previous records
The dragon display broke a mark of 2,247 drones set on the final day of 2025 by an Emirati tourism authority and the emirate itself.
The new weekly total exceeded the earlier figure by 15,268 drones, while the dragon formation surpassed the Emirati mark by 7,936 aircraft.
Sky Elements already holds other titles, among them a gingerbread village built from 4,981 drones and a fictional figure made from 4,979.
Its other entries include a cowboy hat image made from 519 drones and an animation that lasted 30 minutes, the longest by unmanned aircraft.
Though an adjudicator attended the attempts, no independent data in the available account shows how reliably the tray system handles storms or daily launches.

articles.title: La serie de 'Harry Potter' de HBO anuncia a los actores de Lily y James Potter, los padres de Harry
articles.text:
La serie de Harry Potter de HBO, que se estrenará estas mismas navidades, acaba de anunciar a dos de los fichajes más esperados de su reparto. Y es que, por fin, el proyecto ya tiene a los actores que interpretarán a Lily y James Potter, los padres del protagonista. Asesinados por Voldemort cuando el joven era tan solo un bebé recién nacido, su peso en la trama es sin embargo clave en la historia.
Tal y como ha desvelado la compañía, Jasper Talbot y Hannah Chinn serán James Potter y Lily Potter en la serie de Harry Potter. Ambos debutarán, de hecho, en la primera temporada de la serie, titulada Harry Potter y La Piedra Filosofal. En los libros y en las películas, James y Lily aparecen en varias ocasiones en flashbacks o como recuerdos. Por ejemplo en las visiones de Harry en el espejo de Oesed.
Tanto Jasper Talbot como Hannah Chinn son dos desconocidos para el gran público, por lo que el fichaje para la serie de Harry Potter supone un gran salto en su carrera. Talbot ha aparecido en papeles secundarios en filmes como Ruthless (2020) o serie como Broadchurch. Por su parte, Chinn tiene una filmografía que incluye Expediente Warren: El último rito, The Trap o las series Malpractice y Possession.
Más fichajes de la serie de Harry Potter
Al margen de Talbot y Chinn, HBO ha anunciado otro fichaje más para la serie de Harry Potter. Se trata del joven actor Harry Gilby como Charlie Weasley, el segundo hermano mayor de Ron. En su caso, Gilby es conocido por las películas Tolkien, Culpa mía: Londres y la serie The Last Kingdom.
Todos ellos se unen al resto del elenco de la serie de Harry Potter. Estos son Dominic McLaughlin como Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton como Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout como Ron Weasley, John Lithgow como Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer como Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu como Severus Snape, Nick Frost como Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot como Neville Longbottom o Lox Pratt como Draco Malfoy, entre otros.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
De cara a la segunda temporada, la serie de Harry Potter contará los fichajes de Kit Harington como Gilderoy Lockhart, Bonnie Hill como Ginny Weasley, Lenny Rush como Dobby, Billy Barratt como Tom Ryddle, Rafe Spall como Arthur Weasley, Molly Hewitt-Richards como Myrtle la Llorona y Jasper Ambrose como Colin Creevey.

articles.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
articles.text:
Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn’t want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity. But greater model capabilities bring greater risks, and shareholders eager for returns may have little patience for costly safety measures that slow products on their way to market.
Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
Anthropic’s planned IPO raises questions over whether it can maintain its safe and responsible AI priorities.
Sam Altman, the CEO of Anthropic’s archrival, OpenAI, has cited investor pressures as one reason the company is not pursuing an IPO this year. Anthropic hopes it can resist investor pressures with a mind-boggling governance structure.
A “unique and complicated governance structure that has not been used before…creatively designed for this founder-led and mission-driven company.”
University of Pennsylvania law professor Elizabeth Pollman told The Verge that Anthropic has proposed going public with a “unique and complicated governance structure that has not been used before” and that has been “creatively designed for this founder-led and mission-driven company.” Experts say it should give Anthropic freedom to pursue profits without letting shareholders force it to cut corners on safety or rush systems out before they’re adequately tested. But even the strongest legal protections can only go so far, and no corporate structure, no matter how well designed, can completely insulate a public company from the demands of the market.
Foremost, Anthropic is a public benefit corporation. Simply put, it is legally required to focus on more than just maximizing shareholder returns, balancing these with its stated social mission and the interests of stakeholders, such as employees and specific communities. Patagonia and Kickstarter are among the better-known examples, with missions centered on environmental conservation and supporting creative communities, respectively.
Another key safeguard aims to protect Anthropic’s mission by limiting shareholder influence over one of the biggest levers of corporate power: the company’s board of directors. Directors oversee the company and appoint its leadership, including the CEO. Directors can also hold executive roles, as is the case with Anthropic, with CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei both sitting on the board.
Shareholders typically have considerable sway over who sits on the board, giving them a means to replace directors or push for changes if they are unhappy with how the company is being run. For example, if shareholders are unhappy at what they perceive as unnecessary delays to market for optional safety testing, they may remove directors and replace them with ones more aligned with their interests, such as making money and being less cautious.
“Anthropic is entirely insulated from profit seeking pressures, in the sense that ordinary shareholders have no ability to select the board or make business decisions.”
Under Anthropic’s proposed governance structure, ordinary shareholders won’t have much of a say over who is on the board at all. Instead, four of the board’s seven directors will be chosen by a special body called the long-term benefit trust, explains Jens Dammann, a professor in business and commercial law at the University of Texas School of Law. It is a highly unusual setup for a major technology company.
The trust is made up of “five financially disinterested voting trustees” with expertise in “AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise.” Through a special class of share called Class T stock, the trustees can appoint or remove directors in pursuit of their stated purpose: ensuring “that Anthropic responsibly balances the financial interests of stockholders with the interests of those affected by Anthropic’s conduct and our public benefit purpose.” The trust is designed to operate independently of the company’s commercial pressures, allowing it, in theory, to put Anthropic’s mission first.
Ordinary shareholders technically have a say in the board’s three remaining seats. However, Anthropic has created another safeguard that keeps power firmly in the hands of its founders, called “Founder LLC,” which will control 50.1 percent of the voting power on shareholder matters. Given that many shareholder votes are decided by a simple majority, Founder LLC basically gives Anthropic’s founders the ability to block or force through decisions, regardless of how other shareholders vote. This means that they will effectively choose the remaining three directors, Columbia Law School professor Dorothy Lund told The Verge.
The prospectus says Founder LLC will “initially” be seven of Anthropic’s founders: Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah. “Our seven co-founders will initially be the sole members.” Notably absent is another cofounder, Ben Mann, who co-leads the company’s experimental Anthropic Labs arm, as reported by The San Francisco Standard.
All in all, the arrangements would give Anthropic’s founders and the trust “tremendous power” over the company’s direction, shielding it from many of “the pressures associated with being a public company,” Dammann told The Verge. “Given the unusual governance structure Anthropic has chosen, I don’t see how going public, by itself, would undermine its ability to prioritize safety over commercial interests.”
Ann Lipton, a professor at the University of Colorado Law School, agreed, telling The Verge that, legally speaking, “Anthropic is entirely insulated from profit seeking pressures, in the sense that ordinary shareholders have no ability to select the board or make business decisions.” But Lipton cautioned that the founders themselves have financial stakes in the company, which could influence their decisions.
“Investors may not mind their lack of voice as long as things go well. But if things go sour, they may become quite frustrated.”
And there’s a big difference between legal protections and immunity from market pressures. Anthropic, like all AI companies, “desperately needs capital,” Lipton said. “It’s not clear to me that any governance structure will protect against the market reality that unless Anthropic takes advantage of profit making opportunities at a faster pace than its competitors, it will not be able to fund its operations.” Lund expressed similar concerns. Anthropic will still “need to stay in the good graces of their investors,” she said, adding that “competitive pressure and capital needs can erode safety commitments over time.” Anthropic did not respond to The Verge’s request for comment on whether it felt the company could actually resist shareholder pressure to massively accelerate AI at the cost of safety.
Another potential vulnerability emerges if Anthropic’s founders start leaving. In its prospectus, the company says its success is “highly dependent on the continued service” of its senior team, particularly its founders. Dario and Daniela are singled out as being especially “critical” to advancing the company’s research and mission. But beyond the loss of leadership, their departure could trigger significant changes in how the company is structured, potentially stripping away some of the safeguards preventing Anthropic from pursuing profit over safety.
Under the proposed structure, Founder LLC would “sunset” if a majority of its members leave or the group chooses to dissolve it. Once that happens, ordinary shareholders could gain the power to weaken the trust’s protections, even against the wishes of the trustees, and without the support of the founders or employees, who hold different classes of stock, Dammann told The Verge. Other means of subverting the trust also exist, he explained, including coordinated action by the public shareholders, employee stockholders, and founders.
For now, it seems, Anthropic can probably have it both ways. But the protections designed to preserve its commitment to AI safety are far from ironclad, and much depends on market pressures, whether its founders stick around, and directions of the trust. Dammann said he sees a “fundamental dilemma that cannot be resolved in a fully satisfactory way” between Anthropic’s mission and investor demands. As long as things are going well, this tension may be manageable. “Investors may not mind their lack of voice as long as things go well,” Dammann said. “But if things go sour, they may become quite frustrated.”

articles.title: Volkswagen hésiterait entre la Chine et Rivian pour le cerveau de ses futures voitures
articles.text:
Après plusieurs déboires avec sa filiale logicielle Cariad, Volkswagen pensait avoir trouvé la solution en annonçant fin 2024 un accord à 5,8 milliards de dollars (environ 5 milliards d’euros) avec le constructeur américain Rivian. La technologie Rivian devait devenir la colonne vertébrale logicielle des futurs modèles électriques occidentaux du groupe à partir de 2027.
Cette solution pourrait avoir du plomb dans l’aile. Selon les informations publiées par le média allemand Manager Magazin ce 26 octobre 2026, la direction du groupe allemand envisagerait un plan B. Trois marques du groupe seraient susceptibles d’utiliser l’architecture logicielle développée en Chine et déjà opérationnelle sur ce marché, pour équiper une large part des futurs modèles européens de Volkswagen. Si l’entreprise s’est refusée à tout commentaire auprès de Reuters, la récurrence de ces informations sur le rapprochement technologique avec la Chine mérite qu’on s’y attarde.
Attention au raccourci avec le partenariat Xpeng
Affirmer que Volkswagen s’apprêterait à intégrer la technologie Xpeng dans ses modèles européens serait réducteur. Il n’est cependant pas exclu que ce raccourci soit fait par les médias, tant le périmètre de l’accord entre les deux constructeurs reste flou. Le périmètre de l’accord reste d’autant plus difficile à cerner qu’il a évolué depuis sa signature, il y a trois ans.
Le partenariat Volkswagen-Xpeng a d’abord porté sur deux modèles électriques dédiés au marché chinois, avant de donner naissance à la CEA (China Electronic Architecture), une architecture électronique co-développée par Volkswagen Group China Technology Company, Cariad China et Xpeng, et désormais détenue par Volkswagen.
Dans son article, Manager Magazin désigne bien la CEA : l’architecture électronique dite « zonale », qui répartit les fonctions électroniques par zones et s’appuie sur des capacités de calcul centralisées plutôt que sur une multitude de calculateurs indépendants. Il y a donc bien un travail conjoint, comprenant une participation de Xpeng dans cette brique technologique, mais il ne s’agit pas d’un développement du seul constructeur chinois adopté ensuite par Volkswagen.
Vitesse et coûts chinois contre technologie américaine
Le choix de la direction de Volkswagen serait avant tout financier et pragmatique. D’un côté, le groupe dispose avec la CEA d’une brique technologique mature, déjà opérationnelle dans des véhicules de série et moins chère à produire. De l’autre, l’architecture développée avec Rivian n’a pas encore été déployée en série sur un modèle Volkswagen. Le premier véhicule du groupe à en bénéficier est annoncé pour fin 2027 (voire début 2028). Au moment où Volkswagen cherche à réduire ses dépenses, la solution chinoise pourrait donc apparaître particulièrement tentante.
Il faudrait néanmoins adapter l’architecture CEA aux exigences réglementaires et aux procédures d’homologation européennes : normes de sécurité (GSR 2), protection des données (RGPD), homologation des aides à la conduite (ADAS) et sécurisation des mises à jour à distance (OTA). Selon certaines sources internes relayées par la presse chinoise, le coût réel et la faisabilité de cette adaptation ferait l’objet de divisions internes au sein même du groupe.
Une épine dans le pied pour Rivian ?
Si Volkswagen venait à confirmer ce revirement stratégique, la joint-venture avec Rivian ne tomberait pas complètement à l’eau, mais son rôle serait grandement limité. Les contrats sont signés, mais le versement d’importantes tranches de financement reste conditionné à l’atteinte de jalons techniques précis. La pression repose donc sur Rivian qui doit livrer dans les temps.
Le périmètre de cet accord pourrait cependant fondre comme neige au soleil. Si les futurs modèles européens de Volkswagen, Skoda et Cupra basculent sur la technologie chinoise CEA, le partenariat avec Rivian pourrait alors voir son périmètre réduit. Reste à savoir quelles marques et quels modèles continueraient d’utiliser cette architecture, si Volkswagen décidait effectivement de privilégier la CEA pour une partie de sa gamme européenne.
En envisageant d’adopter en Europe une architecture développée en Chine, Volkswagen reconnaîtrait l’avance prise par ses équipes chinoises sur le développement rapide de certaines technologies embarquées. Un choix audacieux en matière de souveraineté technologique, qui risque de faire grincer quelques dents à Wolfsburg comme chez Rivian. Il convient néanmoins de rappeler qu’il s’agit pour l’heure de rumeurs. On devrait rapidement en savoir davantage, si Volkswagen confirme ou précise cette piste.

articles.title: Mixer les purées et les répartir en petits pots : le coffret Nutribullet Baby est à 49,90 €
articles.text:
Le blender pour bébé Nutribullet Baby NBY100 est à 49,90 € (-29 %)
Le Nutribullet Baby NBY100 comprend un blender, six petits pots avec indicateur de date et un plateau de congélation pour préparer et répartir les repas de bébé.
Amazon propose le blender Nutribullet Baby NBY100 à 49,90 €, contre un prix conseillé de 69,90 €, soit environ 29 % de réduction. Le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours était de 52,90 € : la baisse atteint donc environ 6 % sur cette référence. L’ensemble est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec livraison gratuite.
Un blender pour préparer les purées
Le blender Nutribullet Baby comprend un bol d’environ 900 ml et un petit gobelet avec poignée pour varier les quantités préparées. Il mixe les ingrédients, mais ne possède pas de fonction de cuisson.
Six petits pots avec couvercles et indicateurs de date permettent de répartir les préparations. Un plateau de congélation en silicone à six compartiments complète le coffret.
Des accessoires pratiques, avec quelques limites relevées
Les récipients et accessoires compatibles passent au lave-vaisselle, à l’exclusion du bloc moteur. Le kit facilite ainsi la préparation de plusieurs petites portions.
La page Amazon affiche 4,2/5 sur 605 évaluations. Les commentaires consultés apprécient la simplicité et les pots fournis. Certains critiquent toutefois leur petite capacité ou un mixage nécessitant de repositionner les aliments.

articles.title: Apple reconoce fallos en la pantalla de algunas unidades del iPhone Duo: “Somos conscientes de un problema”
articles.text:
A pocos días de su llegada a las tiendas, el iPhone Duo enfrenta reportes de grietas y otros fallos en la pantalla interior. Algunos usuarios aseguran que los daños aparecieron poco después de estrenar el teléfono plegable, y Apple ha reconocido que existe un problema que afecta a un número reducido de unidades. La compañía recomienda a quienes detecten fallos que contacten con su servicio de atención al cliente para solicitar un cambio.
“Tenemos conocimiento de un problema que afecta a la pantalla interna de un pequeño número de unidades de iPhone Duo”, señaló Apple, instando a los clientes afectados a contactar directamente con el servicio técnico de AppleCare.
Apple no ha explicado qué causa el defecto ni ha detallado si modificará el proceso de fabricación. Tampoco ha precisado cuántos dispositivos están afectados. Por ahora, los casos difundidos por usuarios y las pruebas realizadas por especialistas no permiten determinar si se trata de un fallo generalizado.
Usuarios reportan grietas y líneas verdes
Entre los testimonios compartidos, algunos propietarios afirman haber encontrado grietas en la pantalla interior durante los primeros días de uso. Un usuario señaló que escuchó un chasquido tras abrir y cerrar el móvil menos de 20 veces y que poco después la pantalla dejó de funcionar correctamente.
También se han reportado líneas verdes en el panel. El canal de YouTube JerryRigEverything sometió el dispositivo a una prueba de flexión y, durante el ensayo, aparecieron líneas de ese color en la pantalla interior. La prueba muestra una respuesta del dispositivo bajo esas condiciones, pero no demuestra por sí sola que los daños de los usuarios tengan la misma causa.
La rapidez con la que aparecieron algunos de los problemas ha generado preocupación entre los primeros compradores. Sin embargo, los reportes disponibles no permiten establecer qué proporción de los teléfonos presenta fallos ni anticipar si estos aumentarán con el uso. Será necesario contar con más información y observar el comportamiento del modelo durante un periodo mayor.
iFixit examina la bisagra
El equipo de iFixit desmontó el iPhone Duo para analizar su construcción y publicó sus observaciones en un vídeo. Los especialistas describieron la bisagra como un mecanismo complejo, compuesto por engranajes, muelles y otras piezas que trabajan en conjunto para permitir que el teléfono se pliegue.
A partir de su análisis, plantearon una posible explicación para las grietas: una pieza de la bisagra podría no bajar lo suficiente al cerrar el dispositivo. En ese caso, la pantalla podría apoyarse sobre ella y soportar una presión mayor de la prevista.
iFixit no confirmó que ese mecanismo sea el origen de los daños. Su observación es una hipótesis sobre un posible punto de tensión y no una conclusión definitiva sobre las unidades afectadas. Apple, por su parte, tampoco ha señalado la causa del problema reconocido.
Las pruebas muestran otros posibles puntos débiles
Además del desmontaje, se han realizado pruebas de apertura y cierre de la bisagra. En estos ensayos, el mecanismo resistió miles de pliegues, aunque después apareció una marca en el centro de la pantalla. Ese resultado describe el comportamiento del teléfono en una prueba concreta y no permite establecer cuánto durará en condiciones normales de uso.
Los investigadores también probaron el efecto del polvo sobre la bisagra con partículas fluorescentes, visibles al desmontar el dispositivo. Parte del polvo llegó al mecanismo y comenzó a producir un ruido similar a un crujido después de abrir y cerrar el teléfono varias veces. La prueba señala que partículas pequeñas pueden alcanzar la bisagra, pero no confirma que el polvo sea responsable de las grietas reportadas.
Apple recomienda solicitar un cambio
La empresa aconseja a los usuarios que detecten grietas, líneas verdes u otros problemas en la pantalla interior que contacten con Apple o con AppleCare para pedir asistencia y consultar la posibilidad de reemplazar el dispositivo. La respuesta de la compañía confirma que algunas unidades presentan un inconveniente, pero no aclara todavía su alcance ni las medidas que tomará para evitar nuevos casos.
La situación también ha llamado la atención por las críticas que John Ternus, CEO de Apple, había dirigido a algunos plegables con Android, a los que describió como productos baratos y mal construidos. Los problemas reportados en el iPhone Duo han reavivado esas declaraciones, aunque todavía no se sabe si los fallos afectarán a una parte amplia de los teléfonos vendidos.
De momento, los usuarios tendrán que esperar a que Apple ofrezca más detalles y a que nuevas pruebas permitan aclarar el origen del defecto. Si la pantalla de su dispositivo ya presenta daños, la recomendación de la compañía es ponerse en contacto con su servicio de atención al cliente.

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929
