articles.title: SpaceX closes $40 billion debt financing for GPUs expected in the first half of 2027, Musk says — company faces up to $40 billion in additional fourth-quarter capital spending as AI infrastructure costs soar
articles.text:
SpaceX closes $40 billion debt financing for GPUs expected in the first half of 2027, Musk says — company faces up to $40 billion in additional fourth-quarter capital spending as AI infrastructure costs soar
SpaceX is preparing to spend as much as $40 billion in the fourth quarter alone.
Elon Musk has confirmed that SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units (GPUs), with the chips expected to arrive in the first half of 2027. He disclosed the deal on X, October 25 (embedded below) while responding to investor Chamath Palihapitiya, who had warned that mounting financing pressures and delays in data center construction could leave AI computing capacity sitting idle next year.
Musk agreed with that assessment, but argued that SpaceX is better positioned than many of its competitors because it can borrow against revenue from businesses outside AI. “Pretty much,” Musk replied to Palihapitiya on X explaining that debt markets had largely shut off funding for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers.
He further said SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt for GPUs because it has investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and space businesses. “That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many,” Musk wrote.
It is still, however, unclear what Musk meant by “closed” or whether investors had agreed to the final debt pricing. The disclosure comes as SpaceX prepares for another enormous spending period. CFO Bret Johnsen had stated during SpaceX’s Q3 2026 earnings call that the company expects capital expenditure of $35 billion to $40 billion in Q4 “because of the additional capacity coming online this quarter.”
Musk also clarified that the borrowing was primarily callable debt for GPU purchases expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. “This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter,” Musk wrote.
Earlier this month, it emerged SpaceX had proposed a $40 billion debt package for Nvidia hardware, estimating that the proposed funding could cover roughly 360,000 Rubin GPUs across 5,000 Nvidia NVL72 racks. The proposed package reportedly included $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt. Musk has now said the financing has closed, but has not confirmed the specific GPU models or quantities covered by the deal.
The spending fits into Musk’s broader push to expand AI computing capacity. In August, xAI outlined plans to increase its data center capacity sevenfold by 2027, targeting 10 gigawatts. In September, the publication also reported that SpaceXAI planned to add another 660,000 Nvidia GPUs during 2026, potentially bringing its total to around 1.44 million if the planned deployments proceed.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
And GPUs are only part of the bill. Data centers need power, cooling, networking equipment, and physical infrastructure before those accelerators can do useful work, which underscores SpaceX’s latest move.
SpaceX, meanwhile, has begun selling access to its own infrastructure. In May, Anthropic secured access to SpaceX’s Colossus 1 supercomputer, which includes more than 220,000 Nvidia GPUs and over 300 megawatts of computing capacity. Later in June, SpaceX struck a separate deal with Google, which agreed to pay $920 million per month for access to approximately 110,000 Nvidia GPUs and related hardware, with payments scheduled to run from October 2026 through June 2029.

articles.title: America's biggest banks are racing to stop AI agents from going rogue — but I hope they stop short of a full ban
articles.text:
AI agents are going rogue inside bank accounts — and this is exactly what I've been worried about
Major US banks are apparently scrambling to restrict autonomous AI assistants
I like the idea of AI taking care of boring tasks, including sorting through bills and financial paperwork. I can even see the appeal of it helping with shopping. But asking an AI assistant for financial advice and simply handing over the keys to your bank account are different, and this distinction is becoming a problem for some of America's biggest banks.
According to a new Axios report, financial institutions are encountering AI agents while they access customer accounts and seem to be doing more than requested by users. JPMorgan, Chase, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley are all taking steps to protect their customers, but it's a sobering aspect of AI that raises real questions about how much to trust the tech in the world of finance.
While there's no confirmed epidemic of AI assistants emptying savings accounts and the reports don't establish any financial losses, it still makes me nervous to think that we've reached the point where banks are having to worry about whether an AI assistant has decided to improvise with somebody's money.
There's been a real push to encourage the use of ever-more independent AI agents. Every new demonstration seems to involve an assistant that can accomplish increasingly complicated tasks while its owner sits back and watches. That's impressive when the task is organizing a vacation itinerary, but less appealing when the assistant has access to the money that would pay for it.
AI experiments with money
It's notable that it isn't like AI agents are hacking their way into accounts, exactly. Customers might voluntarily share their login credentials with the AI to give the software access to financial information that banks have spent decades trying to protect. I've done it for my own tests, but it's always been simply a way for the AI to look at very specific elements of my finances, never to touch them.
Banking websites can be frustrating, financial paperwork is tedious, and managing money requires more attention than most of us would prefer to give it. An assistant that promises to handle the irritating parts sounds wonderful. But AI agents have a habit of interpreting instructions rather creatively. And while asking it to reduce your monthly expenses and getting a list of subscriptions you might want to cancel is great, giving that same assistant permission to make financial decisions means you're trusting its interpretation of a vague instruction with money you actually need.
That should make people uncomfortable. These systems can misunderstand requests and make incorrect judgments. We've all seen chatbots produce an answer that sounds perfectly reasonable until you discover they've invented half of it, and adding the ability to take real-world actions makes those mistakes considerably more consequential. The fact that banks are already encountering agents whose behavior raises questions about authorization suggests that those limits deserve much more attention.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Keeping AI outside the vault
I wouldn't go so far as to say banks should block AI assistants altogether. There are plenty of good reasons to let people connect these tools to their accounts, and I don't particularly like the idea of banks deciding which services customers are allowed to use.
But I'd be much less comfortable letting that same assistant actually do anything with my money I don't ask for. I'd want it to ask permission every single time, with no room for interpreting something I said last Tuesday as authorization to make a transfer today.
That might defeat some of the appeal of autonomous AI agents, but I'm perfectly fine with that. Saving a few seconds isn't worth the possibility of discovering that an AI assistant has made an expensive decision on my behalf. Most importantly, someone needs to be responsible when an agent makes a mistake, because telling customers to take it up with the chatbot isn't going to cut it.
The frustrating thing is that none of this should come as a surprise. AI companies are racing to give their agents more independence, often before they've worked out how to prevent them from making mistakes. We're supposed to be impressed that an assistant can complete a task without asking for help, but that becomes much less impressive when it does something the user never wanted.

articles.title: En attendant le premier Mac tactile, Apple met à jour les MacBook Pro et iMac avec la puce M6
articles.text:
Les rumeurs ont vu juste : Apple prévoit bien une semaine d’annonces. Après les iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone Duo, les Apple Watch, les AirPods 5, le HomeView, l’Apple TV et le HomePod mini, puis l’iPad mini avec un écran OLED annoncé la veille, la marque poursuit son automne fou avec de petites révisions des MacBook Pro et iMac dévoilées le 27 octobre par communiqué de presse.
Il n’y a pas d’écran OLED ou de nouveau design ici : la grande nouveauté est l’arrivée de la puce M6, déjà aperçue avec le Mac mini fin août.
Un MacBook Pro sans écran tactile en attendant les annonces de mercredi
Seul le MacBook Pro le moins cher est mis à jour : les versions « Pro » et « Max » attendront sans doute mercredi.
Le MacBook Pro 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme conserve le même design que les anciennes générations, mais remplace la puce M5 par la M6. L’ordinateur utilise toujours un mini-LED 120 Hz (jusqu’à 1 600 nits en HDR, avec une option nano-texture) : Apple ne change quasiment rien dans ce qui ressemble à une dernière itération de ce design (l’année prochaine, on peut imaginer que tous les nouveaux MacBook Pro auront le nouveau design tactile). La connectique reste identique (HDMI, MagSafe 3, trois ports Thunderbolt 4, lecteur SDXC et prise jack), tout comme les deux coloris, noir sidéral et argent. Apple annonce jusqu’à 24 heures d’autonomie et une charge rapide jusqu’à 50 % en 30 minutes avec un chargeur de 96 W.
L’iMac 24 pouces, lui, passe directement de la M4 à la M6. Apple en profite pour passer au Wi-Fi 7 et au Bluetooth 6, comme sur le MacBook Pro et le Mac mini M6. L’iMac propose aussi l’Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s, contre 1 Gb/s auparavant, mais seulement en option sur les modèles les plus chers. Attention d’ailleurs à la configuration de base : elle se contente d’une M6 avec 10 cœurs CPU et 10 cœurs GPU. Pour profiter de la puce complète (12 cœurs CPU et 12 cœurs GPU), de quatre ports Thunderbolt 4 au lieu de deux, de Touch ID de série et de l’option nano-texture, il faut monter en gamme. Les sept coloris ne changent pas.
L’Apple M6 est la première puce Apple gravée en 2 nm. Elle compte 12 cœurs CPU (2 « super cores », 4 cœurs de performance et 6 cœurs d’efficacité) et 12 cœurs GPU, avec un Neural Accelerator dans chaque cœur. Comme l’A20 Pro, elle embarque deux Neural Engine 16 cœurs pour gérer plusieurs tâches d’IA en parallèle : Apple les annonce 1,9 fois plus rapides que sur la M5. La bande passante mémoire grimpe à 170 Go/s, mais la mémoire unifiée plafonne toujours à 32 Go (16 Go de série sur le MacBook Pro).
Comme le Mac mini M6, les nouveaux iMac et MacBook Pro devraient être plus puissants, notamment côté GPU : Apple revendique jusqu’à 30 % de performances graphiques en plus. Mais il est peu probable qu’un possesseur de MacBook Pro M5 constate la moindre différence entre les deux générations : cette mise à niveau annuelle suit l’avancée des laboratoires d’Apple mais ne répond pas à des changements techniques majeurs. Le saut est plus net pour l’iMac, qui passe de la M4 à la M6 : Apple promet jusqu’à 2 fois plus de performances graphiques et 5 fois plus en IA. Siri AI est logiquement mis en avant : pour rappel, il fonctionne seulement sur macOS dans l’Union européenne.
Le renouveau du MacBook Pro pour mercredi ?
La grosse annonce arrivera mercredi. Selon les rumeurs, Apple présentera à Los Angeles son premier MacBook Pro à écran tactile, en 14 et 16 pouces. Ce nouveau MacBook Pro haut de gamme, plus cher que le MacBook Pro M6, devrait inaugurer un nouveau design que l’on retrouvera pendant plusieurs années sur les MacBook Pro.
Au programme notamment : un écran OLED, une Dynamic Island à la place de l’encoche et un design plus léger. Les puces M5 Pro et M5 Max ne seraient pas remplacées (une première qui suggère que les puces M6 Pro et M6 Max n’existeront pas) et, pour la première fois, l’écran serait tactile. On imagine que des hausses de prix sont aussi à prévoir : réponse mercredi vers 18 heures, sur Numerama.
Prix et disponibilité des MacBook Pro et iMac M6
Le MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6 démarre à 2 299 euros, contre 2 199 euros pour la version M5 (1 899 euros avant la hausse de juin). L’iMac M6 commence à 1 799 euros, le même prix que la version M4 (1 499 euros avant la hausse de juin). Les précommandes ouvriront mercredi à 18h10, après l’annonce du MacBook Pro tactile, pour des livraisons à partir du 6 novembre.

Abonnez-vous dès maintenant sur YouTube, X, Instagram et TikTok pour ne rien rater à nos images exclusives. Si vous avez des questions, vous pouvez contacter notre journaliste sur place sur X. articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Powers Neural Rendering and AI Characters in Games | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new Windows PC platform for AI development, creation, and gaming in slim laptops and compact desktops. Powered by an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and NVIDIA Grace CPU, it combines up to 128 GB of unified memory with the full NVIDIA CUDA stack and RTX technologies including ray tracing and DLSS 5.
This post covers the following technologies for game developers building on RTX Spark:
- DLSS suite of technologies that boost FPS and improve image quality
- NVIDIA ACE updates for responsive, on-device AI characters
- RTX Kit SDKs for neural rendering, geometry, and character rendering
- NVIDIA Nsight tools for optimizing and debugging native Arm64 and x64 applications
- NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8 for integrating RTX technologies into your Unreal Engine projects
- MotionBricks update for human-character motion
DLSS on RTX Spark
RTX Spark benefits from the full suite of DLSS technologies in supported games, including Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and 3D-Guided Neural Rendering.
DLSS Super Resolution reconstructs frames from a lower resolution input to improve performance. DLSS Ray Reconstruction generates additional pixels to enhance ray-traced scenes. DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation can generate up to 5 additional frames per rendered frame, automatically adjusting the multiplier to maximize smoothness.
The latest NVIDIA app beta also brings a faster Performance Mode (Preset C) for Frame Generation, with minor trade-offs in image quality.
DLSS 5 brings 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is supported on NVIDIA RTX Spark, starting with NBA 2K27.
An October model update runs 2x faster than the September version and halves GPU overhead while maintaining comparable visual fidelity. It also reduces VRAM use at 4K by 20%. The model will ship by default in future DLSS 5 games.
For developers, DLSS 5 adds a final stage to the graphics pipeline that enhances lighting and material detail. The engine-rendered frame, including artist-designed geometry, textures, and lighting buffers, remains the foundation, while developer controls determine what can change. Avalanche Software has taken advantage of DLSS 5’s SDK controls to tune the integration to maintain the artistic intent and style of the game.
Read the full DLSS 5 update here.
DLSS 4.5 Unreal Engine plugin
The updated NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 plugin for Unreal Engine gives developers powerful tools for delivering sharper images and smoother gameplay. Its second-generation transformer model for Super Resolution improves image stability, anti-aliasing, and visual clarity, while Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced image quality.
On supported GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation adapts the frame-generation multiplier as workloads change, with 6x Multi Frame Generation producing up to five additional frames per rendered frame.
A key addition in plugin version 8.9.0 is official Windows on Arm (WoA) support for Unreal Engine 5.8. Native ARM64 binaries and support for building and packaging UE 5.8 applications give developers a supported path to bring DLSS-enabled projects to RTX Spark systems. Alongside updated Streamline and NGX components and fixes for UE 5.8 Frame Generation issues, this release expands the plugin’s platform reach and helps developers prepare their applications for RTX Spark.
NVIDIA ACE introduces Nemotron 3.5 Bolt for on-device AI characters
NVIDIA ACE is our technology suite for creating in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences, and we’ve shared two exciting showcases this year:
- PUBG rolled out AI teammates in a public beta powered by our first-generation Nemotron small language model (SLM). It helped new players land their first chicken dinners and generated viral clips across social media.
- Aniimo debuted our more efficient second-generation Nemotron SLM, turning standard in-game pets into responsive AI companions that react to your voice. Players can check in on their pets’ feelings or teach them new tricks, which will bring a new level of immersion when it releases in early 2027.
More intelligence, less memory
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available. This model offers ~40% higher average quality against our prior model on relevant benchmarks and outputs up to ~80% fewer tokens vs peers.
It is purpose-built to power richer, faster in-game character interactions, with strong conversational capability, autonomous multi-turn tool use, instruction adherence, and grounding to game state, all running locally on GeForce RTX and RTX Spark.
Engineered for maximum intelligence and speed per GB of memory, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB enables responsive local experiences while preserving headroom for graphics rendering and local speech models. Key features include:
- Multi-turn tool use: Call application APIs to carry out tasks across a conversation, with integration guidance for asynchronous tool calls
- Conversational mode: Toggle to encourage concise, speech-ready responses for natural back-and-forth interactions.
- Configurable reasoning: Enable reasoning for complex requests or disable it for faster responses, with integration options to cap thinking to meet latency targets.
- 64k context: Accommodate conversation history, instructions, tool definitions, retrieved information and game state.
- Multilingual capability: Support for 35 languages, building on a base model pre-trained on more than 140 languages.
Get started with NVIDIA ACE
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is available to developers via the In-Game Inferencing (IGI) SDK.
To test it in a game, check out SkyrimNET, an AI NPC modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character with personal memory, voice, and autonomy, enabling dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly. The platform supports both cloud and local inference across multiple language models.
- Download the SkyrimNET Plugin: GitHub Repository
- Download the ARM-Supported Loader: Mod Organizer Release
NVIDIA RTX Kit brings neural rendering SDKs to RTX Spark
NVIDIA RTX Kit brings neural rendering, complex geometry, and realistic character rendering to game development. Eight RTX Kit technologies are published with support for RTX Spark:
- RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC): Uses AI to shrink texture storage while maintaining visual fidelity comparable to traditional block compression.
- RTX Texture Filtering: Uses stochastic texture sampling after shading to reduce artifacts and improve image quality, including for difficult volumes.
- RTX Neural Shaders: Lets developers train neural networks and run them within shaders for new asset compression and approximation techniques.
- RTX Mega Geometry: Speeds up bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) construction for cluster-based geometry, helping developers ray trace more triangles and improve performance in complex scenes.
- NVIDIA Real-Time Denoisers (NRD): Provides denoisers for diffuse and specular lighting and shadows, producing cleaner images from low ray-per-pixel inputs.
- RTX Character Rendering: Provides tools for rendering strand-based hair and skin with path tracing, including subsurface scattering and Blackwell-accelerated hair primitives.
- RTX Global Illumination (RTXGI): Provides several techniques for efficient indirect lighting for ray traced and path traced applications.
- Opacity Micro-Maps (OMM): Used to accelerate ray tracing of high detail geometry by efficiently encoding the opacity states of micro-triangles and micro meshes.
Optimizing and debugging RTX Spark applications
NVIDIA Nsight tools are ready for RTX Spark from day one, supporting graphics developer workflows across native Arm64, emulated x64, and Arm64EC applications.
Nsight Graphics lets developers capture, inspect, and profile individual frames, examining every draw call, shader, and resource to diagnose rendering bugs and tune GPU performance. Nsight Graphics release 2026.3 introduces a new Windows on Arm installer for RTX Spark systems, supporting native Arm64 target applications as well as emulated x64 and Arm64EC targets.
Nsight Systems delivers a system-wide view of application performance, correlating CPU threads, GPU workloads, API calls, and memory activity on a single timeline so developers can pinpoint bottlenecks and balance work across the platform. Starting with Nsight Systems 2026.5, a single installer for all versions of Windows supports both native Arm64 and emulated applications.
Nsight Aftermath helps teams resolve GPU crashes and hangs by generating detailed crash dumps that show what the GPU was doing at the moment of failure, both during development and in the field. Nsight Aftermath SDK 2026.3 includes a Windows on Arm version for integrating into native Arm64 applications. Crash dumps from emulated x64 applications will continue to function as expected with the x64 version of the SDK.
- Download Nsight Graphics for RTX Spark here
- Download Nsight Systems for RTX Spark here
- Download Nsight Aftermath SDK for RTX Spark here
NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8
The release of NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8 (NvRTX 5.8) gives developers an updated foundation for bringing advanced ray tracing and neural graphics to UE 5.8 projects. This update focuses on codebase refactoring, stabilization, and compatibility improvements. Developers can access the branch source through GitHub to integrate and customize NVIDIA RTX technologies for their games and applications.
Simplify runtime character animation with MotionBricks
MotionBricks is open-source research for generating character motion in real time. Rather than hand-authoring every transition and wiring it into an increasingly complex animation graph, developers guide motion through target poses. MotionBricks generates the connecting movement at runtime and adapts as player input or game event changes. Paper GitHub
The model supports control over speed, direction, and movement style, along with pose-guided interactions such as sitting and picking up objects. These capabilities let developers build varied character behaviors through a common pose-based interface. The original research demonstration shows these behaviors working together in Unreal Engine. Research demonstrations
The update builds on this work with:
- New SOMA human-motion models, alongside the existing G1 robot model.
- Downloadable checkpoints, ONNX exports, and export tools for developers building their own integrations.
- An interactive reference implementation built with Newton, demonstrating pose-guided human and robot motion.
MotionBricks is provided as research code and models. The Unreal Engine integration shown in the research demonstration is not included in this release.
Resources for game developers
Check out the full list of game developer resources and stay up to date with the latest NVIDIA game development news:

- Follow us on social: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, and YouTube
- Join our Discord community

articles.title: Mehr Leistung bei geringen Kosten: Für wen GPT-6.1 Terra jetzt bereitsteht
articles.text:
Mehr Leistung bei geringen Kosten: Für wen GPT-6.1 Terra jetzt bereitsteht
Im Juli 2026 hatte OpenAI seine neuen Modellnamen Sol, Terra und Luna mit der Veröffentlichung von GPT-5.6 eingeführt. Jetzt folgt für das Terra-Modell, das als Kompromiss zwischen Leistungsfähigkeit und Kostenfaktor fungiert, die nächste Iteration. Wie das Unternehmen in einer Ankündigung schreibt, soll GPT-6.1 Terra deutlich leistungsfähiger als der Vorgänger sein, was sich gerade in zwei Bereichen zeigen soll.
GPT-6.1 Terra: Was die neue OpenAI-KI leistet
Diese zwei Bereiche sind Kommunikations- und Computeraufgaben. OpenAI nennt hier als Beispiele das „Entwerfen von Angeboten und Interpretieren von technischen Zeichnungen“ oder das „Ausfüllen von Formularen und Bearbeiten von Videos“. Die Computerbedienung wurde dabei mit dem Benchmark „Agents Last Exam“ gemessen, bei dem KI-Modelle etwa Architekturzeichnungen in 3D-Modelle umwandeln sollen.
GPT-6.1 Terra schnitt dabei laut OpenAI sogar teilweise besser als GPT-6 Astra ab und kostet dabei nur einen Bruchteil. Lediglich Claude Opus 5.5 von Anthropic liegt laut OpenAI deutlich vor den eigenen Modellen. Dafür würde die Konkurrenz-KI aber auch deutlich mehr Kosten verursachen. Ähnliche Ergebnisse gibt es bei dem Visual-Reasoning-Benchmark MMMU‑Pro. Hier schnitt GPT-6.1 etwa auf einer Ebene mit GPT-6.1 Sol im Hinblick auf Leistung und Kosten ab. GPT-6 Astra ist erneut etwas besser, aber auch teurer.
Laut OpenAI gibt es bei GPT-6.1 ebenfalls Verbesserungen in den Bereichen Faktentreue und Programmierung. Halluzinationen sollen deutlich seltener vorkommen. In einem Test, bei dem absichtlich Fehler provoziert wurden, lag die Fehlerquote lediglich bei 16,7 Prozent. Bei GPT-5.6 Terra lag sie noch bei 53,6 Prozent. Im Terminal-Bench-Benchmark schnitt GPT-6.1 Terra immerhin noch besser als der Vorgänger ab. Alle anderen Modelle wie GPT-6.1 Sol und Astra waren aber besser als das Mittelklassemodell.
GPT-6.1 Terra steht ab sofort allen User:innen zur Verfügung, die ein Plus-, Pro-, Enterprise- oder Edu-Abo bei OpenAI abgeschlossen haben. Aufgrund seiner Fertigkeiten wird die KI zunächst nur in ChatGPT Work und Codex integriert, um Nutzer:innen bei ihrer Arbeit und beim Programmieren zu unterstützen. GPT-6.1 ist aber auch über die API des Unternehmens abrufbar. Dort bezahlen User:innen einen US-Dollar pro einer Million Eingabe-Token und fünf Dollar für dieselbe Anzahl Output-Token.

articles.title: This is Fine: What NetScaler Zero-Days Tell Us About the New Normal
articles.text:
If you’ve been paying attention to enterprise edge security lately, the September 2026 Citrix NetScaler zero-day advisories probably gave you a familiar case of heartburn. But before everyone panics, let’s step back and look at the bigger picture: what we are seeing right now isn’t a collapse of edge defense. It is, in fact, exactly how modern active defense is supposed to work when high-value, internet-facing infrastructure comes under heavy fire.
First, a quick refresher on why Citrix NetScaler ADC (Application Delivery Controller) and Gateway sit directly in the crosshairs of global threat actors. NetScaler is an everything-at-the-edge solution. It acts as a reverse proxy, load balancer, Web Application Firewall (WAF), traditional firewall, and SSL VPN all rolled into one appliance. Pretty much every major vendor in the perimeter space (F5, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Juniper, and more) went down this path of consolidation over the last decade or so. Instead of managing a bunch of standalone boxes chaining together these individual security controls, larger organizations clearly are showing a preference for a single platform to handle edge traffic. After all, it tends to be cheaper and easier to deploy just the one physical or virtual box from one vendor than to manage a constellation of security control devices.
The trade-off, however, is that spies and extortionists love this architectural shift just as much as IT departments do. If an attacker lands root on an edge device, they effectively gain total control over how that local network communicates with the rest of the world.
So, what went down this September? Sometime in the middle of the month, unidentified threat actors began actively exploiting undisclosed flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway. Dutch government threat analysts, and private sector incident responders, quickly caught wind of suspicious attack traffic. Over the weekend of September 26, resellers and security advisories urged admins to restrict or disconnect edge-facing deployments. By that Sunday, Citrix released patches for a batch of unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities, tracked sequentially from CVE-2026-88771 through CVE-2026-88778.
While it’s not fun to ship or apply emergency patches over a weekend, several factors demonstrate why this quick, after-hours response pattern reflects a stronger defensive posture.
First, global telemetry and monitoring capabilities have improved dramatically, allowing analysts to spot exotic, undocumented zero-days far faster than in the past. This is significantly reducing exploitation windows and rapidly shrinking the operational lifespans for zero-day campaigns. A decade ago, nation-state campaigns could drop zero-day shells on perimeter devices and operate undetected for weeks or months. Today, active exploitation increasingly gets flagged and burned in a matter of days when the attacks are executed over the public internet.
Vendor coordination speed has also accelerated noticeably. While Citrix averaged nearly 40 days from initial bug discovery to CVE disclosure across 2024 and 2025, that response window dropped down to 17 days for the NetScaler product line in 2026, after Citrix established a dedicated NetScaler CNA. That fact alone further demonstrates that Citrix is treating its vulnerability response cadence with the urgency it demands.
Government advisory bodies like CISA are keeping pace with this shift as well. Emergency additions to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on a Sunday used to be virtually unheard of, but these two NetScaler issues may signal that Saturday, Sunday, and holiday additions to the public KEV may become more common. (Before this issue, exactly one CVE was added to the KEV on a Sunday, for Microsoft SharePoint in 2025).
Looking ahead for specifically NetScaler operators, you may see secondary advisories to follow. CVE IDs tend to be reserved sequentially, and as of this writing, there’s a gap in CVE publishing, from CVE-2026-88779 through CVE-2026-88787. So, keep your patch management pipelines primed in case another round of Citrix patches get released soon.
Ultimately, attackers will keep hammering consolidated edge devices because those internet-facing devices deliver the most bang for the hacking buck. However, our collective ability to detect, coordinate, patch, and accurately track perimeter inventory has never been sharper. By staying vigilant, keeping asset data clean, and preparing for emergency patch fire drills, security teams are better than ever at effectively responding to the next internet emergency.
Related: Citrix Urges Immediate Patching of Critical NetScaler Vulnerability
Related: Citrix Confirms 2 NetScaler Zero-Days After Admins Pulled the Plug

articles.title: WhatsApp prepara un nuevo menú de ajustes en Android: así cambiarán Privacidad, Cuenta y Notificaciones
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara un nuevo diseño para el menú de ajustes en Android, con cambios que alcanzarán apartados como Privacidad, Cuenta y Notificaciones. La modificación, aún en desarrollo, reorganizará las opciones de la aplicación en bloques visuales con esquinas redondeadas, una decisión que busca ordenar una de las zonas más utilizadas por quienes quieren controlar su información, alertas y preferencias de uso.
El cambio importa porque los ajustes concentran decisiones sensibles dentro de la plataforma: desde quién puede ver la última conexión hasta la gestión de copias de seguridad, dispositivos vinculados o sonidos de los mensajes.
Con una interfaz más segmentada, WhatsApp pretende que estas funciones sean más fáciles de identificar en pantallas móviles, sin alterar por ahora las herramientas disponibles.
Los ajustes de WhatsApp pasarán de una lista plana a grupos visuales
La novedad fue detectada en la versión WhatsApp beta para Android 2.26.43.3, distribuida a través de Google Play Store. La aplicación prueba un formato conocido como lista segmentada, que agrupa opciones relacionadas dentro de un mismo contenedor.
Hasta ahora, el menú de ajustes presenta sus secciones en una disposición lineal. La futura interfaz dividirá ese listado en tarjetas o módulos separados. Cada bloque reunirá funciones de una misma categoría, con un borde redondeado que marcará la diferencia entre una sección y otra.
En la práctica, los usuarios encontrarán grupos visuales para Cuenta, Privacidad, Notificaciones y el resto de los apartados de configuración. El objetivo no es añadir nuevas herramientas de seguridad o comunicación, sino modificar la manera en que se muestran las ya existentes.
La primera opción de cada conjunto tendrá una curvatura más marcada en la parte superior. La última repetirá ese efecto en el borde inferior. Los elementos intermedios conservarán uniones más discretas con las filas contiguas. De ese modo, la pantalla ofrecerá una separación más clara entre categorías.
El rediseño sigue las pautas de Material Design 3 Expressive
El estilo elegido responde a Material Design 3 Expressive, el sistema de diseño de Google para Android. Esta guía establece criterios visuales para componentes como botones, barras de navegación, paneles y listas dentro de las aplicaciones.
La lista segmentada adapta la forma de los bordes según la posición de cada elemento. Cuando varias opciones pertenecen a un mismo grupo, la interfaz las presenta como una unidad visual. El resultado se asemeja a una cápsula o tarjeta, con espacios definidos entre cada bloque de configuración.
Para WhatsApp, la adopción de este patrón puede aportar una navegación más coherente con otras aplicaciones del ecosistema Android. También puede facilitar la lectura de un menú que ha incorporado nuevas funciones con el paso del tiempo, desde controles de privacidad hasta herramientas de almacenamiento y gestión de chats.
La actualización no modifica el contenido de los ajustes, sino su distribución en pantalla. Los usuarios seguirán accediendo a los controles habituales, aunque dentro de una estructura que separará mejor cada categoría.
Privacidad, Cuenta y Notificaciones tendrán el mismo formato
La compañía no limitaría el nuevo diseño a una única pantalla. Según las pruebas identificadas en la versión beta, el sistema de listas segmentadas se extenderá a toda la interfaz de ajustes.
Esto incluye los controles de Privacidad, donde se administran opciones como la foto de perfil, la hora de última vez, las confirmaciones de lectura y el bloqueo de contactos. También abarcará Cuenta, con apartados relacionados con seguridad, cambio de número y eliminación del perfil.
El mismo criterio llegará a Notificaciones, el menú desde el que se configuran sonidos, vibración, avisos de grupos y alertas de llamadas. La uniformidad visual evitará que cada apartado presente reglas de diseño distintas y permitirá reconocer con rapidez dónde comienza y termina cada grupo de funciones.
WhatsApp también trabaja en cambios para la navegación inferior
El rediseño de los ajustes forma parte de una revisión más amplia de la interfaz de Android. En la versión beta 2.26.41.6, WhatsApp mostró una barra de navegación inferior dinámica.
Con ese sistema, la barra se reduce a una píldora compacta cuando el usuario desplaza la pantalla hacia abajo. Recupera su tamaño completo al volver hacia arriba. La función continúa en fase de pruebas y todavía no está lista para la versión estable.
La aplicación también prevé modificaciones en la barra de chats, dentro de una estrategia orientada a unificar elementos visuales. WhatsApp busca que los ajustes, la navegación y las conversaciones compartan un lenguaje gráfico común en Android.
Por ahora, el menú renovado no está disponible para el público general ni para todos los participantes del programa beta. WhatsApp no ha comunicado una fecha de lanzamiento. Su llegada dependerá de las pruebas internas y de futuras actualizaciones para Android.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733

articles.title: El Metro de Madrid confirma un cambio histórico: doble cabecera y 400 millones de euros para nueva ampliación
articles.text:
Casi se daba por hecho y ahora ha terminado por confirmarse: el Metro de Madrid ya tiene diseño final para la prolongación de la Línea 1. Lo hará con una inversión de 400 millones de euros, la creación de la primera doble cabecera de la historia en el suburbano y el cambio de algunas estaciones.
¿Qué se ha aprobado? Madrid ya tiene una nueva línea de Metro para Madrid Nuevo Norte, una reforma integral en la zona norte de la capital y que también era conocida como Operación Chamartín antes de que el proyecto final fuera elegido. Este proyecto creará un nuevo parque y 10.500 viviendas, la ampliación de la Línea 1 de Metro viene a dar servicio a estas actuaciones.
Finalmente y con cinco proyectos encima de la mesa, lo que se ha propuesto es extender la actual Línea 1 de Metro con una ramificación que partirá de la estación de Chamartín. Esta era la única alternativa que proponía esta solución, las otras cuatro optaban por crear una nueva línea que conectara con la estación de Chamartín.
¿Qué hay de novedoso? Por primera vez, el Metro de Madrid tendrá una línea con dos cabeceras. La extensión de la actual Línea 1 contará con tres estaciones llamadas Centro de Negocios, Fuencarral Sur y Fuencarral Norte. Esta última junto a Pinar de Chamartín (que conecta con la línea 4) será uno de los dos inicios de la línea.
Por lo tanto, quienes viajen en la Línea 1 dirección norte tendrán que fijarse si su tren lleva por destino Pinar de Chamartín o Fuencarral Norte, tal y como sucede en otras ciudades europeas donde dos trenes con destinos diferentes pasan por un mismo andén.
Lo que se ha desechado es la absorción planteada de la Línea 4 sobre la Línea 1 en las estaciones de Bambú y Pinar de Chamartín. El primer proyecto planteaba que la cabecera de la Línea 4 se cambiara a Chamartín. Esto eliminaba esa doble cabecera pero obligaría a los vecinos que viajan al sur a hacer un transbordo apenas dos paradas después de haber tomado el tren, lo que provocó cierto rechazo.
¿Cuánto y cuándo? El nuevo proyecto de ampliación de la Línea 1 de Metro costará unos 400 millones de euros. El proyecto elegido, a pesar de que las opciones alternativas contaban con crear una nueva línea, es el más caro de todos tal y como explican en elEconomista.
Entre las otras cuatro alternativas, dos de ellas optaban por hacer una excavación casi en superficie y los otros dos eran partidarios de hacer excavaciones profundas para pasar por debajo de la M-30. Todos ellos se movían en presupuestos de entre 250 y 265 millones de euros.
En cuanto a la ejecución de las obras, de momento hay que redactar y aprobar los proyectos constructivos. Se espera que este proceso salga adelante entre 2027 y 2028 y que las obras se extiendan entre 2030 y 2032.
Una renovación profunda. La extensión de la Línea 1 de Metro de Madrid se enmarca dentro de una ampliación histórica. Además de esta bifurcación, la ciudad se encuentra inmersa en la ampliación de la Línea 11, conocida como La Gran Diagonal. Este ramal pasará de ser uno de los más cortos de la ciudad a uno de los que más kilómetros sume, dando servicio al este de la capital.
Además, también hay planteada una extensión de la Línea 10 en el sur de Madrid para ofrecer una salida más rápida hasta la capital a municipios como Leganés o Móstoles que ahora mismo tienen que ir hasta Alcorcón para conectar con esta salida hacia el norte de la ciudad.

articles.title: Paris-based Naboo acquires UK meetings and events specialist pro-ven following €58.7 million Series B | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Naboo, a Paris-based EventTech scale-up, has joined forces with UK specialist pro-ven, bringing together two of the Meetings and Events (M&E) sector’s prominent names.
Starting today, pro-ven becomes Naboo UK. Together, the combined entity now oversees €269 million ($300 million) in meetings and events worldwide. The acquisition was financed through an equal split of equity and debt. The move follows Naboo’s €58.7 million Series B funding round earlier this year, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and existing investors Notion Capital, ISAI, and Ternel.
“The future category leader in the M&E spend management market will be a pure player. Both event planners and procurement leaders have very high expectations in terms of user experience, embedded compliance, payment simplification, spend analytics and transparency. It cannot be achieved as a side business by TMCs who are still very much focused on transforming the transient travel experience. Together with pro-ven, that is the leader we are building,” said Maxime Eduardo, co-founder and CEO of Naboo.
Founded in 2022 by Eduardo, Antoine Servant, Lucien Bredin, and Jean-Louis Villeminot, Naboo is a platform for booking, managing, and running corporate events, also known as MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). Its offering spans venue sourcing, AI-assisted procurement, corporate payment cards, accounts payable, and event planning tools for organisers and participants.
The company aims to replace the fragmented event tools with its AI operating system, which uses intelligent agents to handle sourcing, quote comparisons, contract review, and payment processing automatically. According to Naboo, its platform delivers an average saving of 12% per event for clients, which includes Google, Meta, Microsoft, Siemens, as well as a quarter of the French CAC 40 index under exclusive contracts.
Established in 2005, pro-ven has spent two decades building deep relationships with enterprise clients across the UK, Europe, and globally. Its expertise spans venue and supplier sourcing, rate negotiation, approval workflows, centralised invoicing, and lodge card management. The tie-up pairs Naboo’s technological scale with proven client expertise in the UK market, where the former has been expanding since opening a London office in 2025 and has signed clients such as KPMG and HSBC.
“I am incredibly excited for our clients and our team to make such a step into the AI-native world, which I believe is the right technology to create a world leader in the M&E market,” said Julian Laxon, founder and Managing Director of pro-ven, who will continue in his role to help as Naboo builds out its UK presence.
pro-ven has 20 employees, and Naboo said it plans to retain everyone to support its exponential growth in the UK market.
“With Naboo, we are now able to address our clients’ needs for global coverage with equal quality, anywhere in the world. This is the direction our clients’ booking communities and procurement leads are clearly taking: one single vendor of record, anywhere in the world, to cover all the complex elements of venue find, event management and payment,” he added.
The corporate meetings and events sector is estimated at €358 billion ($400 billion) globally, and according to Naboo, the sector is the last major category of enterprise spend that has not yet been digitised. It says the sector has been marked by tension between event organisers looking for experience and agility and procurement and finance teams seeking visibility, compliance, and cost control.
With AI, Naboo says it is economically viable to bridge that gap for every size of event, including the smaller bookings that escaped procurement oversight. The market is reacting to this change with AMEX GBT acquired by Long Lake while Navan acquired Reed & Mackay and partnered with BoomPop.
“We are a service company. Service-as-a-software: it means our software absorbs the operational complexity – the admin, the workflows, the manual steps – so our talents can spend their time on what actually matters: the relationship,” added Eduardo.
The acquisition of pro-van comes weeks after Naboo unveiled a new brand identity in October and opened its first Asia-Pacific office in Singapore. The company has raised €90 million ($100 million) in the past three years) and now aims to exceed €900 million ($1 billion) in business volume by 2027.

articles.title: Renault fait marche arrière sur le design : ces 3 voitures sont les seules à échapper à la nouvelle règle
articles.text:
La Renaulution annoncée début 2021 par Luca de Meo n’avait absolument rien d’une blague. Les nouveaux modèles se sont enchaînés les uns après les autres en étant tous particulièrement réussis. Le Losange a fait un véritable strike avec ses pépites aussi bien issues de sa gamme standard que de sa gamme néo-rétro. La marque paraissait alors inarrêtable en multipliant les produits inédits à coups de communication grandiose.
Cinq ans plus tard, le soufflé risque-t-il de retomber sec ? La suite sera en tout cas différente. En effet, selon Laurens van den Acker, le directeur du design du groupe Renault, les futurs modèles adopteront un design plus sobre entrant dans une gamme plus homogène, surtout. Cette nouvelle direction a été voulue par François Provost, PDG fraîchement investi du groupe Renault. Des voitures plus ressemblantes, donc, mais avec une certaine nuance.
Des icônes légendaires aux styles bien distincts
Dans une interview accordée à Autocar, Van den Acker affirme qu’une distinction franche sera maintenue entre les « icônes légendaires » et les « icônes du futur ». Il précise en détail que « l’objectif des icônes légendaires est avant tout d’être des icônes et d’être reconnaissables. La Twingo et la R5 arborent le logo Renault, mais nous ne cherchons pas à leur donner les mêmes phares ni la même calandre. Le langage stylistique est totalement différent ».
« Or, lorsqu’un client achète une Twingo, il veut avant tout une Twingo et n’adhère pas à un langage stylistique Renault en tant que tel ». Renault a donc longtemps misé sur une réinterprétation des anciens modèles et les derniers concepts présentés au Mondial de l’Auto suggéraient une poursuite de cette stratégie. Les prototypes E-Space et R8 Gordini vous ont donné l’eau à la bouche, pas vrai ?
E-Space et R8 Gordini : la douche froide pour les passionnés ?
Eh bien ils ne devraient pas revenir sous cette forme puisque Van den Acker a confirmé se « regrouper un peu autour des futures icônes » avec Alexandre Malval, directeur du design de Renault. « Lorsque j’ai rejoint [Renault], j’ai créé une marque, de la Twingo au Master, puis Luca [de Meo] est arrivé [en tant que PDG du groupe] et il voulait plus de personnalité dans toutes les voitures », explique le Néerlandais.
« Il n’y a pas forcément de bonne ou de mauvaise approche […]. Nous sommes maintenant à l’autre extrémité du spectre, où elles sont toutes différentes. C’est peut-être le bon moment pour trouver un juste équilibre ». Avant de confirmer que seuls trois véhicules conserveront véritablement un design bien à eux : « nos modèles emblématiques doivent vivre leur propre histoire : ce sera d’abord la Twingo, puis la R5 et enfin la R4 ».

articles.title: La UE abre la vía para multar a Google Maps por representar a Ceuta y Melilla como “territorios en disputa” con Marruecos
articles.text:
Google Maps traza una línea gris discontinua en las fronteras terrestres de Ceuta y Melilla con Marruecos. Una queja ha pedido a la Comisión Europea que actúe para que Google Maps cambie el trazado de acuerdo con el Reglamento de Servicios Digitales.
La nota del Partido Popular sobre este asunto apareció hace poco: un comunicado sobre ambas ciudades, según el cual los coordinadores de la Comisión de Peticiones habían aprobado la iniciativa. Quien interpone la queja considera ambigua la representación de las fronteras y dice que Google debería mostrar una línea continua, no una línea discontinua. Pide a la Comisión Europea que actúe en relación con los riesgos de desinformación que, según la queja, podría generar el mapa. Su queja refleja su posición y no demuestra que se haya incumplido el reglamento.
El Observatorio de Ceuta y Melilla ha informado de que su director, Carlos Echeverría, había escrito a Google España en 2023 sobre el tema. También apareció en una nota del Observatorio el 23 de septiembre de 2026, que afirmaba que el asunto aún no se había resuelto.
Las notas de Google indican que el servicio diferencia entre varias fronteras. En el apartado sobre fronteras y nombres de los países, las líneas grises continuas se reservan a las fronteras internacionales sin discusión, y las discontinuas, a aquellas cuya definición sea objeto de controversia (y a determinados límites provisionales o decididos por tratados). Solo por el estilo de la línea discontinua no se puede distinguir qué categoría aplica Google a cada frontera.
Qué tendría que pasar para que se sancionara a Google
Google Maps está sujeto a normas de cumplimiento adicionales de conformidad con el Reglamento de Servicios Digitales, en virtud del cual la Comisión Europea calificó el 25 de abril de 2023 al servicio de “plataforma en línea de muy gran tamaño”. Según los artículos 34 y 35 del Reglamento, Google debe evaluar los riesgos sistémicos que plantea su servicio y aplicar medidas para mitigarlos.
La Comisión puede solicitar información y obtener pruebas si sospecha que se ha producido una infracción. Antes de decidir sancionar a la empresa por incumplimiento del reglamento, debe acreditar la infracción y darle la oportunidad de presentar sus argumentos.
La sanción por infracción de ese reglamento puede ascender hasta el 6 % de la facturación mundial del proveedor de servicios digitales durante el ejercicio fiscal anterior. Esta cifra se determina en función de varios factores, entre ellos la gravedad de la infracción y su duración. El texto legal establece ese porcentaje como máximo, sin fijar una sanción específica para Maps por su trazado de fronteras. La Comisión también puede ordenar el cumplimiento efectivo de determinadas obligaciones y sus decisiones pueden ser objeto de revisión judicial ante los tribunales de la Unión Europea.
El caso del golfo de México
El 22 de octubre de 2025, la Comisión respondió a una queja de Pedro Lourenco sobre el cambio del nombre del golfo de México en Google Maps. La Comisión mencionó las obligaciones de Google en materia de evaluación de riesgos en su respuesta a la queja de Lourenco y le pidió pruebas de los posibles efectos negativos relacionados con los riesgos sistémicos previstos en el reglamento.
La respuesta se refería a otro nombre geográfico y no a las fronteras de las dos ciudades españolas mencionadas anteriormente. Para que la Comisión sancione a Google por el trazado de fronteras mencionado, primero debe existir una prueba de que Google incumplió sus obligaciones.
